posts.title: Mary Peltola trashes New York Times report on Dan Sullivan plot, calling it a 'distraction'
posts.excerpt: Alaskan Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola dismissed the New York Times investigation into her campaign Wednesday as a "distraction" to sell papers.
posts.content:
During a rally on Wednesday, Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola dismissed a New York Times report alleging that her campaign took part in an effort to peel votes away from incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan to a same-named rival, calling the story a "distraction" used to sell papers.

"This is just another distraction," Peltola said in a video shared on X by local Alaskan writer Matt Tunseth. "It's another diversion. Every day, it’s some new, you know, ‘Look over here moment.’ Not Dan Sullivan, registered Republican, incumbent, voted for this war in Iran 14 times. Lisa Murkowski quit voting for that war in Iran six months ago, and he’s doubling and tripling down."

The New York Times published an investigation on Wednesday that described a covert operation, internally dubbed the "ballot composition project," to recruit spoiler candidates with the same name as Sullivan.

DEM BUCKS PARTY OVER ALLEGED ALASKA VOTE-SIPHONING EFFORT: 'NEITHER PARTY SHOULD BE DOING IT'

According to the report, since 2025, a Peltola staffer was directed to comb through state voter rolls to compile a list of Alaskans named Dan Sullivan.

The operation allegedly involved aides from the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), top campaign advisors, party lawyers and an operative who traveled across the state under assumed names.

"The plan worked. This spring, a retired teacher from a tiny fishing village along the Alaska Panhandle, reachable only by air and sea, announced his candidacy for Senate. His name was Dan J. Sullivan," the Times reported.

At the rally, however, Peltola dismissed the report, claiming that it was made to "get subscriptions."

"And this is not somebody who’s working in our best interest. And anybody who’s working in our best interest isn’t going to talk about the nonsense. This is all stuff to sell newspapers. This is all stuff to get subscriptions. Nobody at The New York Times cares about affordability in Alaska," Peltola said.

SCHIFF ACCUSES DOJ OF TRYING TO 'SUBVERT' ELECTIONS AS GOP ALLEGES SAME-NAME CANDIDATE MEANT TO CONFUSE VOTERS

Fox News Digital reached out to the Peltola campaign and the New York Times for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Sen. Sullivan campaign spokesperson Nate Adams told Fox News Digital, "Instead of admitting she has been caught red-handed in a scheme to manipulate and deceive Alaska voters, Mary Peltola's response is to attack the media outlets she has been lying to for months."

Elisa Rios, Peltola’s former campaign manager who was fired in August, told the Times that while Peltola was not directly involved in orchestrating the project, she was "definitely aware."

In a previous statement to Fox News, the DSCC said it was not involved with the other Sullivan campaign.

TRUMP SAYS 'WE ARE LOOKING INTO' OTHER DAN SULLIVAN ON ALASKA BALLOT, WARNS ABOUT GOVERNOR'S RACE

"Republicans have a long history of recruiting and propping up candidates in an attempt to boost their own campaigns, including recruiting a prisoner with a New York address to run against Mary Peltola and spending nearly half a million dollars to secure a spot on the ballot in Alaska for an Arizona resident in the Senate race this cycle," a DSCC spokesperson said.

In a statement to The New York Times, Peltola’s campaign said, "The Alaskans for Mary campaign has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign and did not recruit any candidates into the race."

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/media/mary-peltola-trashes-new-york-times-report-dan-sullivan-plot-calling-distraction

Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on Thursday as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open.

The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week’s updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital.

Long seen as tennis’ nearly-man, Zverev has enjoyed a stellar 2026, breaking his major duck by picking up the titles at the French and US Opens.

Now he has broken further ground by becoming only the 30th man to claim top spot since the rankings were first published in 1973.

He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday’s new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe.

Due to a knee injury Italy’s Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him.

And the big-serving Hamburg native ensured he did just that ahead of the season-ending ATP Finals next month by seeing off Martin Landaluce and Griekspoor in his opening two matches in Vienna.

Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain’s Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books.

He raced out of the blocks on Thursday, breaking the 30-year-old Dutchman in the very first game and then confidently serving his way into a one-set lead.

The second frame went to 5-5 before Zverev pounced on Griekspoor’s serve to get his nose in front.

The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German’s racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction.

But once the umpire covered the problematic panel up with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/germanys-zverev-becomes-tennis-world-no-1/

posts.title: Albanian opposition lawmakers disrupt parliament with smoke flares and furious attacks on socialist PM
posts.excerpt: Sali Berisha's microphone was cut after he declared ruling lawmakers "deserve tear gas" as Democratic Party members lit flares inside parliament.
posts.content:
Opposition lawmakers in Albania disrupted a parliamentary session on Thursday by setting off flares that filled the chamber with colored smoke, marking an escalation following weeks of student-led anti-government protests.

Members of the main opposition Democratic Party also blocked access to the podium during a vote on a central bank bill, Reuters reported.

"These ruling lawmakers are criminals, and they deserve tear gas, rubber bullets, cracked skulls, and broken bones—not the young people," opposition leader Sali Berisha declared during a speech before his microphone was cut off.

SERBIA’S STUDENT MOVEMENT TOPPLES VUCIC’S PARTY AFTER 14 YEARS, BUT POLITICAL AGENDA REMAINS UNCLEAR

As the chamber devolved into chaos, fellow opposition members surrounded Berisha, holding blue flares, the official color of their party, and displaying images of protesters injured by police rubber bullets.

Albania has been gripped in recent weeks by student-led demonstrations demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama over alleged government corruption, underfunded schools, widespread unemployment, and a lack of economic opportunities.

SERBIA’S LONGTIME LEADER FACES BIGGEST POLITICAL TEST AS STUDENTS MOUNT ELECTION CHALLENGE

The protests began on Oct. 13 and quickly turned violent as demonstrators clashed with police and set fire to government buildings. Protesters also targeted Rama’s ruling Socialist Party headquarters in Tirana, clashing with riot police deployed to protect the property.

The unrest has since spread to several other cities across the country.

THOUSANDS FLOOD BRUSSELS STREETS AS ANTI-AUSTERITY PROTESTS ERUPT INTO CLASHES WITH POLICE

In response, Rama, who has governed since 2013 and secured a fourth term last year, blamed "foreign hands who do not want Albania in the European Union. " He accused outside forces of manipulating the movement, claiming they "represent organized crime rather than students. "

To curb the violence, Rama introduced strict new measures, including $6,000 fines for anyone participating in a protest that turns violent, regardless of whether they personally commit acts of violence.

Another demonstration is scheduled for Saturday.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/world/albanian-opposition-lawmakers-disrupt-parliament-smoke-flares-furious-attacks-socialist-pm

posts.title: Bari Weiss faced 'significant resistance' from CBS News staffers about Alaska ballot scandal, insiders say
posts.excerpt: CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss faced resistance among staff at a meeting when talking about the New York Times' report on the Alaska ballot scandal.
posts.content:
EXCLUSIVE — CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss faced "significant resistance" from staff at Thursday's 9 a.m. meeting about the growing Alaska ballot controversy, network insiders told Fox News Digital.

"This is a scandal," Weiss declared to staff.

According to multiple sources on the call, several CBS News staffers pushed back at Weiss' enthusiasm over the bombshell New York Times report alleging Democrats schemed to find a Dan Sullivan to run against incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, in hopes of aiding Democratic opponent Mary Peltola.

DEM STRATEGIST SHRUGS OFF ALASKA BALLOT SCANDAL ON MS NOW, INSISTS 'THIS STUFF HAPPENS ALL THE TIME'

Many on the call shrugged it off as routine politics and said that Republicans have also engaged in similar scheming.

When Weiss asked for other examples of ballot confusion, "Face the Nation" moderator Margaret Brennan reportedly pointed to New Hampshire Senate candidate John Sununu, suggesting that midterm voters might confuse him with his brother, former Governor Chris Sununu.

ALASKA'S GOVERNOR ODERS INVESTIGATION AFTER NYT REPORT ON ALLEGED DEM-LINKED SENATE ELECTION SCHEME

CBS News political correspondent Ed O'Keefe also insisted that such tactics are nothing new. Earlier that morning, during his appearance on "CBS Mornings", O'Keefe stressed to viewers that what happened in Alaska "could be a dirty trick, but it's not illegal," adding that "this has happened before, kind of." He pointed to the 2016 Alaska Senate race when former Anchorage mayor Dan Sullivan — no relation to the U.S. Senator of the same name — briefly ran against incumbent Sen. Lisa Murkowski in the GOP primary, hoping "name recognition" of the other sitting senator would help his own candidacy.

A separate CBS staffer on the call pushed back against the notion that colleagues like Brennan and O'Keefe were trying to downplay the scandal, telling Fox News Digital they were providing context to the story being discussed.

MARY PELTOLA'S CAMPAIGN, DEMS BACKED COVERT SCHEME TO FIELD SPOILER CANDIDATES IN ALASKA SENATE RACE: REPORT

The staffer also said the meeting was never contentious and that it was a "healthy, good conversation."

Still, Weiss called the uproar in Alaska a "great story" that the network should follow and urged staff to push for stories like the one The New York Times broke, calling it a "learning moment."

A spokesperson for CBS News declined to comment.

Republicans have long been suspicious about the candidacy of Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a retired teacher who is among four Senate candidates listed on Alaska's rank-choice ballot. The Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against the state of Alaska seeking to block certification of the election results if the incumbent senator loses and votes cast for the other Sullivan could have changed the outcome.

On Wednesday, The New York Times alleged his candidacy was no coincidence.

"In the summer of 2025, a staffer for Mary Peltola, the Alaska Democrat who was eyeing a run for Senate, received unusual instructions from top campaign aides: Find as many people named Dan Sullivan in Alaska as you can," the Times began its report Wednesday.

"The staffer complied, combing through voter records to produce a list of Dan Sullivans from across the state. ... [I]f the Peltola campaign or its allies could track down and persuade another Dan Sullivan to run for Senate, the confusion could cost the senator crucial votes on the state’s unusual, four-person ballot. The plan worked," the report said.

SEN DAN SULLIVAN BRANDS PELTOLA'S ALLEGED BALLOT SCHEME A 'SCANDAL AT THE HIGHEST ORDER'

According to Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, Peltola was not directly involved in the scheme but was "definitely aware."

Peltola's campaign has denied involvement in his candidacy.

"But The Times has found, based on interviews and text messages, along with documents prepared for a potential lawsuit against the campaign, that not only did Ms. Peltola’s team work with people trying to recruit Mr. Sullivan to run for Senate, but the effort was much broader," the Times reported. "The group worked to coax other would-be spoilers into the race, to dilute the incumbent’s support and help catapult the Democrat to victory."

Peltola called the Times report a "distraction" and "stuff to sell newspapers." However, Republican Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation into whether any crimes or civil violations were committed.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/media/bari-weiss-faced-significant-resistance-cbs-news-staffers-alaska-ballot-scandal-insiders-say

posts.title: Awujale succession: DSS invites Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders
posts.excerpt: The Department of State Services (DSS) in Ogun State has reportedly invited three leaders of the Fusengbuwa ruling house over the alleged sale of expression-of-interest forms to princes seeking to bec
posts.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Department of State Services (DSS) in Ogun State has reportedly invited three leaders of the Fusengbuwa ruling house over the alleged sale of expression-of-interest forms to princes seeking to become the next Awujale of Ijebuland.

Those reportedly invited are the Chairman of the ruling house, Otunba Abdulateef Owoyemi; the deputy chairman, Otunba Dokun Ajidagba; and the vice chairman, Prof. Fassy Yusuf.

The invitation comes amid an ongoing dispute over the selection of a new Awujale following the death of the previous monarch, Oba Sikiru Adetona, in July 2025, at the age of 91, after 65 years on the throne.

A letter circulating online, purportedly signed by one Yemi Oloto, directed the three ruling house leaders to appear before the State Director of Security at the DSS office in Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 4 p.m.

The letter, which indicated that the meeting was connected with an investigation into the sale of expression-of-interest forms to princes interested in the vacant stool, read in part: “I am directed to invite you for a meeting with the State Director of Security (SDS), Department of State Services (DSS), Ogun State, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, today, 29th October, 2026, 1600 hours (4 p.m.).

“The meeting is in furtherance of investigating activities in respect of the sale of expression-of-interest forms to interested princes for the vacant stool of Awujale of Ijebuland.”

The letter further stated that an officer had been designated at the main gate to facilitate the invitees’ entry into the premises, before concluding with the director’s best wishes.

When contacted, Prof. Yusuf confirmed receiving the invitation but said he was in Abuja attending to a matter before the Supreme Court and would therefore be unable to honour it.

The professor of Mass Communication and lawyer said: “I just received the letter from the DSS not long ago, but I am in Abuja attending to a matter at the Supreme Court. I have discountenanced their letter.”

Similarly, Ajidagba confirmed receiving the invitation on Thursday afternoon, saying it was delivered at about 2:30 p.m. with instructions to report at the DSS office by 4:30 p.m.

He, however, questioned the timing of the invitation, arguing that matters relating to the succession process were already before the courts.

“I received the DSS invitation on Thursday at about 2:30 p.m., and I was told to report at their office by 4:30 p.m. There was, however, no way I could honour such an invitation when all of these matters are already in court. The status quo must be allowed to remain; that is the position of the law,” he said.

There was no immediate confirmation from the DSS on the reported invitations or the allegations prompting them.

The latest development comes against the backdrop of previous engagements between security agencies and stakeholders in the Awujale succession process.

Security agencies, including the Ogun State Police Command, had reportedly summoned nine kingmakers in Ijebu-Ode and the three Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders on two occasions to appear at the police headquarters in Eleweran, Abeokuta.

The invitations were said to be connected with allegations of bribery and financial inducement in the selection of a new Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland.

Owoyemi has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in connection with the succession process.

The three ruling house leaders have also instituted legal proceedings against the Ogun State government over the suspension of the selection process, which has remained stalled since January 2026.

In August, the Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders approached the Ogun State High Court sitting in Ijebu-Ode, seeking orders compelling the completion of the process for selecting the next Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland.

The suit, numbered HCJ/149/2026 and dated August 21, 2026, was instituted by Owoyemi, Ajidagba and Yusuf.

The defendants include Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Mr Oluwasina Ogungbade (SAN); the Ogun State Executive Council; the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Ganiyu Hamzat; and the Secretary of Ijebu-Ode Local Government.

Also joined as defendants are members of the Awujale Afobaje/Kingmakers Council, including Olorogun Sonny Kuku, Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Chief Oluwaranti Lekan Osifeso, Chief Jimi Lawal, Chief Abimbola Okenla, Chief Kunle Ogunade, Chief Agboola Alausa, Chief Adebisi Adaran and Chief Ayotunde Ola Odulaja.

Among other reliefs, the claimants are asking the court to determine whether the state government had the legal authority to order or facilitate the alleged entry into and locking of the Awujale palace on January 20, 2026.

According to the claimants, the action was intended to physically prevent the kingmakers from convening and concluding the statutory process for selecting a successor to the late monarch.

The dispute has further complicated efforts to fill the vacant traditional stool, with the government maintaining that the process must be conducted peacefully and in accordance with the applicable procedures.

Meanwhile, Governor Abiodun has assured the people of Ijebuland that a new Awujale will emerge before May 29, 2027.

The governor gave the assurance on Tuesday at the Ogun East Senatorial District stakeholders’ meeting in Ijebu-Ode, where he engaged representatives of various interest groups on traditional affairs, governance and the economic prospects of the district.

According to a statement issued on Wednesday, Abiodun reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to ensuring a smooth and acceptable succession process.

“On the succession process for the revered Awujale stool, Abiodun assured the people that his administration was committed to facilitating a smooth, peaceful and widely acceptable process leading to the emergence of a new monarch,” the statement said.

The governor acknowledged the significance of the Awujale institution to the cultural heritage, identity and unity of Ijebuland, urging residents to remain calm and patient while the necessary procedures were being concluded.

He added that his administration was giving the matter the attention it deserved to ensure that the process was completed peacefully and that the eventual emergence of a new monarch enjoyed the acceptance and support of the people.

The Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025 following the death of Oba Adetona, who ruled for 65 years and was widely regarded as one of Nigeria’s longest-reigning traditional rulers.

The Ogun State Government halted the succession process in January 2026, citing petitions from security agencies and other stakeholders. The suspension followed an earlier halt in December 2025 over procedural concerns.

A total of 95 aspirants—94 princes and one princess—reportedly emerged from the Fusengbuwa ruling house nomination exercise held in Ijebu-Ode in December 2025 before the government suspended further proceedings.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/awujale-succession-dss-invites-fusengbuwa-ruling-house-leaders/

posts.title: Lane Kiffin's own words come back to bite him, MLB's long winter & Paige Spiranac's Halloween costume tease!
posts.excerpt: Lane Kiffin takes aim at the SEC over Alabama-LSU's afternoon kickoff slot, but college football fans aren't buying his conspiracy theories.
posts.content:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Over the hump and safely onto the other side of the week. Is this the biggest weekend of the year to date?

I think it might be.

We've got football all weekend long, obviously. Duh. More importantly, we also have Halloween, which lands on a Saturday. I did some big J digging, and it's the last time that'll happen until 2037. True story. Eleven years! Lord knows what this place will look like in 11 years, but I assume if this column is somehow still alive, it'll be run by a robot. That's almost a guarantee.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Beyond all of that, we also get an extra hour of Halloween this weekend! That's right. The dreaded "fall back" weekend is upon us. I loved this time of year in college, but that was, admittedly, a long time ago. Nothing hit better than being at a party and seeing the iPhone 4 clock switch back to 1 a.m.

It was the best.

But I have kids now, and they do not care what the clock says. So, come Sunday morning when it says 5:30, they'll be up and ready to roll.

"Just put them to bed later!"

Doesn't work for a 2-year-old, folks. They don't care. Hard hats on, parents. We're all in this together.

On that note, welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where Lane Kiffin, somehow, finds something else to complain about. College football fans ain't having it.

Nor should they.

What else? I've got Paige Spiranac teasing her Halloween costume ahead of the big day, another subdued baseball celebration last night, and where did this MLB postseason rank for you?

I gotta be honest ... it wasn't great. And now we're going into a lockout.

The vibes aren't the best right now! But we'll get into it.

OLIVIA DUNNE POURS BEERS LIKE A PATRIOT WHILE HER LSU TIGERS RUN UP THE SCORE, GATOR BAIT & LANE'S SUBTLE SHOT

Grab you a tiny violin for Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers, and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap!

Let's get this ball rolling, because the rain has finally stopped here in Florida for the first time since Sunday and I've got a pumpkin patch to get to before it starts back up.

Big weekend of college football, as I said earlier. Now, I hate to jump ahead a week, but Lane Kiffin has left me no choice.

For about six months now, fans have had Nov. 7 circled on their calendars. It's shaping up to be, arguably, the greatest weekend of college football ever.

And, of course, Alabama-LSU. That's the big one, right?

... Right?

...... RIGHT?!

"If someone thinks the SEC wants us to win this year after what’s been going on, they must have just been on Mars the last four months. So I guess when I look at it that way, I’m not surprised."

So, Lane Kiffin sent shots at the SEC for next weekend's big game not being in primetime, which is hilarious for a couple different reasons.

So, when Lane was at Ole Miss, everyone was out to get him. Now, he's at LSU and ... everyone's out to get him?

See a pattern? It's silly. I used to love Lane Kiffin, by the way. He was a content machine. He was fun, and likable, and somewhat relatable.

Now? I think he just whines a lot.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I'm not alone:

For what it's worth, LSU is 1-7 since 2012 against Alabama in night games in Baton Rouge. Perhaps Lane should be thanking ESPN/SEC for this one?

OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big night of FOOTBALL!

PS: I know there's an NFL game on tonight, but don't forget about college. Did you know there's a game on ESPN tonight with an OVER/UNDER set at 76.5?!

That's right. North Texas and FAU. A biggie. Does anyone here have the stones to take the over when it's at that number? I think I'll dabble.

Speaking of stones ... how about the Milwaukee Brewers just quietly completing one of the most dominant postseason runs of all time? Think about it.

They manhandles the Padres, swept the Dodgers, and then pretty much had their way with Tampa ...

And then treated winning it all like they'd just polished off a three-game sweep of the Marlins in June:

Thoughts? I've honestly thought all the celebrations this postseason have been pretty t(l)ame. There's certainly something to be said about "acting like you've been there before."

I get that ...

Except this was Milwaukee's first ever World Series title! And that's what we got? I don't know. Just seemed a bit off.

Frankly, this whole postseason did:

I love baseball. I watch every Red Sox game all year long. I'm a 162-er. I'm not trying to knock it here ... but yeah, it was a bad postseason. Sometimes it just happens, right?

The best part was watching the Dodgers lose. I think we can all agree on that, right? But otherwise, there really weren't any moments. I guess you could point to Milwaukee's walk-off against Mason Miller a month ago as a pivotal moment. That was fun.

But you just never really felt it, right? Again, sometimes that's just the way it goes. You're not gonna bat a thousand every year.

Regardless, we're gonna be BEGGING for one of these games in about six months when all we're talking about is salary caps and floors.

Sadly, winter is here — and I fear it's gonna be a long one.

OK, that's it for today. I'll be damned if I end it on a sour note, so here's Paige Spiranac's Halloween tease on the way out.

Zoinks!

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/outkick-sports/lane-kiffin-words-back-bite-mlb-long-winter-paige-spiranac-halloween-costume-tease

posts.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Stablecoins here to optimise financial system, not replace it’
posts.excerpt: Stablecoins could transform cross-border payments by reducing transaction delays, improving liquidity and making money transfers faster and more accessible, speakers at Moonshot 2026 have said. The po
posts.content:
By Efosa Taiwo

Stablecoins could transform cross-border payments by reducing transaction delays, improving liquidity and making money transfers faster and more accessible, speakers at Moonshot 2026 have said.

The speakers made the remarks during a panel session titled “The New Payment Backbone: Stablecoins as Core Infrastructure for Global Liquidity” on the Emerging Tech Stage, where industry leaders discussed how stablecoins could reshape payments across Africa and the global financial system.

Mercy Emmanuel, Stablecoin & Blockchain Vertical Lead, Flutterwave, said stablecoins could simplify international transfers, which often involve multiple intermediaries and take several days to complete.

“Sending money from Lagos to Nairobi goes through a lot. It could take two to five days before it gets to its destination. Stablecoins collapse all these,” Emmanuel said.

She likened the technology to a moving train that operates without the restrictions of banking hours and time zones, arguing that it could make payments almost instantaneous and allow businesses to conduct transactions seamlessly alongside their online operations.

According to her, stablecoins could also encourage businesses to rethink their payment processes and build more efficient financial operations.

“Stablecoins are here to optimise the financial system, not displace the traditional way,” she said, adding that the financial industry was moving towards a system in which the focus would be on how quickly and efficiently money could move from one point to another.

Tayo Oviosu, Group Chief Executive Officer of Paga, said widespread stablecoin adoption would require collaboration among financial technology companies, sufficient liquidity and simpler access for everyday users.

He argued that consumers were more concerned about the cost and speed of financial services than the underlying technology powering their transactions.

“Ultimately, it is giving them what they want: they want to go from fiat to fiat. Stablecoin can be used in between,” he said.

Oviosu added that solving liquidity challenges would make stablecoin transactions easier to access and use, stressing that no single company could independently make the technology a mainstream part of everyday financial life.

“We want to make it simple. The way you can come to Paga and get a naira wallet, get a stablecoin wallet. That is the part of the user,” he said.

He also called for industry players to work together to expand the use of stablecoins, noting that stronger collaboration would be necessary to improve access to the infrastructure and liquidity required to support wider adoption.

Ife Johnson, co-founder of JuicyWay, also emphasised the need for shared infrastructure, urging industry players to move away from isolated systems towards solutions that could support the wider financial ecosystem.

“The mind shift that needs to happen is moving from silos to shared infrastructure for industry players,” Johnson said.

On regulation, Johnson said collaboration between businesses and regulators would be critical to ensuring the technology could develop responsibly.

He noted that adoption could take time because of the broader implications of introducing new payment systems into existing financial structures.

He expressed confidence that demonstrating responsible implementation and addressing potential concerns would help build

regulatory trust and encourage progress.

Oviosu also pointed to changing conversations around stablecoins and digital payments in Nigeria, saying engagement between industry stakeholders and regulators had become increasingly encouraging.

“Three, four years ago, who could have said CBN will support stablecoins, NCC welcomes the idea? It is interesting to see that dialogue,” he said.

He added that Nigeria could help set an example for other African markets if stakeholders maintained constructive engagement and worked together to address the challenges surrounding adoption.

Emmanuel similarly welcomed what she described as growing support from the Federal Government, saying cooperation among industry participants and policymakers would be important to the development of the ecosystem.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/moonshot-2026-stablecoins-here-to-optimise-financial-system-not-replace-it/

posts.title: Grealish dropped for Everton’s League Cup tie after disciplinary breach
posts.excerpt: Jack Grealish was dropped for Everton's League Cup fourth round clash against Newcastle on Thursday after "a breach of club discipline". The post Grealish dropped for Everton’s League Cup tie after di
posts.content:
Jack Grealish was dropped for Everton’s League Cup fourth round clash against Newcastle on Thursday after “a breach of club discipline”.

It was reported that the breach related to Grealish’s unauthorised absence from training.

The 31-year-old missed Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Arsenal in the Premier League due to an illness.

Grealish, who is on a second season-long loan from Manchester City, had started Everton’s three Premier League matches prior to their defeat against champions Arsenal.

The 31-year-old has made six appearances for David Moyes’s side this term, most recently in their loss against Chelsea on October 17.

Grealish has been dogged by criticism of his off-pitch behaviour for several years amid reports of nightclub incidents that saw him fall out of favour at City.

After playing a key role in City’s treble-winning campaign in 2022-23, Grealish became an increasingly sidelined figure at the Etihad Stadium.

Everton are facing Newcastle for a place in the League Cup quarter-finals, with Fleetwood awaiting the winner after their shock victory over Arsenal on Tuesday.

EX-CHIEF SAYS CHRISTA PIKE WAS 'ALMOST GIDDY' DESCRIBING MURDER AS GOVERNOR WEIGHS IN AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION

posts.title: 2027: You are arrogant - Okorocha hits Imo Gov, Hope Uzodinma
posts.excerpt: Former Imo West Senator Rochas Okorocha on Thursday described Imo State Governor Hope Uzodinma as arrogant. Okorocha said Uzodinma acted arrogantly by declaring during the All Progressives Congress, A
posts.content:
Former Imo West Senator Rochas Okorocha on Thursday described Imo State Governor Hope Uzodinma as arrogant.

Okorocha said Uzodinma acted arrogantly by declaring during the All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council inauguration that he would be on the ballot in 2027.

Speaking on Channels Television's Politics Today, Okorocha said, “The day of our inauguration for the PCC, Hope Uzodinma, before the President, announced that, 'I will be on the ballot.' That was so arrogant of anybody to say what is in court. You have already decided that you are going to win.

“When the matter is in court, you must allow the court to take a decision. You are not the court, so you can't arrogate to yourself the power of knowing what's going to happen.”

This comes as the Federal High Court in Abuja declared Okorocha the All Progressives Congress, APC, candidate for the Imo West senatorial seat in the forthcoming election.

Justice Obiora Egwuatu had ruled that Uzodinma should stop parading himself as the winner of the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18 and monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC.

The judge held that evidence presented before the court established that Okorocha won the majority of votes cast in the primary.

posts.title: 2027: Police train officers on election security in Niger
posts.excerpt: The Niger State Police Command has trained its officers on election security management, warning against partisan conduct, arbitrary arrests and interference in the electoral process ahead of the 2027
posts.content:
The Niger State Police Command has trained its officers on election security management, warning against partisan conduct, arbitrary arrests and interference in the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The training, organised in collaboration with the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, was held on Thursday during the command’s end-of-month conference at the Police Officers’ Mess, Dutsen-Kura, Minna.

INEC State Training Officer, Dauda Haruna, said officers must remain professional and impartial while protecting voters, candidates, party agents and electoral officials.

Speaking on professionalism, accountability and credible elections, Haruna stressed the need for officers to enforce electoral laws, make lawful arrests, preserve evidence and document electoral offences.

He cautioned personnel against provocative conduct and actions based on rumours or unverified allegations, urging them to verify claims of misconduct before taking action.

The INEC official also urged officers to de-escalate tensions at polling units, prevent clashes between opposing groups and respect the rights of all electoral participants.

He clarified that the inspection and verification of electoral materials remained the responsibility of INEC and its authorised representatives, while police personnel were expected to provide security within their assigned mandates.

The training also covered electoral offences and penalties under the Electoral Act 2026, alongside procedures for managing misconduct at polling units.

Haruna highlighted the use of Registration Area Centres, RACs, and Super RACs to reduce delays in transporting electoral materials. He also introduced the Collation Support Result Verification System, CSRVS, designed to identify errors during the collation of election results.

In his remarks, the Commissioner of Police, Adamu Abdullahi Elleman, assured INEC of the command’s continued support for peaceful and credible elections.

Elleman said continuous training was essential to improving officers’ professionalism, adding that a team sponsored by the Nigeria Police Trust Fund would visit the command to provide further training on election security.

He also directed officers to intensify surveillance patrols, strengthen intelligence gathering and provide security for political campaigns. He further instructed them to ensure that campaign activities were promptly reported.

2027: Police train officers on election security in Niger

posts.excerpt: Former Imo State Governor, Rochas Okorocha, has taken a swipe at Governor Hope Uzodinma, saying the governor has never won any election in his political career. Okorocha said this on Thursday during a
posts.content:
Former Imo State Governor, Rochas Okorocha, has taken a swipe at Governor Hope Uzodinma, saying the governor has never won any election in his political career.

Okorocha said this on Thursday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, shortly after the Federal High Court in Abuja declared him as the authentic APC candidate for Imo West Senatorial District.

He said that Uzodinma's political history has always been marred by controversy, recalling how he became governor in 2020 after coming fourth in the 2019 governorship election.

"This was the same thing that happened when one person wrote more than 300 results, causing someone who came fourth to become number one. This man has never won any election in his life," Okorocha said.

He said the recent judgment nullifying Uzodinma's senatorial candidacy has again exposed the pattern.

DAILY POST recalls that the court, presided over by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, had ruled that Okorocha won the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, and ordered the party to forward his name to INEC.

Okorocha thanked the judiciary for standing on the side of justice and said the people of Imo West can now breathe a sigh of relief.

"This is a victory for Imo State. The shackles on Imo have been broken," he added.

posts.title: 2027: We were almost discouraged from coming to South-East – Makinde
posts.excerpt: The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Engr Seyi Makinde on Thursday said he was almost discouraged from coming to the South-East to hold his town hall meeting. Makinde, who s
posts.content:
The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Engr Seyi Makinde on Thursday said he was almost discouraged from coming to the South-East to hold his town hall meeting.

Makinde, who spoke in Enugu, where he addressed South-East stakeholders, said he considered the fact that the zone is the stronghold of Mr Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC.

The Oyo State governor, however, said he had enormous regard for the people of the zone.

“We were almost discouraged. Oh, this is the zone for my friend and brother, His Excellency Peter Obi.

“And the South-East is totally for him.

“And we said, well, we definitely will bring our message also to the South-East.

“And my message to you today is that, please, reject all divisions across either religious or ethnic lines. The challenges we are faced with do not know religion, do not know ethnicity,” he said.

The APM candidate stated that he had delayed the release of his manifesto in order to gauge the feelings and needs of the Nigerian masses.

“People have been asking us, where's your manifesto?

“Oh, you've been criticising the current administration, but tell us what you want to do.

“Well, we've been going around the country. We've been to the North-East, the North-West, the North-Central, the South-South, the South-West, and we're now in the South-East.

“We're not like that. We don't just manufacture things from the sky. We listen to our people, we hear from them what they would like to see, and we incorporate it into our agenda.

“So, this is the last of the town hall meetings. Over this weekend, we'll be working around the clock with our team to get our manifesto ready, and it will be launched on the 4th of November, 2026,” he disclosed, adding that his manifesto would contain the needs of Nigerians and proposed solutions.

Makinde also referenced the latest event involving Nyesom Wike’s Rainbow Coalition in Rivers State as a sign of the party’s growth.

Apparently referring to Wike, he said a good friend of his had included the APM in the Rainbow Coalition, an indication that the party was growing.

“I saw a good friend of mine who was putting together the Rainbow Coalition in Rivers State.

“And he listed all the parties in the Rainbow Coalition and mentioned APM.

“And I said, so APM suddenly has graduated to when they will add APM to their Rainbow Coalition?

“They've tried and tried to undermine almost every opposition political party. All the parties have been, one way or the other, undermined.

“They can try. They can pull down posters. They can even ensure that they disturb your campaign while they are giving people money to do their bidding. We are winning hearts.

“So, let them pull the posters down. Let them destroy your billboards. But please, have your voter's card and your thumb. They cannot pull your thumb from you. And that is what you will use to send them away.

“Secondly, they've said we have a lot of money in our external reserves. We have a lot of money. That's what they said. They even said the revenue service has collected enough revenue and taxes to surpass the target for the year.

“But we still have to borrow money. How do we cross this hurdle?” he queried.

While also questioning Tinubu’s trip to Saudi Arabia, Makinde said:

“I was reading on social media last night up until this morning that our president is travelling to Saudi Arabia to pray for Nigeria. Prayers are answered even in this country."

“Please, we will stay here, we will pray for Nigeria, and we will also pray for our leaders' peace. Stop all the deceit and tell Nigerians the exact, true situation of things,” he added.

2027: We were almost discouraged from coming to South-East – Makinde

posts.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Africa must move from content creation to value capture’ — Tech leader Juliet Ehimuan
posts.excerpt: Juliet Ehimuan, founder of Beyond Limits and former Director of Google West Africa, has urged African creatives and technology entrepreneurs to move beyond content creation to building sustainable bus
posts.content:
By Efosa Taiwo

Juliet Ehimuan, founder of Beyond Limits and former Director of Google West Africa, has urged African creatives and technology entrepreneurs to move beyond content creation to building sustainable businesses that own intellectual property and capture value from their work.

Ehimuan made the call while speaking on artificial intelligence (AI) and the future of African creativity at Moonshot 2026 during a keynote speech on Thursday.

She said Africa’s creative economy remained underdeveloped, stressing the need to turn the continent’s creative talent into commercially viable enterprises capable of generating greater economic value.

“Our creative economy is still less than 2% of GDP,” she said, highlighting the need for a shift from producing content to building businesses around it.

According to her, African creators must focus on owning the intellectual property behind their work and exploring different ways to commercialise it.

“We need to move from content creation to value capture. We need to move from having creative talents to building enterprises. We should move from content creation to IP,” Ehimuan said.

She explained that intellectual property ownership could open up multiple revenue streams, noting that a book could be adapted into a series, while a podcast could generate additional commercial opportunities.

“There are so many ways to monetise content if you have the IP for that,” she said, emphasising the importance of owning intellectual property and the infrastructure needed to distribute and commercialise creative products.

Ehimuan outlined three priorities for Africa’s creative and technology sectors: adopting and developing AI capabilities, building and owning valuable assets, and establishing businesses capable of reaching wider markets.

On AI adoption, she encouraged African businesses to develop their capabilities and stay ahead of technological changes, noting that the technology could improve productivity and create new opportunities across industries.

She also urged creators and businesses to protect their rights and permissions while developing distinctive intellectual property that could be commercialised over time.

Vanguard News

posts.title: ‘One in 4 Nigerian stroke patients under 50’
posts.excerpt: “One out of every four cases of stroke in Nigeria could be a case of stroke in the young. The prevalence is as high as 25%" The post ‘One in 4 Nigerian stroke patients under 50’ appeared first on Vang
posts.content:
One in four stroke cases in Nigeria affects people below 50, raising concerns about the disease’s growing burden among young adults.

Prof. Kolawole Wahab, Head of the Stroke Unit at the University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital (UITH), disclosed this on Thursday in Ilorin.

He spoke on the sidelines of a medical rally commemorating the 2026 World Stroke Day, with the theme ‘Every Minute Counts’, which highlights the importance of prompt treatment.

Wahab said research published in 2017 had documented the prevalence of stroke among younger Nigerians.

“When we talk about stroke in the young, we are talking about those who are below the age of 50.

“One out of every four cases of stroke in Nigeria could be a case of stroke in the young. The prevalence is as high as 25 per cent.

“We see people who are in their 40s, some in their 30s, coming down with stroke,” he said.

The neurologist described the stroke burden in the region as epidemic, adding that UITH’s emergency department receives one or two stroke patients daily.

He identified hypertension as Nigeria’s leading stroke risk factor, warning that poor blood pressure control could increase the likelihood of the condition.

According to him, up to nine out of every 10 stroke cases have hypertension as an underlying factor.

Wahab expressed concern that some patients abandon prescribed medication in favour of unproven remedies, leaving their blood pressure uncontrolled.

He also identified diabetes as another major risk factor, noting that some people remain unaware they have the condition.

Others, he said, neglect proper diabetes management in spite of knowing their status.

“It is until they have suffered from stroke that they become aware they have diabetes,” he said.

Wahab listed imbalances in blood fats among other risk factors, explaining that abnormal levels of good and bad fats could contribute to stroke.

He warned against smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, hard drugs and sedentary lifestyles, urging Nigerians to adopt healthier habits.

The expert also advised people to moderate their salt intake, particularly those diagnosed with hypertension.

He cautioned against adding table salt to meals after preparation, stressing the importance of controlling blood pressure.

Also speaking, Dr Wemimo Olaofin, a consultant neurologist at UITH, urged Nigerians to check their blood pressure regularly.

Olaofin said stroke could occur suddenly at any time, but preventive measures and proper health management could reduce the risk.

He encouraged the public to monitor their blood pressure and embrace healthier lifestyles to prevent the condition.

Mrs Tejumola Olayinka, Deputy Director of Nursing in charge of UITH’s Stroke Care Unit, said the commemoration aimed to promote awareness and early hospital presentation.

“Stroke case is an emergency case that requires timely intervention. We can reduce the number of mortality and also reduce the number of people with stroke,” she said.

Olayinka described stroke as a sudden occurrence, “like a slap”, and highlighted facial drooping, arm weakness and slurred speech as warning signs.

She urged people displaying these symptoms to be rushed to hospital immediately for medical attention.

The nursing director also warned stroke patients against failing to take prescribed medication, noting that some patients did not adhere to treatment in spite of knowing their condition.

As part of the commemoration, UITH organised an awareness rally across the hospital and medical outreach programmes at the teaching hospital and Kwara Government House.

Two beneficiaries, Mr Jimoh Abdullateef and Mrs Fatima Abdulazeez, commended the medical team for providing free medical services and distributing drugs.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/one-in-4-nigerian-stroke-patients-under-50/

posts.title: Paris Gun Attack Leaves One Dead, Five Wounded As Suspect Faces Terrorism Probe
posts.excerpt: Of the four people seriously injured in the attack, "three of the victims remain hospitalised as I speak, and one of them is still in life-threatening condition," Christen said. The post Paris Gun Att
posts.content:
A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week that killed one person and wounded five including a child has admitted to “targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African,” prosecutors said on Thursday.

Earlier this week the 39-year-old man, identified as Kevin T., had said he did not “dispute the material facts”, but contested “the racist nature of his crimes”.

On Thursday, national terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen told a news conference that Kevin T. now claims he chose the location for his actions because it was “a hotbed for Islamists”.

The victims were shot from a vehicle driving through the towns of Trappes and La Verriere west of Paris. The suspect was detained later Friday with a machine gun and tear-gas grenades in his car.

He has since been held in police custody and was set to appear before a judge later on Thursday, Christen said, noting that he had requested that he be held in pretrial detention.

France’s counter-terrorism public prosecutor Olivier Christen speaks during a press conference at the Paris Judicial Court, in Paris on October 29, 2026, following the terrorist attack that took place on October 23 in Trappes and La Verriere.Photo by ANNE-CHRISTINE POUJOULAT / AFPOf the four people seriously injured in the attack, “three of the victims remain hospitalised as I speak, and one of them is still in life-threatening condition,” Christen said.

He noted the “very high level of preparation” behind the attack.

Kevin T. nevertheless denied any “terrorist intent,” viewing his actions as “legitimate,” the prosecutor said.

The opening of a judicial investigation by the office of the national anti-terrorism prosecutor (PNAT) allows a judge to take charge of the case, specifically regarding charges of “murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise”.

A search of the suspect’s home had uncovered “weapons or weapon components, specifically a magazine, two pairs of brass knuckles, a steel bayonet, and a silencer,” Christen said.

Also found were several “books, including a Quran, a Bible, and Adolf Hitler’s Mein Kampf”, as well as stickers celebrating the far-right National Rally (RN) party.

Christen said the stickers bore slogans such as “Long live France, RN, proud to be French”, but they were not produced by the party led by Marine Le Pen, who is leading opinion polls to succeed Emmanuel Macron as French president in elections next spring.

Kevin T. had told investigators that “he designed the stickers found in his home himself, and then ordered them to be manufactured via Amazon more than a year ago.”

The suspect had said that “he is neither a member of nor a sympathiser with any political party”, Christen said.

AFP

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/29/paris-gun-attack-leaves-one-dead-five-wounded-as-suspect-faces-terrorism-probe/

posts.title: Rampaging longhorn causes pileup on local road in Putnam County, leads police on wild chase
posts.excerpt: Video shows Maggie the pregnant cow darting between cars and evading police after escaping Little Cabin's Farm in Carmel, NY, causing a pileup.
posts.content:
I think I speak for everyone when I say that traffic jams are the absolute worst.

There is nothing more infuriating than coming home from work or driving to an event like a game or a concert and seeing nothing but brake lights ahead.

If you're anything like me, after the blinding rage wears off, you often wonder what caused the jam to begin with.

Usually, it's because some idiot missed his exit and decided to merge across six lanes of traffic or a college kid who's home on break was texting and driving before rear-endeding someone, but how about when a longhorn busts loose from the farm and leads the cops on a wild chase across a two-lane road?

What, you've never had that happen to you before?

MISSING 1200-POUND GIRAFFE GRACIE FOUND 2 WEEKS AFTER WANDERING AWAY FROM RANCH IN VIRAL SEARCH

It turns out several of the motorists in Putnam County, New York, were treated to a traffic jam of bovine origins when a four-year-old cow named Maggie caused a pileup when she escaped from the friendly confines of Little Cabin's Farm in nearby Carmel, NY.

The video is absolutely hysterical (mostly because I'm not the one behind the wheel) and features police cars and civilians alike trying (and failing) to wrangle the clearly agitated animal as she darts in between several stopped vehicles.

One of the civilians is even seen brandishing a tree branch to use as a whip to try and corral Maggie back onto the other side of the road.

While traffic is at a dead stop in the one lane, the oncoming lane has cars driving at full speed, and one of them even had to slam on their brakes as Maggie scampered back to the grassy shoulder.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

VIRAL VIDEO SHOWS MASSIVE BISON POPPING TOURIST VEHICLE'S TIRE IN YELLOWSTONE NATIONAL PARK

She's lucky some Kia didn't turn her into ground beef!

According to local news affiliate WABC, Maggie was on the loose for four days before finally being brought home, giving drivers all over Putnam County a reason to breathe easier.

What's even crazier is that Maggie is also pregnant, which might explain some of her erratic behavior.

All's well that ends well, though, and it's nice to know she's back on the farm where she belongs.

posts.title: GREGG JARRETT: Obama attacks Trump over Omar probe but there’s a big twist
posts.excerpt: Barack Obama's DHS and FBI investigated Ilhan Omar's alleged marriage fraud in 2016, finding evidence it was fraudulent, The New York Times reports.
posts.content:
We have come to expect sanctimony mixed with hypocrisy from Barack Obama. But his latest endeavor turns out to be a doozy.

Preaching his usual moral superiority, the former president recently took to social media to inveigh against the current president for targeting Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota with a criminal investigation. He called it "appalling."

Obama should have sat this one out at his luxurious spread on Martha’s Vineyard.

OBAMA BACKS ILHAN OMAR AMID PROBE, ACCUSES TRUMP ADMIN OF 'APPALLING' TARGETING IN LENGTHY STATEMENT

Lo and behold, he did the same thing when he was president. And Omar was the target. But, of course, the probe was kept under wraps. Until now.

Reporting by The New York Times reveals that Obama’s Department of Homeland Security and the FBI did a deep dive in the summer of 2016 into whether Omar entered into a sham marriage with her alleged brother, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, to enable him to secure a green card.

OBAMA'S LENGTHY REACTION TO OMAR INVESTIGATION TRIGGERS INSTANT BACKLASH: 'SPARE ME'

Brace yourself for the result. That investigation "found some evidence that it was fraudulent," according to the Times.

Accusations of marriage fraud have long dogged Omar, who has consistently dismissed them as politically driven and a right-wing conspiracy. So much for that argument.

GREGG JARRETT: IN A TORTURED DEFENSE OF ILHAN OMAR, THE NEW YORK TIMES REACHES FOR ITS DARKEST TRUMP ANALOGY

The latest investigation that culminated in a judicially ordered search of Omar’s home on October 12, 2026, reportedly encompasses not only the suspect marriage but troubling questions over whether she ran afoul of the law by using a fake name and false birth date to obtain citizenship. A separate investigation is examining her financial transactions.

The Obama-era inquiry did not end because of insufficient evidence. Instead, the Times divulges that it was shelved "because prosecutors concluded that the potential crime, a felony, fell outside a five-year statute of limitations." The newspaper’s story relied on statements by current and former officials with knowledge of the first case.

ILHAN OMAR ISSUES STUNNING ADMISSION WHEN CONFRONTED WITH BROTHER MARRIAGE RUMORS

That decision to mothball any legal action against Omar makes little sense, unless one factors in political favoritism by Obama and his prosecutorial cohorts.

It is true that marriage fraud is a federal felony governed by a five-year statute of limitations under 8 U.S.C. § 1325(c). However, the clock runs from the last overt act of fraud or submission of false documents, not the date of the wedding ceremony itself in 2009.

WHAT'S NEXT FOR ILHAN OMAR? FORMER IMMIGRATION JUDGE BREAKS DOWN LEGAL RISKS AMID FEDERAL PROBES

Taking steps to later obtain a green card would qualify as an overt act, as would document fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1546). So, too, would any act to cover up a sham marriage or efforts to conceal it. Indeed, it would constitute additional crimes such as conspiracy (18 U.S.C. § 371) and obstruction of justice or obstruction of proceedings (18 U.S.C. §§ 1505 and 1512).

Elmi abandoned his quest for a green card and left the U.S. for London sometime in 2011 when disturbing questions reportedly arose over his application. His actions and any misrepresentations associated with Omar might have brought the case within the permissible statute of limitations.

HOMAN SAYS ILHAN OMAR COULD BE STRIPPED OF NATURALIZATION, DEPORTED IF IMMIGRATION FRAUD IS PROVEN

But never mind all of that.

Obama’s DHS and DOJ could have pursued a simpler approach under civil (not criminal) immigration fraud. Orchestrating a scheme to illegally obtain U.S. immigration status or benefits carries severe legal consequences. There is no statute of limitations.

GREGG JARRETT: ILHAN OMAR COULD FACE INDICTMENT, DENATURALIZATION AND DEPORTATION

If the Obama administration had chosen this logical course, it could have led to Omar’s denaturalization and subsequent deportation. The standard of proof is "clear and convincing evidence," much lower than in criminal prosecutions.

It is unclear, but curious, why this legal road was never taken. We only know that authorities under Obama shuttered the case and buried the investigation. Preferential treatment? Political cronyism? It has the unmistakable stench.

REP ILHAN OMAR'S IMMIGRATION HISTORY FACES NEW SCRUTINY AS FEDERAL INVESTIGATORS SUBPOENA RELATIVES

This makes Obama’s social media screed against President Trump even more outlandish. Trump is doing what Obama did, except that Trump’s administration has expanded the Omar inquiry into areas where the former president’s prosecutors refused to go.

They should have gone there.

Obama’s harangue on X accused Trump of selectively targeting Omar without ever disclosing that his own administration investigated her first. That was dishonesty by omission. A mere oversight? Doubtful.

Obama also pronounced as true certain facts about Omar’s age that may not be true at all. He declared with absolute confidence that she was 17 years old when she applied as a minor for derivative citizenship based on her father’s citizenship.

But her age and birth date are still very much in dispute. Her autobiography and other documents undermine Obama’s claim, indicating that Omar may have been an adult of 18 years and legally ineligible for the type of citizenship that she procured. If she or her father made false statements or committed fraud, it would nullify her citizenship and could lead to removal from the U.S.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

This is not an "unsubstantiated theory," as Obama asserts in his social media post.

The former president accuses Trump of "intimidation" and laments that he is deploying "the full weight of the federal government" to bring down "a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president." Spare us the duplicitous pearl-clutching.

Obama expressed no moral outrage when his successor, Joe Biden, targeted his political opponent with criminal indictments. Going back further to his own presidency, Obama’s dirty fingerprints were all over the initial stages of the government’s damaging investigation of Trump in the phony collusion scandal.

Obama seems to think that Americans are simpletons with anterograde amnesia. It resembles contempt.

The New York Times report exposes Obama’s glaring double standard for what it is — a transparently insincere attack based on shallow evidence. This comes as no surprise.

Obama always seems confident in his righteousness in an irritatingly pious way. Ever the charlatan, he pretends to be holier-than-thou. Sometimes the truth catches up with him.

But don’t expect Obama to change now that his hypocrisy has been revealed. That would require earnest introspection.

Carlo Ancelotti has called three Serie A players for Brazil’s friendly matches against Japan and Singapore, Inter’s Carlos Augusto, Roma winger Wesley and Torino goalkeeper Lucas Perri.

The Italian coach is naturally keeping a close eye on Serie A football to identify form players for his Seleçao.

Brazil are set to play a couple of friendly matches during the November break for international duty.

They will be up against Japan on November 14, then Singapore in a lucrative opportunity on November 17.

(Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)Versatile Inter defender Carlos Augusto can play in a back three, on the right of a five-man midfield or the left, and is their top scorer in the Champions League this season.

Roma winger Wesley is also able to cover either flank, but in a more exclusively attacking role.

Torino goalkeeper Perri arrived over the summer from Leeds United, on loan with option to buy at the end of the season for €16m.

posts.excerpt: Como and Italy striker Moise Kean has been ruled out for another five weeks following...
posts.content:
Como and Italy striker Moise Kean has been ruled out for another five weeks following specialist treatment for a shin injury that has been dragging on for months.

The 26-year-old has struggled with the recurring problem ever since his time at Fiorentina, before making the transfer to Como in August.

He suffered another setback while on international duty for Italy, much to the anger of Como, and had not featured for the club since September 20.

Kean has specialist treatment

Official: Como announce their signing of Italy international Moise Kean on a permanent transfer from Fiorentina (via www.comofootball.com)With no recovery in sight using conservative treatment, Kean visited a specialist in Barcelona, undergoing an unspecified treatment at the world-renowned Cugat Institute.

A statement from the club confirms the treatment was carried out successfully, and the recovery time is estimated at around five weeks.

GENOA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 04: Assane Diao of Como celebrates scoring his team’s fourth goal with Moise Kean during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Como 1907 at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on September 04, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)It is therefore more than likely we won’t see the centre-forward back in action until December at the earliest, depending on how the recovery process develops.

posts.title: Report Gustavo Varela to get first senior Portugal call after 8 goals for Monza
posts.excerpt: Monza striker Gustavo Varela has been an unexpected sensation with eight goals in eight Serie...
posts.content:
Monza striker Gustavo Varela has been an unexpected sensation with eight goals in eight Serie A games, so it’s reported Portugal will call him up for Nations League matches against Denmark and Wales.

The centre-forward was a big investment for newly-promoted Monza in the summer, as he was snapped up from the Benfica B team for €2.5m plus up to €1m in add-ons.

He has more than paid for that fee, scoring eight goals in as many Serie A games, plus two in his only Coppa Italia appearance.

Gustavo Varela ready for Portugal

MONZA, ITALY – OCTOBER 19: Gustavo Varela of AC Monza celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s second goal during the Serie A match between AC Monza and Cagliari Calcio at U-Power Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)According to O Jogo, Varela has also now caught the eye of Portugal coach Jorge Jesus, who has been very impressed with his performances.

It is reported that the 21-year-old received notice he will be in the squad for the Nations League games against Denmark on November 14 and Wales on November 17.

MONZA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 18: Gustavo Varela of AC Monza scores his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between AC Monza and US Sassuolo at U-Power Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)He had spent last season on loan from Benfica at Gil Vicente, scoring just seven goals in 33 matches, so has already surpassed that tally in a more difficult league like Serie A.

The forward already represented Portugal at various youth levels, including four goals in seven caps for the Under-21 side.

posts.title: New San Siro to be called Generali Stadium, confirm Inter and Milan
posts.excerpt: The new Milan and Inter arena at San Siro will be called Generali Stadium, it...
posts.content:
The new Milan and Inter arena at San Siro will be called Generali Stadium, it was announced, be created with a basin shape and on top of a raised podium.

The images of the new design are under embargo until this evening, but some initial details are emerging from the joint press conference held by the two clubs at the Sforzesco Castle.

MILAN, ITALY – JANUARY 18: General view outside the stadium prior to the Serie A match between AC Milan and US Lecce at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on January 18, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)News agency ANSA confirms they announced the naming rights of the new structure have been sold to insurance giant Generali.

It will therefore be called the Generali Stadium, including a sign on the outside where the name is clearly visible.

New San Siro takes shape

MILAN, ITALY – MARCH 08: A general view of the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium San Siro ahead of the Serie A match between AC Milan and Inter at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on March 08, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)Although we do not yet have the images, the design for the project has been described as having a “basin shape” with steep stands to ensure a clear vision from all seats.

It is also going to be built over a podium that allows for elevation.

The first tier should be divided into two parts, with 11,500 seats in each ‘curva’ section.

Inter and Milan hope to begin construction in 2027 and have it fully completed by 2031, so that it can be one of the host stadiums when Italy share the EURO 2032 duties with Turkiye.

posts.title: Resurfaced Peltola 'criminal offense' quote comes back to haunt her after explosive report: 'Turn yourself in'
posts.excerpt: Mary Peltola faces social media criticism after a resurfaced quote clashes with a New York Times report on spoiler candidates in the Alaska Senate race.
posts.content:
Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola is facing an onslaught of social media criticism over a resurfaced quote that critics say reeks of hypocrisy, following an explosive New York Times report this week.

"It should be a criminal offense to lie or mislead the electorate," Peltola says in the clip from August posted by the National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) on Wednesday, shortly after the New York Times reported that her campaign was actively involved in a scheme to peel votes away from incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan by recruiting namesake and spoiler candidates.

Conservatives on social media quickly shared the post and suggested that Peltola should be investigated based on her own words.

"Your terms are acceptable," Townhall columnist Dustin Grage posted on X.

MARY PELTOLA'S CAMPAIGN, DEMS BACKED COVERT SCHEME TO FIELD SPOILER CANDIDATES IN ALASKA SENATE RACE: REPORT

"Turn yourself in, Mary Peltola," conservative radio host Jason Rantz posted on X.

"Amen, Mary! " former Trump campaign national press secretary Hogan Gidley posted on X.

"Well, that’s ironic… ," Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., posted on X.

"Agree!!! " Fox News contributor Marc Thiessen posted on X.

ALASKA'S GOVERNOR ORDERS INVESTIGATION AFTER NYT REPORT ON ALLEGED DEM-LINKED SENATE ELECTION SCHEME

The New York Times report rocked the Alaska Senate race, which could determine the balance of power in the Senate, as questions now swirl over the legality of the campaign's alleged actions. The Department of Justice and the state of Alaska are both investigating the genesis of the alleged scheme to recruit Dan J. Sullivan into the race against incumbent Dan S. Sullivan.

Fox News learned Wednesday that federal prosecutors are conducting an "aggressive criminal investigation" into how the second Sullivan secured a spot on Alaska's ballot, according to two sources familiar with the probe. Investigators are preparing grand jury subpoenas and examining potential violations of voters' rights, with the investigation expected to continue beyond Election Day. The DOJ declined to comment.

Alaska's Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy announced that he was ordering a probe into the matter.

"Today’s New York Times reporting reveals disturbing new evidence of an organized effort to manipulate Alaska’s elections by recruiting candidates — including one with the same name as an incumbent U.S. Senator — to deliberately confuse voters and misdirect their votes. The Alaska Division of Elections investigated these very concerns in June of this year. The new reporting substantially supports the Division’s findings," Dunleavy noted in a post on X.

"I am therefore directing the Department of Public Safety to investigate whether this scheme violated Alaska’s laws and whether criminal charges or civil action are warranted. The evidence will determine what happens next," the GOP governor continued.

The DOJ has issued dozens of subpoenas in the past 24 hours, reportedly looking into whether the campaign violated federal law by conspiring against the rights of voters. Others have argued the alleged actions are not illegal, and simply a "dirty trick" that is sometimes utilized in campaigns.

Fox News Digital reached out to Peltola's campaign for comment.

Peltola has dismissed reports of the alleged election scheme as "just another distraction," arguing that The New York Times’ report was solely purposed to "sell newspapers."

Her campaign also continues to assert innocence, previously telling Fox News in part that the Alaskans for Mary campaign "has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign."

posts.title: Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen
posts.excerpt: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that had resulted in the freezing of more than $2.5 billion in an effort to prevent them from being stolen. The compa
posts.content:
Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that had resulted in the freezing of more than $2.5 billion in an effort to prevent them from being stolen.

The company — the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said it had suspended trading on certain products.

It nevertheless insisted: “User funds are completely safe.”

Several experts said it looked like a massive amount of assets had been stolen.

“It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the group but remains a majority shareholder.

Paolo Ardoino, the CEO of Tether — a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT — said his firm froze about $1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.”

Circle boss Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC.

USDT and USDC are both “stablecoins,” or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar.

For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.

Some said it could be the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind, with a haul exceeding the $1.5 billion stolen in February 2025 from the Bybit platform — an incident attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea.

Bitcoin prices fell more than three percent on the news.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/crypto-platform-binance-confirms-major-hack-more-than-2-5bn-frozen/

posts.title: AFCON to hold every two years again as CAF reverses decision
posts.excerpt: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-yea
posts.content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle.

The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation’s Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026.

The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition.

CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable.

In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation’s 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent.

“The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa,” he said.

Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition.

He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future.

Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament.

The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year.

Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries’ ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027.

He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa’s cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together.

“The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa’s rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa’s 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world,” he said.

“The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa,” he added.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/afcon-to-hold-every-two-years-again-as-caf-reverses-decision/

posts.title: Gunmen kill four in Plateau community
posts.excerpt: Four persons were reportedly killed when gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night. The post Gunmen kill four in Pl
posts.content:
By Golok Nanmwa, Jos

Four persons were reportedly killed when gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night.

The attackers were said to have stormed the community at about 8pm and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to check attacks and restore security.

A resident of Barkin Ladi, Mr Bulus Jok, who confirmed the incident, said, “The gunmen struck the community around 8pm despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically.”

Jok said, “They were shooting at anything they saw. The attack created panic in the community, and four people were killed.”

He added, “The incident is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack.”

Also confirming the incident, Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, Mr Rwang Tengwong, said, “Terrorist gangs reportedly attacked Sabon Angwa, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area, and shot four people dead.”

Tengwong condemned the attack, describing the killing of innocent residents as unacceptable, adding, “We condemn this latest attack in strong terms and lament the loss of these lives.”

He said, “It is disturbing that communities are still being attacked despite the security measures and curfew put in place to protect residents.”

The BYM spokesman urged security operatives to intensify surveillance and take proactive measures to prevent further attacks on vulnerable communities, saying, “We call on security agencies to strengthen their presence and respond promptly to early warning alerts.”

Efforts to reach security operatives for more details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/gunmen-kill-four-in-plateau-community/
