posts.title: Why fans think Arsenal's Ethan Nwaneri will play for Nigeria
posts.excerpt: Here is why fans think Arsenal's Ethan Nwaneri might have reached an agreement with Eric Chelle and the NFF to play for Nigeria. The post Why fans think Arsenal's Ethan Nwaneri will play for Nigeria a
posts.content:
Here is why fans think Arsenal's Ethan Nwaneri might have reached an agreement with Eric Chelle and the NFF to play for Nigeria.

Arsenal youngster Ethan Nwaneri has sparked fresh speculation about his international future after reportedly following Nigeria's official Instagram account, prompting excitement among Super Eagles supporters who believe the highly rated midfielder could be preparing to represent the country.

The 19-year-old, who is currently on loan at German Bundesliga side Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal, has Nigerian heritage and remains eligible to represent the Super Eagles despite previously featuring for England at youth international level.

His latest social media activity has reignited conversations about a possible international switch, with Nigerian fans hoping to see him join the country's growing pool of talented young players.

However, there has been no official confirmation from Nwaneri, the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) or the player’s representatives that he has agreed to commit his international future to Nigeria.

Ethan Nwaneri

Which countries can Ethan Nwaneri represent?

Born on March 21, 2007, in London, England, Nwaneri is eligible to represent three countries:

Nigeria: Through his Nigerian father, who is of Igbo descent.

England: Through his English birthplace and heritage.

France: Through his mother's French heritage.

Nwaneri has represented England at various youth levels, including the U16, U17, U18, U19 and U21 teams. However, he has not made a competitive senior appearance for England, meaning a switch to Nigeria remains possible under FIFA's eligibility regulations, subject to the applicable requirements.

Which of his parents is Nigerian?

Nwaneri was born to a Nigerian father and an English-French mother.

His Nigerian roots have previously been a subject of discussion, particularly following comments he made during an interview while playing for Marseille in February 2026.

When asked about former Nigerian internationals Taye Taiwo and Wilson Oruma, who previously played for Marseille, Nwaneri proudly acknowledged his heritage, saying:

"Yes, I know. I'm Nigerian, and I am here to help the team as much as possible."

Although the comment demonstrated his connection to Nigeria, it was not an announcement that he had chosen to represent the Super Eagles.

Ethan Nwaneri

What position does Ethan Nwaneri play?

Nwaneri is an attacking midfielder who can also operate as a right winger and, when required, in more advanced attacking positions.

The left-footed youngster is particularly known for his close control, dribbling ability, creativity, vision and capacity to operate between the lines.

His versatility and attacking qualities make him an interesting prospect for Nigeria, especially as the Super Eagles continue to look towards building a competitive team for future international tournaments.

Has Nwaneri previously spoken about playing for Nigeria?

While Nwaneri has openly acknowledged his Nigerian heritage, there is no verified public statement from him confirming that he has decided to play for Nigeria.

In March 2025, reports emerged that he was open to representing whichever country approached him first, with Nigeria and England both reportedly interested in securing his services.

There were also reports in February 2026 that Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle had made contact with people close to the youngster to discuss the possibility of representing Nigeria.

His February 2026 comments about being Nigerian further strengthened hopes among supporters, but an official commitment has yet to be announced.

Would Ethan Nwaneri be a good addition to the Super Eagles?

There is little doubt that Nwaneri would be an exciting addition to the Nigerian national team.

At just 19, he has already gained valuable experience in some of Europe's biggest football environments, having developed at Arsenal, featured in the Premier League and UEFA Champions League, and gained experience on loan at Marseille before joining Borussia Dortmund.

His ability to play as a number 10 or on the right wing would give Nigeria additional options in attack.

More importantly, his creativity, technical ability and confidence in one-on-one situations could provide the Super Eagles with another dimension in the final third.

posts.title: Zambrotta unusual surgery for Italy’s 2006 World Cup winner
posts.excerpt: Italy’s World Cup winner Gianluca Zambrotta was well known for being bow-legged, but reveals they...
posts.content:
Italy’s World Cup winner Gianluca Zambrotta was well known for being bow-legged, but reveals they had become so painful that he had experimental surgery to correct them.

The 49-year-old was one of the key figures in Italy’s 2006 World Cup triumph, as well as amassing silverware playing for Juventus, Barcelona and Milan.

His unusual gait and running style were in part because he was bow-legged, but what had seemed to be an advantage in his playing career brought much bigger problems off the field.

Pain prompted Zambrotta operations

Fabio Grosso celebrates his goal with Italy teammate Gianluca Zambrotta in the 2006 World Cup semi-final against GermanyZambrotta revealed he had two operations to straighten out his legs, hoping this will reduce the pain that he said was becoming unsustainable, making even going up and down stairs extremely difficult.

“People used to recognise me first by looking at my legs, then my face,” joked Zambrotta in La Gazzetta dello Sport and Corriere della Sera.

“However, I have to think about my health. I probably should’ve had this operation 10 years ago, but I delayed it. The situation really started to deteriorate after I stopped my playing career.”

GENOA, ITALY – OCTOBER 12: Italy head coach Cesare Prandelli and the captain Gianluca Zambrotta look on as Serbia fans riot during the UEFA EURO 2012 Group C qualifying match between Italy and Serbia at Luigi Ferraris Stadium on October 12, 2010 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)He already had the operation on his left leg a year ago, and has now gone under the knife for the right leg too.

This is a genetic condition, and his medical approach inspired his father Alberto to follow suit with similar surgical intervention.

Curiously, father and son went in for the same operation on the same day in the same structure, the Istituto Ortopedico Rizzoli in Bologna.

posts.title: Ramon targeted by Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United, but Como and Real Madrid have control
posts.excerpt: Como defender Jacobo Ramon is attracting attention from numerous Premier League clubs including Arsenal, Chelsea...
posts.content:
Como defender Jacobo Ramon is attracting attention from numerous Premier League clubs including Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United, but Real Madrid have a very special deal in place.

The 21-year-old centre-back has been one of the most impressive players over the last year at the Stadio Sinigaglia, helping them secure Champions League qualification for the first time in their history.

This has brought him to the attention of several Premier League sides, above all Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United, especially after he scored against the Old Trafford team in a thumping 4-1 Como victory.

Ramon owned by Como and Real Madrid

TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: Jacobo Ramon of Como 1907 scores his team’s first goal past Lucas Perri of Torino FC during the Serie A match between Torino FC and Como 1907 at Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino on October 27, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)However, much like with Nico Paz, the likelihood of this player going to England is extremely slim.

Ramon is another product of the Real Madrid youth academy, who joined Como in the summer of 2025 for just €2.5m, leaving 50 per cent of the contract with the Spaniards.

Notably, this also includes a series of buy-back options, meaning Real Madrid could bring Ramon back to base for just €9m.

ITALY – SEPTEMBER 14: Jacobo Ramon of Como 1907 celebrates with teammate Nico Paz after scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and Parma Calcio at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)So if the Premier League giants do want to sign the Spanish defender, they’ll have to deal with Real Madrid first.

Como renegotiated their deal for Nico Paz to purchase more of his ownership, and could well do the same with Ramon to have greater power over his future.

posts.title: Gattuso: ‘Incidents went against Italy, but enthusiasm fuel for Lazio’
posts.excerpt: Gennaro Gattuso looks back over his ill-fated Italy experience where ‘incidents went against us,’ but...
posts.content:
Gennaro Gattuso looks back over his ill-fated Italy experience where ‘incidents went against us,’ but has taken that passion to Lazio as they host Cagliari. ‘When we play with enthusiasm, it’s better.’

It kicks off at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome on Sunday at 14.00 GMT (15.00 CET).

This is a big opportunity to go clear at the top of the table, as current joint leaders Inter face a difficult Derby della Madonnina this evening.

Meanwhile, Cagliari are coming off three consecutive defeats, including a 4-2 in this very stadium to Roma on Tuesday evening.

Gattuso keeps Lazio fire burning

REGGIO NELL’EMILIA, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: SS Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso during the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and SS Lazio at Mapei Stadium – Citta’ del Tricolore on October 27, 2026 in Reggio nell’Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)“We want to give a sense of consistency to what we are doing, and our fitness tests show the players recovered well from the midweek round,” explained Gattuso in his press conference.

Considering his remarkable start to the season with Lazio, is the coach revitalising his reputation after the ill-fated Italy experience and World Cup play-off defeat in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

“Football is made up of incidents, and they went against us that day, but the great thing about this sport is it gives you another opportunity. The important thing is to learn and improve, not get depressed. I am fortunate to have support from friends and family, including a wife of 30 years, she was always there during my toughest moments.”

Gennaro Gattuso’s during his first press conference at Coverciano on September 1, 2025.That passion Gattuso has for the sport can at times be counter-productive, but it fuels him.

“I get fired up when playing cards with my son, I always want to win. If I don’t feel that buzz, I may as well spend my time going for walks with my wife and dog.

“Whenever I got hammered by results, I still had that fire inside me. I feel alive with these things, and I thank the fans for the spectacle they put on, it felt almost like a Scudetto party on Tuesday. The lads deserve the credit for that, they created this enthusiasm, and we hope to continue it.”

Lazio too have been a revelation considering how badly they struggled in recent years, but Gattuso is not getting ahead of himself.

“Our target is 40 points. I am not used to seeing the table like this, but we have a road ahead of us and we need to be prepared. What I can say is that if we play with enthusiasm, it’s better. There are 29 games to go, a lot of points up for grabs, then we’ll see where we end up.”

TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Gennaro Gattuso, Manager of S.S. Lazio, celebrates after the Serie A match between Juventus and SS Lazio at Allianz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images)What he has brought is a different mindset, the kind that singled him out in his playing career.

“I see players who don’t hold back and think with one mind, those who come off the bench do so in top gear, so I am proud of how they are all training and working. Naturally, some are a little sadder, or even annoyed, but it’s part of the job.”

Cagliari have lost three on the bounce, but had a strong start to the season and upset some big teams.

ROME, ITALY – JULY 20: SS Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso reacts during the friendly match between SS Lazio and SS Lazio U20 at the Formello Sport Centre at Formello Training Center on July 20, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)“Cagliari know how to sit back and are then damaging on the counter-attack. The most important thing is that when we do lose, and we will eventually, it’s because our opponents did better and not that we underestimated them.

“We’ve got to keep our DNA and mentality going, then if we are beaten fair and square, we’ll take our hats off to them. If we fall asleep or don’t go at full speed, we concede, like we did against Sassuolo. That’s the secret.”

Has President Claudio Lotito spoken to Gattuso about the way this season is going?

“I speak to the President often, he will again eat with the squad tonight before the home game, speak to the players and show his presence.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/gattuso-incidents-italy-enthusiasm-fuel-lazio/

posts.excerpt: Christian Pulisic’s new Milan contract puts him level with the club’s top earners, and the...
posts.content:
Christian Pulisic’s new Milan contract puts him level with the club’s top earners, and the Rossoneri are now turning their attention to extensions for Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cissé.

According to Calciomercato.com, the bonuses in the American’s deal, which runs to 2031, are tied to both personal and team targets. Appearances, goals and assists all count, as do the side’s objectives, and they could take his base salary of €6.5m a year up to €10m. That puts Pulisic alongside Mike Maignan among Milan’s best-paid players, and Rabiot is expected to reach similar figures in his own new deal.

ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Alphadjo Cisse of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Bologna FC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)Milan target Rabiot and Cisse renewals after Pulisic deal

Niccolò Ceccarini, writing in his TMW editorial, via MilanNews, reports that Rabiot is next on the list after Pulisic. The France midfielder’s contract runs until June 2028, and Milan want to add two more years.

The club are also keen to tie down Cisse, who is expected to attract plenty of interest. He has seven goals this season, including a brace in Wednesday’s 4-2 defeat to Bologna.

Ceccarini adds that Milan are planning another major investment in attack next summer, and have been linked with Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi.

MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 13: Nicolo Tresoldi of Club Brugge KV celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between FC Internazionale Milano and Club Brugge KV at Stadio San Siro on October 13, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)The 22-year-old, a boyhood Milan fan, scored a hat-trick against Inter at San Siro in the Champions League this month. Chelsea, Manchester City, Tottenham, Manchester United, Atlético Madrid and Borussia Dortmund are all following him.

Marco Palestra has made his first Premier League start for Chelsea, lining up against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge.

The Italy full-back was in Xabi Alonso’s starting XI for the lunchtime kick-off, after an injury in pre-season disrupted his preparation for his first campaign in England.

(Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)Palestra joined Chelsea in record Atalanta deal

The 21-year-old came through the Atalanta academy and joined Chelsea in July for around €57m plus add-ons, signing a contract until 2033. It was the biggest sale in Atalanta’s history, beating the €53.2m they received from Manchester United for Rasmus Højlund. Inter had also tried to sign him, but Chelsea’s offer was higher.

Palestra made his name on loan at Cagliari last season, where his performances earned him recognition as one of Serie A’s best defenders.

He starts against a United side under pressure. Michael Carrick’s team are on an eight-game winless run and just one point above the relegation zone.

posts.title: Power sector fix ‘ongoing work’ — APC-PCC; bonds can’t light homes, says ADC-PCC
posts.excerpt: “Paying old debts is not the same as building new power infrastructure. Bonds cannot be presented as a substitute for power in people’s homes" The post Power sector fix ‘ongoing work’ — APC-PCC; bonds
posts.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi & Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA—The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, and African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, were yesterday locked in a verbal war over President Bola Tinubu’s declaration during his campaign in 2023 that if he failed to give Nigerians power, they should not re-elect him in 2027.

Read Also: Banks raise lending rates for top borrowers despite CBN cuts

While APC-PCC said the President’s fixing of the country’s electricity sector was ongoing and had signed the Electricity Act 2023 to enable states generate, distribute and transmit power, ADC-PCC insisted Nigerians could not power their homes and businesses with laws, bonds and project announcements.

In a statement yesterday, the spokesperson of APC-PCC, Dele Alake, said recent public commentary had reproduced the campaign promise without its closing qualification.

Speaking to members of the Organised Private Sector, OPS, in Lagos, ahead of the 2023 general elections, Tinubu, then the APC candidate, had reportedly said: “Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore.

‘’A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons I couldn’t deliver.”

Alake said the commentary left out the final part, that “should he fall short, he would owe Nigerians an adequate explanation before seeking their support for a second term.”

He argued that a fair assessment of the pledge should consider the full statement, alongside the administration’s record since 2023, measured against measurable improvements in electricity supply, metering, infrastructure and market stability.

“While fixing the power sector crisis remains unfinished, the President is working consistently to deliver on his promise to Nigerians, and his commitment to face the challenges head-on has never diminished,” the council said.

The APC-PCC said Tinubu signed the Electricity Act, 2023, on June 9, within two weeks of taking office.

According to the council, the law liberalised and deregulated the power sector and moved it away from the Exclusive List, so states can take part in power generation, distribution and transmission.

It said Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger states had started using the law to set up their own electricity regulatory agencies and attract private capital.

On debts, the campaign council said Tinubu “took on the over N6 trillion legacy debt that had accumulated from 2015 to 2025,” adding that the administration created a N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified legacy debts owed 21 power generation companies, Gencos, and gas companies, Gascos.

The council said the first and second tranches of the programme had raised over N1.2 trillion, and noted that the effect was becoming evident in the ability of Gencos to invest in upgrading their plants.

“Just a few days ago, Geregu Power Plc announced investments in new power transformers to enhance operations at the Geregu 1 Power Plant. Other firms are making similar investments,” it said.

On metering, the council said Tinubu started a Presidential Metering Initiative to close a gap of over seven million meters, noting that well over 1.5 million customers had been metered under the initiative in the last three years.

The APC-PCC added that the Rural Electrification Agency had connected universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power.

It said the government had also unveiled plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre, which it said was built over 60 years ago, with plans to build an East-West super grid.

On transmission, the council said Tinubu reviewed the Presidential Power Initiative, PPI, which was started by the late President Muhammadu Buhari, and signed an Acceleration Agreement in December 2023 with the German partners.

It said the Federal Executive Council, FEC, approved the contract for the first batch of five Transmission Company of Nigeria, TCN, substations in key load centres by December 2024.

These projects, it said, “are now being completed and will be commissioned before the end of the administration’s first term.”

In June 2026, the council added, FEC approved the contract for a second batch, covering eight new substations and the upgrade of four existing ones.

“Power project implementation requires equipment that is a long-lead item and thus cannot be achieved overnight,” the council said.

… on tariffs

On tariffs, APC-PCC said Tinubu “significantly aligned the tariffs to cost to restore liquidity to the electricity market” and put in place a system to protect low-income households.

‘’The creation of service bands with different tariffs was a first step to improve the financial viability of distribution companies and cash flow in the sector. It also reduced the government’s financial burden from tariff subsidies.’’

ADC-PCC says bonds can’t light homes, slams APC over Tinubu’s power pledge

Replying the APC, African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, in a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, accused the APC campaign council of celebrating policy documents and financial interventions instead of addressing the failure to translate them into reliable electricity.

“The APC should spare Nigerians the spectacle of celebrating paperwork while homes and businesses remain in darkness. After three and a half years, families still struggle to keep their homes lit. Traders and small business owners spend scarce resources on alternative power, yet struggle to keep their businesses alive.

‘’Nigerians are billed for electricity they cannot rely on. President Tinubu promised steady power and an end to estimated billing. That promise has not been kept,” he said.

It also faulted the electricity band system, arguing that consumers were paying different tariffs without corresponding improvements in supply.”

ADC campaign council cited Band A tariffs of about N209.50 per unit in many areas, before VAT, to illustrate the burden on consumers, insisting that Nigerians across all five bands continued to pay for electricity they could not reliably access.

“No family should have to weigh the cost of electricity against the cost of food. No business should be left to pay more while receiving less,” the council said.

Electricity subsidies

It also demanded clarity on the federal government’s plan to end electricity subsidies from 2027, questioning what the move would mean for household and business electricity bills.

The council proposed working with state governments and regulators to abolish the existing band system and introduce what he described as a fairer, more affordable framework that would hold power companies accountable for electricity delivered.

ADC-PCC lampooned the administration’s multitrillion-naira bond programme to settle legacy debts owed generation companies which, he said, could not be mistaken for investment in new electricity generation infrastructure.

It alleged that the Tinubu administration had not built any new generation infrastructure of its own to expand Nigeria’s power capacity.

“Paying old debts is not the same as building new power infrastructure. Bonds cannot be presented as a substitute for power in people’s homes,” he said.

He also raised concerns over VAT on electricity and the five per cent surcharge provided for certain fossil fuels, including petrol and diesel, under the Nigeria Tax Act.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/power-sector-fix-ongoing-work-apc-pcc-bonds-cant-light-homes-says-adc-pcc/

posts.title: N70,000 allowance showdown: Civil servants fire back at TUC
posts.excerpt: Civil servants, under JNPSNC, have defended the N70,000 transportation allowance agreement reached between the federal government and labour The post N70,000 allowance showdown: Civil servants fire ba
posts.content:
*Insist FG-Labour agreement stands *JNPSNC reveals details of agreement, including 6-month transport allowance, others

By Victor Ahiuma-Young

Civil servants, under the aegis of Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, have defended the N70,000 transportation allowance agreement reached between the federal government and organised labour, insisting that the rejection of the deal by the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, would not affect its implementation.

Read Also: TUC rejects FG’s proposed N70,000 monthly transport allowance for workers

The council said the agreement, signed on October 27, 2026, followed more than six hours of intensive negotiations and constructive engagements involving the federal government, the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, JNPSNC and the Joint Health Sector Unions JOHESU.

The position of the council was contained in a circular signed by the National Secretary, Mr Gbenga Olowoyo, and addressed to the national presidents and general secretaries of affiliated unions, as well as state chairmen and secretaries of the Joint Public Service Negotiating Councils across the federation.

The unions

JNPSNC is made up of the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria, ASCSN; Nigeria Civil Service Union, NCSU; Nigeria Union of Public Service, Reportorial, Secretarial, Data Processors and Allied Workers, NUPSTRAW; Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria, MHWUN; and National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives, NANNM.

Others are Nigeria Union of Agriculture and Allied Employees, NUAAE; Amalgamated Union of Public Corporations; Civil Service Technical and Recreational Services Employees, AUPCTRE; and National Union of Printing, Publishing and Paper Products Workers, NUPPPPROW.

On the government side are the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment; Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation; Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation; Federal Ministry of Justice; Federal Civil Service Commission; National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission; Federal Ministry of Finance; Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation; and Budget Office of the Federation.

In the circular, Olowoyo explained that the N70,000 transportation allowance would be paid monthly to public servants for six months, beginning from November 2026, to cushion the impact of rising transportation costs on workers and their dependents.

He also urged state and local governments to embrace the agreement and complement the federal government’s intervention, particularly in view of the substantial revenue accruing to the sub-national governments.

The circular read, among others: “The meeting was not only tough but also took more than six hours before both the Federal Government and labour sides could enter into terms.

“On the issue of payment of N70,000 transportation allowance, which will be paid for the next six months to public servants, starting from the month of November 2026, it was meant to subsidise the unbearable transportation cost being experienced by Nigerian workers.

“It is expected that state and local governments will be patriotic enough (and with humongous money accruable to both state and local governments) to concur with the agreement in order to complement the federal government’s effort to facilitate its implementation at both states and local government levels purposely to ameliorate the hardship of Nigerian workers and their dependents.

“Also, the agreement cemented the implementation of the long overdue 40% peculiar allowance that will reflect the N70,000 minimum wage. The implementation of the peculiar allowance ought to have started since July 2024 when the implementation of 2024 New National Minimum Wage commenced.

“This will equally be domesticated at the sub-national levels (i.e. state and local governments) with effect from November 2026, while the arrears from May 1, 2026, will be paid in three tranches to all public servants in Nigeria.

“It is very expedient to state loudly that federal government agreed to set up the Tripartite Negotiation Committee (which will comprise government, labour and NECA representatives) with immediate effect, which formed part of focal requests from the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, under the national leadership of Benjamin Anto Uyanto, that necessitated the three days warning strike called ab initio by the national leadership of JNPSNC on October 2, 2026.”

The council further disclosed that the negotiations addressed several longstanding demands in the health sector, including the adjustment of the Consolidated Health Salary Structure, CONHESS, which health workers have reportedly been demanding for the past 13 years.

13-week timeframe

According to the circular, the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, NSIWC, was given three weeks to complete its work and forward the outcome to the Presidential Committee on Salaries, headed by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, for final approval and implementation.

It also stated that the meeting approved the payment of 19 months’ arrears of health workers’ allowances in three installments, beginning from December 2026.

The circular read: “In the same vein, the meeting was able to resolve the issue affecting the issuance of circular that will facilitate the payment of hazard allowance to agricultural professionals officers in the public service in Nigeria.

“The National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission is to issue a circular on the template table that will culminate into its implementation within the next three weeks.

“On the tax relief to public servants and private sector operators, the landmark resolution on tax relief was that the matter will be presented to the National Economic Council, NEC, to deliberate on it because it will involve both federal and state governments as well as other critical stakeholders in the Nigeria economic management.

‘’Council also disclosed that the parties agreed to reconvene within one month to assess the level of implementation of the resolutions and ensure that no party reneged on its commitments.’’

It expressed concern over the persistent trust deficit surrounding labour agreements in the country, noting that several previous agreements with trade unions had suffered implementation challenges.

On the controversy surrounding TUC’s rejection of the N70,000 transportation allowance, JNPSNC maintained that the congress was not part of the negotiations that produced the agreement.

The council, however, acknowledged the TUC’s right to express its position, while challenging it to negotiate a higher amount if it believed workers deserved more than the N70,000 already agreed upon.

It further argued that the agreement was reached through consultations involving major labour stakeholders representing public servants, adding that opposition from another labour centre should not derail its implementation.

NLC membership

The council said: “It is equally expedient to disabuse the notion that the NLC, is a union of junior workers, whereas, all the unions affiliated to Nigeria Labour Congress have members across all the ministries, departments and agencies, MDAs, in the public service up to directorate level. “Even some top-notch public servants are due-paying members of trade unions of their respective choices.

“The above clarification became necessary because of the position taken on the matter by the TUC that it rejected the approved N70,000 transportation allowance, of which TUC was never part of the discussion (although has explicit right to express its opinion on any matter the TUC is directly involved in, but not on what it was not part of at any stage of the engagement or negotiation with the Federal Government).

“However, it will be highly commended that the Trade Union Congress can get a higher amount above N70,000 already agreed to by the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC; Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, and Joint Health Sector Unions, JOHESU, which will be an added benefit to Public Servants.”

The JNPSNC, established in 1948, serves as a negotiating platform between government and public service trade unions on issues relating to wages, minimum wage implementation, workers’ welfare and industrial disputes.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/n70000-allowance-showdown-civil-servants-fire-back-at-tuc/

posts.title: Highly capitalised stocks push gain to N2trn in October
posts.excerpt: The Nigerian stock market strengthened Month-on-Month (MoM), in October 2026, as renewed buying interest in heavyweight stocks lifted the benchmark The post Highly capitalised stocks push gain to N2tr
posts.content:
*…as investors reap N4.5trn WoW

By Peter Egwuatu

The Nigerian stock market strengthened Month-on-Month (MoM), in October 2026, as renewed buying interest in heavyweight stocks lifted the benchmark of the Nigerian Exchange, NGX Index above the 250,000-point psychological threshold.

Read Also: Banks raise lending rates for top borrowers despite CBN cuts

The rally added N2.01 trillion to market capitalisation, reflecting strong price appreciation in selected large-capitalised stocks across the Industrial Goods, Financial Services and Energy sectors.

According to analysts, although the market’s upward movement suggests renewed investor confidence, the uneven distribution of gains points to a selective investment strategy.

Investors appear to be concentrating on stocks with significant market influence while maintaining a cautious approach towards other equities. This divergence between index performance and market breadth remains an important consideration in assessing the sustainability of the current rally.

Specifically, breakdown of trading in October showed that the NGX market capitalisation closed at N165.114 trillion from 163.104 trillion in September.

Similarly, the NGX All Share Index, ASI surged by 1.2% to close at 254,299.49 points from 251,211.67 points in September.

Meanwhile on Week-on-Week, WoW the market gained N4.595 trillion as market capitalisation rose from N160.519 trillion the previous week in October to close at N165.114 trillion last week while the NGX ASI rose by 2.9% from 247,222.27 points previous week to close at 254,299.49 points last week.

On the global market, the oil prices continued to record performance as the retreat in prices last week reflected a reassessment of geopolitical risks as diplomatic efforts sought to revive peace negotiations.

However, analysts noted that the outlook for oil remains sensitive to developments in the region, and renewed escalation could quickly alter market expectations.

For Nigeria, movements in crude oil prices have implications for government revenue, foreign exchange supply and broader economic expectations.

Higher oil prices can support public revenue and external balances, although their overall effect depends on production levels, domestic fuel costs and other economic conditions. Lower oil prices may ease some cost pressures but could also weaken revenue expectations if the decline is sustained. The effect on listed companies will vary according to their exposure to energy prices, foreign exchange movements, production costs and domestic demand.

On market outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited stated: “Investors should therefore consider international oil movements alongside domestic economic indicators and company-specific developments rather than treating changes in crude prices as a uniform signal for the entire equities market.

‘‘More broadly, expectations regarding interest rates, inflation, corporate earnings and foreign exchange conditions may influence portfolio allocation decisions.

‘‘Where investors anticipate improved corporate profitability and more favourable financing conditions, equities may continue to attract demand. ‘‘Conversely, uncertainty over costs, earnings and valuations could encourage profit-taking in stocks that have recorded substantial price appreciation.”

Vanguard News

posts.title: Why food security remains intractable
posts.excerpt: He got the loan, after “settling” bank officials. Until I left Sokoto in 1990, no wheat was harvested from the farms. In fact, the farmer, after collecting the funds, relocated to Kaduna The post Why
posts.content:
By DELE SOBOWALE

Vanguard’s cartoonist, Oladejo Akande, on the Editorial page of the paper published a brilliant and comical piece about the high food import bill. A driver with a truck fully loaded with imported food chasing a Nigerian farmer out of the way, mockingly saying: “Stop wasting your time and energy!” It was comical and tragic at the same time. On October 3, 2026, another report appeared; titled “Import waivers, insecurity end two-year agric trade surplus.”

The two reports point to an existential Nigerian problem regarding sustainable food security. Nigeria is far from being food sufficient for various reasons to be addressed shortly. We face a serious national dilemma, import or not, on food production – which is not receiving the attention it deserves. The Ministers in charge of Agriculture are not performing their duties as they should. As a farmer President of America had said: “Farming would be mighty easy; if is carried out in cozy offices and with biros.” Nigeria’s Ministers of Agriculture are desk-bound operators. The fault is not entirely their own.

Insecurity takes its toll

Taraba’s bloody market day – Daily Trust, October 26, 2026

The report informed Nigeria and the world that another rural and farming community has been emptied of its people in the most tragic way possible. “An attack launched by gunmen suspected to be bandits on Binnari town in Karim-Lamdo Local Government Area of Taraba State has reportedly claimed the lives of over 50 persons, including women and children.” Possibly, another attack by bandits took place simultaneously elsewhere in Nigeria. Even if Binnari town alone was attacked by the hoodlums, certain repercussions, none good for food self-sufficiency, would inexorably follow.

First, the slain farmers have reduced the number of field hands. Most probably, harvesting, now underway, will grind to a halt on their farms. Food already produced will be left to rot away. Post-harvest food loss statistics would notch up on account of it. Multiply the Binnari loss by thousands of communities now deserted nationwide; then you might begin to have an idea of the implications of the Binnari attack.

Second, every successful attack on any community induces a domino effect. Refugees not only troop out of the affected settlements, but, from the surrounding communities as well. Massive exodus from several places exacerbates the impact of the original damage caused by spreading panic far beyond the place attacked.

Third, farmers-turned-refugee, like the rest of us, still have to eat. Hitherto, they fed themselves, and perhaps others. Henceforth, they have to be fed by a diminishing population of farmers. It is a double loss for the nation.

Fourth, even those still persevering, despite the attendant risks to lives, now work under conditions which no other farmer on Earth can imagine; and none should endure. Farming, at its best, and for optimum output, is a painstaking undertaking. The right things must be done at the right time; inputs must be provided at the right quantities and as specified. Any disruption invariably leads to sub-optimization of results. Compared to global standards, yield per hectare of Nigerian farms is generally low; and that places us at a competitive disadvantage, ab initio. The handicap is multiplied when the farmer is unable to attend to the farm as required by best practices on account of intrusions by herdsmen, kidnappers and other hoodlums.

Land for large scale farming exists in insecure places

“Land is the basis of farming.” That has been the axiom on which agriculture was based at the dawn of civilisation. But, today, other mediums of farming are producing food items. Israel’s Kibbutz system produces for domestic consumption and export more tomatoes than Nigeria. Landless farming is an idea we have not started to explore in this country. Yet, it might be one of the solutions to our food shortage problem.

Nigeria’s food production still relies largely on subsistence farmers. The large land mass required for large scale farming exists in very rural communities. They are also the most unsafe. Consequently, few investors are willing to venture inland.

Meanwhile, the tractors procured by the Federal and state governments are under-utilised. They are not meant for small farms; and few large scale farms exist anywhere.

Most of the 5,000 tractors acquired by the FG last year have not been put into operation; and the 10,000+ promised for over five years will suffer the same fate – tractors without drivers. Nobody wants to die driving a tractor in a rural area.

Briefcase farmers collect lion’s share of agric loans

“People who pretend to be legitimate farmers claim significant portions of these (agric) loans and obtain government subsidies, subsidized loans and input support without actually running a farm” – Weekend Trust, October 24, 2026.

One of the easiest ways to defraud governments and banks, especially the Central Bank and the Bank of Agriculture, is to establish a farm; promising to produce rice, wheat or cotton. Space in this article would not allow me to reveal the depth of corruption associated with agriculture. Every Nigerian government has been duped by phony large scale farmers – with strong political connections. Two examples will help to illustrate how the scam works.

In late 1988, when the Babangida administration embarked on the Wheat Project; designed to make Nigeria self-sufficient in wheat production; a well-connected fraudster leased several hectares of farmland at the Bakolori Dam area, near Talata Mafara, Zamfara State now, Sokoto State then. The farm was very close to our own rice farm. First, he presented a feasibility study for a farm 20 times his leased land area. Second, he projected harvests of wheat far in excess of what the most efficient farm in the world could achieve. He got the loan, after “settling” bank officials. Until I left Sokoto in 1990, no wheat was harvested from the farms. In fact, the farmer, after collecting the funds, relocated to Kaduna.

The second is more recent. Buhari’s Anchor Borrowers Programme aimed to revive the Textile Sector by vastly increasing the output of cotton. Over 60 per cent of the loans granted for that purpose went to one individual – Buhari’s in-law; now late. It was not the only example of briefcase farmers receiving huge loans for agriculture – which are subsequently diverted. Consequently, “approximately N4.7 trillion of this fund (ABP loans) remained unrecovered” (Week End Trust). The story does not end there; a substantial percentage of recovered loans were discovered to have been diverted to other sectors – mostly real estate.

When government fails, food supply suffers

“Nigeria misses 10-month revenue target by N20.7tn” – Report, October 27, 2026.

The FG, since 2015, has become the largest obstacle in the way of sustainable food security. In no single year, out of almost twelve, has the FG been able to fully collect the budgeted revenue. Promised allocations to the ministry were never delivered.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/why-food-security-remains-intractable/

posts.title: Banks raise lending rates for top borrowers despite CBN cuts
posts.excerpt: “The divergence reflects the uneven transmission of monetary policy into bank lending rates, alongside differences in how individual banks price credit" The post Banks raise lending rates for top borr
posts.content:
*Raise prime rates in 8 sectors, cut maximum rates *Agric, construction, manufacturing face higher rates *Analysts warn of delayed impact of CBN rate cuts

By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor

Despite interest rate reductions by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), banks have raised average prime lending rates in several key sectors of the economy, defying expectations of cheaper loans for businesses across the country.

Read Also: Why food security remains intractable

The CBN in September 2025 announced the first reduction in the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR), the financial market interest rate benchmark, to 27 per cent from 27.5 per cent, followed by another 50 basis points (bpts) reduction to 26.5 per cent in February 2026, and a massive 350 bpts cut to 23 per cent in September 2026. The latest reduction in the MPR followed a three consecutive month downward trend in the inflation rate to 15.39 per cent in August 2026 from 15.93 per cent in May 2026.

This moderation continued in September when the inflation rate dropped to 14.63 per cent.

The 450bpts reduction in the MPR in the 13 months to September 2026 had fuelled expectations that banks will reduce lending rates thus providing relief for businesses and households.

However, Financial Vanguard findings from the CBN’s published interest rate schedules for August 2025 and October 2026 show that average prime lending rates — the preferential rates extended to creditworthy corporate borrowers — increased in eight of 11 key economic sectors.

The eight sectors are agriculture, forestry and fishing; construction; government; human health and social work; real estate; manufacturing; education; and finance and insurance. The increases ranged from 0.33 percentage points in finance and insurance to 1.33 percentage points in agriculture, forestry and fishing.

Average prime lending rates in agriculture, forestry and fishing rose to 24.77 per cent from 23.44 per cent, while construction increased to 26.40 per cent from 25.25 per cent.

Government borrowing rates rose to 26.49 per cent from 25.52 per cent, while human health and social work advanced to 26.96 per cent from 26.11 per cent.

In real estate, the average prime rate increased to 26.57 per cent from 25.82 per cent, while manufacturing rose to 24.36 per cent from 23.79 per cent.

Education increased to 26.85 per cent from 26.33 per cent, and finance and insurance rose to 25.88 per cent from 25.55 per cent.

However, prime lending rates declined marginally in arts, entertainment and recreation, oil and gas, and information and communication, falling by 0.66, 0.24 and 0.08 percentage points, respectively.

The development contrasts with a decline in average maximum lending rates across 10 sectors — arts and entertainment, government, education, human health, finance and insurance, manufacturing, oil and gas, agriculture, information and communication, and construction — from 33.78 per cent to 32.58 per cent, representing a reduction of 1.20 percentage points.

The Financial Vanguard analysis indicated that while some borrowers may be benefiting from lower quoted lending rates, preferred customers in important segments of the productive economy have yet to experience a uniform reduction in borrowing costs.

Uneven transmission of rate cuts

Commenting on the development, Tunde Abioye, Head, Equity Research, Quest Merchant Bank, said the divergence between the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) and sectoral prime lending rates did not necessarily indicate a breakdown in monetary policy transmission.

He explained, “Lending rates reflect not only the policy rate but also banks’ funding costs, liquidity conditions, borrower mix and risk-adjusted pricing considerations.

‘‘What the data may be showing is a lagged and uneven transmission of monetary easing across sectors rather than an outright failure of the easing cycle to lower borrowing costs.”

Citing an independent analysis of the CBN’s rate publications conducted by his bank, Nnamdi Nwizu, Co-Founder, Comercio Partners, a Lagos based investment bank, also attributed the divergence to uneven transmission and differences in how banks price credit.

He said: “The divergence reflects the uneven transmission of monetary policy into bank lending rates, alongside differences in how individual banks price credit.

“Although CBN has reduced its benchmark policy rate, commercial banks determine lending rates based on several considerations, including funding costs, liquidity requirements, operating expenses, credit risks and competitive conditions.

“Our analysis suggests that the increase in average prime lending rates was not widespread across banks. Of the 174 comparable bank-sector prime lending rate observations across the seven identified sectors, 65 recorded reductions, 79 remained unchanged and only 30 recorded increases.

“This suggests that the increase in average prime lending rates was influenced by relatively large upward adjustments at a smaller number of banks, rather than a general increase across the banking system.”

Savings and deposit rates also decline

The movement in lending rates has occurred alongside reductions in the rates banks offer depositors.

Financial Vanguard findings show that the average savings deposit rate declined to 6.61 per cent in October 2026, from 7.81 per cent in August 2025, a reduction of 1.20 percentage points.

Average time-deposit rates recorded a sharper decline, falling by 2.24 percentage points to 12.28 per cent from 14.52 per cent, over the period. Average demand deposit rates also declined, although marginally, to 1.48 per cent from 1.59 per cent.

For savings deposits, the prevailing benchmark rate offered across major commercial lenders dropped to 6.90 per cent from 8.25 per cent. The average rate on time deposits fell from 14.52 per cent, within a reported range of 6.91 to 21.51 per cent, to 12.28 per cent, with the range narrowing to 0.10 to 17.04 per cent.

Nnamdi asserted that the findings suggest that monetary policy transmission remains uneven, although it would be premature to conclude that monetary easing has failed to translate into cheaper credit.

The decline in average maximum lending rates across the sectors examined, alongside reductions in deposit quotations and several bank-level prime lending rates, indicates that some re-pricing has already occurred. “Nevertheless, the increase in the average quoted prime lending rate across six of the seven highlighted sectors suggests that these benefits have not been uniformly reflected in the lending terms available to preferred borrowers.

“Importantly, the CBN’s 350-basis-point MPR adjustment occurred on 22 September 2026, just 17 days before our October lending-rate observation.

“It may therefore be premature to assess its full impact on borrowing costs, particularly as the CBN characterised the adjustment as an operational recalibration. This is consistent with a June 2026 IMF study highlighting asymmetric interest-rate transmission in Nigeria, where lending rates respond faster to monetary tightening than to easing.

“Consequently, the benefits of lower policy rates may take longer to materialise.

‘‘The decline in maximum lending rates and deposit quotations already suggests some repricing, although the transmission to prime borrowers remains incomplete.”

Implications for businesses

According to Abioye and Nnamdi, the divergence between prime and maximum lending rates has implications for companies planning to expand production, acquire equipment or finance working capital.

Abioye warned that persistently elevated lending rates for prime borrowers could increase financing costs beyond what businesses would normally expect during an easing cycle.

He said, “If lending rates for prime borrowers remain elevated or continue to rise, affected firms could face higher financing costs than would otherwise be expected during an easing cycle.

‘‘This may moderate the appetite for new borrowing, particularly for discretionary expansion projects, capital expenditure, and long-term investments.

‘‘However, the impact is likely to vary across sectors and borrowers.”

Nwizu warned that sustained high borrowing costs could weaken private investment, corporate profitability and employment creation, while constraining improvements in productive capacity.

He explained, “Persistently elevated lending rates could continue to constrain investment, corporate profitability and business expansion, particularly in sectors where access to affordable bank financing is critical.

“For manufacturing and agriculture, expensive credit raises the cost of financing raw materials, inventories and working capital.

“In real estate, higher financing costs could affect project viability and delay new developments, while businesses in education, information technology and financial services may reconsider expansion or capital expenditure plans.

“At the macroeconomic level, sustained high borrowing costs could weaken private investment, slow employment creation and constrain improvements in productive capacity.

“These supply-side pressures could also complicate efforts to achieve sustainable disinflation. Nevertheless, our findings suggest that these pressures are not uniform across the banking system.”

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/banks-raise-lending-rates-for-top-borrowers-despite-cbn-cuts/

posts.title: Collins accuses Schumer of pushing attack ads filled with 'outright lies' in tight Maine race
posts.excerpt: Collins said Democrats are using a national political strategy to distract voters from local issues, while the latest Fox News poll shows her Maine Senate race tied at 49%.
posts.content:
Sen. Susan Collins on Sunday blasted Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and the Democratic Party over what she described as a wave of false attack ads targeting her and other Republican candidates, saying she has never seen a campaign with "so many outright lies."

She made the remarks during an interview with Fox News on Sunday, just two days before Election Day in Maine, where she is seeking reelection in a closely watched race against Democratic rival Troy Jackson. According to the latest Fox News poll, the two candidates are tied at 49%.

Collins accused Democrats of following "Chuck Schumer's playbook," pointing to attack ads she said were nearly identical to those targeting other Republican lawmakers.

MANCHIN CALLS SCHUMER 'CRAZY' FOR TRYING TO OUST GOP SENATOR IN CRUCIAL SENATE SHOWDOWN

"One of the outrageous, completely false ads against me had to do with Jeffrey Epstein. And it turns out, in talking to two of my colleagues who are in tough races, that they had virtually identical ads run against them. So this is part of Chuck Schumer's playbook," she said.

"There are a lot of differences between my opponent and me, but I've never seen a campaign with so many outright lies. It's very frustrating," she added.

Collins further accused Democrats of trying to shift the focus away from local issues and toward divisive national political battles.

"It's certainly an attempt by my opponent and Chuck Schumer and their allies to nationalize this race," she said.

SENATE CONTROL IS A COIN FLIP — AND DEMOCRATS’ PATH RUNS THROUGH TRUMP COUNTRY

Turning to her own campaign, Collins portrayed herself as a bipartisan lawmaker willing to work across party lines, arguing that the Senate needs more centrists as moderates increasingly leave Washington.

"Unfortunately, a lot of them have given up and retired or decided they just didn't want to run again. And that's one reason I am running again," she said.

"We need more people who are willing to work across party lines. That is really important," she said.

FOX NEWS POLL: NAIL-BITER IN MAINE SENATE RACE

She also described herself as the "most independent senator on either side of the aisle," pointing to her voting record and saying her decisions are based on what she believes is right, rather than who occupies the White House or what President Donald Trump supports.

"There's this phony figure out there that I voted with President Trump 95% of the time. That's based on a sample of only 30% of the votes. If you look at a broader sample of 90% of the vote, that drops significantly to like 72%. And I voted against the president's policies 138 times," she said.

While Jackson previously told Fox News that he believes he has a "good shot" at defeating Collins, the longtime Republican senator touted strong voter support and said she is more optimistic than ever about her reelection chances.

"I'm feeling very optimistic based on the great response I get in visiting communities all over the state," she said.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/collins-accuses-schumer-pushing-attack-ads-filled-outright-lies-tight-maine-race

posts.title: Missing Utah teen Kylie Arellano found safe in Oregon after 500-day search
posts.excerpt: Kylie Arellano was found safe in Oregon with a 39-year-old man after vanishing from Utah more than 500 days ago, ending a massive FBI search.
posts.content:
A Utah teenager who vanished nearly a year and a half ago has been found safe in Oregon, ending a lengthy nationwide search that spanned more than 500 days.

Kylie Arellano, now 17, was last seen by her family on May 29, 2025, at their home in Garden City, Utah, when she was 15 years old.

Kylie's disappearance had triggered a wide federal and state investigation that led officials through dozens of unconfirmed sightings before culminating in her recovery on Sunday.

MISSING TEEN FOUND HIDING IN CONVICTED SEX OFFENDER'S CLOSET IN FLORIDA, SHERIFF SAYS

Law enforcement officers in Oregon, working directly with the FBI's Salt Lake City field office and the Rich County Sheriff's Office, safely recovered the teen, according to a law enforcement news release.

Kylie, they said, was found with a 39-year-old man in Oregon. The man was taken into custody without incident.

"The FBI and the Rich County Sheriff’s Office have been actively investigating this case for more than a year and pursuing every lead received from across the U.S. and in other countries.

FBI NABS MORE THAN 350 ALLEGED CHILD SEX ABUSE OFFENDERS

"As this case is ongoing, no further information will be released at this time," the FBI's Salt Lake City field office said in a statement on Sunday.

Federal authorities also credited the Oregon State Police, the FBI's Portland field office and the Utah Department of Public Safety for their assistance in the operation.

"Tonight, local police in Oregon brought a minor who had been missing for a year and a half to safety, acting on information provided by our FBI Salt Lake City Field Office," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital.

"We are grateful she can return home, and we will continue working with our partners to hold those responsible accountable," Patel added.

MIKE WALTZ, TIM TEBOW LAUNCH EFFORT TO COMBAT ONLINE CHILD EXPLOITATION: 'IT'S HAPPENING IN THEIR BACKYARD'

"To anyone using gore groups to target and exploit children: the FBI and our partners are coming for you.

"We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice and protect America’s children."

Kylie Arellano’s grandmother also thanked the authorities for finding her. "THANK YOU for all you and your agents and teams are doing to find our baby girl, Kylie Arellano and bring her home!!!" she wrote on X.

According to a law enforcement source, the suspect allegedly met the teenager on Snapchat before her disappearance.

Last year, Rich County Sheriff Dale Stacey said detectives had chased reports of sightings across multiple states and urged the public to preserve any photographic or timestamped evidence.

TWO MISSING CHILDREN RESCUED FROM TRAILER AS POLICE ARREST BABYSITTER ON KIDNAPPING CHARGES

New details about the investigation had also emerged days before Kylie was found.

Unsealed search warrants reviewed by KUTV on Oct. 29 showed that investigators had previously scrutinized Kylie's mother, Stephanie Coleman, and questioned her about a 2024 allegation of physical abuse.

There were also questions about discrepancies involving missing text messages from the night Kylie vanished and suspicious marks in the home.

Coleman had denied having any role in her daughter's disappearance or abusing her, providing timestamped "good night" text messages from May 29, 2025.

She said the marks were caused by an injured cat and maintained that Kylie had likely been groomed and lured away by someone she encountered online, the outlet reported.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/us/missing-utah-teen-kylie-arellano-found-safe-oregon-after-500-day-search

posts.title: Chris Pratt went from living in a van to Hollywood stardom after chance encounter changed everything
posts.excerpt: Chris Pratt recalls the moment Rae Dawn Chong walked into Bubba Gump Shrimp Company and offered him a role that launched his Hollywood career.
posts.content:
Chris Pratt's journey to becoming one of Hollywood's go-to action stars started with him living in a van in Hawaii.

In a recent post on X, the 47-year-old actor reflected on his beginnings: "Before Hollywood, I was living in a van in Hawaii and waiting tables at Bubba Gump Shrimp Company," revealing that a chance encounter working one night changed his life.

"One day, the incredible Rae Dawn Chong walked into the restaurant, and naturally, I went up to her table and said, 'Hey, you’re a movie star! What are you doing here?'" he recalled. "She asked if I could act, and I said, 'F- - - yeah, put me in your movie!'"

Since he didn't have a phone, he gave Chong his friend Mike's number, who told him a few days later that someone had called for him.

NICKI MINAJ, ANNA NICOLE SMITH AND MORE STARS WHO GOT THEIR START WAITING TABLES AT RED LOBSTER

"I called her back, and sure enough, she was serious," he wrote. "I drove over to pick up the script, went back to Mike’s house, and read all 120 pages three times in a row. First script I’d ever read. My character's name was Devon, and I remember thinking, 'Sweet! I could totally play a Devon!'

After the audition, he recalled Chung telling him he "could act and offered me the part."

While he lived in Hawaii, the movie was filming in Los Angeles, which made Pratt a little nervous, as he had "about $60 to my name, a bag of clothes, and some rollerblades." He then found out that Chung would fly him out to Los Angeles for production.

"I remember thinking right then and there, my life just changed forever. I'm going to be an actor," he wrote. "That little movie was 'Cursed Part 3,' a low-budget horror comedy that opened the door to Hollywood for me. I'll forever be grateful to Rae for taking a chance on a kid working at a shrimp restaurant. Everybody starts somewhere, and this is where it all began for me."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Pratt's role in "Cursed Part 3" led to bigger projects, including his breakout role playing Andy Dwyer in the hit NBC show, "Parks and Recreation."

He then landed the role of Peter Quill, or Star-Lord, in the Marvel movie, "Guardians of the Galaxy," playing the character in the film's two sequels, as well as in "Avengers: Infinity War" and "Avengers: Endgame."

When speaking to Moviefone in May 2023, Pratt shared he is "grateful" for "Guardians of the Galaxy" director James Gunn for casting him as the lead in the movie, saying, "He's changed my life" and the life of his children.

"He found a working actor who had already at that point done way better than most people who come out to town. I wasn't a waiter any longer, I was a series regular on a show. I was getting recognition," he said. "He brought me to a whole new level that ultimately changed the entire way the industry saw me. I no longer was auditioning. That was the last audition I ever had. So he changed my life."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Since becoming a Marvel superhero, Pratt has starred in the "Jurassic World" franchise, voiced characters in "The Lego Movie" and its sequel, "The Super Mario Bros. Movie" and its sequel and "Onward," and has starred in the TV series "The Terminal List" since 2022.

He has also starred in a number of standalone blockbusters, including "Passengers," "The Magnificent Seven," "The Tomorrow War" and many others.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Pratt was married to actress Anna Faris from July 2009 to August 2017, when they announced their separation. They share one child together, a son named Jack, 14.

He then married Katherine Schwarzenegger in June 2019, and they share three children together; Lyla, 6, Eloise, 4, and Ford, 1.

"It's an incredible blessing to be a father. It's also a lot of hard work. And so I think I just want to teach them that ... I don't know, I want to do my best," he told Fox News Digital in October. "I basically want to get right everything my dad got right and get right everything my dad got wrong. And I'm sure I'll screw up both, you know?"

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/entertainment/chris-pratt-went-from-living-van-hollywood-stardom-after-chance-encounter-changed-everything

posts.title: Ukraine says air alert system hacked after false radiation warning in Kyiv
posts.excerpt: Ukraine's Air Force said its air alert system was hacked after false radiation hazard and chemical attack warnings spread panic across Kyiv on Sunday.
posts.content:
Ukraine officials said the country’s official air-raid alert app was likely hacked after emergency alerts warned on Sunday that there was a "radiation hazard" and a "chemical attack alert" in Kyiv.

The false warnings urged residents not to go outside.

"There is a radiation hazard alert in Kyiv. Do not go outside!" read one alert.

RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE

"There is a chemical attack alert in Kyiv. Do not go outside!" another one read.

The public air alert online map also displayed Kyiv and other areas as under a nuclear alert. The app also issued false warnings about Russia’s hypersonic Oreshnik missile and alleged street fighting in Kyiv.

Additionally, loudspeakers in the streets blasted a recorded message instructing people to take precautions.

But Ukraine’s Air Force said its air alert app was hacked and that there was no radiation hazard to be concerned about.

"The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!" the Ukrainian Air Force said in a statement posted to Telegram.

Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications blamed Russia for the incident, although no group had publicly claimed responsibility.

CHINA-LINKED HACKERS INFILTRATED US GOVERNMENT NETWORKS BEFORE FBI TAKEDOWN

Separately, Russia’s Emergencies Ministry said early Monday that its mobile application had been hit by a "massive cyberattack" that allowed attackers to send false information to the public.

"Attention! The mobile application of the Ministry of Emergencies of Russia has been subjected to a massive cyberattack, enabling attackers to send false information to the public," the ministry said on Telegram.

Fox News' Simon Owen contributed to this report.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/world/ukraine-air-alert-system-hacked-false-radiation-warning-kyiv

posts.title: Big 12 Conference admits officials got call wrong that benefited BYU Cougars in win over Arizona State
posts.excerpt: The Big 12 admitted replay errors in BYU's games against Notre Dame and Arizona State, raising questions about the conference's officiating process.
posts.content:
Maybe the BYU Cougars being a religious school can pay some dividends.

The Cougars have benefited from a very fortunate run of officiating in recent weeks. At home against the then-No. 2 ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish, BYU pulled off a stunning upset. Thanks in small part to yet another controversial literal last second clock call this college football season.

Quarterback Bear Bachmeier found tight end Walker Lyons with 1:47 remaining in the fourth quarter to give the Cougars a 28-24 lead, putting Notre Dame's winning streak in jeopardy. The Irish drove down the field, converting a six-yard pass on fourth-and-5 to give themselves one last shot at the end zone from the 8-yard line with four seconds left. C.J. Carr's pass fell incomplete, and fans stormed the field.

BIG 12 CONFERENCE ADDRESSES OFFENSIVE CHANTS FROM UCF FANS DIRECTED AT BYU DURING UPSET WIN

Except, eagle-eyed viewers noticed that the stadium game clock clearly read 0:01 as the ball hit the turf. And the Big 12 Conference acknowledged they were right, and that Notre Dame should have had time for one last play.

"Following the Big 12's review of the final play of Saturday's Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew," they explained in a statement. "The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games."

Yes, BYU may still have stopped the Irish and won the game anyway, but it was a clear officiating mistake that benefited the Cougars. It happened again the next week.

On the road at UCF, BYU found themselves locked in a tight game late in the fourth quarter against what should have been an overmatched opponent. With the game tied 24-24 and 11 seconds left, the Knights set up for a field goal attempt on third down. Kicker Will Stone's attempted was blocked without crossing the line of scrimmage, and Stone recovered it himself.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

As he was tackled, his helmet came off, with the officials throwing a flag for a BYU facemask. Which they promptly picked up. Not only that, they then incorrectly applied a 10-second runoff for the helmet coming off. As rules analysts explained, that runoff is only required when the helmet coming off is the reason for the clock stoppage. But the clock also stopped because of a "legal kick down," per Terry McAulay, meaning that the runoff should not have been applied.

Instead of UCF having another opportunity at a game-winning field goal, the game went to overtime. That said, the Cougars did wind up losing in double overtime anyway, thanks in part to some less-than-beneficial officiating. As Stone made a field goal to go up 34-31, BYU's Kendall Wall was flagged for roughing the kicker. Instead of the Cougars needing just a field goal to tie the score, UCF converted the ensuing first-and-goal for a touchdown, making the two-point conversion as well.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

BYU had four tries from the four-yard-line, but came up empty, and the Knights pulled off the upset. Still, there's a case to be made that the game may never have reached overtime in the first place, had the rules been correctly applied.

Well, fast-forward to BYU-Arizona State on Halloween, and it happened again. Though at least this mistake wasn't in the closing seconds of the game.

In the first quarter in Provo, Bachmeier tried to run the ball in for a touchdown from the one-yard line, but fumbled immediately after the snap. Sione Moa jumped on it, advancing it into the end zone for a touchdown. Replay review confirmed that Bachmeier had indeed fumbled, and separately confirmed that Moa had scored.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

But the review team should never have allowed the touchdown to stand, because the whistle blew on the play to signal that Bachmeier had been ruled down. Once that happened, the ball could not be advanced after a fumble. Inexplicably though, they awarded the Cougars a TD anyway.

And now the Big 12 Conference has been forced to issue yet another statement that the officiating crew had made a mistake.

"Replay was incorrect in awarding a score," the statement read. "The correct ruling should have been BYU ball for a third-and-goal from the 2-yard line."

Sure, the Cougars may have punched it in from the two, but you never know in college football, and the call handed them a touchdown that should not have happened. Understandably, ASU head coach Kenny Dillingham was furious with the officiating crew at the time, and after the game.

"I was trying to argue that he does have the right to recover it post-whistle, but that's not a clear advancement, which means the ball should be at the three," he said. "Obviously, that wasn't what happened. It's not the officials' fault. Those officials don't have say in that. That's all back home."

There's little doubt that these mistakes are simply that, mistakes, and not some grand conspiracy by the Big 12 Conference to help get BYU to the College Football Playoff. But it's a sign of the seemingly growing officiating problem in college football, and yet another example of the fact that referees can, and often do, impact a game negatively. Some Cougars fans will also be quick to point out any number of calls they believe went against their team.

Normally, over the course of a season, these things even out. It's just unfortunate when there are several high-profile mistakes all happening around the same program.

BYU has yet another massive game this Saturday, as they travel up the road to play their heated rivals, the Utah Utes, in Salt Lake City. The No. 3 Utah Utes and No. 7 BYU Cougars. Just as everyone expected. And given the tight Big 12 race, with Utah 5-0, BYU 4-1 and Texas Tech 4-1, it could have tremendous implications in determining which teams will play in the conference championship game, as well as a spot in the playoff.

Hopefully we're not talking about the refs after this one.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/outkick-sports/big-12-conference-admits-officials-got-call-wrong-benefited-byu-cougars-win-arizona-state

posts.title: Michael Douglas says Jack Nicholson 'has disappeared' from the Hollywood spotlight
posts.excerpt: Michael Douglas claims Jack Nicholson is enjoying "walking around in his slippers" after essentially disappearing from Hollywood following 2010 film.
posts.content:
Michael Douglas admitted his longtime friend, Jack Nicholson, has essentially "disappeared" from the spotlight.

Douglas, 82, reflected on his storied career and missed opportunities while discussing his new memoir, "One Helluva Ride."

When asked who he never had a chance to work with, Douglas noted that he "would have liked to have acted with Jack," according to The Independent.

"He's not working any more. He's well," Douglas said. "He has disappeared. I know that."

JACK NICHOLSON'S DAUGHTER CALLS OUT HOLLYWOOD'S STATUS-CHASING ELITE IN SCATHING NEW ESSAY ABOUT MODERN LA

The "Wall Street" actor added, "I still see him, but he is fine. He is up there by his house and walking around in his slippers. It happens. He deserves it. I understand. He is a few years older than me, but I understand."

Nicholson, 89, is rarely seen in public and was last credited on the 2010 film "How Do You Know."

PARIS JACKSON SAYS DAD MICHAEL’S UNUSUAL RULE HELPED PROTECT HER CHILDHOOD

Last week, Crystal Hefner exposed secrets about the Playboy Mansion and its star-studded roster of attendees.

Hefner, 40, name-dropped one Hollywood heavy-hitter who was known for his frequent trips to the Holmby Hills home during an episode of her "After the Mansion" podcast.

"I think a lot of celebrities came because they were just curious, and others used it as their personal country club," she said.

"They used to call it Jack Nicholson’s drive-thru at one point because he would drive up, grab some food or whatever else he could get there and leave."

Nicholson's daughter, Lorraine, once shared her own experiences at the famous mansion where she spent her childhood playing with Hef's sons, Marston and Cooper.

"People assume that my father took me to the Mansion, but they assume wrong," she wrote in a 2024 essay for Vanity Fair. "In fact, I can venture with confidence that I spent more time there than my father ever did."

Lorraine wrote about growing up as the daughter of somewhat controversial parents, and noted that her friend's parents were "not so keen on letting their children come over to Jack Nicholson's house."
