posts.title: AI-Generated Photos: We Are Already Cleaning Up Our Register – INEC
posts.excerpt: INEC, however, clarified that not every photograph enhanced with artificial intelligence would be removed, distinguishing between images generated entirely by AI and genuine photographs improved with
posts.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has commenced the process of cleaning up its preliminary Register of Voters following the identification of records with suspected AI-generated photographs and other irregularities.

The commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, said on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics that its Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) had flagged 268 records for review.

“What we are currently doing now is looking at all these 268 records that ABIS already flagged as AI-generated or even something of irregularities,” he said.

Bayode explained that some people allegedly used their official credentials to create questionable profiles, exploiting a registration option designed for persons with disabilities who do not have complete fingers or have no fingers.

According to him, the option, known as special registration, was used to deceive the system and was among the irregularities detected by ABIS.

He said the commission had begun cleaning up the affected records.

“Those that we have seen, we are cleaning up,” Bayode said.

Bayode Lawrence

However, he clarified that not every photograph enhanced with artificial intelligence would be removed, distinguishing between images generated entirely by AI and genuine photographs improved with AI tools on mobile phones.

“Those that we know it is the AI on the phone that helped enhance their pictures, we can’t exclude such people because it was the AI on the phone that does that. Such people will still be on the register but those AI-generated, those photographs, all these will be removed. We are already looking at them,” he said.

The controversy followed the publication of INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters online on October 26, after screenshots circulated on social media showing questionable photographs attached to voter records, including entries from parts of Edo State.

The concerns also included allegations of duplicate entries and reports that names of deceased persons appeared on the register.

In response, INEC said the online version was the same preliminary register displayed physically at Registration Areas nationwide from October 9 to 15. It explained that the publication did not reflect all the data-cleanup activities already in progress.

The commission also said the register was not yet the final certified version and that the display, claims and objections exercise was designed to allow members of the public to identify inaccuracies and questionable entries before certification.

INEC has said it will complete the necessary verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes before certifying the final Register of Voters on December 15, 2026.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/11/01/ai-generated-photos-we-are-already-cleaning-up-our-register-inec/

posts.excerpt: Emergency crews on Sunday afternoon responded to the scene of a plane crash in Greenacres, a city in Palm Beach County, Florida, United States. The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, in a statement,
posts.content:
Emergency crews on Sunday afternoon responded to the scene of a plane crash in Greenacres, a city in Palm Beach County, Florida, United States.

The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, in a statement, said the incident occurred in the area of Military Trail, between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North.

All northbound and southbound lanes of Military Trail are currently closed until further notice, with motorists advised to avoid the area and seek alternate routes.

Videos online show the aircraft taking a sharp turn before nosediving into the ground near a mobile home park, demolishing one trailer in a huge fireball.

Information from ADS-B Exchange website shows the plane descended 27,000 feet in the course of one minute, before flight tracking data cut off.

There are reports of "several fatalities," although the figure is still unconfirmed. It is also not yet clear whether anyone on the ground was killed or injured.

The aircraft, a Learjet 60, had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was heading to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas.

Learjet 60, a business jet manufactured by Bombardier Aerospace, is typically configured to accommodate six to seven passengers alongside a two-person crew.

The Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board will investigate the crash, according to the FAA.

posts.title: Arsenal End 14-Year Winless Run At Anfield To Go Top Of Premier League
posts.excerpt: Defeat leaves fifth-placed Liverpool nine points adrift of the leaders and already facing a mountain to climb to get back in the title race. The post Arsenal End 14-Year Winless Run At Anfield To Go T
posts.content:
Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz’s early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners.

The defending champions were made to suffer after the German’s 16th-minute opener but held out for what could be a telling win in their quest to retain the title.

Arsenal climbed three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table.

But with City expected to be hit with a severe points penalty, unless they can overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules, Arsenal dealt a huge blow to their most likely rivals for the title.

“It’s been such a long time without this feeling here, that we really needed it,” said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. “We are extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody has done.”

Liverpool produced arguably their best spell of Andoni Iraola’s early months in charge with a blistering 30 minutes after conceding, but failed to take their chances as the Spaniard suffered just his second defeat in 14 games since arriving from Bournemouth.

Liverpool’s Argentinian midfielder #10 Alexis Mac Allister (R) vies with Arsenal’s Norwegian midfielder #08 Martin Odegaard (2R) and Arsenal’s English midfielder #41 Declan Rice (L) during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 1, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP)

Arteta was stinging in his criticism of the Arsenal side that crashed out to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday in one of the biggest ever League Cup shocks.

The Arsenal boss got the response he desired in a strong start from the champions.

Havertz was one of the biggest culprits for wasting chances in midweek but made amends with a simple finish from Declan Rice’s precise low cross.

The early goal lit the touchpaper for a pulsating first 45 minutes as Liverpool roared back.

Isak honesty saves Arsenal

Iraola and Arteta played together as boys for Basque side Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea.

Arteta’s old friend gave his side one of the most uncomfortable afternoons they have experienced in recent seasons as Arsenal’s rock-solid defence was left clinging on for half-time.

“I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down,” said Iraola. “I loved a lot of moments of the game.

“We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. Arsenal are in the best of the situations but it is just the start of November today.”

Liverpool’s Argentinian midfielder #10 Alexis Mac Allister indicates he’s been butted during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 1, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP)

All of Liverpool’s three £100 million-plus ($134 million) forwards started together and there are signs the relationship between Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola is beginning to flourish.

Isak did Arsenal a favour by not going down as he was pulled back by Jurrien Timber when just failing to connect with a wicked delivery from Barcola.

“The Alex one is a clear penalty,” added Iraola. “We can all see that he holds the shirt (but) because he doesn’t go to the floor, you are not going to call the penalty? I don’t understand it.”

Wirtz curled a free-kick onto the bar from a narrow angle and Alexis Mac Allister should have buried a header into the goal rather than finding the stand behind David Raya’s goal.

Half-time allowed Arsenal the chance to reset and take the wind out of Liverpool’s sails as Iraola’s men tired in the second period.

Alisson Becker produced a stunning save to turn behind Christos Tzolis’s shot that was arrowing into the bottom corner to keep Liverpool in the game.

That intervention counted for little as Arsenal rode out the closing stages to register another clean sheet and an eighth win in nine league games.

Defeat leaves fifth-placed Liverpool nine points adrift of the leaders and already facing a mountain to climb to get back in the title race.

AFP

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/11/01/arsenal-end-14-year-winless-run-at-anfield-to-go-top-of-premier-league/

posts.title: Spalletti: ‘Juventus players deserve credit for victory, but we need fans by our side’
posts.excerpt: Luciano Spalletti said Juventus players ‘deserve all the credit’ for the 2-0 win over Napoli,...
posts.content:
Luciano Spalletti said Juventus players ‘deserve all the credit’ for the 2-0 win over Napoli, but hits back at the boo boys. ‘We need our fans by our side, the real face of this stadium.’

The Bianconeri mood was dire going into this game, especially after the 2-0 defeat to relegation battlers Genoa on Wednesday evening.

Juan Cabal hit the woodwork, and Guglielmo Vicario needed a stunning early save on Lorenzo Lucca, but there were two moments of magic late on to seal the 2-0 victory.

Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga hit screamers from outside the box, around a Luca Marianucci second bookable offence.

Spalletti stands up for Juventus players

TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Luciano Spalletti, Manager of Juventus, looks on before the Serie A match between Juventus and Atalanta BC at Allianz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)At the final whistle, the coach pulled his staff members into a massive embrace.

“They suffer along with me, they too work from morning till night, I am the first to arrive and the last to leave, but they are usually there with me for most of it,” Spalletti told DAZN Italia.

“However, the credit this evening must go to the team. They managed to dig into themselves and find that desire to take the first step, to go forward, think positive, and then they managed it in the second half with a few adjustments.

“I think tonight they fully deserved the victory, restoring some of the self-esteem in the football they can play.”

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Jeremie Boga of Juventus celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)It was for long spells far from a convincing performance, but this result can be a massive confidence-booster going forward, so how did it come about?

“The most important speech was made by Carnevali, because they are not accustomed to hearing his voice, so that alone forced the players to prick up their ears, listen and absorb those words, as it was the first time he’d done that,” revealed Spalletti.

“All we can do is be by their side, but there are players who genuinely plunge into this spiral and lose confidence in everything they do, even the most normal things. When there’s a misplaced simple pass or hesitation in making a decision, which is worse than making the wrong decision, that lack of confidence gets transferred to the rest of the team.

“Napoli had started the match well, we hit back two or three times, but as the game wore on, the lads did really well in making the right choices, pushing forward, thinking positive and leaving space behind them that is hard to defend against. The players deserve all the credit this evening.”

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Weston McKennie of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)There were some fresh concerns, as Weston McKennie went off at half-time with an adductor issue, while Alajbegovic was spotted on the bench with an ice pack strapped to his calf after the goal.

When Spalletti was asked if this Juventus side can be structured to win with the current group or if they need big investments in future, he was not impressed.

“I know the game you are playing, with the pressure to put on the other, to have an advantage. At this moment, we are not structured in anything, because tonight I had to take McKennie off, Sarr had a fever and couldn’t play, all the substitutions I made were forced ones, and we’ve got to play again on Thursday.”

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Players of Juventus applaud the fans after the team’s victory in the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)Fans in the Allianz Stadium were shouting insults and calling for the team to show guts from the very first minute of tonight’s match with Napoli, with a protest outside the stadium before kick-off.

“We’ve just got to keep going. This is a moment we have to handle, then you can talk about what you want. Right now, we must be solid, along with a stadium whose real face is that of the second half, fighting alongside the team,” he added.

“You can say Spalletti’s no good, that player’s no good, get rid of everyone, but right now we need to be united, and this stadium must return to being our fortress. Even if we don’t make them that happy, we still need our fans by our side, so we thank all those today who applauded us and stayed with us.

“This is a moment where we need to hold hands and stand together, try to push forward and be positive, which isn’t easy when there are so few of us available. It was a victory deserved by the players, who deserve a big round of applause. Well done, lads.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/spalletti-juventus-players-deserve-credit-fans/

posts.title: Injury concerns after McKennie, De Bruyne and Di Lorenzo substitutions in Juventus 2-0 Napoli
posts.excerpt: Napoli star Kevin De Bruyne was subbed off in an away game against Juventus with...
posts.content:
Napoli star Kevin De Bruyne was subbed off in an away game against Juventus with a sprained ankle, while Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Weston McKennie suffered adductor injuries.

Juventus and Napoli had to make several substitutions during their meeting at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday night.

Injury updates on McKennie, De Bruyne and Di Lorenzo

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Weston McKennie of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)Napoli’s De Bruyne and Di Lorenzo were substituted at half-time, both due to fitness problems. Sky Sport Italia reports that De Bruyne suffered a sprained ankle, while Di Lorenzo picked up an adductor injury.

Gazzetta reports that Juventus midfielder McKennie also suffered an adductor injury and was replaced at half-time.

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Mario Hermoso of AS Roma battles for possession with Giovanni Di Lorenzo of SSC Napoli during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)Juventus ultimately won 2-0, with goals from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga in the second half.

Both Juventus and Napoli have a tight fixture list, with two more games coming up in the next seven days.

Napoli will visit Porto in the Champions League next Wednesday before hosting Lazio in Serie A next Sunday.

Juventus, meanwhile, will visit AZ in the Europa League next Thursday, then travel to Fiorentina on Sunday.

posts.title: Di Lorenzo: ‘Napoli struggle with consistency, I was forced to go off’
posts.excerpt: Giovanni Di Lorenzo confirms he was ‘forced’ to come off for Napoli at half-time in...
posts.content:
Giovanni Di Lorenzo confirms he was ‘forced’ to come off for Napoli at half-time in the 2-0 defeat to Juventus, but was glad to reunite with his old coach Luciano Spalletti.

The captain and Kevin De Bruyne went off at half-time with injuries, the Belgium international turning his ankle, and the team never quite stepped up the performance in the same way.

Di Lorenzo suffers new Napoli setback

NAPLES, ITALY – MAY 11: Giovanni Di Lorenzo of SSC Napoli celebrates after scoring his side first goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Bologna FC 1909 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on May 11, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)“We have many games weighing on us and I was forced to go off, which disappointed me, as I really wanted to keep going,” Di Lorenzo told DAZN Italia.

“We had that big chance to take the lead with Lucca, but we were unable to maintain the same level after the restart and the game slowly drifted into Juve’s hands. It’s a pity, because this is a blow for our position in the table and we are falling behind.”

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Federico Gatti of Juventus is challenged by Scott McTominay of SSC Napoli during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)Napoli are eight points worse off than at this stage last season, when after 10 rounds they were alone in first place, and currently sit in eighth position alongside Bologna.

“I think we are lacking consistency, because we have some really good performances and alternate them with negative ones, while even over the course of 90 minutes we struggle to stay at the same level. We have to stay united and try to improve our position in the table.”

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Nick Woltemade of Juventus is challenged by Giovane of SSC Napoli during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)Stanislav Lobotka, Benoit Badiashile, Leonardo Spinazzola, David Neres, Alisson Santos, Costantino Favasuli and Alessandro Buongiorno were already out of action, and they seemed to be fatigued after the midweek 4-1 win over Monza with very little room for squad rotation.

“If we are in this situation, then we all have to raise the bar. We are aware it’s a tough moment and we’re trying to work hard to improve, but the results are deficient right now. The team will do everything to turn it around.”

There was a reunion with Juventus boss Spalletti, who won the Scudetto with Di Lorenzo at Napoli in 2023.

“He asked me how my family was doing, I have a strong rapport with the coach, we had two incredible years together at Napoli with the Scudetto, and I will always remember him with pleasure,” concluded the defender.

Source: https://football-italia.net/di-lorenzo-napoli-struggle-with-consistency/

posts.title: Landucci: ‘Napoli had a bad second half, Juventus deserved win, but new injury problems’
posts.excerpt: Max Allegri’s assistant Marco Landucci reveals new Napoli injury problems, but ‘we had a bad...
posts.content:
Max Allegri’s assistant Marco Landucci reveals new Napoli injury problems, but ‘we had a bad second half and Juventus deserved to win, there’s not much else to say.’

The coach completed his two-match touchline ban by sitting in the stands of a stadium he knows so well thanks to 10 years at Juve in two different spells.

Assistant Marco Landucci was on the bench for this evening’s big match, but there were some late decisions forced upon them, with Rasmus Hojlund and Vanja Milinkovic-Savic laid low by a virus.

Stanislav Lobotka, Benoit Badiashile, Leonardo Spinazzola, David Neres, Alisson Santos, Costantino Favasuli and Alessandro Buongiorno were already out of action.

It was an even match with few big chances until two moments of individual magic, as Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga hit stunners from outside the box, along with Luca Marianucci’s second yellow card.

Landucci acknowledged Napoli errors

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Federico Gatti of Juventus is challenged by Scott McTominay of SSC Napoli during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)“Quite simply, we had a bad second half and Juve deserved to win. When you lose, you have to just stay quiet and accept it,” Landucci told DAZN Italia.

“We had some absences, but this isn’t an excuse, we should’ve done better after the break. I thought it was a good first half, Lucca was denied by a great Vicario save, but that wasn’t enough.”

Napoli are now stranded in eighth place on 14 points alongside Bologna, already nine adrift of Como in the Champions League spots.

They are eight points worse off than at this stage last season, when after 10 rounds they were alone in first place.

“We are not worried, but we are very disappointed, because we cared about this match. The truth is that’s how the game went, we need to shut up and prepare for Wednesday. We have many injuries, as many teams do with this fixture list, it is somewhat inevitable and you have to keep going.”

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Jeremie Boga of Juventus celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with team mates during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)It was noted that on the two goals, the Napoli defenders backed off and allowed the Juventus players to come forward, so was that a tactical choice from the bench?

“Absolutely not,” replied Landucci. “Those were great finishes, but we should not have allowed them to get into that space. We back-tracked too much, this is the difference between conceding and not conceding, and it’s not the first time. If you push up and defend well, you’re not going to concede that.

“We all could’ve done better in the second half. It seems a clear and logical analysis to me. Juventus did better than us and deserved to win.”

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Weston McKennie of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)Napoli looked as if they had more injury problems, because Kevin De Bruyne and Giovanni Di Lorenzo were substituted at half-time, then Matias Olivera looked distraught when hobbling off the field just after the Marianucci red card.

“Clearly, they could not continue. De Bruyne had a problem with his ankle, Giovanni Di Lorenzo I’m not sure, but he could not continue either. Even with that, we need to do better. It was a balanced encounter decided by these great goals, but we didn’t help our own situation.”

Has Landucci spoken to Allegri yet, seeing as the coach was in the stands?

“Yes, we spoke in the dressing room, but there’s not a lot to say. Obviously, he wasn’t happy, would you have been happy? He just said we should’ve done better in the second half, we paid a heavy price for errors, that’s it.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/landucci-napoli-had-a-bad-second-half-juventus/

posts.title: Serie A Round 10 table: Lazio back on top after 16 years, Juventus overtake Napoli
posts.excerpt: Lazio are alone at the top of the Serie A table after Round 10, while...
posts.content:
Lazio are alone at the top of the Serie A table after Round 10, while Juventus have overtaken Napoli following a 2-0 win on Sunday night.

Serie A Round 10 will complete on Monday with Sassuolo-Fiorentina and Atalanta-Parma, but Lazio already know they’ll spend the next week alone at the top of the Serie A table.

ROME, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Andrea Pinamonti of SS Lazio celebrates a second goal during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on November 01, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)Gennaro Gattuso’s men completed a comeback at home against Cagliari on Sunday, securing a 2-1 win which allowed them to overtake Inter at the top of the table.

The Nerazzurri lost the derby against Milan 3-1 on Saturday.

Lazio have 28 points in the opening ten rounds, collecting nine wins and one draw.

ROME, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: SS Lazio Gennaro Gattuso celebrates after goal during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on November 01, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)It’s nearly a record in Italy: only Rudi Garcia’s Roma in 2013-14 collected more points, winning all their opening ten league games, reports Matteo Di Gangi. Lazio were last alone at the top of the table 16 years ago, under Edi Reya.

The top four teams in the Serie A table are separated by five points. Inter sit second with 25 points, Roma have 24, and Como have 23.

ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Yunus Musah of AC Milan runs with the ball during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)Milan remain two points below the top four after beating Inter in the derby, while Juventus have overtaken Napoli and are now seventh, three points behind sixth-placed Frosinone, arguably the most surprising team in Serie A so far this season.

posts.title: Serie A | Juventus 2-0 Napoli: Alajbegovic and Boga magic revives Juve
posts.excerpt: Juventus got back on track by beating 10-man Napoli 2-0 thanks to a pair of...
posts.content:
Juventus got back on track by beating 10-man Napoli 2-0 thanks to a pair of long-range screamers by Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga, but Luca Marianucci saw red.

Both teams were locked together on 14 points going into this clash, so desperately in need of a result. The Bianconeri put their squad in a training camp after Wednesday’s 2-0 defeat at Genoa, losing three of the last four Serie A games, but Nico Gonzalez, Francisco Conceicao, Zeki Celik, Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khephren Thuram and Kamil Grabara were still sidelined.

The Partenopei were revitalised by a 4-1 win at Monza, but Rasmus Hojlund and Vanja Milinkovic-Savic were ruled out by a virus, with Amir Rrahmani not at 100 per cent, Stanislav Lobotka, Benoit Badiashile, Leonardo Spinazzola, David Neres, Alisson Santos, Costantino Favasuli and Alessandro Buongiorno injured.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Luciano Spalletti, Manager of Juventus, looks on before the Serie A match between Juventus and Atalanta BC at Allianz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)Lorenzo Lucca had a rare start and almost marked it with a victory after eight minutes, but his diving header on the Matteo Politano cross was palmed off the line by Guglielmo Vicario in a remarkable save.

Teun Koopmeiners was fortunate to avoid a yellow card for his mistimed tackle on Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa, landing on his ankle, but Juventus had appeals of their own.

Juan Cabal’s header from a corner bounced off the frame of the goal, then as the move continued, Cabal collided with Matias Olivera, but the contact seemed to be as the boot came back down.

Both sides wasted good opportunities from 12 yards, as Noa Lang and Alajegovic blasted over the bar, with Bremer doing the same after good work from Alajbegovic to dribble past two.

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Weston McKennie of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)Deep into first half stoppages, Alajbegovic also drew a tough save out of Alex Meret with his angled drive from 12 yards, as Pierre Kalulu was unable to make the most of the rebound.

There were some big changes over half-time, with Luca Marianucci moving to right-back and Juve seemed to be in a 3-5-2 shape.

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Federico Gatti of Juventus is challenged by Scott McTominay of SSC Napoli during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)Kolo Muani wasted a good counter-attacking situation when over-hitting the past for Alajbegovic, but the Bosnia and Herzegovina talent broke the deadlock with a moment of magic out of nowhere, unleashing a screamer into the top corner from the edge of the area, in off the far post.

WHAT A STRIKE

Kerim Alajbegovic lets fly from 20 yards to put Juventus ahead

Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/d1kb5dbJkY

— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 1, 2026

Woltemade failed to get on the end of a Koopmeiners pull-back from six yards, but Napoli then went down to 10 men for the second Luca Marianucci yellow card for stepping on Cabal’s foot.

Matias Olivera also limped off with a muscular problem, and Juventus doubled their lead with a not dissimilar goal, this time Jeremie Boga’s right-foot curler into the far bottom corner from outside the box.

posts.title: Dangote challenges Lotus Capital to take ‘Elephant Steps’ in Nigeria
posts.excerpt: By Matthew Johnson PRESIDENT and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, has challenged Lotus Capital Limited to take “elephant steps” in its next 20 years by expanding investmen
posts.content:
By Matthew Johnson

PRESIDENT and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, has challenged Lotus Capital Limited to take “elephant steps” in its next 20 years by expanding investments in Nigeria’s productive sectors.

Speaking at the company’s 20th anniversary celebration in Lagos, Dangote identified manufacturing, agriculture, infrastructure, energy and industrial development as critical areas where non-interest finance could mobilise long-term capital and accelerate economic growth.

He stressed that trust and integrity were fundamental to attracting investment, insisting that investors must first have confidence in those managing their funds.

“Money doesn’t follow profit only; it follows trust first. That’s why we all invested when she came with the idea. The first number one rule is that you must trust a person before you invest. Money follows trust, then profit,” he said. Disclosing that his family was among Lotus Capital’s earliest major corporate clients, Dangote commended its Managing Director, Mrs Hajara Adeola, for sustaining the pioneering non-interest financial institution despite initial challenges.

He urged the company to strengthen partnerships with international financial institutions to attract more Sharia-compliant capital into Nigeria and Africa. Adeola said Lotus Capital was established 20 years ago to promote financial inclusion by providing investment opportunities aligned with religious and ethical values.

She disclosed that the company had established four Securities and Exchange Commission-registered mutual funds, collaborated with the Nigerian Exchange to develop the NGX Lotus Islamic Index and advised the Federal Government on its first three sovereign Sukuk issuances, which funded over 4,000 roads and nine bridges.

She said the company would deepen partnerships with businesses and industrial players to support agriculture, manufacturing, real estate and renewable energy. Chairman of Lotus Capital, Mr Fola Adeola, said the company’s first investment product, the Halal Fund, was oversubscribed after it sought to raise N1 billion, reflecting growing acceptance of non-interest finance.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/dangote-challenges-lotus-capital-to-take-elephant-steps-in-nigeria/

posts.title: How I ended 10-year employment freeze at UNIBEN — VC
posts.excerpt: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — The Vice Chancellor of the University of Benin (UNIBEN), Prof. Edoba Omoregie, SAN, has said his administration has restored recruitment at the institution after a 10-yea
posts.content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY — The Vice Chancellor of the University of Benin (UNIBEN), Prof. Edoba Omoregie, SAN, has said his administration has restored recruitment at the institution after a 10-year break, with about 500 people employed last year and a similar number expected to be recruited this year.

Omoregie disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard, explaining that his administration adopted a strategy of replacing workers who retired, resigned, were dismissed, transferred or otherwise left the university.

He said the vacancies created by staff departures had remained unfilled for years because successive administrations believed there was a government embargo on employment.

According to him, the government had only restricted new appointments in some universities but allowed institutions to replace workers through attrition.

He said: “Even from calculating from those who were going to retire alone, we got over 400 spaces this year. So we calculated all that, approached the appropriate approving body for those who are leaving to be replaced, for those who have left to be replaced. That was what they didn’t do for 10 years.

“That was why our emolument cost plummeted significantly. UNIBEN used to have one of the highest employees.” Our employee strength plummeted too, from about 8,000 to about 5,000 when I took office.”

The vice chancellor said the last major recruitment exercise at the university before his administration was in 2015, adding that the prolonged gap affected the institution’s workforce and academic operations.

“The last time any employment took place on this campus until last year was in 2015. So for 10 years the university bled. They had to start moving non-academic staff into academic staff; they started recruiting adjuncts. You don’t run a university like that. Those gaps, by the grace of God, are now being filled,” he said.

Omoregie said the university recruited about 500 workers last year and planned to employ a similar number this year, covering both academic and non-academic positions.

“We did about 500 last year and by the special grace of God, this year we are still going to do an equal number,” he said.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/how-i-ended-10-year-employment-freeze-at-uniben-vc/

posts.title: Monarch’s murder: Nwifuru seeks death penalty for kidnappers
posts.excerpt: By Jeff Agbodo Ebonyi State Government has forwarded an executive bill to the State House of Assembly seeking to make kidnapping a capital offence punishable by death without an option of alternative
posts.content:
By Jeff Agbodo

Ebonyi State Government has forwarded an executive bill to the State House of Assembly seeking to make kidnapping a capital offence punishable by death without an option of alternative punishment.

Governor Francis Nwifuru disclosed this at the weekend during the funeral of the slain traditional ruler of Ndufu-Alike autonomous community in Ikwo Local Government Area, HRH Eze Francis Igwe.

Igwe, father of the immediate past Deputy Governor of Ebonyi State, Eric Igwe, was abducted on Sunday, March 1, while on his way to church. He was reportedly killed by his abductors a day after.

Speaking at the funeral, conducted by the Assemblies of God Church, Nwifuru lamented what he described as the moral deterioration among Nigerian youths, expressing concern about their readiness to assume leadership positions in the future.

He also pledged to implement any court decision against those arrested over the monarch’s murder, adding that the proposed legislation was intended to deter kidnapping and abduction in the state.

The governor said: “I am worried about our present-day youths taking up leadership positions tomorrow. Some of our youths are not well informed, and they act so irrationally.

“I am concerned because, with some of their attitudinal dispositions, there seems to be no future for our youths.

“The youths need to have a rethink concerning certain actions of theirs, especially as concerns their attitudes towards community leaders. They should desist from treating their leaders as holders of their destinies.”

He warned that the monarch’s murder should be the last such incident in Ikwo and other parts of the state.

“I will not wait to execute the decision of the court over the murderers of this monarch, HRH Eze Francis Igwe. We have sent a bill to the House of Assembly to make kidnapping attract the death sentence by hanging in the state, with no other option. This should serve as a deterrent to those planning a kidnap, whether for political reasons or otherwise,” the governor said.

Nwifuru described the late monarch as a forthright, vocal and astute parliamentarian who represented his people effectively in the old Anambra State and attracted development projects to his community, including the popular Folk Technical College, which has produced prominent Nigerians.

In tributes, former governors Sam Egwu and Martin Elechi, as well as former Senate President, Anyim Pius Anyim, described the deceased as a statesman, peacemaker, renowned educationist, administrator and passionate leader who left enduring legacies. They urged the family and the Ikwo people to take solace in his contributions to society.

In his tribute, the monarch’s first son, Igwe, described his father as a devoted family man and role model who guided him on family life, religion, politics and culture.

He said the circumstances surrounding his father’s death remained difficult for the family to comprehend but expressed confidence that his legacies would endure across generations.

Thanking sympathisers and well-wishers who attended the funeral, Igwe disclosed that his father’s last wish was for Governor Nwifuru to secure a second term.

Earlier, in a sermon titled, “Prepare for Eternity”, the General Superintendent of Assemblies of God, Nigeria, Rev. Dr. Abel Amadi, represented by the church’s General Treasurer, Rev. Dr. Gabriel Michael, urged Christians to remain prepared for eternity, noting that no one knew the hour of their death.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/monarchs-murder-nwifuru-seeks-death-penalty-for-kidnappers/

posts.title: 2027: Obi will win Bayelsa, Niger Delta, Nigeria — Dickson
posts.excerpt: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Seriake Dickson, has expressed confidence that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win Bayelsa
posts.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Seriake Dickson, has expressed confidence that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win Bayelsa State, the Niger Delta and the country at large in the January 16, 2027 general election.

Dickson also declared that the All Progressives Congress (APC) had nothing to offer the people of Bayelsa, accusing the ruling party of failing to deliver meaningful infrastructure, including roads and bridges, to the state and the wider Niger Delta region.

The former Bayelsa State governor spoke during a visit to his home state and community, Toru-Orua, alongside Obi and other NDC leaders.

In a statement posted on his Facebook page on Sunday, Dickson claimed that the APC had never defeated him politically or won Bayelsa State through the ballot.

He also boasted that he had been the major obstacle preventing the APC from winning the state since 2015, despite the defeat of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) at the federal level.

“The APC never defeated me and they have never won Bayelsa on the ballot. I have been the obstacle stopping them from winning Bayelsa since 2015, even with the defeat of the PDP at the centre,” he said.

Dickson accused Governor Douye Diri, whom he said he had supported and helped bring to power, of handing the state over to the APC, thereby turning him and his political associates into opposition members in an administration they helped establish.

He, however, described Diri as his brother and compatriot, saying their disagreement was over the political direction of the state.

“The governor is still my person, my brother, my compatriot and our governor. But he is now someone I disagree with, as he and the people in his government are wrong with the direction they are taking our state to,” Dickson said.

The senator said he had deliberately refrained from making extensive public comments on the political developments in the state to preserve peace and prevent a crisis.

He, however, urged his supporters and Bayelsans to make their political positions known ahead of the 2027 elections, while appealing to them to remain peaceful and avoid attacks, threats or abuses against political opponents.

Dickson also alleged that some of his supporters had experienced intimidation, harassment and dismissal from political appointments, although he did not provide specific details to substantiate the claims.

He maintained that his opposition to the APC was informed by what he described as the absence of tangible federal development projects, life-changing policies and adequate representation for the Niger Delta in federal appointments.

According to him, the NDC is committed to equity, justice and an inclusive Nigeria, insisting that the interests of the Niger Delta must be pursued alongside those of other regions.

The former governor urged party members to mobilise across their communities and constituencies, promising to join them in the campaigns.

He also called on them to resist electoral intimidation and any unlawful attempts by security personnel or electoral officials to undermine the will of voters.

“Those who claim to be popular should test that popularity at the polls and allow the votes to count,” he said.

Dickson said he was accompanied on the visit by Obi, the Director-General of the NDC National Campaign Council, Mallam Ibrahim Abdulkarim, and other party leaders.

He thanked the party’s National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas, members of the National Working Committee, state and local government executives, ward chairmen and other stakeholders for their participation in the visit.

He also disclosed that the delegation commissioned the party’s state secretariat before proceeding to his country home in Toru-Orua, where they were received by traditional rulers, chiefs, elders, youths, women and other residents.

Dickson said he introduced Obi to the people of Bayelsa and urged them to support and vote for him, as well as other NDC candidates in the 2027 elections.

He further called on the people to honour the legacies of political figures associated with the Niger Delta struggle, including Harold Dapabiriye, the late Chief Melford Okilo, Isaac Adaka Boro, former Bayelsa governor Diepreye Alamieyeseigha and the late Pa Edwin Clark.

The senator also recalled his role in the emergence of Diri as governor, saying his succession decision was informed by the need to sustain Ijaw political leadership and promote fairness among communities in Bayelsa.

He alleged that the state’s political transition to the APC had undermined the sacrifices made by him and other party members to establish the current political structure.

The visit also featured cultural performances, including an Ijaw traditional war boat regatta organised in Dickson’s honour, which he said he was pleased to share with Obi.

He thanked the people of Bayelsa, traditional institutions, party supporters, security agencies, musicians and media organisations for their participation in the visit.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027-obi-will-win-bayelsa-niger-delta-nigeria-dickson/

posts.title: How melted nylon additive keeps plantain chips crunchy
posts.excerpt: "If the chips go soft, the customers will throw them back at us. Nobody asks how the crunch is made; they just want the crunch" The post How melted nylon additive keeps plantain chips crunchy appeared
posts.content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

For some years, plantain chip has been one of Nigeria’s ultimate snacks which is affordable, accessible, and portable. But as inflation hovers at historic highs, a sinister economic survival tactic has crept into the informal food sector.

Read Also: NAFDAC secures five-year jail term for fake Goya oil manufacturer

Economy&Lifestyle discovered that to cut costs and keep chips crispy for days, some street entrepreneurs are turning to a dangerous additive: melted cellophane bags.

The cost of a crunch

The mathematics of running a small-scale food business in Nigeria today is brutal. The price of vegetable oil, cooking gas, and raw plantains has tripled over the last two years.

For vendors like Halima Mohammed, who operates a roadside frying station, the pressure to maintain profit margins without raising prices is suffocating.

“If I increase the price of a small pack from N200 to N400, the students will walk away.

“People don’t have money. So, vendors look for shortcuts to make the oil last longer and keep the chips from getting soggy in humidity.”

The “shortcut” involves tossing polyethylene plastic bags directly into the scalding oil.

As the plastic melts, it blends with the vegetable oil, creating a glazing agent. When the plantain slices are fried in this mixture, they form a glassy, ultra-crisp outer shell.

Crucially for vendors, the plastic coating prevents the chips from absorbing moisture, extending their shelf life from two days to over two weeks.

A lifestyle of hustle and denial

In the underbelly of Nigeria’s entrepreneurial ecosystem, the practice is an open secret, driven by sheer desperation.

The lifestyle of a micro-entrepreneur in Nigeria is defined by any-way-raw-iron—a slang term for survival by any means necessary.

With no safety nets and a failing grid that forces reliance on expensive petrol generators, the boundary between ethical business and hazardous malpractice has blurred.

Osaro Jimoh, a distributor who supplies packaged chips to traffic vendors on the , admitted that the market rewards the longest-lasting product.

“The boys selling in traffic need chips that stay crunchy under the hot sun for days. If the chips go soft, the motorists will throw them back at us. Nobody asks how the crunch is made; they just want the crunch.

“I don’t know the preservative used to achieve such crunchiness.”

For the millions of consumers who rely on these cheap snacks to get through grueling multi-hour commutes, the lifestyle implications are passive but deadly.

Plastic-infused oil releases carcinogenic compounds, heavy metals, and microplastics into the food, posing severe long-term risks to liver and kidney health.

The regulatory blindspot

Agencies have repeatedly warned the public against consuming street foods prepared with plastic additives.

However, enforcing regulations in a vast, informal economy is nearly impossible.

Millions of fryers operate out of residential backyards, unbranded and untraceable.

Public health advocate, Dr. Duro Ifagbemi, emphasized the gravity of the situation.

“We are looking at a ticking time bomb of gastrointestinal complications and cancer cases,” he warned.

“But you cannot solve a public health crisis without addressing the economic reality.

“When people are starving, long-term health risks feel invisible compared to immediate poverty.”

Surviving at all costs

Though Mohammed denied using the plastic trick herself but acknowledges that the economic system pushes many over the edge.

“Nigeria makes entrepreneurs out of necessity, not out of choice.

“When the government makes it impossible to do business cleanly, people will find a way to survive in the dirt.”

Until the macroeconomic pressures ease, the crisp snap of a roadside plantain chip will carry a cost far heavier than the few Naira exchanged on the asphalt.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/how-melted-nylon-additive-keeps-plantain-chips-crunchy/

posts.title: Gully erosion destroys 30 houses, cuts off Edo communities
posts.excerpt: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — No fewer than 30 houses have been destroyed by a ravaging gully erosion at Agor-Uwagboe community in Oredo Local Government Area of Edo State. The erosion has also cut of
posts.content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY — No fewer than 30 houses have been destroyed by a ravaging gully erosion at Agor-Uwagboe community in Oredo Local Government Area of Edo State.

The erosion has also cut off the community’s access road linking it with Ofumwengbe and Egbiri communities, leaving residents with limited means of movement.

To ease the situation, residents have constructed a makeshift wooden bridge to enable motorcycles conveying passengers to cross the affected area.

Residents of the community on Sunday staged a peaceful protest to draw the attention of the Edo State Government to their worsening situation.

Speaking during the protest, a community member, Mr Ernest Uwagboe, said the gully was gradually extending into the community, threatening more homes and property.

He warned that the entire community could be consumed by the erosion within three years if the state government failed to urgently intervene.

The community’s spokesman, Kenneth Adoni, said residents had written several letters to relevant government agencies seeking assistance but had yet to receive any intervention.

He appealed to Governor Monday Okpebholo to come to their aid, lamenting the hardship caused by the erosion.

“We are begging Governor Monday Okpebholo to come and help us. For the past three years, the gully has caused lots of problems. We cannot cross to other communities. Whenever it rains, children cannot go to school,” he said.

The residents called on the state government to urgently address the erosion menace and restore access to neighbouring communities to prevent further destruction and alleviate their hardship.

posts.title: Philadelphia Eagles lose sixth straight as Washington Commanders score 27 unanswered points
posts.excerpt: Tanner McKee's turnovers and a costly illegal formation penalty doomed the Philadelphia Eagles as Washington scored 27 unanswered points Sunday.
posts.content:
The Philadelphia Eagles are in free-fall. After building an early 10-0 lead, Philadelphia gave up 27 unanswered points in a 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football.

Philadelphia started fast. Jake Elliott hit a 40-yard field goal, and Saquon Barkley scored on a three-yard run after a Washington turnover. The Eagles never scored again. Washington took over behind Jayden Daniels and kicker Drew Stevens.

Stevens hit a 56-yard field goal late in the first quarter, Daniels found Stefon Diggs for an eight-yard score in the second, and Stevens added a 39-yard kick before halftime to put Washington up 13-10.

JALEN HURTS TO REPORTEDLY MISS REMAINDER OF NFL SEASON AFTER BLOOD CLOTS FOUND IN QUARTERBACK'S LUNGS

Philadelphia has no answers without Jalen Hurts. Tanner McKee looked like a backup all night, holding the ball, taking sacks, refusing to throw downfield and turning the ball over twice.

Without Hurts, Washington stacked the box and held Barkley to 30 yards on 13 carries.

The turning point came in the third quarter. Dorance Armstrong strip-sacked McKee, and Charles Omenihu recovered the fumble. Daniels hit Treylon Burks for 53 yards on the next play, setting up a 25-yard Stevens kick.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

When Philadelphia finally drove into scoring position in the fourth quarter, mental mistakes wiped it out. Elliott made an apparent 36-yard field goal to cut the deficit to three, but an illegal formation penalty on left tackle Jordan Mailata took the points off the board. Backed up five yards, Elliott missed wide right.

Washington closed it out. Stevens kicked a 42-yard field goal with 3:43 left. Commanders cornerback Rasul Douglas intercepted McKee on the next possession.

Rachaad White broke off a 33-yard run and scored from a yard out with 1:52 remaining, and Austin Ekeler ran in a two-point conversion to make it 27-10.

Daniels finished with 217 passing yards, one touchdown and no turnovers. Philadelphia has lost six straight games, falling to 2-6. Washington improves to 2-4-1, climbing out of last place in the NFC East.

posts.title: Export truckers allege N50,000 charges per container at Tin Can port
posts.excerpt: By Efe Onodjae Truck owners operating around the Tin Can Island Port corridor, Lagos, have raised the alarm over alleged multiple charges imposed on export-laden containers, claiming that the payments
posts.content:
By Efe Onodjae

Truck owners operating around the Tin Can Island Port corridor, Lagos, have raised the alarm over alleged multiple charges imposed on export-laden containers, claiming that the payments amount to about N50,000 per container and undermine efforts to promote non-oil exports.

The Chairman of the Association of Container Truck Owners of Nigeria, ACTOAN, Ridwan Bello, who raised the concern, accused the Nigerian Ports Authority, NPA, and other agencies operating around the port corridor of creating additional hurdles for truckers despite the introduction of the electronic call-up system.

Bello, in an interview with Vanguard, alleged that the manifest requirement had become an additional burden on truckers, questioning why it was being prioritised over the electronic call-up system designed to improve traffic management and eliminate human interference in port access.

He said the situation had made it increasingly difficult and costly for truckers transporting export containers to gain access to the port.

According to him, truckers are also subjected to multiple payments at different stages of the export process, including an alleged N15,000 payment to facilitate the dropping of each container and additional charges at terminal facilities.

He further alleged that terminal operators sometimes demand as much as ₦10,000 to offload export containers.

Bello claimed that the cumulative charges could reach ₦50,000 per container, taking a significant portion of truckers’ earnings and threatening the sustainability of their businesses.

He questioned how haulage operators could remain profitable under the circumstances, particularly when the Federal Government was pursuing policies aimed at expanding non-oil exports and diversifying the economy.

Nigeria’s non-oil exports reportedly reached $6.1 billion in 2025, up from $5.46 billion in 2024, highlighting the importance of efficient port operations to the country’s export drive.

The ACTOAN chairman called on the NPA authorities to explain the rationale behind the manifest requirement and clarify whether the electronic call-up system remained effective.

He also faulted trucking associations for what he described as their silence over the alleged practices, urging stakeholders to address the challenges confronting operators along the port corridor.

Bello called on the relevant authorities to review the charges and operational procedures, warning that the alleged practices could discourage investment in the haulage sector and undermine the country’s export ambitions.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/export-truckers-allege-n50000-charges-per-container-at-tin-can-port/

posts.title: Constitution amendment must protect IGP, CPs from abuse — Okiro
posts.excerpt: Former Inspector-General of Police and one-time Chairman of the Police Service Commission, Sir Mike Okiro, in this interview, speaks on the proposed establishment of state police, funding, training an
posts.content:
Former Inspector-General of Police and one-time Chairman of the Police Service Commission, Sir Mike Okiro, in this interview, speaks on the proposed establishment of state police, funding, training and safeguards against possible abuse by state governors.

The amendment to Section 214 of the 1999 Constitution on State Police has received the concurrence of about 30 State Houses of Assembly. But one of the core issues is funding, especially given the paucity of funds. How do you think this can be addressed?

When the amendment receives presidential assent, the dual police structure will come into effect. From then on, state governments will have to fund the respective police forces in their states. They have to source the funds. After all, they have been supporting the Nigeria Police Force all these years.

As a Commissioner of Police in Lagos and Benue states, and later as the IGP, I can attest to the operational and funding support given to the police by state governments. A number of them purchase patrol vehicles for most of the state, area commands and divisions in their respective states. Some, like Lagos, have set up State Security Trust Funds for this purpose. So, I have no doubt in my mind that they will do this effectively.

Like I said before, Lagos State, which established Operation Sweep 30 years ago, has demonstrated that it is possible. It has the Lagos State Security Trust Fund, a state-of-the-art surveillance system, as well as a world-class Forensic Analysis Centre. For over 30 years, Lagos has been equipping Operation Sweep, which morphed into the Rapid Response Squad (RRS), with modern vehicles and communication equipment. It even has drones and, I think, a helicopter for policing. So, the state is ready.

Similarly, Enugu State also has a state-of-the-art Command and Control Centre, known as the Enugu State Digital Surveillance Control Centre, for effective surveillance of the state. The sophisticated security infrastructure, which comes with facilities for DNA analysis, is aimed at promoting scientific, evidence-based justice and the war against crime.

You see, security is essential to all aspects of development. In fact, it is the pivot around which all aspects of development, social, educational and economic, revolve. No investor will invest resources in an unsafe state, and that makes security very crucial.

Besides, Chapter Two of the Nigerian Constitution says that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government. That makes it incumbent on federal and state governments to ensure this to the letter.

I agree that some governors are grappling with the regular payment of salaries to teachers and nurses. I know state police will be one of the essential services in any state. If a governor cannot pay teachers, he must still pay the police. Should a governor face difficulties, the Federal Government can step in to help with salaries and other obligations.

The fact is that many governors have been providing operational vehicles to the police for many decades. These governors also have security votes, and federal allocations to states have been on the rise for some time now. So, I think we can be hopeful because the decentralisation of policing will enhance the security and welfare of the people, the major reasons for the existence of government.

The issue of training is another central matter. How can this be addressed?

The current police force has its curriculum at the police colleges, Police Academy and specialised training institutions across the country. Since this dual structure will come into effect, the course content can be harmonised. Besides, that means each state has to set up its police colleges while retaining the existing course curriculum.

There is no doubt that Nigeria is under-policed by all international standards, and with this decentralisation, the manpower requirement can be met in no time. Nigeria has many qualified but unemployed school certificate holders, National Diploma and degree holders in such areas as Criminology, Sociology, Psychology and Law who can be absorbed into the respective state police forces.

More importantly, Nigeria has thousands of qualified lecturers, including retired police officers, who are ready to teach at and manage these proposed police colleges. Interestingly, under the amendment, the State Police Council will formulate policing policies in their respective states, manage recruitment and training of new intakes, and ensure accountability to the people.

The possibility of abuse by state governments is an issue, especially during elections. How do you think this should be addressed?

Provisions should be made in the law to ensure that the offices of the Inspector-General of Police and Commissioners of Police are insulated from abuse. I had recommended that the office of the IGP be tenured, which is now contained in the Police Act Amendment 2024. The amendment empowers the IGP to complete his four-year term instead of the previous civil service requirement of retiring at the age of 60 or after 35 years in service.

In that regard, the IGP cannot be removed from office except for reasons of misconduct or gross violation of the Constitution. That should be extended to Commissioners of Police. Their removal should be approved by a two-thirds majority of the Senate or the State House of Assembly for the IGP and CPs, respectively.

As contained in the amendment, the State Police Council should have direct oversight, while the Commissioner of Police, who will be appointed by the governor, will be the secretary of the council. He will serve a single term of four years.

Here lies the fear of abuse by state governors, as was the case during the First Republic, when regional premiers used the police against the opposition. But there must be safeguards in this case. Governors could become so powerful that they exploit their positions. There should be checks and balances to make it impossible for a governor to have 100 per cent control. This is a federation, and no governor should be able to take actions detrimental to other states. If such actions occur, there must be clear consequences written into the law.

The legislation clearly bars governors from deploying state police for partisan, ethnic, religious, sectional or personal purposes. It stipulates that the President and governors may issue only lawful, general policy directions in writing and prohibits any directive targeting named persons, political parties or groups, or requiring violations of rights.

Of course, there are also tight restrictions on the deployment and removal of police chiefs to prevent abuse. This is in addition to the Complaints Response Unit in each state, which will handle complaints against the police. This is also a check. All these fears are anticipated and addressed in the bill.

Interestingly, the National Assembly will prescribe national minimum standards for recruitment, training, vetting, promotions, discipline, use of force, firearms, complaints procedures, accountability, data management and professional conduct. States may set higher standards but cannot go below the federal baseline.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/constitution-amendment-must-protect-igp-cps-from-abuse-okiro/

posts.title: Catholic Priest leads congregation in song for Obi, Kwankwaso
posts.excerpt: A Catholic priest has been filmed leading worshippers in a church service in a song endorsing Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and his running mate, Rabiu Mu
posts.content:
A Catholic priest has been filmed leading worshippers in a church service in a song endorsing Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a video circulating on X, the priest is seen leading members of the congregation in singing a song rendered in Igbo, describing the NDC as a better political platform.

The priest sang: “Party Peter Obi ka mma; Party Kwankwaso, ka mma!” meaning “Peter Obi’s party is better; Kwankwaso’s party is better.”

The video has drawn attention to the growing involvement of religious leaders in political conversations ahead of the 2027 elections, with some publicly expressing support for candidates while others have criticised particular political arrangements.

In August, Islamic cleric, Sani Jingir, reportedly urged Muslims to vote for a Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket in the 2027 election.

Jingir made the call at a mass wedding organised by the Kano State Government for 1,500 couples, where he urged Muslims to vote in a manner that would reflect their numerical strength in the country.

President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who are both Muslims, currently occupy the country’s two highest executive offices.

Nigeria has an informal tradition of balancing presidential tickets along religious lines, usually pairing a Muslim presidential candidate with a Christian running mate.

Kwankwaso had condemned Jingir’s remarks in a post on X.

In another development, the Charismatic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) endorsed Tinubu for a second term in office.

The endorsement was announced during the group’s 2026 synod in Abuja, attended by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, and the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris.

Representatives of the conference from the six geopolitical zones reportedly mandated its President-General, Leonard Kawas, to announce the decision.

Kawas said the CBCN had members in 52 countries, including 950 canonical bishops in Nigeria.

He recalled that the conference was among religious organisations that expressed concerns over the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket adopted by the All Progressives Congress (APC) during the 2023 general elections.

However, he said Tinubu had surprised the group through the appointment of Christians to key positions in his administration.

According to him, the president had demonstrated an ability to accommodate Nigeria’s diversity.

“We are here today to reassure him of our solid support. We are standing with him in prayers and advocacy for the good programmes he has brought forth for the liberation of Nigeria,” Kawas said.

“We stand with the president today, and as long as he is willing to be our president and even come in 2027, we will still be standing with him.”

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/catholic-priest-leads-congregation-in-song-for-obi-kwankwaso/

posts.title: Kyari: 33.5m food insecurity projection not political forecast
posts.excerpt: The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has cautioned opposition politicians against using the October 2026 Cadre Harmonisé food security assessment for political propag
posts.content:
The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has cautioned opposition politicians against using the October 2026 Cadre Harmonisé food security assessment for political propaganda ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Kyari, in a statement on Monday, said the projection that 33.5 million Nigerians could face severe food and nutrition insecurity between June and August 2027 should not be interpreted as an assessment of the performance or electoral prospects of any political administration.

He described attempts by opposition voices to link the projection to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid as a misrepresentation of the technical assessment.

The minister explained that the Cadre Harmonisé was developed by the Permanent Inter-State Committee for Drought Control in the Sahel (CILSS), alongside regional and technical partners, to identify food and nutrition security risks and enable governments and development partners to respond early.

He said the assessment, supported by organisations including the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), World Food Programme (WFP), FEWS NET, UNICEF and the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), was not designed as an election forecast.

According to him, the projected figure of 33.5 million represents a decline from the 34.8 million projected for the corresponding period in 2026.

Kyari, however, noted that the assessment does not conduct retrospective analysis after the projected period to establish whether the forecasts were accurate.

He identified climate change, inconsistent rainfall, prolonged dry spells and disruptions to weather patterns associated with the Super El Niño phenomenon as some of the factors contributing to food and nutrition insecurity.

The minister said these challenges had affected planting seasons and crop production, particularly among farmers dependent on rain-fed agriculture.

He added that the assessment did not attribute the projected food insecurity figures to the continuation of any particular political administration.

Kyari said the Federal Government was responding to the identified risks through expanded access to fertiliser and other agricultural inputs, increased mechanisation, irrigation and dry-season farming, improved agricultural financing, and investments in storage, processing and climate-resilient agriculture.

He also highlighted improved security in some farming communities, saying it had enabled farmers who previously could not access their farmlands to resume cultivation.

According to him, areas such as Marte and Guzamala in Borno State, which were previously inaccessible to data collectors, have recorded improved stability, allowing the Cadre Harmonisé assessment to be conducted.

The minister further listed progress in fertiliser distribution and local blending, support for smallholder farmers, mechanisation partnerships, expansion of dry-season farming and improved agricultural financing through the Bank of Agriculture as some of the government’s interventions.

He acknowledged that the interventions would not resolve the country’s food insecurity challenges overnight, describing the problem as longstanding and structural.

“Food insecurity is a longstanding and structural challenge that has developed over many years and predates this administration,” he said.

Kyari, however, maintained that agriculture had recorded progress since Tinubu assumed office, adding that the government remained committed to increasing food production and strengthening the country’s food supply systems.

“As Minister, I accept the responsibility that comes with this challenge. When the data identifies a risk, our duty is to act on it, not to hide from it,” he said.

He urged political actors to exercise caution when discussing food security data, warning against reducing the livelihoods and welfare of millions of Nigerians to political talking points.

The minister said the government welcomed scrutiny and constructive criticism but insisted that technical assessments should not be deliberately misrepresented for electoral purposes.

He added that the government would use the findings of the Cadre Harmonisé to strengthen interventions, support farmers, protect livelihoods and improve access to safe, nutritious and affordable food.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/kyari-33-5m-food-insecurity-projection-not-political-forecast/
