posts.title: Nigerian workers face growing social security risks, NSITF warns
posts.excerpt: "The message must therefore be clear: Social protection is not simply a benefit to be discussed after a worker suffers an unfortunate incident" The post Nigerian workers face growing social security r
posts.content:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young

The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund, NSITF, has raised the alarm over growing social security risks facing Nigerian workers, warning that the rapid transformation of the labour market through artificial intelligence, AI, automation, digital platforms and the gig economy could leave millions of workers without adequate protection.

The Fund has consequently called for urgent measures to close existing social protection gaps, strengthen employer compliance and build a sustainable safety net that guarantees workers’ welfare, dignity and economic security, irrespective of their employment arrangements.

The NSITF also emphasised the need for government, employers, organised labour, social security institutions and the media to work together to ensure that technological advancement and changing employment patterns do not create a new generation of economically active but inadequately protected workers.

The Managing Director/Chief Executive of NSITF, Oluwaseun Faleye, raised the concerns in his keynote address at the Labour Writers’ Association of Nigeria (LAWAN) Annual Workshop, in Lagos, The address, titled Social Security and Workers’ Welfare in Nigeria’s Political Transition: Closing the Protection Gaps and Building a Sustainable Safety Net, was presented on his behalf by the Deputy General Manager, and Head of Corporate Affairs Department, Alexandra Mede.

Faleye described social security as an investment in human dignity, social stability and economic resilience, insisting that its importance should not be measured merely by institutional structures, regulations, financial contributions and statistics.

According to him, social security is fundamentally about protecting workers and their families against unforeseen circumstances, including workplace injuries, disabilities, occupational accidents and the sudden loss of a family’s principal breadwinner.

He said, “At its heart, social security is about people. It is about the worker who suffers an injury in the course of employment. It is about the family that suddenly loses its principal breadwinner. It is about a worker whose ability to earn an income is affected by an occupational accident.”

The NSITF MD/CEO warned that Nigeria’s rapidly changing world of work was creating new challenges for traditional social protection systems, particularly with the growing adoption of technology, artificial intelligence, remote work, automation and digital employment platforms.

While acknowledging the opportunities associated with these developments, he expressed concern that workers operating within emerging employment arrangements might be left outside established social protection structures.

He questioned how the welfare of workers engaged through digital platforms could be guaranteed and how protection could be extended to people whose employment relationships no longer follow conventional patterns.

“How do we ensure that technological progress does not create a new generation of workers who are economically active but insufficiently protected?” he asked.

Faleye maintained that Nigeria’s social protection framework must evolve in line with developments in the labour market to ensure that technological progress does not undermine workers’ welfare and security.

On the existing protection gaps, he identified the exclusion of workers outside formal employment structures, inadequate integration of employers into social protection systems and insufficient awareness of available protection mechanisms as major challenges.

He stressed that closing these gaps required more than legislation, noting that awareness, compliance, accessibility, efficient institutions, reliable data and sustained stakeholder collaboration were essential.

According to him, social security advocacy must move beyond government offices and conference halls to workplaces, businesses, communities and emerging sectors of the economy.

He also underscored the importance of the Employees’ Compensation Scheme (ECS), describing it as a critical instrument for protecting employees against work-related injuries, disabilities and occupational risks.

The scheme, he explained, represents a social compact involving employers, workers, workplaces and the wider society, adding that its effectiveness depends largely on awareness, compliance and efficient administration.

Faleye called on employers to understand and fulfil their responsibilities while urging workers to become more aware of their rights and the benefits available under the scheme.

He noted that institutions responsible for administering social protection programmes must continuously improve their efficiency, transparency and accessibility to deliver better services to beneficiaries.

“The message must therefore be clear: Social protection is not simply a benefit to be discussed after a worker suffers an unfortunate incident. It is a system of preparedness and protection that should exist before the risk occurs,” he declared.

The MD/CEO further challenged employers to regard workers’ protection not merely as a statutory obligation but as an essential component of responsible corporate citizenship.

He argued that compliance with social security obligations contributes to workplace stability, productivity, employee confidence and sustainable enterprise, urging employers to see it as an investment rather than a burden.

He said NSITF would continue to engage employers, simplify processes, improve service delivery and deepen understanding of the Employees’ Compensation Scheme.

Turning to the role of the media, particularly labour journalists, Faleye urged members of LAWAN to go beyond reporting industrial disputes and become active interpreters of labour policies and social security issues.

He said responsible labour journalism could help workers understand their rights, educate employers about their obligations and enable institutions to appreciate the concerns of the people they serve.

He encouraged journalists to interrogate policies, ask critical questions, report accurately and explain complex social security issues in language accessible to ordinary Nigerians.

On the implications of political transition for workers’ welfare, Faleye maintained that although political transitions naturally generate debates about governance and national development priorities, the responsibility to protect workers must remain constant, irrespective of changes in government.

He called for sustainable, accountable and responsive social security institutions capable of providing continuity across successive administrations and generations of workers.

Looking ahead, he identified digital and platform workers, informal-sector employees, technological disruption, occupational diseases, artificial intelligence and automation as emerging issues that Nigeria’s social protection system must adequately address.

He stressed that no single institution could close the country’s social protection gaps without collaboration among government agencies, employers, workers, organised labour, the media, technology experts, academia and development partners.

Reaffirming NSITF’s commitment, Faleye said the Fund would continue to strengthen stakeholder engagement, embrace technology, improve service delivery and deepen public awareness of the protections available under the Employees’ Compensation framework.

He added that the Fund’s ambition was to become increasingly accessible, responsive, transparent and trusted, with the Nigerian worker remaining at the centre of its mandate.

Faleye called on stakeholders at the LAWAN workshop to translate discussions into practical ideas and actions capable of strengthening social security, advancing workers’ welfare and promoting inclusive national development.

He maintained that an effective social security system should go beyond responding to vulnerability to become a foundation for economic resilience, decent work and sustainable development.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/millions-of-nigerian-workers-face-growing-social-security-risks-nsitf-warns/

posts.title: Dino Melaye challenges Tinubu to Quranic citation contest
posts.excerpt: Melaye issued the challenge in a post on his X handle on Monday, saying he was ready to compete with Tinubu in citing passages from the Quran when the President returns to Nigeria. The post Dino Melay
posts.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Former Kogi West Senator and ADC Chieftain, Dino Melaye, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to a Quranic citation contest, following the President’s ongoing spiritual visit to Saudi Arabia for Umrah, the lesser Hajj.

Melaye issued the challenge in a post on his X handle on Monday, saying he was ready to compete with Tinubu in citing passages from the Quran when the President returns to Nigeria.

He wrote, “Now that Alhaji Bola Tinubu is in Umrah. Immediately he comes back I challenge him to a Quanic citation competition with me. No one can mock God. SDM”

Now that Alhaji Bola Tinubu is in Umrah. Immediately he comes back I challenge him to a Quanic citation competition with me. No one can mock God. SDM pic.twitter.com/lssJkwMUz6

— Senator Dino Melaye. (SDM) (@_dinomelaye) November 2, 2026

The challenge comes amid public attention surrounding Tinubu’s spiritual activities in Makkah, where he performed the Umrah pilgrimage and was granted access to pray inside the Holy Ka’abah.

Vanguard reported that Tinubu arrived in Saudi Arabia on Thursday, October 29, ahead of the religious exercise, which he performed at the Grand Mosque, Masjid al-Haram, on Friday, October 30.

The President was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques.

According to the Presidency, Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led Tinubu into the Ka’abah, where he offered prayers of gratitude and sought divine guidance for Nigeria.

In his reflection on the spiritual experience, Tinubu said he had prayed for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians.

He also cited Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26 of the Quran, which speaks about Allah’s ultimate authority over power and sovereignty.

“There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority,” the President said.

Tinubu subsequently reaffirmed his commitment to national development, saying his determination to build a prosperous Nigeria had been strengthened by the spiritual experience.

The President travelled to Saudi Arabia with a delegation that included the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate; and governors of Borno, Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Yobe and Kwara states, among other officials and business leaders.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/dino-melaye-challenges-tinubu-to-quranic-citation-contest/

posts.title: Kidnappers hijack vehicle conveying corpse in Benue
posts.excerpt: Six persons travelling along Adoka-Otukpo Road in Benue State have reportedly been abducted by gunmen who abandoned the corpse of a woman in their vehicle. The victims were said to be travelling from
posts.content:
Six persons travelling along Adoka-Otukpo Road in Benue State have reportedly been abducted by gunmen who abandoned the corpse of a woman in their vehicle.

The victims were said to be travelling from Kano to Okpoga, in the Okpokwu Local Government Area of Benue State, with the corpse of the woman, who was being taken home for burial.

The incident reportedly occurred at about 8:00 p.m. on Friday, when the travellers were intercepted by the kidnappers around Adoka Road.

The abductors allegedly whisked away the six occupants, leaving the woman's corpse in the vehicle.

An activist and citizen journalist, Meddy Olotu, disclosed the incident in a video shared on social media, calling on security agencies and other relevant authorities to urgently intervene.

Olotu said family members lost contact with the travellers after they arrived in Adoka on Friday night.

He added that operatives of the Federal Road Safety Corps, FRSC, discovered the corpse the following morning and took it to the police station in Adoka, before it was deposited in a mortuary.

According to him, the kidnappers have demanded a ransom of N15 million for the release of the six abducted persons, who were still being held in captivity as of Monday.

“Last night, I spoke with one of the family members, who said the kidnappers had been calling. Fortunately, he understands Hausa and has been able to communicate with them,” Olotu said.

He lamented that the family, already mourning the death of the woman, was now faced with the burden of raising the ransom demanded by the abductors.

Olotu appealed to the authorities to take urgent steps to secure the release of the victims and enable the family to take the woman's remains home for burial.

Efforts to reach the Benue State Police Command spokesperson,DSP Orchia Peter Aondong, for confirmation and comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

Kidnappers hijack vehicle conveying corpse in Benue

posts.title: Police investigate discovery of beheaded teenager’s body in Cross River
posts.excerpt: The Cross River State Police Command has commenced an investigation into the discovery of the body of an unidentified teenage boy, with his head severed, in Yahe River, Yala Local Government Area of t
posts.content:
The Cross River State Police Command has commenced an investigation into the discovery of the body of an unidentified teenage boy, with his head severed, in Yahe River, Yala Local Government Area of the state.

The deceased, estimated to be about 16 years old, was recovered from the river on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at about 5:30 p.m.

The Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Eitokpah Sunday Akata, disclosed this in a statement issued in Calabar, Monday morning.

According to the statement, the incident was reported by the Officer-in-Charge of Yahe Outstation, ASP Ekurbe Abi, while bloodstains observed at the scene raised concerns about the circumstances surrounding the teenager's death.

The police said the body was subjected to medical examination and deposited in a mortuary, while efforts were ongoing to identify the deceased and establish how he died.

The Commissioner of Police, Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, has ordered a thorough investigation into the incident and directed that anyone found responsible be brought to justice.

The command appealed to residents of Yahe and neighbouring communities to report any missing person matching the description of the deceased or provide useful information that could assist the investigation.

Police investigate discovery of beheaded teenager’s body in Cross River

posts.title: SSANU, Sokoto State University commences five-day warning strike
posts.excerpt: The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities, SSANU, Sokoto State University, SSU, has begun a five-day warning strike following unpaid staff entitlements. SSANU, SSU, chapter warned that it
posts.content:
The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities, SSANU, Sokoto State University, SSU, has begun a five-day warning strike following unpaid staff entitlements.

SSANU, SSU, chapter warned that it may embark on an indefinite strike if the Sokoto State Government fails to address its demands.

The industrial action commenced on Monday, November 2, following the expiration of a 14-working-day ultimatum issued to the state government on October 14.

In a statement jointly signed by its chairman, Ismail Bala Muhammed, and secretary, Mansur Ahmad, the union explained that it was compelled to withdraw its services after several attempts to resolve the dispute through dialogue proved unsuccessful.

The union informed the university community and the general public that it has commenced a five-working-day warning strike following the failure of the government to address its outstanding demands.

"The union’s demands include the payment of arrears arising from the 25 per cent salary increment, approval and implementation of the 35 per cent Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance, CONTTA, annual salary increments for eligible members and payment of outstanding check-off dues," the statement said.

According to SSANU, it had held several meetings with the Commissioner for Higher Education, the Permanent Secretary of the ministry and the Deputy Governor in an effort to secure the government’s intervention, adding that the government subsequently constituted a committee to engage university-based unions from Sokoto State University and Shehu Shagari University of Education, but without any headway on its demands.

The union said the outcome of a meeting with the government on October 9 was unsatisfactory, saying that the government maintained that arrears from the 25 per cent salary increment would not be paid, while the implementation of CONTTA would commence in January 2027, subject to budgetary provision.

SSANU rejected the position, insisting that the allowance was a legitimate entitlement of its members, saying that similar allowances had been approved for academic staff under the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, and other categories of workers in state-owned tertiary institutions.

The union further explained that it resubmitted its demands following a request by the Permanent Secretary but received no concrete response before the ultimatum expired.

SSANU appealed to Governor Ahmed Aliyu to intervene personally and ensure the immediate resolution of the dispute.

It then called on traditional rulers, parents, students and other stakeholders to prevail on the government to address the issues before the warning strike escalates, assuring that failure to address their demands at the end of the five-working-day warning strike may compel the union to embark on a total and indefinite shutdown of services at the university.

SSANU, Sokoto State University commences five-day warning strike

Source: https://dailypost.ng/2026/11/02/ssanu-sokoto-state-university-chapter-commences-five-day-warning-strike/

posts.title: Gov Eno Approves 13th-Month Pension For Retirees
posts.excerpt: The State Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Pastor Sylvester Nkodo, thanked the Governor for his compassionate and impactful leadership, describing his commitment to the welfare of the elde
posts.content:
Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has approved the payment of a 13th-month pension bonus to all pensioners in the State, as well as a N10,000 one-time welfare support for November, 2026.

Governor Umo Eno disclosed this during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, who also endorsed him for re-election in 2027.

Governor Eno, who was particularly impressed by their sense of gratitude and quality organisation, assured that the Government under his leadership will continue to prioritize the welfare of pensioners and elderly citizens in the State.

“This is indeed humbling to me. It shows that you are truly technocrats with a laudable sense of organization. You may be retired but not tired. I celebrate and appreciate you greatly.

“I am now directing that N10,000 be added to the November 2026 pension payment of every pensioner in support of your welfare,” he said.

Governor of Akwa Ibom State, Pastor Umo Eno waves to retirees at the meeting.

He urged them to equally enroll in the State’s health insurance scheme, which he said was free for 65-year-olds and above, to enable them to enjoy quality healthcare and a good rest across the state.

Gov noted that he had promised to clear the backlog of gratuities, stressing that N100 billion has so far been paid, from the accumulated N111 billion since 2012, assuring that before the end of his first term, the balance will be cleared.

He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for making funds available to states, which, according to him, has made it possible for him to keep to his promise of clearing the arrears of gratuity.

Governor Umo Eno during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners.

Earlier, in his welcome remarks, the State Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Pastor Sylvester Nkodo, thanked the Governor for his compassionate and impactful leadership, describing his commitment to the welfare of the elderly and retired public servants as heartwarming and unprecedented.

He also noted that Gov. Eno’s policies have significantly improved their living standard and lifted them from abject poverty to a life of dignity.

He expressed gratitude to the Governor for the release of over N100 billion for the payment of inherited gratuities dating back to 2012 and prayed that God will grant the wishes of pensioners by granting him a second term in 2027.

Following a motion moved and seconded by Comrade James Inim and Dr. Mrs. Uduak Udoaka, respectively, the pensioners unanimously endorsed President Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Governor Umo Eno and other candidates of the APC for re-election in 2027.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/11/02/gov-eno-approves-13th-month-pension-for-retirees/

posts.title: EPL: Iwobi eyes record as Africa’s most-capped Premier League player

posts.content:
Alex Iwobi has set his sights on becoming the African player with the most Premier League appearances, DAILY POST reports.

The Fulham midfielder climbed to second place on the all-time list following his side’s 1-1 draw against Aston Villa at Villa Park last Saturday.

Iwobi was previously tied in second position with former Liverpool winger Mohamed Salah.

The 30-year-old has so far registered 329 appearances across spells for three clubs.

Iwobi made 100 and 123 appearances for Arsenal and Everton respectively. He has so far played 106 times for Fulham.

Former Ivory Coast international Kolo Toure tops the list with 352 appearances.

"But I'm trying to break the record, I think Kolo Toure is up there, so I'll keep my eyes going forward and see if I can break that," Iwobi said to FFC TV.

posts.title: Jerry Jones says Cowboys coach won't be fired after loss but Indy's Shane Steichen has no such pledge Monday
posts.excerpt: Jerry Jones says Brian Schottenheimer remains the Cowboys coach while the Colts continue to quit on season, suggesting Shane Steichen's eventual ouster
posts.content:
The painful but seemingly inexorable march toward head coach unemployment took another significant step in the careers of Brian Schottenheimer and Shane Steichen on Sunday.

Both coaches are headed to similar dismissals which are deserved and the only reason it hasn't happened already is because the owners of the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys are eccentric and perhaps arrogant enough to believe what is an obvious lost cause can still be redeemed.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said after Sunday's come-from-in-front overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals that Schottenheimer remains the Cowboys' coach and firing him is not a looming move.

MIKE TOMLIN'S COACH CRITICISM MAKES HIM BETTER TV ANALYST BUT RAISES QUESTION WHETHER HE'S EYEING COWBOYS JOB

"We're not going to get into anything, that's not in my mind at this time," Jones told the usual gaggle of reporters he entertains after home games. "The main thing that's in my mind is we tee it up for those kind of spots to win it. We really do want those situations. Call for it. Bring it on."

The Cowboys got the situations they wanted, leading 14-3 at halftime and 17-10 after three quarters against the Cards. And they blew the game.

The upstart Cardinals rallied behind Gardner Minshew throwing to Michael Wilson or handing it to Tyler Allgeier, who rushed for 147 yards against Dallas after gaining 64 yards the previous three games.

Jones saw his team lose at home for the third time in four games.

COWBOYS COACH BRIAN SCHOTTENHEIMER DEFENDS PLAYERS-ONLY MEETING DESPITE MIKE TOMLIN'S CRITICISM

He saw his team fail to string together consecutive wins for the third time this season. Indeed, winning streaks are foreign to the Cowboys under Schottenheimer, because they have won consecutive games only once in his tenure.

And out of all this, after losing to a roster that is less talented and slightly less experienced, Jones blamed practically everyone except Schottenheimer.

"A lot of people let Brian down today," Jones said. "And so for whatever criticism we want to have of Brian, we can all get in line. To use a cliché, that was a total team effort out there for us. And we have to be, for our fans, we have to be better than that when we got our hands on a win and then drop the ball."

So, Jones is staying the course for now. But that doesn't answer the fundamental question why?

JONATHAN TAYLOR'S WIFE KNOWS THINGS SO DIRE FAMILY IS ON 'COLTS TRANSACTION WATCH' EXPECTING TRADES OR FIRING

COLTS TRADE PRO BOWL GUARD QUENTON NELSON TO SEAHAWKS, THE FIRST OF WHAT COULD BE MULTIPLE DEADLINE MOVES

The Colts were similarly trying to find answers to their continued problems after Sunday's blowout 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The Colts have lost four consecutive games, fired their general manager, traded multiple star players, are on the verge of also trading running back Jonathan Taylor, and Steichen was somehow searching for reasons he's got problems.

"I'm going to evaluate everything, every position going forward," Steichen said at one point when someone asked if Daniel Jones would remain his starting quarterback.

Earth to Steichen: Where was this evaluation of Jones before you and deposed GM Chris Ballard agreed to give the quarterback a two-year extension in March?

The coach who was all in on Jones in the offseason seemed suddenly willing to get out on Sunday. And that seems to be the prevailing culture in Indy.

Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has quit on the season by firing the GM, and ordering the systematic trading of top talent to the highest draft choice bidder.

Steichen has been seemingly picked up on that and turned on Jones. And some players are turning on the season as seen by them letting the Jaguars tear through weak tackle attempts to the tune of 183 rushing yards and three passing TDs by Trevor Lawrence.

Because of all this, it would not really surprise if Irsay-Gordon soon turns her quitting on Steichen. As early as Monday. With the coach's ouster.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Should that guillotine not fall on Monday or this week, it would merely be a temporary stay and not a permanent sign of confidence.

But if the ax falls, the Colts can hand the interim head coach job to defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo or offensive coordinator Jim Bob Cooter – both of whom have interviewed for NFL head coach vacancies in the past.

Either way, change has come to the Colts and it will not be long before it claims Shane Steichen.

posts.title: Charter school founder backs Trump administration push to decentralize K-12 education
posts.excerpt: Salt Lake City charter school founder Carolyn Sharette backs the Trump administration's efforts to cut federal red tape and return education to states.
posts.content:
SALT LAKE CITY — A charter school founder and executive is throwing her support behind the Trump administration’s effort to strip federal bureaucracy from classrooms and return education authority to the states.

"It is very helpful to return the funding to the states that we already get, but with less regulation on those funds so that I can serve our students' needs — precisely what they need — instead of maybe what somebody in Washington thought they needed," Carolyn Sharette, founder and executive director of American Preparatory Academy (APA), told Fox News Digital.

Sharette founded APA in Utah in 2003. The public charter school network now serves more than 5,000 students across eight Utah campuses.

DENVER MOTHER FIGHTS FOR HER DAUGHTER'S EDUCATION AS ADVOCATES MAKE NATIONWIDE SCHOOL CHOICE PUSH

"We know exactly what our students need here to progress, and so returning the education to the states means we get to use the money in more flexible ways to help our students," Sharette said.

On Oct. 20, APA’s West Valley City campus served as the 47th stop on Education Secretary Linda McMahon’s 50-state "Returning Education to the States Tour," which aims to highlight the Trump administration's K-12 reform efforts.

Delivering a keynote speech titled "The Next 250: K-12 Education," McMahon emphasized shifting authority back to local leaders, investing in proven academic interventions and expanding school choice for families.

According to U.S. Department of Education officials, more than $3 trillion in federal taxpayer money has been funneled into K-12 education in recent decades. Despite the massive expenditure, national assessment data shows only about three in 10 students perform at or above proficient levels in math and reading.

AMERICAN SCHOOLS COST MORE THAN EVER BUT OUR STUDENTS STILL KEEP FAILING

Upon taking office, McMahon pledged to work toward dismantling the federal education agency, including installing leaders tasked with phasing out their own divisions. The effort aligns with President Donald Trump’s broader educational agenda, which he highlighted during a White House Rose Garden event championing school choice.

"School choice is really profound, actually," Sharette told Fox News Digital. "The role we play because we provide a place for parents to choose a different school if they'd like, and it's wonderful that they have that option."

MCMAHON PLANS TO 'FIRE' HERSELF FROM A JOB, STRIVING TO SHOW CONGRESS THAT THE DEPARTMENT OF ED IS NOT NEEDED

"We provide a school that is a classical school," Sharette added. "We teach through literature, we teach the science of reading. We've always had very high reading scores at our school. So parents who are looking for a rigorous and classical education can choose our school and have that freedom."

Trump has also pledged to eliminate "far-left extremism" from classrooms, arguing that decades of federal administrative oversight have failed to yield acceptable academic results.

To streamline operations, the Department of Education recently launched a new waiver process allowing state leaders to request greater flexibility when spending federal funds, while significantly cutting administrative red tape. Iowa became the first state in the nation to participate in the flexibility initiative.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/media/charter-school-founder-backs-trump-administration-push-decentralize-k-12-education

posts.title: Type 2 diabetes patients 21 times more likely to achieve remission with intensive lifestyle changes
posts.excerpt: A low-calorie diet paired with resistance training helped participants lose 18.5 pounds without shedding muscle, according to a new Lancet study.
posts.content:
A strict routine combining a low-calorie diet with supervised strength and aerobic training helped more than half of younger adults reverse type 2 diabetes within six months, according to a study published in The Lancet Regional Health - Americas.

The study, dubbed the RESET for Remission trial, found that 54% of participants under age 45 who completed the intensive lifestyle program achieved disease remission.

In comparison, only 4% of participants receiving standard medical care reached the same milestone.

VITAMIN SUPPLEMENT MAY DELAY DIABETES IN SELECT GROUPS, RESEARCHERS SAY

Type 2 diabetes diagnosed at a younger age is historically aggressive, according to medical literature.

Patients diagnosed before 45 face a faster loss of blood sugar control, earlier cardiovascular complications and a shorter overall life expectancy than those diagnosed later in life.

Researchers from McGill University in Canada and the University of Leicester in the United Kingdom enrolled 96 adults between the ages of 18 and 45 who were living with obesity and early-onset type 2 diabetes. None of the participants were using insulin.

The intervention group halted their blood sugar and blood pressure medications under medical supervision and began an intensive 800- to 900-calorie daily diet.

SIMPLE EXERCISE DONE JUST ONCE A WEEK COULD HELP LOWER BLOOD PRESSURE

For the first two weeks, patients consumed only meal-replacement products. From weeks three through 12, they were allowed one structured meal of lean protein and vegetables each day alongside meal replacements, before shifting into a weight maintenance phase for the final 12 weeks.

The program paired calorie restriction with supervised aerobic and resistance training twice weekly, plus one weekly solo workout.

"Our study shows that it is possible to combine a low-calorie diet with supervised exercise in young adults with type 2 diabetes," lead author Dr. Kaberi Dasgupta, a professor of medicine and director of the Division of General Internal Medicine at McGill University, told Fox News Digital.

"There has previously been some concern about combining the two as being too much of a burden for people. However, people in our study stayed in our study."

Only 10% of participants failed to complete the final evaluations, and patients attended a median of 17 out of 20 scheduled supervised gym sessions.

The researchers emphasized resistance training to combat the loss of lean muscle mass, a major risk associated with rapid weight loss.

4 SIMPLE HABITS CAN HELP SLOW MUSCLE LOSS AS YOU AGE, FITNESS EXPERT SAYS

People who lose weight through crash dieting or appetite-suppressing medications may shed muscle along with fat, experts warn. If the weight returns, some research suggests it may come back disproportionately as body fat, potentially affecting muscle health and metabolism over time.

"In our study, we think the diet provoked the weight loss, and exercise helped make sure it was [not] from muscle," Dasgupta said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"We were happy and surprised that not only did people lose fat from their organs and liver, our MRI studies indicated their muscle did not decrease at all and their handgrip strength went up."

Participants shed an average of 18.5 pounds over 24 weeks, while significantly boosting their treadmill endurance and overall cardiovascular fitness.

To meet the official standard for remission, patients had to maintain an HbA1c blood sugar level below 6.5% after going at least 12 weeks without any glucose-lowering drugs.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

After accounting for baseline health factors, researchers concluded that patients on the diet and exercise program were 21 times more likely to achieve remission than those receiving routine care.

Despite the promising outcomes, experts emphasized notable limitations. The trial was small, examining fewer than 100 individuals across medical centers in England and Canada over a relatively short six-month window.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Dasgupta also noted that the study could not determine exactly what was responsible for each benefit.

"The main limitation is that we had to compare the diet plus exercise with usual care," he told Fox News Digital. "We would have liked to compare diet alone against diet and exercise to perfectly prove the point that the improvements in muscle and fitness were from the exercise."

The strict routine also took a physical toll. Roughly 86% of the intervention group reported mild to moderate side effects, primarily during the early weeks, including headaches, fatigue, dizziness and constipation, though researchers noted that no severe medical complications occurred.

Health professionals cautioned that diabetes remission is not a permanent cure, and sustaining an 800-calorie threshold alongside supervised gym can present steep hurdles for busy adults outside a clinical setting.

Study authors noted that longer-term trials in real-world settings are still needed to determine whether patients can keep the weight off, preserve their muscle gains and remain medication-free once regular daily routines resume.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/health/type-2-diabetes-patients-21-times-more-likely-achieve-remission-intensive-lifestyle-changes

posts.title: JACKSON THOMPSON: Abdul El-Sayed suggests males in girls' sports is manufactured issue
posts.excerpt: Abdul El-Sayed told "60 Minutes" he's "not running to govern sports" when pressed on transgender athletes, calling it a distraction from economic issues.
posts.content:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed said he was "not running to govern sports" when asked about transgender athletes during a "60 Minutes" interview, suggesting that the issue is manufactured.

"And instead, we're out here talking about who gets to play what sport, which, you know, should be the question of the people who govern sports. I'm not running to govern sports, right?" El-Sayed told correspondent Ross Douthat during the interview.

The discussion came as Douthat asked a broader question about parental control over education and tensions between some Muslim voters and cultural liberalism. His examples included what schools teach and transgender students’ participation on sports teams.

"Like these are places where rights are in conflict," Douthat said before asking how those disagreements should be resolved.

"I don't know that that's actually true," El-Sayed responded. "I think we manufacture these social issues because here's the thing about it, Ross. You have an iPhone in your pocket probably or is it an iPhone or a Samsung?"

El-Sayed went on to argue that smartphones and the internet make it unrealistic for parents to prevent children from encountering ideas they find objectionable. He said parents should explain their beliefs and help children navigate what they encounter.

"I think it's really important for us to recognize that the free flow of information is actually a beautiful thing," he said.

He then returned to sports while accusing people who emphasize cultural disputes of diverting attention from economic problems.

"A lot of the cultural war issues that get fought right now are about trying to distract us from the fact that we can't afford our gas, can't afford our groceries, can't see a doctor, are worried about whether or not our kids are going to have a good life," he said.

MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT AWKWARDLY PIVOTS TO CIRCUMCISION DURING HEATED FOX NEWS DEBATE ON CHILD SEX CHANGES

El-Sayed did not specify in the exchange which eligibility rules he believes sports organizations should adopt, or whether he would support federal legislation restricting transgender athletes’ participation in girls’ and women’s sports.

CBS released extended candidate interviews alongside its Sunday broadcast. El-Sayed faces Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers in Tuesday’s election for the Michigan Senate seat held by retiring Democrat Gary Peters.

Rogers posted a clip of El-Sayed's answer on the topic on X, which prompted widespread viral criticism against the Democrat.

The candidates have previously taken sharply different positions on transgender participation in female sports.

During his 2024 Senate campaign, Rogers signed Independent Women’s Voice’s Stand With Women Commitment, promising to support legislation preserving female opportunities and private spaces.

"Biological men should not be competing with our daughters, period," Rogers said at the time.

Rogers also made the issue part of an Aug. 28 campaign advertisement this year, released with the National Republican Senatorial Committee as part of what his campaign described as a coordinated seven-figure advertising buy.

MICHIGAN DEM SENATE NOMINEE COMES UNDER FIRE OVER RESURFACED BLOG POST LINKING FOOTBALL TO 'TOXIC MASCULINITY'

"Abdul thinks football is bad, but men playing in women's sports is good," Rogers said in the ad.

El-Sayed previously advocated government action to protect transgender students’ access to sports teams matching their gender identity.

In a March 2018 interview during his campaign for Michigan governor, Pride Source asked whether he would fight at the state level for students’ access to bathrooms, athletic facilities and teams consistent with their gender identity. El-Sayed said the state should "protect access to bathrooms, to locker rooms, to sports teams of choice for young people."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

He argued that exclusion could compound bullying and mental-health problems for transgender students, and that government had a responsibility to protect them.

The dispute has also produced federal investigations and litigation in Michigan.

The U.S. Education Department announced June 18 that it was opening Title IX investigations into Ann Arbor Public Schools, Monroe Public Schools and Chippewa Valley School District over allegations concerning athletic participation and locker-room access based on gender identity. The announcement opened investigations; it did not establish that the districts had violated the law.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

In October, Monroe volleyball player Briley Lechner and her father sued Monroe Public Schools, the Michigan High School Athletic Association and district officials. Their attorneys allege school officials concealed an opposing transgender player’s participation and allowed the teams to share locker-room facilities.

Monroe’s superintendent said in April that an independent investigation found the district’s Title IX allegations unsubstantiated.

On Oct. 13, Monroe’s school board voted 5-2 to restrict girls’ sports and girls’ locker rooms to biological females, CBS Detroit reported.

At the college level, the NCAA changed its policy in February 2025 following President Donald Trump’s executive order on women’s sports. Its rules prohibit athletes assigned male at birth from competing on women’s teams, while permitting them to practice with those teams.

Sports eligibility has also been the subject of Senate votes. On March 3, 2025, a motion to advance the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act received 51 votes in favor and 45 against, falling short of the three-fifths threshold required. The legislation would define sex for Title IX athletics compliance according to reproductive biology and genetics at birth.

posts.title: SCHOEN, COOPERMAN: Democrats close in as Republicans scramble to hold Congress
posts.excerpt: Polls, forecasts and prediction markets flash alarm bells for Republicans as Democrats eye their largest House majority since 2009 in the midterms.
posts.content:
In the closing days of the 2026 midterm cycle, all available evidence suggests that the trends are moving in Democrats’ favor. Polls, forecasts, and prediction markets are now ringing alarm bells for Republicans, as virtually all key races move in Democrats’ direction.

Indeed, on Saturday, Cook Political Report shifted "a dozen more House races" toward Democrats, now projecting that Democrats will flip 12-25 House seats, potentially giving them their largest majority since 2009.

As a result, political forecasting sites VoteHub and Decision Desk have updated their odds of Democrats taking the House to their highest levels of the cycle: 89% and 83%, respectively, as of Sunday afternoon.

EVERYTHING TO KNOW ABOUT HOUSE AND SENATE CONTROL, BALLOT MEASURES AND 2026 ELECTION DAY POLL CLOSING

Prediction markets have followed suit: Kalshi gives Democrats a 93% chance to take the House and a 71% chance to win the Senate as well.

To that end, the trends in the Senate point in the same direction, and while Republicans have slightly better odds of keeping the upper chamber, it’s clear that the momentum is with Democrats.

SENATE CONTROL IS A COIN FLIP — AND DEMOCRATS’ PATH RUNS THROUGH TRUMP COUNTRY

Final polls ahead of the election show all or most of the seven key races shifting to the left, including in Kansas, where Democrat Adam Hamilton leads in the four most recent polls, including one from The Washington Post in which he led Republican incumbent Roger Marshall by 9%.

True, that is an outlier — and its accuracy is being reviewed by The Washington Post — but the fact that every other poll is within six points in a state that has not had a Democratic senator in over 90 years indicates that the underlying trend is moving in Democrats’ favor.

MAINE, KANSAS SENATE RACES NECK AND NECK AS DEMOCRATS LEAD IN TEXAS, MICHIGAN, POLL SHOWS

Other Republican-held seats in South Carolina, Iowa, Maine, Texas and Ohio are also increasingly within reach for Democrats.

Of those races, South Carolina and Iowa are the only two where the Republican candidate has a polling lead, but it’s under three points in South Carolina and under one point in Iowa. Thus, both races are statistically tied and within reach for Democrats.

GOP SENATE MAJORITY FACES FRESH UNCERTAINTY AS 2 KEY RACES TIGHTEN DAYS BEFORE MIDTERMS

In the other states — Maine, Texas, Ohio and Michigan — the polls have consistently shown Democratic candidates leading.

And while those leads are small, they have not contracted, and Michigan in particular has seen a noticeable widening, with Abdul El-Sayed now leading Republican Mike Rogers by roughly four points.

However, it will be interesting to see whether Rep. Haley Stevens’ endorsement of Rogers impacts the race, particularly among moderates and Black voters, as polls show that El-Sayed has struggled with both key demographics.

DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS ENDORSES GOP SENATE NOMINEE MIKE ROGERS AT DETROIT CHURCH

That said, given that North Carolina’s Senate race is effectively decided for Democrat Roy Cooper — who leads Republican Michael Whatley by nearly 11 points — Democrats now have a wide range of possible routes to winning the Senate.

VETERAN DEM OPERATIVE SAYS SUBPAR GOP CANDIDATES POISED TO HAND OVER SENATE MAJORITY

Immediately after the 2024 election, it may have seemed improbable that just two years later, Democrats would be on the verge of retaking both the House and Senate, let alone possibly winning states like South Carolina, Alaska, Iowa, Texas and Kansas.

Yet it is a very real possibility, owing in no small part to President Trump’s approval rating, currently below 40%.

SCHOEN, COOPERMAN: DEMOCRATS COULD BE RIDING A MIDTERM WAVE. THESE NUMBERS SHOULD TERRIFY THE GOP

On key issues, it’s even worse. Less than 3 in 10 (29%) Americans approve of Trump’s handling of the economy, and an even smaller 22% approve of how he’s handled inflation, per Fox News polling.

Even as Republican candidates and operatives talk up their chances in these close races, there are signs of panic within Republican ranks.

TRUMP-BACKED SENATOR ADMITS GOP FACES NIGHTMARE SCENARIO IN STATE REPUBLICANS HAVEN'T LOST IN 90 YEARS

Trump’s decision to cancel then reschedule rallies in Kansas and Iowa this weekend says as much. Republicans in those two deep-red states should not need a boost from the president, but with the national environment tilting toward Democrats, they do.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Put another way, if Republicans were confident in their chances, they would not need the president to campaign in some of the deepest-red states and districts.

Ultimately, while we will only know the true picture after all the votes have been counted, coming out of the campaign’s final weekend, it is clear that Democrats have the advantage.

Carly Cooperman is CEO of Schoen Cooperman Research.

posts.title: George Floyd-era police watchdog chair charged with selling name to inmate who vowed to 'blow down' witness
posts.excerpt: Hassan Bennett, chair of Philadelphia's police watchdog, allegedly sold a witness' name in an attempted murder case to a man who vowed violence.
posts.content:
The chair of Philadelphia's city-run police watchdog is accused of selling a witness' name in an attempted murder case to a man who threatened to "blow down the witness in broad daylight."

Hassan Bennett, chair of the Philadelphia Citizens Police Oversight Commission, faces charges after investigators say he sold a witness' name and an unredacted arrest report to a prison inmate in a domestic violence attempted murder case to Thomas Scott, who allegedly vowed to "blow down" the witness "in broad daylight." Bennett also works at the Defender Association of Philadelphia.

Investigators listened to prison calls and heard Bennett read Scott details from the arrest report in the attempted murder case, the Philadelphia District Attorney's Office said in a news release. Bennett also allegedly handed over the witness' full name.

MADISON BROOKS RAPE SUSPECT'S ATTORNEY HELD IN CONTEMPT FOR USING HER NAME TO TRY TO BAN PINK IN COURTROOM

Scott then asked Bennett for a copy of the paperwork, offering to pay him $500, officials said. The documents were sent to Scott, who sent them to various other people "in order to intimidate the witness in the open case," the district attorney's office said.

The district attorney's office said Scott was recorded saying he "was searching for the witness' location, that the witness needs to recant his statement."

LUIGI MANGIONE JUDGE SAYS JURORS WILL REMAIN ANONYMOUS AFTER THREATS AND HARASSMENT OF WITNESSES

Officials say Scott was recorded saying "the whole purpose of his social media posts was to prevent the witness from coming to court."

Bennett, who now leads the Citizens Police Oversight Commission, a body formed after the 2020 protests over George Floyd's death, was convicted of second-degree murder in 2008. He was acquitted at a 2019 retrial, where one of the victims and a co-defendant testified that their earlier statements implicating him had been coerced by a then-homicide detective.

EMBATTLED SOROS-BACKED DA BLAMES ‘CRIMINAL’ POLICE MISCONDUCT IN ACCUSED PHILLY COP KILLER’S PRIOR MURDER CASE

Both men face felony charges of intimidation of witness/victim, conspiracy, criminal use of communication facility and bribery.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

National Police Association spokeswoman Sgt. Betsy Brantner Smith told Fox News Digital that the incident should be a "cautionary tale" for other cities.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

"When you are given that much access to people's private information, and you are giving that much access to inside information, the city in this case needs to be very sure that he is someone who is ethical," Smith said. "Just because you have had a felony conviction overturned doesn't mean that you have the ethics necessary to handle this sensitive information."

SEND US A TIP

"We believe that this entire commission in Philadelphia needs to be looked at, each person individually," she added.

District Attorney Larry Krasner said Bennett's alleged crimes are "serious" but "not a reflection on the work of the Citizens Police Oversight Commission or the Defender Association of Philadelphia."

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"I would like to be in a position to say that this defendant had no such involvement, but he did, and the evidence is strong," Krasner said.

DEM JUSTICES SLAP SOROS-BACKED PHILLY DA WITH POWER STRIP IN STUNNING DECISION: 'NOT RELIABLE'

In a statement, the Philadelphia Citizens Police Oversight Commission said Bennett is on leave.

"We recognize the seriousness of this matter. We will respect the legal process, refrain from commenting on legal allegations that are under investigation and take appropriate steps to protect confidential information," the commission said. "Our responsibility to the people of Philadelphia remains unchanged. We will continue our work to strengthen police accountability, promote transparency, and build public trust."

Fox News Digital reached out to Scott's attorney. Bennett could not immediately be reached for comment.

posts.title: Experts call for Curtis Jones after disappointing Barella display in Milan derby
posts.excerpt: Nicolo Barella is among the Inter players to come under criticism after Saturday’s 3-1 defeat...
posts.content:
Nicolo Barella is among the Inter players to come under criticism after Saturday’s 3-1 defeat against Milan in the Derby della Madonnina, and experts including Paolo Di Canio feel that it is only a matter of time before summer signing Curtis Jones becomes the starter in the Italian’s preferred position.

Di Canio: ‘Jones will be a starter, Inter’s most evolved midfielder’

Inter were beaten 3-1 by Milan in the derby on Saturday: They have now gone eight matches without a victory in the Derby della Madonnina, drawing twice and losing six times since their most recent victory over the Rossoneri in April of 2024.

ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Nicolo Barella of FC Internazionale is challenged by Strahinja Pavlovic and Koni De Winter of AC Milan during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)Saturday’s defeat against Milan also ended Inter’s unbeaten start to the 2026-27 Serie A season and has seen them knocked off top spot by Lazio, who have collected 28 points from a possible 30 after 10 league matches.

Among the Inter players facing criticism after the derby defeat is Italy international Barella, who committed the foul just outside the penalty area that led to Diego Moreira’s excellently-taken free-kick, which sent Milan into a 3-1 lead.

Paolo Di Canio, on punditry duty with Sky Sport Italia on Sunday, feels that this isn’t an uncommon thing for Barella.

ROME, ITALY – MAY 14: Paolo Di Canio attends during the A-Words at Ara Pacis on May 14, 2019 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images for Lega Serie A)“Inter suffered against Milan. It was a team that looked terrified, especially after going 3-1 down. Barella commits the foul and it’s a bad one, the one that led to the goal for 3-1. It’s things we’ve spoken about before, impromptu little heel kicks and things like that,” said Di Caino (via TMW).

“They confirmed it themselves by saying that they might’ve lost a bit of hunger or that they’ve taken their foot off the gas. We’re not making that up. They are still the strongest team, but they didn’t bounce back against Milan. It’s a team that has a few problems. Most importantly, they need to get their best players back.”

Di Canio feels that Inter would be better off with Jones starting in Barella’s position in midfield.

“Remember: Curtis Jones will be a starter. He brings aggression and also helps out in front of the defence. He will play, he’s their most evolved midfielder.”

MADRID, SPAIN – SEPTEMBER 08: Curtis Jones of Internazionale has a shot during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Real Madrid C.F. and FC Internazionale Milano at Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on September 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)Jones has made four Serie A appearances for Inter following his €35m summer transfer from Liverpool, but has missed the last five with an adductor injury, which has kept him out of action since the September-October international break.

Stefano Pioli, also in the Sky studio on Sunday, agreed with Di Canio’s verdict on Jones: “I like him a lot, he’s an all-rounder,” said the former Nerazzzurri head coach.

Pioli feels that the absence of Lautaro Martinez is hurting Inter more than anything right now, though.

“There’s an Inter with Lautaro and an Inter without him. Every coach wants a captain like that. He fights for every ball and plays every game with passion and a desire to help the team. I’ve always really admired him.

“Sometimes in the dressing room, what a teammate says to you can be the most important thing.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/experts-call-for-curtis-jones-after-milan-loss/

posts.title: Pioli analyses Juventus 2-0 Napoli: ‘Kolo Muani is working hard from what I can see’
posts.excerpt: Stefano Pioli shared his thoughts following Juventus’s 2-0 victory over Napoli in Serie A on...
posts.content:
Stefano Pioli shared his thoughts following Juventus’s 2-0 victory over Napoli in Serie A on Sunday evening, suggesting that the hosts’ ‘desire’ is what got them over the line, and that Luciano Spalletti is doing everything he can to get the best out of Randal Kolo Muani.

Pioli analyses Juventus 2-0 Napoli

Juventus picked up a much-needed 2-0 victory at home against Napoli in Serie A thanks to goals from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga on Sunday evening, bouncing back after a midweek 2-0 defeat away against Genoa.

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Players of Juventus applaud the fans after the team’s victory in the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)The Bianconeri are now up to seventh place with 17 points from their first 10 league matches of the season, whilst Massimiliano Allegri and Napoli are on 14, one place behind them in the table.

Pioli was a guest in the Sky Sport Italia studio for Sunday’s coverage of Juventus’s 2-0 victory over Napoli and shared his thoughts on the game after full-time.

“It was an exciting game in the first half, but Juventus went on to show the desire to win and it’s a game that will give the Bianconeri a bit more trust,” said the former Milan, Inter, Fiorentina and Lazio head coach (via TMW).

FLORENCE, ITALY – NOVEMBER 2: Head coach Stefano Pioli manager of ACF Fiorentina looks on during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and US Lecce at Artemio Franchi on November 2, 2025 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images)Juventus have recently been playing in a 3-5-2 with Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade up front with injuries to several key attacking players, but then decided to bring on more natural wide players in Jeremie Boga and Edon Zhegrova in the second half.

Asked whether it makes a big difference if Juventus play with wingers or with a two-man striker partnership, Pioli said: “I think so, but Juventus have a lot of wingers. The pairing of Woltemade and Kolo Muani makes sense, but Spalletti made good changes and interpreted the game well. The Bianconeri had a lot of shots from outside the box and they were rewarded for that tonight.”

TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 22: Randal Kolo Muani looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Juventus and Stade Rennais FC at Allianz Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)And on Kolo Muani specifically, Pioli said: “As long as he shows a willing attitude, Kolo Muani is working hard from what I can see, he’s just missing that decisive moment. You have to help him on a psychological level, being there for him and giving him confidence or putting him in different areas on the pitch: In short, basically what Spalletti is trying to do.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/pioli-analyses-juventus-2-0-napoli/

Report: Thiago Motta could replace Fonseca at Lyon

Despite sitting in third place in Ligue 1 after nine matches of the 2026-27 season, recent reports suggest that former Milan head coach Fonseca could leave Lyon in order to his native Portugal to take over from Rui Borges as head coach of Sporting CP instead.

epa11787602 Milan’s head coach Paulo Fonseca gestures during the Italian Serie A soccer match between Hellas Verona and AC Milan, in Verona, Italy, 20 December 2024. EPA-EFE/FILIPPO VENEZIAFonseca has reportedly requested to leave Lyon according to recent reports from l’Equipe.

If Fonseca does leave, Lyon will be left needing a replacement, and according to l’Equipe, Thiago Motta is among the list of potential replacements.

Motta has been available since leaving Juventus in March of 2025, less than a year after he was appointed as Bianconeri head coach. He had been handed the job after an impressive season with Bologna, which ended with Champions League qualification at the end of the 2023-24 season.

TURIN, ITALY – FEBRUARY 16: Thiago Motta, Head Coach of Juventus, applauds during the Serie A match between Juventus and FC Internazionale at Allianz Stadium on February 16, 2025 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)Though he left Juventus in March of 2025, Thiago Motta remained on the club’s payroll for more than a year afterwards, before seeing his contract formally terminated at the start of June this year. This means that he is fully available and does not need to terminate any other outstanding agreements if he is to take on a new job in the near future.

posts.title: The greatest dynasties in Italian football
posts.excerpt: Much like other major sports, the history of professional football is littered with clubs that...
posts.content:
Much like other major sports, the history of professional football is littered with clubs that have enjoyed sustained periods of dominance.

That point undoubtedly applies to Italian football, with numerous clubs establishing dynasties that were difficult to topple.

Genoa and Pro Vercelli were powerhouses in the pre-Serie A years, but the landscape changed when Italy launched a unified national competition.

While the pitch has traditionally been the stage for these sporting legacies, the principles behind building a dominance-driven era are universally shared across modern competitive disciplines.

Looking at top Counter-Strike teams today, it becomes clear that sustained success is rarely built around individual talent alone. Modern esports dynasties rely on team chemistry, tactical discipline and strategic recruitment to maintain their grip at the high level, constantly adapting as the competitive landscape evolves.

Much like legendary football sides, the most formidable esports organisations depend on a shared tactical vision and a backroom infrastructure capable of adapting when the broader competitive environment shifts. Even as roster rotations, mounting pressure and rising challengers threaten to disrupt their momentum, the teams that preserve their core philosophy while integrating fresh talent are the ones that endure.

The same foundational elements allowed Italian giants such as Juventus, Inter Milan and AC Milan to forge their own historic eras, demonstrating that the mechanics of building a lasting dynasty transcend the boundary of the football pitch.

Read on as we look at some of the greatest dynasties in Italian football, starting with the club who set the early standards in Serie A.

Juventus (1930-35)

Juventus claimed five consecutive titles from 1930-35, laying down a tactical blueprint that was also utilised by the Italian national team.

Manager Carlo Carcano masterminded the tactics, physical discipline and structured style of play that subsequently became commonly associated with Italian teams.

The club was backed by the Agnelli family, who used the wealth they generated from their ownership of the automobile company Fiat to blow their rivals out of the water.

The core of the Juventus squad also formed the backbone of the Italian team which won the 1934 FIFA World Cup on home soil.

Torino (1942-49)

Torino won the Serie A title five times in the 1940s, but a tragic air crash towards the end of the decade stopped them in their tracks.

Their expansive style of play bore plenty of similarities to the ‘Total Football’ system made famous by the Netherlands during the 1970s.

However, the Superga air disaster in May 1949 killed the entire squad and shattered Torino’s hopes of maintaining their dominance in Italy.

By the time the European Cup was launched in 1955, Torino were struggling to stay afloat in Serie A. But for the plane crash, they could have dominated Europe.

Inter (1962-66)

Sandro Mazzola and Ferenc Puscas after the 1964 European Cup Final (inter.it)Inter’s decision to appoint Helenio Herrera as the manager in 1960 proved to be inspired, as the club went on to enjoy success at home and abroad.

They won the Serie A title in 1962/63, 1964/65 and 1965/66, utilising a ruthless counter-attacking style of play that earned widespread admiration.

Inter claimed the 1963/64 European Cup without losing a game, and they successfully defended the title the following season.

Herrera is widely regarded as one of the best managers of all-time, despite some critics accusing him of being overly defensive.

Milan (1987-95)

1 Apr 1995: Roberto Baggio (left) of Juventus takes on Franco Baresi (right) of AC Milan during a Serie A match at the San Siro Stadium in Milan, Italy. Juventus won the match 2-0. Mandatory Credit: Allsport UK /AllsportMilan were universally admired for their exploits at home and abroad during one of the most iconic periods in the history of Italian football.

Dutch trio Ruud Gullit, Marco van Basten and Frank Rijkaard added flair to the defensive foundations established by Italian stars Franco Baresi, Paolo Maldini and Alessandro Costacurta.

They won the Serie A title four times in seven seasons and never finished outside the top three in the three years they fell short.

Milan also won back-to-back European Cups in 1988/89 and 1989/90, then thrashed Barcelona’s ‘Dream Team’ in 1993/94 after defeat in the final the previous season.

Juventus (2011-20)

Paulo DybalaHaving regained their place in Serie A following a season in the second tier, Juventus were unable to break the stranglehold the two Milan clubs had on the title race.

After moving into their new stadium in 2011, the club signed 12 new players and appointed Antonio Conte as manager. They dominated Serie A for the rest of the decade.

They won an unprecedented nine consecutive Serie A titles, starting under Conte and continuing through Massimiliano Allegri and Maurizio Sarri.

Success eluded Juventus in the Champions League, with two appearances in the final resulting in defeats to Barcelona (2014/15) and Real Madrid (2016/17).

Source: https://football-italia.net/the-greatest-dynasties-in-italian-football/

posts.title: Pressure mounting on Allegri after Juventus defeat as three key issues arise
posts.excerpt: Pressure is beginning to mount on Napoli head coach Massimiliano Allegri after losing on his...
posts.content:
Pressure is beginning to mount on Napoli head coach Massimiliano Allegri after losing on his return to Juventus on Sunday evening, which has left the Partenopei with just 14 points after their first 10 league matches of the 2026-27 season.

Juventus defeat mounts pressure on Napoli and Allegri

Napoli were beaten 2-0 by Juventus at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday evening after well-taken goals from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga. This leaves Napoli with four wins, two draws and four defeats from their first 10 league games of the season, which is enough for an eight-place ranking as things stand.

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Jeremie Boga of Juventus celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with team mates during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)The Partenopei have also lost two of their first three matches in the Champions League this season, leaving Allegri with more defeats (six) than victories (five) across his first 13 competitive Napoli fixtures.

Three key issues are emerging in Allegri’s Napoli side, the most important of all being their lack of results. Whilst there has been the occasional sign of encouragement, such as a 3-0 victory over Frosinone and a 4-3 Champions League win over Bodo/Glimt, Napoli have failed to win any of their ‘big’ tests so far this season, losing against Como, Inter, Arsenal and Juventus while also being held at home against Roma.

There are also concerns regarding Napoli’s performance and their lack of identity under Allegri. Somewhat surprisingly, this Napoli side have occasionally shown signs of attacking quality, but have lacked defensive solidity, which is the opposite of what the head coach is best known for.

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Massimiliano Allegri, SSC Napoli head coach, reacts to his expulsion during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)And then there is the issue with the squad itself: Napoli had an incredibly quiet summer transfer window, and TMW suggests that this is a squad that looks like it is coming to the end of a cycle rather than one at the beginning of a new journey under a relatively recently appointed head coach.

If there is one encouraging precedent for Allegri to cling onto in these testing times at Napoli, it is that he has once started a Serie A season worse than in 2026-27, back in 2015-16, when he and his Juventus side had picked up just 12 points after 10 matches leaving them in 12th place, before going on to win the Scudetto by the end of the season.

That said, the current Napoli squad is not quite on the same level as the 2015-16 Juventus side, which was in the middle of winning nine consecutive league titles.

Source: https://football-italia.net/pressure-mounting-on-allegri-juventus-defeat/
