posts.title: Trump calls Iran conflict a 'soft war,' insists US holds the cards ahead of midterm elections
posts.excerpt: Trump called the Iran conflict a "soft war" on "Hannity" just hours after the United States struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
posts.content:
President Donald Trump sought to reassure voters the day before the midterm elections that Iran is not a "forever war," but a "soft war" that the United States could end at any time.

"We're not fighting a war … When was the last time we fired anything? This isn't a war, this is a very soft war," Trump said Monday on "Hannity."

Iran could be a key deciding issue as voters go to the polls on Election Day Tuesday as Americans continue to grapple with surging gas prices and the economic fallout from the United States’ conflict, which began eight months ago.

AMERICANS 'FRUSTRATED' ABOUT IRAN WAR GOING INTO MIDTERMS AS TRUMP ADMIN HAS DECISION TO MAKE: GOP LAWMAKER

"What’s a war? A war is fighting. Take a look at World War I, World War II. When was the last time you saw us fighting with them? We go months and months, we talk," Trump told host Sean Hannity.

"This is not much of a war, Sean, because there hasn't been shooting for months."

TRUMP ADMIN THREATENS IRAN WITH 'CONSEQUENCES' AS ALLIES CONVENE AMID THREATS OF POST-ELECTION ESCALATION

Trump’s comments come shortly after the United States struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz Monday after Iran fired at a U.S. aircraft. Officials confirmed to Fox News that the "defensive" strike does not indicate a return to full-blown U.S. military strikes in Iran.

The president said Monday that he was in no hurry to resume military strikes against Iran but warned that the U.S. will give Iran "the hammer" soon if the latest round of peace talks are not fruitful.

TRUMP WARNS IRAN WILL BE HIT 'REALLY HARD' IF NUCLEAR NEGOTIATIONS COLLAPSE AGAIN

"With [Operation] Midnight Hammer, we bombed out all of their potential nuclear power. Now we have might have to go after Pickaxe [Mountain], but that's not a big deal. We can do it in literally one hour," Trump told Fox News.

"This isn't like a war that's going on, there’s no war raging," he added. "It could happen if they don't make a deal. But they want to make a deal very badly, and there is a very good chance we make a deal."

FOX NEWS POLL: 71% THINK TRUMP ADMINISTRATION LACKS PLAN TO END IRAN WAR

The financial toll of the Iran conflict has emerged as a political liability for Republicans ahead of Election Day as the Pentagon estimates the war has cost taxpayers more than $47 billion.

President Trump, however, dismissed criticism of the staggering price tag, describing the expense as "peanuts" and saying that the war was necessary to disarm Iran from building a nuclear weapon.

TRUMP SAYS IRAN IS ‘DEAD’ — EXPERTS POINT TO THE REAL SIGN TEHRAN IS NEARING THE BRINK

"Their military is gone, their navy is gone, their air force is gone, their anti-aircraft is gone, and they have some missiles, but they don't have many of them – very little capacity to build more. They have drones, but they don't have very many, they have very little capacity to build more," he said.

"What we’ve done is amazing," the president continued.

Trump said the U.S. is dealing from a position of "total strength" and that the conflict can be ended "at any time."

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/media/trump-calls-iran-conflict-soft-war-insists-us-holds-cards-ahead-midterm-elections

posts.title: Child’s measles death marks New York state’s first in more than 30 years amid outbreak
posts.excerpt: A child in Lewis County marks New York's first measles-associated death in over 30 years as Gov. Kathy Hochul urges people to get their vaccinations.
posts.content:
A child in New York state's Lewis County died in the first known measles-associated death in the state in more than 30 years amid an ongoing measles outbreak, officials announced on Monday.

Gov. Kathy Hochul said she was "heartbroken" to learn of the child's death.

"As a mother and grandmother, I cannot imagine what this family is going through. My heart goes out to everyone who knew and loved this child," Hochul said in a statement.

"Measles is highly contagious, and vaccination remains our best protection against this dangerous disease. This is New York’s first measles-related death in 30 years, a devastating reminder of what’s at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses," she added. "In New York, we will continue to stand by proven public health measures and do everything we can to keep New Yorkers safe and healthy."

DEADLY MEASLES OUTBREAK HITS NORTHEAST AS STATE RECORDS FIRST DEATHS IN 35 YEARS

The Trump administration has made changes to federal vaccine policy, including revising the childhood immunization schedule and reviewing how vaccines are recommended. The CDC, however, continues to recommend two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine for children and says two doses provide the best protection against measles.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services for a response to Hochul's comments.

The child's death comes four weeks after Hochul declared a State Disaster Emergency in response to the measles outbreak across areas of New York and neighboring states, expanding the pool of eligible people who can administer measles vaccines and providing quick access to additional resources if needed.

The governor said last month she planned to seek federal assistance to combat the outbreak.

TRUMP SURGEON GENERAL PICK BACKS MMR VACCINE, REJECTS LINK BETWEEN CHILDHOOD VACCINES AND AUTISM

The New York State Department of Health said it is working with county health departments and local partners to provide the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine to any unvaccinated people who request it and to closely monitor and investigate all reported cases.

As of Oct. 24, New York had recorded 178 measles cases this year — 170 outside New York City and eight in the city.

State health officials urged New Yorkers to protect themselves by making sure they are up-to-date on their measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccines and be aware of health advisories if traveling with unvaccinated people, especially young children.

"We are deeply saddened by the death of a child in Lewis County associated with the ongoing measles outbreak. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the child's family and loved ones and ask that their privacy be respected during this difficult time," the New York State Department of Health said in a statement.

The department said measles is a highly contagious disease that can cause serious complications and death, stressing that vaccination is the "best protection against measles."

"The Department has offered resources to Lewis County to assist with community outreach and support local vaccination efforts – both in response to this case, and as part of our ongoing efforts to support counties that are facing this ongoing measles outbreak," the department's statement reads. "We urge New Yorkers to ensure they are up-to-date on measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccinations and speak to their healthcare provider about immunizations."

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/health/childs-measles-death-marks-new-york-states-first-more-than-30-years-amid-outbreak

posts.title: Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN
posts.excerpt: Currency held outside the banking system by Nigerians rose by 103.8 per cent to N4.923 trillion in September 2026 from N2.416 trillion in September 2023 The post Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3
posts.content:
•Demand deposits climb 71% •Analysts highlight cash dependence, financial inclusion challenges

By Peter Egwuatu

Currency held outside the banking system by Nigerians rose by 103.8 per cent to N4.923 trillion in September 2026 from N2.416 trillion in September 2023, highlighting the persistent demand for physical cash despite the expansion of electronic payment channels in the country.

Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics, also showed that currency outside banks increased by 10.3 per cent year-on-year from N4.465 trillion in September 2025 to N4.923 trillion in September 2026.

The figures indicate that cash held outside the banking system has more than doubled in three years, reflecting the scale of currency demand within the economy and the challenges facing efforts to deepen the use of formal banking and electronic payment systems.

A breakdown of the data showed that currency outside banks increased by 66.2 per cent from N2.416 trillion in September 2023 to N4.016 trillion in September 2024.

The figure subsequently rose to N4.465 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 11.2 per cent from the corresponding period in 2024, before climbing further to N4.923 trillion in September 2026.

According to analysts, the latest increase indicates that the preference for cash transactions remains significant, notwithstanding the growing adoption of mobile banking, electronic transfers, point-of-sale terminals and other digital payment platforms.

Demand deposits rise 71%

Meanwhile, demand deposits in the banking system increased by 70.8 per cent to N39.124 trillion in September 2026 from N22.903 trillion in September 2023.

The CBN data showed that demand deposits rose to N31.842 trillion in September 2024, representing an increase of 39.0 per cent against the corresponding period in 2023.

The figure climbed further to N34.642 trillion in September 2025, an increase of 8.8 per cent year-on-year, before rising to N39.124 trillion in September 2026, representing a 12.9 per cent increase over September 2025.

The growth in demand deposits indicates an expansion in funds held in bank accounts that are generally accessible for payments and withdrawals on demand.

Reacting to this data, Clifford Egbomeade, Economic and Communications expert, said: “The simultaneous increase in demand deposits and currency outside banks points to the coexistence of formal banking balances and substantial demand for physical cash in Nigeria’s payment system.

‘‘However, the two indicators measure different components of monetary activity. Demand deposits represent bank-account balances, while currency outside banks represents cash held outside the banking system.

‘‘Their growth rates alone do not establish how much of the increase in cash holdings is attributable to economic growth, inflation, informal transactions or changes in payment preferences.”

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/currency-outside-banks-rises-104-in-3-yrs-cbn/

posts.title: Women in Politics: Nigeria’s political structure not built for women — Adeola Azeez
posts.excerpt: Adeola Azeez is daughter of late Afenifere leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo and one of the Founders of Women in Management, Business & Public Service, WIMBIZ The post Women in Politics: Nigeria’s political str
posts.content:
By Ebunoluwa Sessou

As Nigeria prepares for another general election in 2027, the question of women’s participation in politics and access to elective offices remains a subject for debate.

Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters

Adeola Azeez, a daughter of the late Afenifere leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo and one of the Founders of Women in Management, Business & Public Service, WIMBIZ, a founding member of Women in Politics (WIMPol) and a former Deputy Country Representative, Nigeria, of Deutsch e-Bank; was recently declared winner at the Ijebu Central Federal Consistency primary election on the platform of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Ogun State.

In this interview, she speaks on her experience contesting for the House of Representatives, the challenges of securing a party ticket, the influence of party structures on women’s political ambitions and her determination to contest again in 2027.

She also discusses the need for women who have secured elective positions to support aspiring female politicians and explains why she believes women must remain committed to political participation despite the barriers they face.

Excerpts:

You transitioned from the corporate world to politics after your retirement in 2020. What informed that decision?

I have always believed in the importance of women’s participation in leadership. By the time I retired in 2020, I had prepared myself for a career in politics. From 2013, I knew that politics was something I wanted to pursue, so I began preparing for it.

I eventually contested for the House of Representatives in 2023 to represent Ogbomoso Central Federal Constituency. I approached the contest with the same seriousness, preparation and determination as any other candidate.

What were the major challenges you encountered as a woman contesting for political office?

The challenges women face in politics are well known. They include political violence, limited access to funding and other barriers.

Interestingly, funding was not a major challenge for me because of my corporate experience and the relationships I had built over the years. Having supported, mentored and nurtured women in business, I had established a strong network of sponsors and supporters. My reputation also helped me attract people who believed in my ambition.

However, the major challenge was the political structure itself. Nigeria’s political system is not structured to accommodate women adequately.

Despite your corporate experience, network and supporters, you did not secure your party’s ticket in 2023. What went wrong?

I believe the challenge was the party structure and the people who control access to political opportunities.

I had expected that my pedigree, experience and contributions to society would count for something. I did my research, reached out to my constituency and carried out the necessary groundwork.

I wanted to become a symbol of a new chapter for women in Nigerian politics. I believed that if more women with experience, credibility and the capacity to lead could successfully navigate the political system, it would encourage others to participate.

Unfortunately, I did not secure the ticket.

You have said that funding was not a major problem for you. Did you face pressure to engage in money politics?

I was determined not to engage in money politics or buy votes. I believed doing so would compromise my principles and disappoint the people who had supported me, including my family.

I wanted to run a campaign based on my record, ideas, engagement with the people and the support I had earned.

Although I had supporters and people who believed in my ambition, that was not enough to overcome the challenges within the party structure.

There was also the question of whether I would play politics in the same way as others. I believe women should be able to participate in politics without being expected to compromise their values to gain acceptance.

Do you think the political system discriminates against women who refuse to play by the established rules?

The political structure presents significant challenges for women. My experience made me realise that having the qualifications, resources, networks and willingness to serve does not automatically translate into securing a party ticket.

Women must navigate party structures and the interests of those who control them. This is one of the reasons we must continue to examine the barriers preventing women from participating fully in politics.

We need a system that recognises competence and allows women to compete meaningfully for elective positions.

What lessons did you learn from your 2023 electoral experience?

I learnt that political participation requires persistence. I did not give up after 2023 and I remained committed to my constituency.

Although I did not secure the ticket, the experience gave me visibility. People in my constituency came to know me, my ambition and the kind of campaign I ran.

I believe political participation should not begin and end with winning an election. There is a responsibility to continue contributing to the development of the people, regardless of whether one occupies political office or not.

What are your plans for the 2027 general election?

I am preparing to contest again in 2027, this time on a different party platform.

My experience in 2023 has strengthened my resolve. The people in my constituency know me, and I believe my previous campaign helped establish a relationship with them.

I am determined to continue and look forward to the next election.

Beyond your political ambition, what have you done to improve the lives of people in your constituency?

I have continued to support initiatives that respond to the needs of the people.

This year, I facilitated the establishment of a technology hub and supported a back-to-school initiative. These projects were funded with the support of my partners.

For me, leadership is about impact. Even when you are not holding an elected office, you can still contribute to the development of your community.

I want people to understand that political aspirations should not prevent anyone from serving. We must continue to identify needs and provide support where possible.

Some women who have secured elective offices are criticised for not doing enough to support other aspiring female politicians. Do you share this concern?

There is still a lot of work to be done. We have women who are interested in politics, women who are preparing themselves and women who have the capacity to lead. The challenge is creating an environment where they can participate meaningfully.

One concern is that some women who eventually get elected may not use their positions and influence to create opportunities for other women.

When women get into the Senate or the House of Representatives, they should remember the challenges they faced on their way to those positions.

They should use their influence to support other women who are trying to enter the political space. Women’s political representation should not be about individual achievement alone but creating a pathway for others.

What practical steps should political parties take to improve women’s representation?

We must move beyond simply encouraging women to participate, we must address the structural barriers that prevent them from securing party tickets and winning elections.

Women need support, access to political opportunities and a system that recognises their capacity to lead.

We must also build stronger networks of women who are willing to support one another. Those who have the resources, experience and influence should help aspiring female politicians navigate the political process.

There are women who are prepared to serve, but we must create an environment where their preparation and capacity can translate into meaningful political participation.

What is your message to women who are discouraged by the challenges of Nigerian politics?

Women must not give up. We are trying, and we are rebuilding. There is a growing pool of women who are interested in politics and willing to contribute to national development.

However, the fact that many women are trying but are not making significant progress in representation shows that there is still much work to do.

We must continue to organise, support one another, build networks and challenge the barriers within the political system.

I remain committed to that cause, and I believe women must keep pushing for their place in leadership.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/women-in-politics-nigerias-political-structure-not-built-for-women-adeola-azeez/

posts.title: 2027: Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse — Mutfwang
posts.excerpt: He also declared there was no vacancy in the Presidential Villa (Aso Rock) and Plateau Government House in 2027, equally dismissing any talks of rainbow coalition. The post 2027: Tinubu inherited Nige
posts.content:
•Declares no vacancy in Aso Rock, Plateau Govt House •Says no rainbow coalition, Plateau going APC

By Golok Nanmwa

JOS — Plateau State governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Tinubu inherited an economy that was tottering on the brink of collapse from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023.

Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters

He also declared there was no vacancy in the Presidential Villa (Aso Rock) and Plateau Government House in 2027, equally dismissing any talks of rainbow coalition.

Mutfwang, who stated this during the formal inauguration of All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council in Jos yesterday, also defended Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election.

“Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria tottering on the brink of collapse; Nigeria that could not service its external debts; Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home. And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria because they could not get the dollars to take back their money.

“Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades. Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” the governor said.

He alleged further that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming more than N30 trillion was printed.

Governor Mutfwang said: “When the President took over in 2023, the government he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank.

“They printed over N30 trillion which went down the drain. Today, by the grace of God, Central Bank has stabilised and that deficit has been done away with.’’

On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents.

“I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. They never brought any wealth. They brought fictitious documents, claimed monies and subsidies.

“You cannot continue to borrow money to give to thieves. You have to stop it at some point. And when it is stopped, there will be a payback; there will be a recovery time,” he said.

The governor said the availability of fuel had improved, despite the increase in its cost, recalling the long queues that previously characterised fuel stations across the country.

“Today, by the grace of God, we have solved one side of the equation. Today, fuel is available. It may not be cheap but it is available.

“Those of us who are of my age bracket or little below will remember the times we spent days in petrol stations queuing for fuel that we could hardly get. But we have been able to resolve that,” Mutfwang said.

He also claimed that the previous administration had sold crude oil in advance, saying the country was now servicing obligations arising from such arrangements.

“Part of the problem of the Buhari regime is that they got to a point that they didn’t know what to do, so they sold our future crude. The crude we are yet to dig from the ground has been sold in advance. And today, we are paying that debt. And so we cannot expect things to simply change overnight,” he said.

The governor said his administration was taking steps to cushion the effects of the economic adjustment on Plateau residents, citing the introduction of metro buses and revival of the railway system within Jos metropolis.

“I’m glad that Plateau people have commended us for the metro buses we bought early in the regime. I’m glad we’re able to revive the railway system within the metropolis. I’m glad that we’re able to reduce school fees for our students in tertiary institutions by 50 per cent. I’m glad that we’re able to raise their allowances by about 300 per cent,” he said.

He also commended the federal government’s student financing initiatives, saying Plateau indigenes studying in universities had benefited from the scheme.

“It is also a great joy in my heart that the President also came up with a new scholarship for students called NELFUND. Today, hundreds of millions have been given to Plateau indigenes who are studying in different universities. Some are getting N20,000 monthly, N40,000 monthly. It has never happened before,” he said.

On the 2027 elections, Mutfwang called for power rotation between the North and South, saying political arrangements should be respected.

“We must agree that power should rotate between the North and the South. And if the North spends eight years, which we have nothing to show for, it is only fair that we allow the South to do eight years because if we don’t respect that sharing arrangement, it will come back to haunt us someday,” he said.

Mutfwang also declared that there was no vacancy in Plateau State Government House, ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

“That is why in Plateau State, we have already agreed that it is two terms per senatorial zone. Except the northern zone does not want to produce a governor until 2035, then you can toy with my mandate,” he said.

Governor Mutfwang urged APC candidates and campaign council members to communicate the achievements of the administration to the electorate and avoid actions capable of deepening divisions.

“We must, therefore, go about this campaign with facts, with honesty, with seriousness. Part of the reason people are still apprehensive is because we have not communicated the real message, and we have a responsibility to ensure that that message is properly communicated.

“I’d like to urge all our candidates for the various positions, you must lead from the front. You must be bridge-builders.”

“I am confident that come January 16, 2027, by the grace of God, Plateau State will return President Bola Ahmed Tinubu with a resounding victory. And two weeks later, the people of Plateau will renew their mandate for us to continue on the good journey we have started,” he said.

On security, Mutfwang acknowledged the persistence of insecurity, adding that his administration was taking steps to strengthen security and facilitate the return of displaced persons to their communities.

“On security, I know our opponents will say there is hunger in the land. We don’t deny it. They will say that the insecurity situation has not abated. We don’t deny it. But if they say we have not taken steps at all to address those issues, they know they are lying.

“Insecurity is not like tap water, where you simply turn on the tap and it flows down. It requires concerted, deliberate, intentional, sustained efforts before you get results.

“By the grace of God, we have understood what the issues are, and we have begun to make sure we propose solutions in the right places that matter,” he said.

The governor said his administration would continue to protect communities and disclosed plans to deploy additional security personnel.

“One thing I have committed myself to is that I will ensure the protection of every inch of land in Plateau State.

“Very soon, we are going to be taking practical steps to facilitate the return of internally displaced persons back to their communities. And so, all we are asking is for Plateau people to trust us, be patient with us, and by the grace of God, you will not regret it.”

No rainbow coalition, Plateau going APC

The governor dismissed talks of any “rainbow coalition” ahead of the 2027 elections , declaring that there was no vacancy in Aso Rock and the Plateau Government House as he inaugurated the presidential and state campaign councils of the All Progressives Congress, APC.

Mutfwang said Plateau people had chosen the APC as their political vehicle for the 2027 elections, urging party faithful and campaign officials to mobilise across the state.

“Some people are talking about rainbow, we are talking about a unification movement. Plateau people have decided 2027 to go one direction. And we have chosen that the wings on which we have chosen to fly in 2027 are the wings of the APC,” the governor declared

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027-tinubu-inherited-nigeria-on-brink-of-collapse-mutfwang/

posts.title: Give Tinubu, Otu another term for Bakassi seaport, coastal highway — Shettima
posts.excerpt: Vice President Shettima has assured Cross River that Bakassi Deep Seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway will be delivered, urging them to re-elect President Tinubu and Governor Otu The post Give T
posts.content:
By Ike Uchechukwu

CALABAR — Vice President Kashim Shettima has assured Cross River residents that the proposed Bakassi Deep Seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway will be delivered, urging them to re-elect President Bola Tinubu and Governor Bassey Otu in 2027.

Shettima gave the assurance yesterday while representing Tinubu at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the U.J. Esuene Stadium, Calabar.

He thanked the people of Cross River for supporting the administration over the past three years, describing the relationship between the government and the electorate as “an alliance of prosperity, an alliance of opportunity.”

“Over the past three years, you have shown us support, and you have resisted the lies and propaganda intended to misrepresent us,” he said.

The Vice President urged voters to renew the mandates of Tinubu, Otu and APC candidates seeking election into the National Assembly and the state House of Assembly.

He said the party was seeking another mandate based on its stewardship, stressing that elected officials must account to the people who entrusted them with power.

On infrastructure, Shettima said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway would link coastal communities, ease the movement of goods and people, boost tourism and attract investment to the region.

He added that the project would create thousands of direct and indirect jobs, while opening up economic opportunities for communities along the corridor.

On the Bakassi Deep Seaport, the Vice President said the project had received Federal Government approval, expressing optimism that it would become an international maritime gateway upon completion.

“When completed, it will become an international maritime gateway. It will attract shipping companies. It will generate employment,” he said.

Shettima said the seaport and coastal highway were central to efforts to position Cross River as a major beneficiary of Nigeria’s maritime economy.

On education, he said the government’s student financing initiative would promote human capital development, reduce the financial burden on parents and expand access to higher education.

He added that the intervention was intended to ensure that financial constraints did not prevent children from pursuing their education

posts.content:
By Yinka Kolawole

The Federal Government has fully disbursed the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion has been disbursed to 15,018 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to boost domestic production, expand businesses and create jobs.

Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole, disclosed this in an address on “Harnessing Nigeria’s Economic Potential for Greater Prosperity”.

Oduwole said the interventions were part of the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen local industries, improve productive capacity and drive sustainable economic growth.

The disbursements were made under the Federal Government’s N200 billion intervention package, managed by the Bank of Industry (BoI), to support businesses, boost domestic production and create jobs.

The package comprises the N50 billion Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme for nano businesses, the N75 billion FGN MSME Intervention Fund for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and the N75 billion FGN Manufacturing Sector Fund for manufacturing businesses.

Oduwole noted that the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund had been fully disbursed to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion had been disbursed to 15,018 businesses under the MSME Intervention Fund as of the first quarter of 2026.

She, however, stressed that the impact of government funding should be measured by stronger businesses, increased production and improved livelihoods rather than the amount disbursed alone.

The minister acknowledged that access to finance remained a major challenge for manufacturers seeking to acquire equipment, purchase raw materials, expand production capacity and create employment.

She said Nigeria’s economic transformation required fiscal discipline, monetary stability and policies that supported domestic production and competitiveness.

According to her, the government is working to remove barriers to investment, production and trade while creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive.

Highlighting developments in the manufacturing sector, Oduwole said cement manufacturing grew by 11.53 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, while motor vehicle assembly expanded by 5.44 per cent during the period. She added that vehicle assembly grew by 40.6 per cent in 2025, while cassava starch production recorded growth of 474.74 per cent.

“Processing locally grown cassava into industrial starch will support manufacturers, while vehicle assembly will create opportunities for engineers, technicians and supply-chain businesses,” she said.

The minister also highlighted opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), noting that intra-African trade had grown by 21 per cent.

posts.title: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters
posts.excerpt: The findings raise questions about whether the increasing number of registered voters will translate into participation in the 2027 elections The post Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to vote
posts.content:
*Taraba, Plateau, Jigawa, Bayelsa, Benue among states with thousands of cards awaiting collection *Sokoto, Nasarawa, Zamfara, Yobe record significant increase in voter population *Kano yet to compile collection figures; Borno, Bauchi, Kebbi withholding data *Lagos, Ondo, Ogun, Ekiti, Osun, Kaduna, Adamawa report growing voter numbers *INEC intensifies mobilisation ahead of January 16 presidential election

By Soni Daniel

ABUJA — Three weeks after the collection of Permanent Voters Cards, PVCs started across the country, the failure of no fewer than 14 million eligible voters to collect their PVCs, is emerging as a major concern for the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC.

Read Also: Critics of Rainbow Coalition can’t unite their families – Wike

Investigations by Vanguard across several states show that while the Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise attracted millions of new registrants, a significant number of produced PVCs remain uncollected, potentially denying their owners the opportunity to participate in next year’s elections.

Vanguard’s checks showed that 6.26 million PVCs were not collected before the 2023 general elections. In the last Continuous Voters Registration, CVR, exercise, the electoral commission registered 10,772,421 new voters. At press time, many states are yet to release their tallies of uncollected voter’s cards estimated at over 14 million.

The situation is particularly worrying in states like Plateau, Taraba, Jigawa, Benue and Bayelsa, where INEC has disclosed substantial numbers of cards awaiting collection.

In Plateau, about 95,000 PVCs from previous registration exercises remain unclaimed. Taraba has 29,314 outstanding cards, while Jigawa has 33,079 cards ready for collection. Bayelsa, on its part, has 52,225 PVCs from the first phase of the recent registration exercise awaiting collection.

Benue has also recorded considerable activity, with 58,581 PVCs collected during the recent display of the voters’ register, although thousands of additional cards are still being processed or await collection.

Beyond the collection challenge, voter registration figures indicate growing electoral participation across the country, with Sokoto, Zamfara, Nasarawa, Benue, Ogun, Kano and other states recording significant additions to their voter registers.

However, the picture is incomplete in some states. While Kano is yet to compile its PVC collection figures across its 44 local government areas, INEC officials in Borno, Bauchi and Kebbi declined to provide updates, describing the requested information as sensitive.

In the South-West, Lagos says its final register will not be available until December 15, after conclusion of the claims and objections exercise. Ondo, Ogun, Ekiti and Osun have reported increases in registered voters, although some are still compiling their PVC collection figures.

The findings raise questions about whether the increasing number of registered voters will translate into participation in the 2027 elections, beginning with the presidential and National Assembly polls on January 16.

Taraba: 29,314 PVCs uncollected

In Taraba State, the number of registered voters stands at 2,254,380, according to INEC.

However, no fewer than 29,314 PVCs remain uncollected across the commission’s offices in the state.

The Resident Electoral Commissioner, REC, Dr Sa’ad Umar Idris, said the outstanding cards comprise 13,826 legacy PVCs from previous electoral cycles between 2011 and 2023 and 15,488 cards processed during the latest registration exercise.

He explained that the commission processed 31,676 cards arising from new registrations, voter transfers and replacements during the 2025–2026 exercise. Of these, only 16,188, representing about 51 per cent, had been collected.

Expressing concern over the low collection rate, Idris appealed to political parties, traditional rulers, religious leaders and civil society organisations to mobilise residents to visit INEC local government offices and collect their cards.

Plateau: 121,821 new voters, 95,000 PVCs uncollected

In Plateau State, INEC recorded 121,821 new voters during the latest CVR exercise, while about 95,000 PVCs from previous registration exercises remain uncollected.

The REC, Prof. Samuel Egwu, disclosed this during a meeting with political party leaders and other stakeholders in Jos.

He said women accounted for 65,928 of new registrants, while men represented 55,893.

The commission also received 38,399 requests for voter transfers within and outside the state.

Egwu said the outstanding PVCs remained a major concern as INEC intensified preparations for the 2027 elections.

Jigawa: 33,079 PVCs ready for collection

Jigawa State has 2,351,298 registered voters, according to the REC, Prof. Muhammad Bashar.

Bashar said 33,079 PVCs are ready for collection by people who registered for transfers, corrections and replacements between August and December 2025.

He also disclosed that the state recorded 515,878 new voters during the three phases of the recent CVR exercise.

Jigawa has 27 local government areas, 287 registration areas and 4,522 polling units.

Zamfara adds 313,115 voters

In Zamfara State, INEC recorded 313,115 new voters under the CVR exercise as of August 2026.

The REC, Dr. Mahmud Isa, disclosed this to Vanguard in Gusau, explaining that the new registrants are additional to the 1,952,060 registered voters recorded in the state for the 2023 general elections.

Kaduna: 61,494 PVCs collected

In Kaduna State, 61,494 PVCs had been collected as of October 28, according to figures obtained from INEC.

An official of the commission, Hajiya Rukaiyatu, said the figure comprised 12,741 old PVCs and 48,753 newly-issued cards.

Women collected 32,589 cards, comprising 6,782 old and 25,807 new PVCs, while men collected 28,905, comprising 5,959 old and 22,946 new cards.

The figures indicate a higher collection rate among female voters.

Nasarawa: Voter population hits 2.1m

Nasarawa State’s registered voter population has risen to approximately 2.1 million, following registration of 247,000 new voters between 2025 and July 2026.

The REC, Mallam Mohammed Abullahi Sadiq, disclosed this, commending residents for their response to the registration exercise.

He urged those yet to collect their PVCs to visit INEC offices in their respective local government areas.

Sokoto: 2.63m registered voters

Sokoto State has recorded 2,633,113 registered voters, including 461,057 captured during the latest CVR exercise.

The commission’s Public Relations Officer, Hassan Kaoje, said the figure represented 2.55 per cent of the national voter register.

He said INEC was intensifying efforts to ensure that all eligible registrants collected their PVCs before the 2027 elections.

Kaoje urged those who had completed registration but were yet to collect their cards to visit designated INEC offices and collection centres.

Adamawa: 2.43m million registered voters

Adamawa State has 2,431,146 registered voters as of July 2026.

INEC’s Head of Voter Education and Information in the state, Alhaji Aliyu Shaba Lafiagi, disclosed that 49,304 PVCs had been collected as of October 23.

He also reported that 11,725 voters’ cards had been transferred into the state, comprising 6,255 belonging to men and 5,520 belonging to women.

Borno, Bauchi, Kebbi withhold figures

In Borno State, INEC declined to provide the latest figures on registered voters and PVC collection, describing the information as sensitive.

Officials said the commission is yet to ascertain the actual number of newly-registered voters and PVCs collected because the exercise is ongoing.

However, the 2023 register put the state’s voter population at 2,564,197.

A similar situation played out in Bauchi, where INEC officials declined to release requested figures, insisting that the information is not for public consumption.

Efforts to obtain updated figures from Kebbi also proved unsuccessful.

Benue: 3.05m registered voters, 279,498 new registrants

Benue State has 3,057,225 registered voters, including 279,498 new registrants across its 23 local government areas.

The REC, Mallam Aminu Idris, said INEC received 101,695 PVCs from its headquarters for the first phase of the CVR and voter transfers.

The consignment comprised 54,724 new PVCs and 46,971 transferred cards.

During the display of the voters’ register between October 9 and 15, 2026, at registration area level, 58,581 PVCs were collected.

The breakdown showed that 9,139 were old cards previously held in storage, 28,854 were new CVR cards, 12,707 were transferred cards and 7,881 were replacement cards.

Idris said all existing PVCs remained available for collection at INEC offices in the state’s 23 local government areas.

He added that the commission would announce the availability of cards processed during the second and third phases of the CVR exercise after receiving official notification from its headquarters.

Kano yet to compile PVC collection figures

Despite having one of the country’s largest voter populations, Kano State is yet to determine the total number of PVCs collected across its 44 local government areas.

INEC’s Public Relations Officer, Nahila Bello Dandago, said the commission was still compiling the figures because the collection exercise was ongoing.

She disclosed that Kano had 6,570,276 registered voters, making it the state with the second-highest voter population after Lagos, which has 7,488,633.

Yobe: 283,525 new voters

In Yobe State, the voter population has increased from 1,485,146 in 2022 to 1,768,671 in 2026, representing an addition of 283,525 voters.

In Damaturu Local Government Area, 11,911 PVCs had been collected, leaving 9,137 unclaimed.

The Electoral Officer for Damaturu, Ahmed A. Waziri, said INEC had 21,048 cards available for collection, comprising 8,100 outstanding cards from the 2023 exercise and 12,948 received during the first phase of the latest distribution.

He said Damaturu was yet to receive cards under the second and third phases of the distribution exercise.

Waziri added that the commission’s ICT department was better positioned to provide comprehensive figures for the state’s 17 local government areas.

Lagos: Final register expected December 15

In Lagos State, INEC said the final Register of Voters would not be available until the conclusion of the claims and objections exercise on December 15, 2026.

The commission’s Public Affairs Officer, Tope Adenuga, said the final figures for newly registered voters could not be provided until the exercise was completed.

He said: “The final Register of Voters requested will be made available until after the conclusion of the ongoing claims and objections exercise.”

According to him, the final list is expected to be ready on December 15.

The state recorded 7,488,633 registered voters in the figures available to Vanguard.

INEC was yet to provide the latest PVC collection statistics.

Ondo: 2.05m registered voters

In Ondo State, the total number of registered voters stands at 2,053,061, with 76,285 new registrants.

The Head of Voter Education and Publicity, Olayinka Ogunseye, disclosed that 1,771,326 PVCs had been collected.

He, however, cautioned that the figures were preliminary and not final.

Ekiti: Voter population rises to 1.05 million

Ekiti State’s registered voter population has increased to 1,055,708, according to INEC.

The figure represents an increase of 68,061 over the 987,647 registered voters recorded during the 2023 general elections.

The commission could not immediately provide the latest PVC collection figures because the exercise was ongoing.

Ogun: 348,703 additional voters

Ogun State has recorded an increase of 348,703 registered voters, bringing its voter population to 3,037,008 as of October 2026.

The figure represents an increase from the 2,688,305 registered voters recorded for the 2023 general elections.

INEC officials said PVC distribution was still ongoing at the commission’s local government offices.

Osun: 2.33m registered voters

In Osun State, the total number of registered voters stands at 2,339,233.

The INEC Public Relations Officer, Musa Olurode, said the figure was the same as that used for the August 2026 governorship election because no fresh CVR exercise was conducted after the poll.

He disclosed that 1,906,390 PVCs had been collected as of August, adding that the figure would be updated after the ongoing collection exercise.

He said: “As at today, the total voters register in Osun State is 2,339,233. This is the figure for the governorship election and it cannot change because the Continuous Voters Registration did not take place in the state after the August poll.”

He added that the number of collected PVCs would change as more registered voters collected their cards.

Delta: INEC declines to release PVC figures

In Delta State, INEC officials declined to provide statistics on PVC collection, directing enquiries to the ICT department.

The Head of Voter Education, Nse Abasi Udom, said the ICT unit was responsible for monitoring and keeping the relevant records.

However, she declined to provide the contact details of the department’s head, saying officials were in an important meeting.

A similar experience occurred during a previous visit to a PVC collection centre at Uzor Igwe Primary School, Nnebisi Road, Asaba, where an INEC official declined to disclose the number of cards available or collected.

The official, however, acknowledged an impressive turnout of residents.

“What I can tell you, which you can verify from the atmosphere here, is that the turnout is impressive. People are coming and collecting,” the official said.

The commission’s inability to provide the figures has made it difficult to establish the number of PVCs still awaiting collection across the state.

Bayelsa: 52,225 PVCs await collection

In Bayelsa State, INEC has put the total number of registered voters at 1,200,691, with 52,225 PVCs from the first phase of the recent CVR exercise awaiting collection.

Ekeremor and Sagbama local government areas recorded the highest numbers of registered voters, with 12,023 and 10,080 respectively.

Ogbia recorded the lowest figure of 3,132, followed by Nembe with 3,620 and Kolokuma/Opokuma with 3,712.

INEC said collection commenced at registration area level on October 9 and ended on October 15, after which the exercise was moved to the commission’s offices across the state’s eight local government areas.

The commission urged eligible registrants who missed the ward-level distribution to visit the respective local government offices to collect their cards.

With thousands of PVCs still awaiting collection in several states, the findings underscore the challenge facing INEC as it prepares for the 2027 general elections.

While the increasing number of registered voters points to growing interest in the electoral process, the commission’s ability to translate registration into actual voter participation will depend significantly on the success of its PVC collection and mobilisation campaigns.

Clifford Ndujihe, Dayo Johnson, Umar Yusuf, Ndahi Marama, Femi Bolaji, Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo, Peter Duru, Hadiza Yusuf, Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Musa Ubandawaki, Idris Salisu, Edwin Philip, Golok Nanmwa, Muhammad Inuwa, Christopher Ameh, Egufe Yafugborhi, Rotimi Ojomoyela, Olayinka Ajayi, Shina Abubakar, Emem Idio & James Ogunnaike contributed to this report.

posts.title: Christian Yelich says 'Brewer Ball' is hard to replicate for this season after World Series triumph
posts.excerpt: Milwaukee Brewers star Christian Yelich says team togetherness fueled their World Series run, from sweeping the Dodgers to beating Tampa Bay.
posts.content:
The Milwaukee Brewers’ celebration continues, and it likely won’t be stopping for quite a while.

After all, the organization and its fan base have never celebrated a World Series title, and the entire state, let alone the city itself, is still on cloud nine after the five-game victory over the Tampa Bay Rays.

Christian Yelich has been waiting for this moment since he landed in Milwaukee in 2018, and since that last out was made at Tropicana Field, he understood immediately how much it means to the loyal fan base as well as his teammates.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"It’s been awesome," Yelich told OutKick just before celebrating once more with Brewers fans at Raising Cane’s for a victory "shift" in Greendale, Wisconsin. "We’ve been busy kinda bouncing around everywhere. Not a whole lot of sleep, but I think that’s kinda how it should be. Still taking it all in and celebrating with everybody still. It’s been an awesome couple days."

But, while the Brewers relish their first-ever title, all 29 other MLB teams might be trying to rethink how to play the game itself after "Brewer Ball" took over this season.

Milwaukee’s style of play, which emphasizes fundamentals and situational baseball — think compared to the launch angle, raw power mindset others have adopted in today’s game — earned the moniker whilst winning 103 regular-season games. Then, they made a postseason run that shocked some, especially after sweeping the back-to-back-champion Los Angeles Dodgers and almost doing the same to the Rays in the World Series before a Game 4 walk-off by Tampa Bay saved them for another day.

MILWAUKEE BREWERS BROKE BASEBALL ON THEIR WAY TO REMARKABLY DOMINANT WORLD SERIES RUN

Does Yelich believe the league will follow suit and get back to fundamentals being top priority? "Brewer Ball" is clearly successful, but there’s a caveat for Yelich.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Yeah, I think everybody tries to do it, but it’s really hard to do it," he explained. "It takes a team that’s together and everybody’s bought in and going in the same direction. I think that was one of our biggest strengths – the togetherness of everybody and everybody sharing a common goal. Being willing to do whatever it took to accomplish that."

Perhaps Yelich’s point is the biggest part of "Brewer Ball" – having a team bought into doing the little things needed to win those close matchups. It takes a special group, which is what Milwaukee had been all season long through the highs and lows.

Now, Yelich and the rest of the crew are reaping the benefits of that selfless style of play that other teams may be trying to replicate down the road.

While they try, Yelich will keep interacting with fans like he did on Monday, surprising more than 400 fans at Raising Cane’s following Friday’s victory parade through the streets of Milwaukee. He, Brice Turang and manager Pat Murphy even made an appearance on "Saturday Night Live" over the weekend.

Yelich, joined by his mother, grandmother and dog Winston, greeted fans, signed baseballs, jerseys and more, and continued to party on.

"Just seeing people make memories and celebrate the championship with us. We knew how much it meant to everybody and how much everybody wanted us to get this done," he said. "We’ve been close for a while now and finally getting over that hurdle and finally getting it done has been awesome. Just really cool to see how happy it’s made people and how much fun everybody’s been having the last few days."

posts.title: Associated Press Top 25 poll voters hit a new, ridiculous low with this week's results
posts.excerpt: The Associated Press Top 25 poll gives the SEC special treatment, ranking Florida and South Carolina despite three losses each already this season.
posts.content:
At this point, it's reasonable to wonder if the voters who determine the Associated Press Top 25 poll are even trying anymore.

It's been a recurring problem in recent years, with the first part of the 2026 season showing once again that many poll voters are either not paying close enough attention, or are hopelessly consumed, or confused, by specific pro-conference or pro-team biases.

That observation was even more evident with the release of this week's poll, which has conclusively demonstrated, yet again, that preseason polls are given far too much importance and that no other conference gets the special treatment the SEC receives.

YES, THE SEC IS STILL GETTING RIDICULOUS PREFERENTIAL TREATMENT IN THE AP TOP 25 POLL

First? The Texas Longhorns. Texas has two poor quality losses this year, to the Oklahoma Sooners and a home loss to the Florida Gators. They have the miraculous escape over Ohio State, and a win over Ole Miss. They're No. 10 in the country. Texas Tech has just one loss, a bad one at Cincinnati, but two "ranked" wins in a surprisingly strong Big 12 Conference. They're No. 13.

We've had an entire offseason and half a season with SEC coaches, cough Lane Kiffin cough, complaining about moving to a nine-game schedule and demanding preferential treatment for their schedules, all while they're already getting it.

Missouri is No. 19, for some reason, despite an extremely unimpressive resume of providing losses for other SEC teams. They were blown out 31-3 by Ole Miss, lost to what's clearly a mediocre Mississippi State team, though at least that was with Kamario Taylor, but their big win over Florida now looks much less impressive considering the Gators' collapse.

But the biggest problem? Their ridiculous handling of that Florida team and the South Carolina Gamecocks. Exclusively because of their conference affiliation.

Florida has two impressive wins, over Ole Miss and Texas, but has three awful losses. Not one, not two, but three losses. They were blown out 45-17 at Missouri, blown out 38-19 by South Carolina, and blown out 27-8 by Georgia. That 27-8 loss was just on Saturday. Why are they ranked?

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

You could make the case that the Gators deserve to be in the top 25 had their three losses been even remotely close. They weren't. This is a deeply flawed team that is capable of flashes of brilliance against some opponents. They shouldn't be ranked. And they wouldn't be, if their jersey patch didn't have the SEC logo on it.

Meanwhile, Northwestern isn't ranked, despite having just two losses. Two close losses, to Indiana and a still-feisty Oregon Ducks team.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

South Carolina also has three losses, yet not only are they ranked, they're No. 23. At least Florida can point to Ole Miss and Texas, but the Gamecocks jumped into the top 25 after beating a very mediocre Oklahoma team. They lost to Mississippi State, Kentucky, and were blown out 49-18 by Alabama. While they did beat Tennessee, there's little to justify being ranked with three losses this early in the season.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

To be fair to the SEC, the voters' handling of Notre Dame is also bizarre. The Irish have taken advantage of an easy schedule this year, going 7-1 with wins over Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State, Purdue, North Carolina, Stanford and Navy. They lost their only "tough" game on the road at BYU. So why are they No. 4, ahead of an undefeated UCLA and one loss Indiana team? The Hoosiers, after all, lost in close fashion to Ohio State, with starting QB Julian Sayin. They've won everything else.

UCLA hasn't lost at all, the only team in the Big Ten or SEC able to say that. Sure, they've had a pretty easy schedule, but they have wins over Wisconsin at home and Oregon on the road...how's that any different from Notre Dame? Especially considering, again, they haven't lost?

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

The reality here is that poll voters are hopelessly committed to brand names. Whether those brand names are at the team or conference level. After Kiffin and Sarkisian have spent weeks complaining about the SEC's schedules and how they're handled, it's clear that the AP Poll is giving them an enormous amount of deference, likely undeservedly so.

The reality is that the SEC this year, and the Big Ten for that matter, are filled with teams that are far less talented than in years past. NIL and the transfer portal have flattened out college football, and brand names matter less than ever. You'd think that watching Indiana win a national championship would show voters that the traditional pathways and powerhouse programs should not be given the benefit of the doubt.

Some of this will sort itself out as November plays out, but there's no question that the AP Poll will impact the College Football Playoff selection committee rankings. The ones that actually matter. It's clear that they shouldn't.

posts.title: Angel Reese steps back from 'Unapologetically Angel' podcast after Atlanta Dream's Finals loss
posts.excerpt: Angel Reese announced a six-month break from her "Unapologetically Angel" podcast after the Atlanta Dream fell to the Golden State Valkyries.
posts.content:
Angel Reese is logging off. Well, mostly.

After the Atlanta Dream dropped Game 7 of the WNBA Finals to the Golden State Valkyries, the forward announced a six-month break from her podcast.

Reese took to social media to tell followers she is stepping away from "Unapologetically Angel." She made it clear that she needs to dedicate the offseason to herself.

Reese is heading to Florida for the break to spend time with her boyfriend, Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. The rest of the plan is to rest, lift weights, build her brand and find "peace."

Over the past year, Reese used the mic to complain that her WNBA salary could not cover her $8,000 monthly rent, lectured Cam Newton on why men must pay every bill, and took routine swipes at Caitlin Clark fans. The feed never lacked for eye-rolls.

The media break follows a rough finish on the court. Atlanta reached the finals for the first time since 2013, but the Dream dropped Game 7, 68-63.

Reese struggled to score during the elimination game. She logged 33 minutes but managed only eight points on 3-for-7 shooting. She grabbed 12 rebounds but gave away four turnovers. Over the seven-game series, she coughed up the ball 27 times, setting a WNBA Finals record.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

After dropping Game 7, she declared she had "nothing to hang my head about." Naturally, out came the playbook: every defeat is a lesson, a championship is "delayed, not denied," and she wants more. It was textbook deflection.

CASUAL BASKETBALL FANS GOBSMACKED AT HORRIBLE ANGEL REESE HIGHLIGHTS FROM AN ACTUAL WNBA FINALS GAME

The Dream front office might prefer an appetite for ball security. For the next six months, the basketball world gets a welcome breather from her weekly studio declarations. Reese claims she will return to work after her Florida stay.

Whether the time away produces better fundamentals on the court remains to be seen.

posts.title: APC Rally: Hard part of our economic reset over; next term is pure harvest – VP Shettima

posts.excerpt: Bendel Insurance technical adviser, Kennedy Boboye, says that his players followed the tactical plans in the win over Kwara United. The Benin Arsenals came from behind to secure a 2-1 win over the Har
posts.content:
Bendel Insurance technical adviser, Kennedy Boboye, says that his players followed the tactical plans in the win over Kwara United.

The Benin Arsenals came from behind to secure a 2-1 win over the Harmony Boys in Ilorin on Sunday.

Kayode Oke and Chinedu Nwosu were on target for the Benin-based club, while Stephen Gideon netted for Kwara United.

Boboye commended his players for coming back to snatch the victory in the game.

"We have our formation to execute while coming here which paid off, though we lost concentration with the first goal we conceded," Boboye reacted in a chat with Sports digital.

"We were pressing to make sure we get the three points which paid off.

"We pressed to ensure we equalised and the second one was on another counter attack to make them lose concentration in the defence to get the winner for us."

Bendel Insurance moved up to third position on the league table following the win.

They have garnered 18 points from 10 matches.

Bendel Insurance will take on Rangers in a rescheduled fixture in Awka on Wednesday.

posts.content:
Properties worth millions of naira have been destroyed as a result of fire that ravaged a feed mill factory in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital.

The incident occurred at a feed mill factory located at Podo area of Ibadan.

The incident occurred on Monday, and the fire affected a prefabricated building being used as a store at the factory, with items worth millions of naira destroyed.

Chairman, Oyo State Fire Service, Maroof Akinwande, who confirmed the incident, said that no life was lost.

Akinwande in a statement made available to DAILY POST on Monday said, "On arrival, it was discovered that a prefabricated building being used as a store had been severely affected by the fire. The fire was successfully brought under control and restricted from spreading to other buildings and facilities.

"Preliminary investigation suggested that the fire might have been caused by a spontaneous reaction of materials used in the factory".

posts.title: US-bound passengers must declare DR Congo travel under new Ebola rules
posts.excerpt: Anyone boarding an international flight to the United States must sign a statement that they have not been present in the DRC in the 21 days before their travel, according to the CDC. The post US-boun
posts.content:
US-bound air passengers must sign a statement that they have not travelled to the Democratic Republic of Congo, the epicentre of a deadly Ebola outbreak, under new rules coming into force on Tuesday, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), according to the continent’s top health agency.

Anyone boarding an international flight to the United States must sign a statement that they have not been present in the DRC in the 21 days before their travel, according to the CDC.

The CDC said the rules are required as “a public health measure intended to reduce the risk of Ebola being introduced into the United States through air travel.”

posts.title: Senate rejects move to revive Nigeria Airways, Air Nigeria
posts.excerpt: The President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, said, "We can't revive what is already dead." Instead, the leadership advised pursuing an entirely new, viable national carrier. The post Senate
posts.content:
*** Urges FG to re-ajudge BASA agreement for Nigeria Air services fly directly to China

*** Says we should not waste time on dead issues; calls for a national carrier with Nigeria’s flag

*** We can’t revive what is already dead, Akpabio.

By Henry Umoru, Abuja

The Senate has rejected calls for the revival of Nigeria Airways and Air Nigeria while it urged the Federal Government to renegotiate and enforce Nigeria’s Bilateral Air Services agreement, BASA, with China to allow Nigerian airlines to operate direct flights to the Asian country.

According to the Senate, there was the urgent need for a review of existing aviation arrangements to address the imbalance in flight operations between both countries and ensure that Nigerian carriers enjoy reciprocal access to China directly.

The Upper Chamber has also urged the Federal Government to explore ways of establishing a viable national carrier that would fly the nation’s flag to ease the challenges confronting Nigerian air travellers rather than what it described as wasting time in discussing dead issues.

The Senate also asked the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs to initiate diplomatic talks with China regarding business visa facilitation for Nigerian traders and reciprocal slot allocations to Chinese airports.

Resolutions of the Senate on Tuesday were a sequel to a motion titled “Enforcing the Bilateral Air Service Agreement (BASA)”. The motion was moved by the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, APC, Borno North.

The Upper Chamber has mandated the committees on Aviation and Foreign Affairs to ensure compliance and report to the Senate in 4 weeks.

The Senate also noted the growing trade relationship between both countries and the need for Nigeria to maximise the economic benefits of that partnership.

An additional prayer by Senator Ned Nwoko, APC, Delta North, to revive the defunct airline sparked an additional debate as it was dismissed.

The President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, said, “We can’t revive what is already dead.” Instead, the leadership advised pursuing an entirely new, viable national carrier.

Senator Akpabio, who questioned the wisdom of reviving an airline that had long ceased operations, said, . ‘We can’t revive what is already dead. Did Nigerian airways ever work?

While acknowledging the importance of having a Nigerian-owned airline, the President of the Senate recalled that the country once operated a fleet of nearly 40 aircraft and how Nigeria got to where we are, saying, “Common campaigns, we cannot have planes to hire.”

Akpabio, however, warned that Nigeria might have to reconsider the privileges granted to Chinese airlines if Nigerian carriers were not allowed reciprocal access to operate direct flights to China.

Recall that the plane unveiled as Nigeria Air in May 2023 was alleged to be a chartered Ethiopian Airlines aircraft leased for just a 72-hour display before being flown back to Addis Ababa.

Earlier in his presentation, Senator Monguno noted that Nigeria and China have significant populations of citizens living in each other’s territories, creating substantial demand for direct air connectivity.

He argued that a more balanced agreement would reduce travel time, improve supply-chain efficiency, boost trade and limit foreign exchange outflows associated with international travel.

Monguno said that the Senate notes that the Administration of the late former President Muhmmadu Buhari, Nigeria-China, signed a Bilateral Air Service Agreement (BASA) to establish a direct commercial air link and govern flight frequencies;

“Also notes that the volume of trade between Nigeria and China reached $18 billion in the first half of 2025 (a 35% increase year-on-year, building on a total of $28 billion recorded in 2026);

“Aware that the BASA instrument is intended to establish a direct scheduled Nigeria-China flight that would transform Murtala Mohammed International Airport, Lagos, and the Nnamdi Azikwe International Airport, Abuja, from mere origin/destination points into the primary gateway linking West and Central Africa to East Asia;

“Also aware that the population of Nigerians in China is more than 1,000,000 people, while that of China in Nigeria is more than 5,000,000, and this has generated the interest of China in Nigeria because it is Africa’s most populous nation and largest economy, offering massive markets on the African continent;

“Further aware that the benefits of enforcing such a bilateral agreement will reduce drastically travel time and increase supply chain velocity, retention of foreign exchange (capital flight reduction), aeronautical revenues for Nigerian gateways, increase commercial SME growth and non-oil export expansion, and accelerated perishable exports, among other benefits;

“Appreciates that the utilisation of BASA between Nigeria and China will actualise the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Ahmed Bola in facilitating the ease of doing business in Nigeria, enhancing bilateral and diplomatic relationships, creating massive employment (both direct and indirect jobs), and opening up export opportunities;

“Acknowledges that what is urgently required to enforce such a fantastic Air Agreement lies across the Executive Policy instrument from the Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development, the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Nigeria Customs Service; and

“Notes that enforcing the BASA instrument between Nigeria and China, the Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the NCAA hold direct regulatory levers by enforcing strict BASA reciprocity, rationalising sixth freedom competition, bilateral code-share mandates, temporary airport fee waivers, direct Naira settlement window using the existing bilateral currency swap framework, bypassing the US dollar, among other enforcing mechanisms.”

In his contribution, Senator Abdul Ningi, Bauchi Central, argued that Nigeria was not receiving commensurate benefits from its relationship with China, despite the Asian country’s growing influence in the global economy.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/senate-rejects-move-to-revive-nigeria-airways-air-nigeria/

posts.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA records improved truck turnaround at Olusosun dumpsite after upgrade
posts.excerpt: The Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, has recorded improved truck turnaround and reduced compactor queues at the Olusosun dumpsite following the extension and stabilisation of its E1 tipping pl
posts.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, has recorded improved truck turnaround and reduced compactor queues at the Olusosun dumpsite following the extension and stabilisation of its E1 tipping platform.

LAWMA’s Executive Director, Finance, Mr Kunle Adebiyi, disclosed this on Tuesday, saying the upgrade has enhanced the efficiency of waste discharge operations and significantly reduced waiting time for compactors by facilitating faster evacuation of waste.

According to him, “the improved turnaround has also strengthened LAWMA’s capacity to clear accumulated waste backlogs and address identified black spots across the state.”

Adebiyi however, expressed concern over continued indiscriminate disposal of waste and re-emergence of refuse at locations previously cleared, warning that such practices undermine sanitation efforts.

He urged residents to desist from dumping refuse on road medians and other unauthorised locations, particularly in areas recently cleared by the authority, and to patronise their assigned Private Sector Participation, PSP, operators for proper collection and disposal.

Adebiyi reiterated that sustaining a cleaner Lagos requires collective responsibility, calling on residents to support ongoing efforts by adopting responsible disposal practices.

He said LAWMA remains committed to strengthening operational efficiency and improving waste evacuation across the state for a cleaner and healthier Lagos.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/waste-crisis-lawma-records-improved-truck-turnaround-at-olusosun-dumpsite-after-upgrade/

posts.title: UEFA to observe one-minute silence for Tenerife forward who died at 30
posts.excerpt: UEFA will observe a one-minute silence at all its matches this week in honour of CD Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda, who has died at the age of 30. The post UEFA to observe one-minute silence
posts.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

UEFA will observe a one-minute silence at all its matches this week in honour of CD Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda, who has died at the age of 30.

The European football governing body announced the tribute on Tuesday, November 3, following the death of the Spanish striker, which has drawn tributes from across European and Spanish football.

In a statement shared on its official X account, UEFA said the football community was mourning the loss of De Miguel and extended its condolences to his family, friends and teammates.

“We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends and teammates during this incredibly difficult time,” the statement read.

UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin also expressed sadness over the forward’s death, saying the governing body had struggled to find words to describe the loss.

“We are heartbroken by the death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda,” Čeferin said.

“We have searched for words and found only silence. In that silence, our hearts and thoughts are with his family, his teammates, everyone at CD Tenerife, and all those who mourn this tragic loss.”

De Miguel, who played for several clubs in Spain’s lower divisions, helped Tenerife secure promotion to the Segunda División last season.

CD Tenerife confirmed his death in a statement, saying he passed away at 8:00 a.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

The club described the news as devastating and said there were no words to ease the grief felt by his family, loved ones and the Tenerife football community.

It also conveyed the family’s appreciation for the messages of support received, while appealing for their privacy to be respected during the difficult period.

The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) also paid tribute to the striker, expressing its condolences to his family, friends, CD Tenerife and the club’s supporters.

The federation described his death as a loss to Spanish football.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/uefa-to-observe-one-minute-silence-for-tenerife-forward-who-died-at-30/

posts.title: 'He needs sleep' - NDC clears air on Peter Obi's health
posts.excerpt: The Deputy Campaign Spokesperson of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Dr. Sam Omale, has dismissed concerns over the health of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, saying he is in perfec
posts.content:
The Deputy Campaign Spokesperson of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Dr. Sam Omale, has dismissed concerns over the health of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, saying he is in perfect health but only suffering from exhaustion.

Omale stated this during an interview on Channels Television, where he explained that Obi’s demanding schedule and constant movement between locations had left him physically exhausted.

According to him, Obi is passionate about his political activities and often handles several tasks simultaneously, leaving little time for rest.

“Sometimes I wonder where he gets his energy from. He is in London today and the following morning in Enugu. I’m wondering how he does it. Exhaustion comes in; he is a human being,” he said.

Omale, however, insisted that there was nothing medically wrong with Obi, adding that members of his team were trying to persuade him to get some sleep and rest.

“He is in perfect health. There’s nothing wrong with him. It’s just exhaustion, and we are trying to calm him down to take a sleep. He is fine,” he added.

He further maintained that Obi’s exhaustion would not affect the party's ongoing campaigns.

'He needs sleep' - NDC clears air on Peter Obi's health
