posts.title: High Court Hears Bid To Overturn Australia Social Media Ban
posts.excerpt: Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said. The post High Court Hears Bid To Overturn Australia Social Media Ban appeared f
posts.content:
Australia’s landmark social media ban faces a legal test on Tuesday, as online platform Reddit urges the nation’s highest court to scrap the world-leading restrictions.

Social media companies have been forced to purge millions of accounts after Australia banned under-16s from the likes of Facebook, TikTok and Reddit last December.

The High Court of Australia will sit on Tuesday and Wednesday as Reddit, one of the most popular websites in the world, argues the laws are misguided and should be overturned.

Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media.

“The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited,” reads Reddit’s submission.

Australia’s ban works by restricting children under 16 from holding accounts on the world’s biggest social media platforms.

Map of AustraliaThese platforms are responsible for weeding out underage users and face hefty fines if they are found to be falling short of their obligations.

Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features.

Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said.

“Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been,” its submission read.

Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content, online predators and predatory algorithms designed to keep people scrolling.

While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no “scientific consensus”.

Political discourse

Reddit, which has also argued it should be exempt from the ban, said there was little research on whether certain platforms were safer than others.

The High Court will also consider arguments from Australia’s Digital Freedom Project, which believes the ban restricts teens’ ability to take part in political discourse.

“Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16,” the advocacy group argued in written submissions.

“The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation,” it added.

Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project separately announced last year they would challenge the ban.

It was not clear how long it would take the high court to consider the case, although even the quickest decisions typically take months.

Social media firms face mounting scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to extreme content to keep them scrolling.

Several countries have indicated an interest in following Australia’s lead, including New Zealand, the UK, France and Turkey.

A team of Australia-based researchers published a study earlier this year that found little evidence to suggest teenagers have turned away from social media as a consequence of the restrictions.

AFP

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/11/03/high-court-hears-bid-to-overturn-australia-social-media-ban/

posts.title: Americans vote in midterms set to upend Trump presidency
posts.excerpt: Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands The post Americans vote in midterms set to upend Trump presidency appeared first o
posts.content:
Americans voted on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Donald Trump’s chaotic second term in the White House.

Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials.

The election amounts to a nationwide judgment on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war against Iran.

All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands.

Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans.

The 80-year-old’s approval rating has hovered near the low 30s.

In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future.

“I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP.

Economic discontent

Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans, and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals.

But in his final public campaign appearance on Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington’s Reflecting Pool.

“This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime,” he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a “pathetic closing message.”

Some Republican supporters remain confident.

“We’re going to win. As a matter of fact, we’ve probably already won,” Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP.

But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the political battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska.

Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.

Decision Desk HQ’s final forecast projected 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority.

Disputed results?

Polls can underestimate one party’s support, and Republicans hope their voters turn out in force on Election Day.

More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating the high energy.

The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, while mega-rich Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts.

As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans.

Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats — with no evidence — of cheating.

The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election.

And the Supreme Court rejected on Monday an emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens.

Trump, who will watch the midterms results at the White House on Tuesday night, signaled that if he does lose control of Congress he could simply defy Democrats.

“I veto everything,” he told a podcast on Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/americans-vote-in-midterms-set-to-upend-trump-presidency/

posts.title: TikTok Dance: Feminist group slams Hisbah over arrest Of 3 women in Kano
posts.excerpt: By John Alechenu ABUJA-The Feminist Digital Watch (FemDigital Watch) has condemned the arrest and arraignment of popular TikTok creator Amani Ishaq and two others by the Kano State Hisbah Board over d
posts.content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA-The Feminist Digital Watch (FemDigital Watch) has condemned the arrest and arraignment of popular TikTok creator Amani Ishaq and two others by the Kano State Hisbah Board over dance videos posted on social media.

The collective, convened by the Redefining Alternative Civic Engagement for Africa (RACE Centre), said Hauwa Khamis and Sa’adatu Muhammad were arrested alongside Ishaq for allegedly contravening public morality and religious guidelines.

They were arraigned before Magistrate Court No. 5, Court Road, Kano.

This was contained in a statement signed by Evelyn Ugbe on behalf of the collective, in Abuja, on Tuesday.

FemDigital Watch said while charges, bail conditions and detention status were still being verified, the incident marks a “troubling escalation in the systemic surveillance and criminalization of women’s creative self-expression in digital spaces.”

According to the group, the targeting of the three women is not isolated enforcement of local ordinances but reflects an entrenched pattern of technology-facilitated, gender-based suppression.

“Across Nigeria’s digital ecosystem, women creators consistently face disproportionate scrutiny, online mobbing, and state-backed censorship for routine digital expression that is widely normalized for men,” the statement said.

The group said weaponization of morality laws to police women’s online participation shrinks civic and creative space for female creators who rely on platforms like TikTok for livelihood, encourages coordinated online abuse, and undermines constitutional rights.

It said the action conflicts with Section 39 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) which guarantees freedom of expression and Nigeria’s obligations under the Maputo Protocol.

FemDigital Watch demanded immediate, unhindered access to legal representation and equitable bail terms for the three women and respect for their fundamental human rights without moral prejudice.

It also called on the Kano State Hisbah Board and regulatory authorities to cease arbitrary surveillance, arrest and detention of female content creators exercising their right to peaceful freedom of expression and bodily autonomy online.

The collective said it is documenting state-enforced and tech-facilitated abuses against women and girls and mobilizing legal-defense partners and civil society networks to track proceedings in Kano.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tiktok-dance-feminist-group-slams-hisbah-over-arrest-of-3-women-in-kano/

posts.title: Johnny Depp no longer rules out a 'Pirates of the Caribbean' return after years away from franchise
posts.excerpt: Johnny Depp told Entertainment Tonight he's open to reprising Captain Jack Sparrow if Jerry Bruckheimer is involved and the sendoff is right.
posts.content:
Johnny Depp isn't shutting the door on a return to the "Pirates of the Caribbean" franchise.

"Pirates of the Caribbean" is one of the most successful franchises in Hollywood history. The first film — "Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl" — was released in 2003 and ushered in a new era of superstardom for Depp. It also launched the A-list careers of Kiera Knightley and Orlando Bloom.

Four more films were released between 2006 and 2017 with Depp always reprising his role of Captain Jack Sparrow.

TOM CRUISE IS REPORTEDLY GOING TO MAKE AN INSANE AMOUNT OF MONEY FOR TOP GUN 3

However, the franchise never returned past 2017 following the fallout between Johnny Depp and his ex-wife, Amber Heard, who he famously and successfully sued for defamation over abuse allegations published in the Washington Post.

Depp previously said there wasn't anything that could convince him to return to the franchise after the fallout.

Now, it sounds like he's changing his tune and is open to reprising his role as Jack Sparrow if the situation is right.

"If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they are going to top off the 'Pirates.' The only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note," Depp told Entertainment Tonight in a video published Monday.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

He continued, "I'll go to work with [producer Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything, you know. Doesn't matter. If it's Jerry, I trust him and we have deep friendship."

You can watch his full comments in the video below, and let me know your thoughts at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

"Pirates of the Caribbean" at its best — certainly the original film — is what great cinema is at its finest. It's fun, original, entertaining and doesn't take itself too seriously. There's also no preachy woke nonsense. Granted, that garbage didn't really exist in 2003.

While it's very unclear if Depp will ever return to the "Pirates" universe, he has plenty of other things going on as he builds his career back up.

He starred in "Jeanne du Barry" in 2023 and is starring in "Ebenezer," set for release Nov. 13, 2026, and "Day Drinker," scheduled for release in 2027.

Both of his upcoming releases are major productions with stacked casts.

Would you like to see Johnny Depp run it back once more as Captain Jack Sparrow? Let me know at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

posts.title: The economy is on the ballot. 3 charts reveal the reality voters face as they head to the polls
posts.excerpt: Inflation outpacing wages, gas prices above $4, and mortgage rates past 7% are squeezing voters even as the S&P 500 surges over 26% under Trump.
posts.content:
Voters who have already cast ballots and those heading to the polls on Tuesday are weighing an economy shaped by rising everyday costs, surging home prices and strong gains in the stock market.

President Donald Trump vowed a better economy and a brighter financial future in his 2024 bid for office. But nearly two years into his second term, fuel prices have surged, inflation has accelerated and buying a home remains expensive — all pressures that put Republicans' affordability promises to the test in this midterm election cycle.

Three charts help exhibit the economic forces shaping voters’ choices as control of Congress hangs in the balance and the future of Trump's agenda is put on the line.

HIGH PRICES PUT TRUMP’S ECONOMY IN THE SPOTLIGHT AS THE GOP FIGHTS TO HOLD CONGRESS

The latest inflation report showed consumer prices rose 3.7% over the year through September and 0.6% from August. The Consumer Price Index tracks prices across a broad range of household expenses, including food, housing, medical care and transportation.

Trade policy has added to some of those costs.

A New York Federal Reserve study found that Trump's tariffs added about 2.9 percentage points to prices across the consumer goods researchers examined.

Roughly one-third of the increase came from U.S.-made products, as domestic manufacturers faced higher costs for imported materials and components under Trump's agenda.

The impact varies by household, but these figures offer a snapshot of the price pressures voters may weigh ahead of the midterms. They show how costs have changed, though not how voters will assign responsibility.

Higher energy costs are putting pressure on households and businesses, as the wars in Iran and Ukraine disrupt global fuel supplies.

Diesel prices have climbed sharply, rising from about $3.45 per gallon in early 2025 to a peak of $6.53 in October 2026, according to data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

The increase matters beyond the pump because trucks, freight trains and farm equipment rely on diesel.

AMERICAN-MADE GOODS ALSO GOT MORE EXPENSIVE UNDER TRUMP TARIFFS, NEW RESEARCH FINDS

Higher fuel costs can raise expenses for businesses moving groceries, packages and building materials, which may absorb some of the increase or pass it along to customers.

Gasoline prices are also adding to household costs. They jumped 9.1% in September, accounting for more than half of that month’s overall increase in the Consumer Price Index.

Housing remains a major affordability challenge, particularly for prospective buyers.

Freddie Mac’s 30-year mortgage rate averaged 7.24% as of Oct. 29, while the latest median price for an existing home was $417,500 in September, according to the National Association of Realtors.

Mortgage rates shape buyers’ monthly payments, and home prices determine how much they need to borrow, making it harder for many households to enter the market.

TRUMP’S HOUSING CHIEF PAINTS A GRIM PICTURE FOR HOMEOWNERSHIP IN ONE MAJOR AMERICAN CITY

Rising home values can benefit people who already own property, but that wealth is difficult to access without selling or borrowing against a home. For renters and first-time buyers, the costs are more immediate.

The data offer a snapshot of the costs voters have faced, but the charts alone cannot show how they will weigh the economy — or which party they will hold responsible — as results come in.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/economy-ballot-3-charts-reveal-reality-voters-face-head-polls

posts.title: Juventus shareholders approve accounts as Bianconeri prepare transfer budget investment
posts.excerpt: Juventus shareholders have approved the club’s latest accounts and backed a capital increase of up...
posts.content:
Juventus shareholders have approved the club’s latest accounts and backed a capital increase of up to €250m, with at least €100m expected to go into new investment, mainly in the squad.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, 99.9% of shareholders voted to give the board the power to launch the capital increase at Tuesday’s meeting at the Allianz Stadium. The aim is to strengthen the club’s finances and sporting competitiveness, upgrade strategic property such as the stadium, and build the brand.

The 2025-26 accounts showed a loss of €66m, up from €58.1m the year before. The increase was largely due to missing out on Champions League qualification.

SPA, BELGIUM – JULY 28: John Elkann, Chairman and CEO of Ferrari looks on, on the grid prior to the F1 Grand Prix of Belgium at Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps on July 28, 2024 in Spa, Belgium. (Photo by Mark Thompson/Getty Images)Exor guarantee Juventus capital increase

Exor, the majority shareholder of Juventus with a 65.4% stake, has agreed to cover its own share and any part of the increase that other shareholders don’t take up. It has already paid in €60m as an advance.

Around 45-50% of the total will go towards strengthening the balance sheet over this season and next. That leaves roughly €100m for investment, with the first team the priority.

General manager Giovanni Carnevali promised “commitment and seriousness” in the January transfer window.

posts.title: 2027: ADC urges Nigerians to replicate US voters’ revolt against ruling party
posts.excerpt: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has urged Nigerians to take a cue from American voters by using the 2027 general elections to reject the ruling All Progressives Con
posts.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has urged Nigerians to take a cue from American voters by using the 2027 general elections to reject the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, over economic hardship, worsening insecurity and declining living standards.

The party said Tuesday’s US midterm elections had demonstrated that no government could take voters for granted, insisting that Nigerians must put their welfare above political loyalty, sentiments and personality politics when deciding who governs them.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the American election outcome as a decisive rebuke of the ruling Republican Party’s leadership and economic policies, saying it offered an important lesson for Nigeria’s democracy.

“Americans have shown that when politicians become arrogant, when policies punish ordinary people, and when those in power mistake popularity for a permanent licence to govern, the ballot box remains the ultimate instrument of accountability,” the party said.

The opposition party said Nigerians had endured years of economic hardship and worsening insecurity under the President Bola Tinubu-led APC administration, questioning why the ruling party should be rewarded with another mandate.

“We cannot continue to complain about the cost of living while voting for a President who has made life unaffordable. We cannot demand security while rewarding failure. We cannot earnestly yearn for change while sustaining the very political system responsible for our collective impoverishment,” the ADC said.

Urging Nigerians to mobilise ahead of 2027, the party called for massive voter turnout, describing the Permanent Voter Card as an instrument for changing the country’s political direction.

“History beckons in 2027. Our voters’ cards must become instruments of change, not souvenirs of citizenship. Nigerians must turn out massively and vote for their own interests,” Abdullahi said.

The party also unveiled its campaign message, presenting itself and its candidates as an alternative to the APC-led government.

“The ADC and its candidates are offering Nigerians a clear alternative: Make Nigeria Affordable Again. Make Nigeria Safe Again. Give Nigerians Jobs Again,” the statement said.

Drawing a direct parallel with the American elections, Abdullahi urged Nigerians to make their votes count in 2027, warning that the APC should not mistake its hold on power for a permanent mandate.

“If Americans can use their votes to demand better, Nigerians can do the same. In 2027, let our votes speak louder than the APC-induced suffering,” he said.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027-adc-urges-nigerians-to-replicate-us-voters-revolt-against-ruling-party/

posts.title: Iran supreme leader says those expecting US policy shift ‘seriously mistaken’
posts.excerpt: Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said Wednesday that anyone expecting a shift in US policy was "seriously mistaken", hours after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump. The pos
posts.content:
Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said Wednesday that anyone expecting a shift in US policy was “seriously mistaken”, hours after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump.

“Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken,” Khamenei said in a written statement published on his website.

Democrats seized control of the US Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, reflecting anger over living costs, tariffs and the US war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring.

Khamenei’s remarks come with diplomatic efforts underway to avert renewed fighting in the war, which broke out on February 28.

US and Israeli leaders have in recent days threatened to resume attacks against Iran.

“Should such aggressions be repeated, the war’s scope will become much wider,” said Khamenei, who has yet to appear in public since he took power in March.

Earlier, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said Americans had voted against war.

“Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message,” he posted on X.

“If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare,” Ghalibaf said.

Iran’s judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been “defeated both militarily and politically”.

“We will certainly inflict further defeats on him,” he added.

Khamenei, 57, was named supreme leader after US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war killed his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The new leader has since communicated through written messages.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/iran-supreme-leader-says-those-expecting-us-policy-shift-seriously-mistaken/

posts.title: 2027: APC cannot find evidence against Obi – Utomi
posts.excerpt: Prof. Pat Utomi has said the inability of the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led Federal Government to prosecute the presidential candidate, of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, over alleg
posts.content:
Prof. Pat Utomi has said the inability of the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led Federal Government to prosecute the presidential candidate, of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, over alleged wrongdoing reflects the absence of credible evidence against him.

Utomi made the assertion in a post on his X platform on Wednesday, arguing that if Obi had engaged in corruption or had any incriminating issues, the government would have used them to move against him, particularly as an opposition figure.

He alleged that the political establishment was uncomfortable with Obi because it could not find credible wrongdoing to use against him.

“I’ve said this many times, if Peter Obi had any skeletons in his cupboard or was corrupt like many other politicians, this APC-led administration would have seized the opportunity to arrest him, lock him up and keep him behind bars until after the election, especially as an opposition figure,” Utomi wrote.

He added that the inability to find what he described as damaging information against Obi had made the former Anambra State governor a threat to the political establishment.

The political economist also questioned what he described as a contradiction in the attitude of Nigerians who, according to him, reject Obi despite his willingness to be investigated by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), while embracing politicians he accused of betraying the public trust.

“What strange contradiction has taken hold of some of our consciences? You reject a man who openly challenges the EFCC to prove that he is corrupt (which he is not), yet readily and openly embrace those who have stolen your future,” he said.

Utomi further criticised what he described as public acceptance of political leadership associated with corruption, questioning why some Nigerians appeared comfortable with conditions that had contributed to their suffering.

He urged Nigerians to reflect on their attitude towards integrity and accountability in public office.

The comments come amid continuing political debates over Obi’s record in public service, accountability and the conduct of political leaders ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/utomi-apc-cannot-find-evidence-against-obi/

posts.title: Spain’s transport minister resigns after train crash kills 69
posts.excerpt: Spain’s Transport Minister, Oscar Puente, has resigned less than a week after a deadly train collision that killed 69 people, making it the second major railway disaster in the country in less than a
posts.content:
Spain’s Transport Minister, Oscar Puente, has resigned less than a week after a deadly train collision that killed 69 people, making it the second major railway disaster in the country in less than a year.

Puente also withdrew from the upcoming general election, saying he had initially decided to step down immediately after last week’s accident but remained in office to coordinate the government’s initial response.

“A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot continue in office with two accidents of this severity in less than a year,”

Puente said, referring to the latest collision and a high-speed train derailment in Andalusia in January, which claimed 46 lives.

The latest accident occurred last Wednesday when a high-speed train operated by state-owned Renfe crashed into a stationary train on the Madrid-Seville line in central Spain’s Castilla-La Mancha region.

The collision reportedly happened at an estimated speed of between 100 and 125 miles per hour, after the Renfe train slammed into a privately operated Iryo train.

Reports indicated that trains on a section of the route had been ordered to stop following a signal failure. However, central controllers in Madrid, who had assumed control after the failure, authorised the Renfe train to continue its journey, resulting in the collision.

Following the accident, services on the Madrid-Seville route have been reduced as the Railway Safety Agency reviews the line’s safety systems.

The government is also working to complete the delayed deployment of the European Rail Traffic Management System, which is designed to improve railway safety and coordination.

Additional measures under consideration include an artificial intelligence system designed to reduce human error by detecting anomalies and monitoring conversations between train drivers and railway controllers.

Puente said Spain would become the first country to introduce such a safety mechanism.

Meanwhile, victims of the latest accident and their families are expected to receive compensation under a 30-million-euro ($33.5 million) assistance package announced by Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.

Bereaved families will receive 72,121 euros ($80,776) in direct assistance, alongside an equal amount in advance compensation.

The latest disaster has renewed concerns about railway safety in Spain, particularly following two major train accidents within a period of less than a year.

posts.title: Mane, Hakimi, Amad make CAF Men’s Player of the Year shortlist [Full List]

posts.content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

Senegal forward Sadio Mane, Morocco defender Achraf Hakimi and Ivory Coast winger Amad Diallo have been named among the 10 nominees for the 2026 Confederation of African Football Men’s Player of the Year award.

The nominees were announced by CAF on Wednesday, with the trio joined by seven other players in the race for the continent’s top individual football honour.

The full list comprises Amad Diallo (Ivory Coast), Yoane Wissa (DR Congo), Antoine Semenyo (Ghana), Ismael Saibari, Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz (Morocco), Ismaila Sarr, Pape Gueye, Sadio Mane (Senegal) and Teboho Mokoena (South Africa).

Other categories announced include the Men’s Young Player of the Year, Men’s National Team of the Year, Men’s Club of the Year and Men’s Coach of the Year.

The 10 nominees for the Young Player of the Year award are Ibrahim Maza, Christian Kofane, Christ Inao, Yan Diomande, Hamza Abdelkarim, Caleb Yirenkyi, Ismaël Kamissoko, Abdellah Ouazane, Ayoub Bouaddi and Ibrahim Mbaye.

The 10 nominees for the Men’s Goalkeeper of the Year award are Oussama Benbot (Algeria), Vozinha (Cabo Verde), Yahia Fofana (Ivory Coast), Lionel Mpasi (DR Congo), El Mahdy Soliman, Mostafa Shobeir (Egypt), Ahmed Reda Tagnaouti, Yassine Bounou (Morocco), Édouard Mendy (Senegal) and Ronwen Williams (South Africa).

For the Men’s National Team of the Year, Algeria, Cabo Verde, Côte d’Ivoire, DR Congo, Egypt, Ghana, Morocco, Senegal, South Africa and Tunisia made the shortlist.

The Club of the Year category features CR Belouizdad, USM Alger, AS Maniema Union, Zamalek SC, AS FAR, Olympic Club Safi, RS Berkane, Mamelodi Sundowns, Al Hilal SC and ES Tunis.

Meanwhile, Lamine N’Diaye, Pedro Leitão Brito, popularly known as Bubista, Sébastien Desabre, Hossam Hassan, Moatamed Gamal, Alexandre Santos, Mohamed Ouahbi, Walid Regragui, Pape Thiaw and Miguel Cardoso are nominated for the Men’s Coach of the Year award.

The 2026 CAF Awards ceremony is scheduled to take place in Lagos on Monday, December 7.

posts.title: I was once a taxi driver in America - Tinubu
posts.excerpt: President Bola Tinubu has said that he was once a taxi driver in the United States of America. Tinubu, in a statement, compared his past experiences with his administration’s student loan programme. A
posts.content:
President Bola Tinubu has said that he was once a taxi driver in the United States of America.

Tinubu, in a statement, compared his past experiences with his administration’s student loan programme.

According to him, after arriving in the United States, he drove a taxi to raise money for his education and postponed starting school for several months in order to save enough funds.

He said that once in Chicago he took on different jobs to support himself and pay his way through university, covering tuition, accommodation and living expenses.

He noted that those experiences have remained with him and that he understands the pressure of managing education costs while studying.

President Tinubu added that education created opportunities in his own life and that he believes Nigerian children should have similar access regardless of where they are born or their parents’ financial situation.

“I was once a taxi driver in America. Those experiences have remained with me and I understand the pressure of managing education costs while studying.

“Education created opportunities in my own life and I believe Nigerian children should have similar access regardless of where they are born or their parents’ financial situation,” Tinubu said.

The President cited this background as one reason education is a priority for his administration.

He stated that NELFUND has provided over N372 billion in student loans for institutional fees and upkeep to help young Nigerians remain in school.

I was once a taxi driver in America - Tinubu

posts.title: Ex-minister John Nwodo rejects APC campaign council appointment
posts.excerpt: Former Minister of Information and immediate past President-General of Ohanaeze Ndigbo, Chief John Nwodo Jnr., has rejected his appointment as a member of the Advisory Council to Governor Peter Mbah’s
posts.content:
Former Minister of Information and immediate past President-General of Ohanaeze Ndigbo, Chief John Nwodo Jnr., has rejected his appointment as a member of the Advisory Council to Governor Peter Mbah’s Gubernatorial Campaign Council in Enugu State.

Nwodo announced his decision in a letter dated October 28, 2026, addressed to Governor Mbah, following a media publication listing him as one of the members of the campaign council.

In the letter, the former minister appreciated the governor for the confidence reposed in him but said he would not accept the appointment because of his commitment to political neutrality.

He explained that his position as the immediate past President-General of Ohanaeze Ndigbo required him to remain nonpartisan and serve as a father figure to all, rather than get involved in local partisan politics.

Nwodo stated, “As President-General of Ohanaeze, I swore whilst I was in that office to be nonpartisan. I believe, out of that office, I should remain a father and in that respect be completely nonpartisan in our local politics in Igboland.”

He further disclosed that he currently does not belong to any political party and intends to maintain that position for the rest of his life.

“I presently have no membership card of any political party and I intend to keep it so until I die. This, I believe, will enable me to intervene as a father in any intra-party disputes amongst Igbos in politics,” he said.

Nwodo stressed that his decision was not directed at Mbah personally, adding that it would not affect their relationship or his willingness to offer counsel to the governor.

“This decision has nothing to do with you particularly. I however open my doors to all politicians in the State to enable me to continue to counsel them on love and unity amongst all of you,” he stated.

He also asked the governor to instruct his staff to remove his name from all campaign-related publications.

“Please kindly instruct your staff to delete my name from all party notices, including my name as a member of your Campaign Council,” the letter partly read.

The former Ohanaeze leader, however, reaffirmed his personal relationship with Mbah, describing him as a friend and assuring him of his continued patriotic counsel.

He added, “This decision will in no way affect my personal relationship with you as a friend or my genuine and patriotic counsel to you as my governor.”

Ex-minister John Nwodo rejects APC campaign council appointment

Source: https://dailypost.ng/2026/11/04/gov-mbahs-campaign-council-suffers-setback-as-ex-minster-john-nwodo-rejects-appointment/

posts.title: Three Nigerians arrested in Ghana over alleged robbery of bank customers
posts.excerpt: The Ghana Police Service has arrested three Nigerian nationals suspected of belonging to a criminal syndicate allegedly responsible for a series of robberies targeting bank customers in Kumasi and sur
posts.content:
The Ghana Police Service has arrested three Nigerian nationals suspected of belonging to a criminal syndicate allegedly responsible for a series of robberies targeting bank customers in Kumasi and surrounding communities in the Ashanti Region.

The suspects were identified as Aboy Promise, 30, Favour Uwalaka, 45, and Kingsley, 35. A fourth alleged member of the group, identified as Chinedu, also known as Alhaji, is reportedly on the run.

The Ashanti Regional Police Command confirmed the arrests in a statement issued on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and signed by the Head of its Public Affairs Unit, Superintendent Godwin Ahianyo.

According to the police, the arrests followed an intelligence-led operation conducted on October 31 at about 11:30 p.m. by an Inspector-General of Police Special Team comprising personnel from the Anti-Armed Robbery Unit of the Criminal Investigations Department Headquarters and the Accra Regional Police Intelligence Directorate.

The operation initially led to the arrest of Aboy Promise and Favour Uwalaka at a hotel in Moshie Zongo, where a search reportedly uncovered GH¢1,600 in cash, assorted mobile phones, a Royal motorcycle and a master key suspected to have been used to gain unauthorised access to vehicles belonging to bank customers.

The police said the two suspects, during interrogation, allegedly admitted involvement in the robberies and identified two other accomplices, including Kingsley, alias KC, and Chinedu, alias Alhaji.

Acting on information provided by the suspects, security operatives subsequently proceeded to another hotel in Dechemso, a suburb of Kumasi, where Kingsley was arrested.

However, Chinedu remains at large, prompting the police to appeal to members of the public to provide credible information that could assist in his arrest.

Providing details of the alleged criminal operation, the police said preliminary investigations indicated that the syndicate monitored banking facilities, identified customers who withdrew substantial amounts of money and followed them before robbing them.

The suspects were also accused of breaking into unattended vehicles belonging to bank customers using a master key to steal cash and other valuables.

The police further disclosed that the arrested suspects allegedly confessed to robbing a bank customer of GH¢15,000 at Asokore Mampong on October 27, 2026, shortly after the victim withdrew the money from Kwamang Rural Bank.

They also reportedly admitted involvement in similar incidents around the Atonsu branch of Fidelity Bank, the Ahodwo branch of Access Bank and other locations within Kumasi and its environs.

The three suspects have since been handed over to the Ashanti Regional Police Command and are assisting with ongoing investigations.

Meanwhile, the police have urged bank customers to remain vigilant, particularly when withdrawing large sums of money, and to be cautious of suspicious persons around banking premises.

The Command also warned motorists against leaving cash and other valuables unattended inside their vehicles.

Members of the public with information regarding the whereabouts of the fleeing suspect have been encouraged to report to the nearest police station or contact the Ghana Police Service through its emergency numbers 191, 112 or the toll-free MTN and Telecel line 18555.

The police reaffirmed their commitment to tackling robbery and other criminal activities across the Ashanti Region while commending residents for their continued cooperation.

Three Nigerians arrested in Ghana over alleged robbery of bank customers

posts.title: Spain’s transport minister quits following rail disaster that left 69 dead
posts.excerpt: Spain’s Transport Minister, Óscar Puente, has resigned following a devastating train collision that claimed at least 69 lives and left dozens injured, intensifying pressure on the government over rail
posts.content:
Spain’s Transport Minister, Óscar Puente, has resigned following a devastating train collision that claimed at least 69 lives and left dozens injured, intensifying pressure on the government over railway safety and its handling of the disaster.

Puente announced his resignation on Tuesday evening after facing intense scrutiny from lawmakers during a lengthy parliamentary session concerning the October 28 collision near Urda, south of Madrid.

The crash occurred when a moving train struck the rear of a stationary train, triggering one of the deadliest railway disasters in modern European history and the country’s worst train accident since 2013.

Explaining his decision to leave office, Puente said the scale and frequency of the recent tragedies had made his continued stay in government untenable.

“A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot remain in office after two accidents of this seriousness in less than a year,” he stated.

The minister was referring to another fatal railway accident in January, which reportedly claimed 46 lives on the same line.

Beyond relinquishing his ministerial position, Puente also announced his withdrawal from the list of candidates for the forthcoming early legislative elections.

“I am not only stepping down from my position as minister of transport, but I am also withdrawing my name from the lists for the early legislative elections,” he said, describing the decision as an act of “political dignity”.

His resignation followed days of mounting pressure from opposition parties, particularly the conservative People's Party (PP) and the far-right Vox, both of which had called for him to accept responsibility for the latest disaster.

The controversy also exposed divisions within the governing coalition, with some political allies questioning whether Puente could remain in office while public confidence in the country's railway system continued to decline.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has acknowledged the growing public concern, admitting that confidence in the railway system was “broken”.

Meanwhile, opposition lawmakers criticised Puente over his earlier comments suggesting that human error could have contributed to the collision, accusing him of attempting to shift responsibility away from the government's oversight of the railway network.

Although the minister had indicated days earlier that he intended to remain in office, his appearance before Congress on Tuesday became a critical moment in the growing political crisis.

During the parliamentary session, he outlined proposed measures to strengthen railway safety before facing further questions from lawmakers over the circumstances surrounding the collision.

The tragedy has also cast a shadow over the country's political situation ahead of the November 29 early general elections, with the governing Socialist-led administration facing increasing criticism over its handling of the railway disaster.

With Puente's departure, attention is now shifting towards his successor, the ongoing investigation into the collision and the measures the government will introduce to prevent further tragedies.

Spain’s transport minister quits following rail disaster that left 69 dead

Source: https://dailypost.ng/2026/11/04/spains-transport-minister-quits-following-rail-disaster-that-left-69-dead/

posts.title: Rufai, Abati disagree over Natasha's bundle of cash in Kogi
posts.excerpt: There was drama on Arise TV Morning Show on Wednesday as anchors Rufai Oseni and Reuben Abati disagreed over cash distribution by Kogi Central senator, Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan to her constituents. Nat
posts.content:
There was drama on Arise TV Morning Show on Wednesday as anchors Rufai Oseni and Reuben Abati disagreed over cash distribution by Kogi Central senator, Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan to her constituents.

Natasha has been under fire after videos showed her displaying bundles of naira notes during her 3rd anniversary empowerment programme in Kogi.

But she defended her action, saying she gave sewing machines in the past but beneficiaries sold them to pay rent and boost businesses.

Reacting on Arise TV, Rufai defended Natasha.

"You can't blame Natasha, she tried the machines, they sold them. People need cash for their businesses," Rufai said.

He said Natasha showed what she did openly, unlike other lawmakers who hide constituency money, adding that the real problem is poverty, not Natasha.

However, Abati disagreed immediately, saying that displaying bundles of cash on tables is not empowerment.

"Displaying bundles of cash is not empowerment. You don't build the economy by displaying cash," Abati fired back.

According to him, there is nothing wrong with helping people with money, but making it a show for cameras is wrong.

He stated that the money should have been transferred quietly.

Abati added that groups like MonITNG that criticised Natasha were right, stating that cash handouts cannot replace infrastructure, education, healthcare and jobs.

The clash got heated as Rufai insisted Nigerians need immediate cash to survive, while Abati maintained that leaders should focus on sustainable development, not cash display.

Rufai, Abati disagree over Natasha's bundle of cash in Kogi

posts.title: 4,000 Newly Employed Public Servants To Strengthen A’Ibom Civil Service, Says Gov Eno
posts.excerpt: Some of the newly recruited civil servants expressed excitement over their appointments, describing the opportunity to join the state workforce as a significant milestone. The post 4,000 Newly Employe
posts.content:
Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has said the recruitment of 4,000 new civil servants was aimed at filling identified vacancies and strengthening the state’s public service for improved efficiency and service delivery.

Governor Eno spoke on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, during an orientation programme for the newly recruited workers at the Ibom Tropicana Event Centre, Uyo.

The orientation follows his earlier announcement directing the newly employed civil servants to resume work on October 1, 2026.

Explaining the rationale behind the recruitment, Eno said a staff verification exercise conducted after he assumed office revealed more than 2,000 ghost workers, as well as several employees who had retired but remained on the payroll.

He explained that after addressing the identified irregularities, the government found it necessary to fill the resulting vacancies and strengthen the workforce.

According to him, the recruitment was not intended to inflate the size of the civil service but to address manpower shortages and improve its capacity to deliver public services.

“There was a huge vacancy gap in the Service, so we are not recruiting to bloat the service but to strengthen and make the public service more efficient for excellent work output,” the Governor said.

A cross-section of the newly employed civil servants on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

He charged the new employees to demonstrate commitment, discipline, and professionalism in their duties, urging them to bring fresh ideas and innovation into the system.

Governor Eno further reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the prompt payment of salaries and gratuities.

Earlier, the Head of the Civil Service, Mrs. Elsie Peters, expressed confidence in the quality of the newly recruited workforce, describing the orientation and training as important steps towards revitalising the state civil service.

She acknowledged Governor Eno’s support for the public service and expressed optimism that the new employees would contribute to improved performance and greater efficiency across government institutions.

Some of the newly recruited civil servants expressed excitement over their appointments, describing the opportunity to join the state workforce as a significant milestone.

They also commended the recruitment process, which they described as fair and credible, saying their selection was based on merit and not favouritism.

Among the beneficiaries who shared their experiences were Jennifer Ekott, Glory Wilson and Imo Obot, who expressed appreciation for the opportunity to serve the state.

The orientation programme is expected to familiarise the new employees with the values, expectations and responsibilities of the public service as they begin their careers in the Akwa Ibom State Civil Service.

posts.title: Bonta says he'll counter DOJ election monitors with observers of his own
posts.excerpt: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is deploying state election observers amid concerns the DOJ's federal monitoring could intimidate voters.
posts.content:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta said Tuesday afternoon that his office will deploy election observers in response to concerns that Justice Department monitors could intimidate voters.

Bonta said California was taking the same approach it used during the previous two elections, when the state dispatched its own observers alongside federal monitors.

The DOJ's Civil Rights Division has sent 1,000 monitors across the country to ensure election integrity and protect Americans' right to vote, a plan that has been public knowledge for months. The monitors will be personnel from across the DOJ, U.S. Attorney's Offices and employees from the Office of Personnel Management.

The department confirmed Tuesday that while federal election monitoring is routine, this year's operation is the largest in its history, with monitors deployed to all 50 states for the first time.

DOJ FIRES BACK AT DEM AG OVER ELECTION DAY GUIDANCE TELLING OFFICIALS WHEN TO CALL COPS ON FEDERAL AGENTS

The DOJ also released a list of cities where monitors are being deployed. In California, they are being sent to Los Angeles, Alameda, Sacramento and San Diego.

Bonta and other critics have argued that the unusually large federal presence could spook voters or discourage some from casting ballots.

Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, who leads the Civil Rights Division, told Bloomberg in an August interview that the role of DOJ election monitors would be to observe election practices and pursue investigations into any possible instances of fraud after the fact — not to intervene directly while people are voting.

In Tuesday's announcement, the DOJ added that monitors will also be responsible for ensuring that polling places are accessible for those with disabilities.

DOJ OFFICIAL DEFENDS TRUMP'S NONCITIZEN VOTER PROBE ON '60 MINUTES,' ACCUSES SHOW OF EDITING OUT HER ANSWERS

In her Bloomberg interview, Dhillon said the election monitors would respect the laws of whichever states they end up in. Many states restrict monitors from entering polling places and require them to remain behind designated boundaries outside.

"We respect state law," Dhillon told Bloomberg at the time. "We reach out to the states. If their perimeter is 150 yards, we respect that."

Dhillon also pointed out that the DOJ sent more than 80 monitors to observe primary elections across seven states this year, including locations in Minnesota, Michigan, Florida, Wyoming, South Carolina, Massachusetts and New Hampshire.

The nationwide deployment appeared to be proceeding without major incident Tuesday afternoon, with no significant confrontations involving federal monitors publicly reported.

This comes after the Supreme Court on Monday rejected the Trump administration's effort to require California election officials to segregate ballots cast by 20,000 voters the DOJ believes are noncitizens.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/bonta-counter-doj-election-monitors-observers

posts.title: Trump pledges to veto 'insane' Dem bills, pinpoints issue partially to blame for Republican losses
posts.excerpt: President Donald Trump blamed rising gas prices from the Iran conflict for GOP midterm losses, saying Americans backed the war but not the pain.
posts.content:
President Donald Trump vowed to veto "insane" legislation from Democrats following the party's major midterm election victories Tuesday, while acknowledging that rising gasoline prices stemming from the conflict with Iran likely contributed to Republican losses.

Trump, speaking to Fox News Channel during live Election Night coverage, said he was surprised by the GOP's performance but expressed confidence that he could work with Democrats despite their electoral gains.

"They'll send over things that are insane and I'll veto them," Trump said. "And after a couple of months of vetoes, they'll go out and they'll say, ‘How do we get this stuff done?’ And we'll work together."

TRUMP CONGRATULATES DEMOCRATS AFTER DOMINANT MIDTERMS, SAYS HE LOOKS FORWARD TO WORKING WITH THEM

Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, flipping at least seven Republican-held Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts. The sweeping victories dealt a major blow to Trump and the GOP, leaving Democrats positioned to block the president's legislative agenda, reject his nominees and launch investigations into his administration during his final two years in office.

The president pointed to his veto authority as a negotiating tool and revealed that several Democratic lawmakers had already reached out to him.

"You know, I have a lot of friends that are Democrats, believe it or not. I've already spoken to some of them," Trump said, adding that he had spoken with Democratic members of Congress, with others waiting to call.

Trump also addressed the GOP's disappointing election-night performance, suggesting that Americans were reacting more to higher gasoline prices than to the military campaign against Iran itself.

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

"I don't think it's the war, Bret, I think it's the gasoline price," Trump told "Special Report" anchor Bret Baier. "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran, but they really probably weren't willing to do the short-term consequence of paying more for gasoline."

Trump defended his administration's actions against Iran, arguing that the economic consequences were temporary and necessary to achieve longer-term national security objectives.

"I think a part of it was Iran. But at the same time, people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran," Trump said. "I think historically it's going to be much more important than this evening, because you can't let the number one state sponsor of terror have a nuclear weapon."

The president also blamed some Republican candidates for failing to energize his supporters, arguing that enthusiasm at his campaign rallies did not necessarily translate into votes for those he endorsed.

"I'm a little bit surprised. I thought they'd do better," Trump said. "We had tremendous rallies. We had about 30 of them."

Trump said some candidates had alienated his MAGA base by previously opposing him, while others simply failed to inspire voters to turn out.

'POD SAVE AMERICA' HOSTS CALL DEMOCRATIC PARTY'S MIDTERM WINS 'THE END OF THE TRUMP ERA'

"They didn't like the candidates and some of the candidates that I endorsed fought me, and they didn't like that they fought me," Trump said.

"And I wasn't on the ballot. If I was on the ballot, they would have gotten out," he added.

Despite expressing disappointment over Republican losses, Trump praised Democrats for their performance while rejecting the suggestion that the results amounted to a personal defeat.

"I think the Democrats did a good job, I really do. I think they did a good job. They fought hard," Trump said.

"I don't like to consider it a defeat," he added. "If you're on the ballot, it's different than if you're not on the ballot."

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-pledges-veto-insane-dem-bills-pinpoints-issue-partially-blame-republican-losses

posts.title: ‘LAWYER UP’: Democrats, Republicans waste no time in setting social media ablaze after midterm sweep
posts.excerpt: Sen. Ron Wyden's one-word post — "Subpoenas" — set the tone as Democrats celebrated reclaiming both the House and Senate in 2026 midterms.
posts.content:
Explosive reactions to the 2026 midterm elections quickly spread online as it became clear that Democrats had routed Republicans in key contests, reclaiming control of both the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate early Wednesday morning.

While Republicans quickly looked for a source of blame, jubilant Democratic reactions ranged from calling the moment the end of Trump’s MAGA movement to aggressive predictions of what the party could accomplish with their newfound majorities.

Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., summed up his vision for Senate committees in only one word.

"Subpoenas," Wyden said in a post on X.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

Democrats like Wyden have long promised to summon members of the current administration, former officials and business leaders before lawmakers for questioning if they captured a majority.

In the House, Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., echoed Wyden’s thinking with a brief post of his own.

"LAWYER UP," Garcia wrote.

Still other voices in the Democratic Party expressed the magnitude of the victory in more colorful terms.

"WE’RE GONNA PUT YOUR ASS IN JAIL EVERYONE GET MORE WORK RIGHT NOW !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!" Hasan Piker, a progressive streamer and socialist, said in a post to X.

Piker, who aligned himself closely with the progressive wing of the Democratic Party in the 2026 midterms, supported several candidates backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA). He also campaigned with Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Michigan, who won his race against Mike Rogers, a former congressman.

"GOD IS NONBINARY NOW MFS!!! IT'S LAW!!!" he wrote in another post, referring to James Talarico’s Senate victory in Texas over Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Talarico received widespread criticism from Republicans for past comments where he described God as "nonbinary" — an instance Republicans used to characterize Talarico as too progressive to represent a Republican-leaning state like Texas.

DEMS SEIZE THE SENATE AS BLUE TIDAL WAVE CRASHES DEEP INTO TRUMP COUNTRY, TOPPLES GOP STRONGHOLDS

After Fox News Decision Desk projected victories by Talarico and Democratic gubernatorial nominee Gina Hinojosa over Gov. Greg Abbott, other progressives cast the wins as a symbol of Democratic momentum.

"TEXAS IS BLUE. THIS IS HISTORY," Dean Withers, another progressive political commentator, wrote in a post to social media.

"MAGA IS DEAD. THEY’RE F---ING DEAD. WOKE HAS NEVER BEEN MORE BACK," he added.

On the other side of the aisle, Republicans and conservatives took to social media to vent frustrations and begin identifying where they thought the party had lost traction with the public.

To Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., who lost a primary earlier this year to a Trump-backed challenger, the midterm outcome boiled down to a set of unfulfilled promises: broken pledges to stay out of foreign conflicts and commitments to bring transparency around Jeffrey Epstein, the disgraced businessman who had died in prison while awaiting trial.

"Tonight’s outcome isn’t about placing faith in Democrats or socialist principles; it’s about holding Republicans accountable for betraying their promises. All Republicans had to do was: 1. put Americans First 2. not start another war 3. prosecute sex traffickers," Massie wrote.

Marjorie Taylor Greene, a former congresswoman who resigned her seat earlier this year over disagreements with the administration, delivered a similar message.

"Trump’s biggest betrayal to the American people isn’t what he failed to do. It’s what he promised NOT to do… and did it anyway," Greene wrote in a post to X.

"We gave President Trump our support, we gave him our money, we gave him our vote and gave him our time and we got behind him publicly, and he didn’t deliver," she added.

Conservative political commentator Matt Walsh offered similar criticisms of Trump, focusing on the U.S. conflict with Iran.

CONSERVATIVES STUNNED BY 'CATASTROPHIC' MIDTERM BLUE TSUNAMI, BLAME TRUMP'S IRAN WAR, HIGH GAS PRICES

"The Iran War is the greatest political blunder in the last two decades at least. A catastrophically stupid decision. An unforgivable betrayal of America First principles," Walsh said.

"There’s no way to soft-pedal this. It’s a political catastrophe of historic proportions. The Republican Party needs all new leadership. None should be spared from blame, starting at the top," Walsh added in a separate post.

posts.title: El-Sayed mocks Trump, Vance and Rogers in gloating victory speech signaling combative tone in Senate
posts.excerpt: Abdul El-Sayed mocked Trump and JD Vance in a combative victory speech after defeating Mike Rogers, calling his opponents "the bad guys" who lost.
posts.content:
Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed mocked President Donald Trump and his opponent in a combative victory speech Tuesday night in Michigan.

El-Sayed, who defeated Republican Mike Rogers, said his opponents "went all-in on one of the ugliest campaigns we've seen in our lifetimes."

"They might have been pointing at my name and my faith, but we all know my name and my faith aren't the reason you can't afford your gas or afford your groceries," El-Sayed said.

ABDUL EL-SAYED DELIVERS MAJOR BLOW TO GOP IN MICHIGAN AFTER BRUISING SENATE RACE

He said Trump's comments about him became "uglier and coarser" and that "to all the parents who struggle to explain why the president openly mocked someone for their name or how they pray, let them know tomorrow that the bad guys lost."

"They want an America that is too small for some of us, but we know America is big enough for all of us," he continued.

VANCE'S CAMPAIGN BLITZ PUTS HIM AT THE FOREFRONT OF THE GOP'S MIDTERM PUSH, AS INSIDERS PRAISE PACKED SCHEDULE

He also mockingly spoke of Vice President JD Vance, a foe he has combatted with frequently in recent months, saying, "There is this delicious irony in the fact that you're constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January. So you know what that means. Wolverine one. Buckeye zero."

He then shifted his focus to Israel, saying Americans want their money spent in the U.S.

TRUMP SAYS ISRAEL WILL STOP RECEIVING $4B IN US AID BY YEAR'S END, CAN STILL BUY WEAPONS

"We don't want our money spent on apartheid or genocidal war," he added.

El-Sayed also had mocking words for his opponent, telling Rogers to "enjoy your retirement."

"May we never have to see the likes of you in the state again," he added.

EL-SAYED, ROGERS CLASH OVER MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD, TRUMP AND GUNS: 5 FIERY DEBATE MOMENTS

Throughout the campaign, El-Sayed outran alleged ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, concerns about his rhetoric over Israel and Jewish voters in Michigan and criticism from fellow Democrats for his ties to controversial political streamer Hasan Piker.

Rogers failed to outrun the political headwinds that have buffeted Republicans this cycle, including affordability issues, President Donald Trump's trade war with Canada launched in the thick of the midterms and the Iran war, despite his attempts to distance himself from the latter issues.

El-Sayed’s victory serves as a major blow to the GOP’s push against the progressive lean in Democratic politics, where for much of the cycle after his shock win over Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., Republicans painted him as the face of socialism and communism in their messaging.

Fox News' Alex Miller and Luke Trevisan contributed to this report.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/el-sayed-mocks-trump-vance-rogers-gloating-victory-speech-signaling-combative-tone-senate

posts.title: Dem AG pulls off upset of sitting Republican governor after blistering campaign in key swing state
posts.excerpt: Attorney General Aaron Ford ousts Gov. Joe Lombardo to become Nevada's first Black governor, handing Democrats unified control of state government.
posts.content:
Nevada Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford has successfully ousted Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo in Nevada, a significant pickup for Democrats in the critical battleground state, The Associated Press projects.

Ford's defeat of Lombardo comes in one of the most closely watched gubernatorial races in the country.

Ford’s victory makes him Nevada’s first Black governor and gives Democrats control of the governor’s office for the first time since Lombardo defeated Democratic Gov. Steve Sisolak in 2022.

Ford, who has served as Nevada’s attorney general since 2019, campaigned on affordability, housing, education, healthcare and protecting access to abortion. He argued that Nevada families were struggling with high housing costs, energy bills and other rising expenses under Lombardo and the Republican administration.

FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: THE TOP RACES TO WATCH AS 36 STATES CHOOSE THEIR NEXT GOVERNOR

The result could also give Nevada Democrats unified control of state government depending on Tuesday night's election results, with the party already holding majorities in both chambers of the state Legislature. Ford will enter office with a legislative majority aligned with his agenda, although significant disagreements could remain over taxes, education spending, public safety and the state’s business climate.

Ford repeatedly criticized Lombardo for aligning himself with President Donald Trump and national Republicans. He argued that Nevada needed a governor who would challenge the administration on federal funding, immigration and voting rights while focusing on the state’s cost-of-living crisis.

The Republican incumbent defended his record on public safety, education, economic development and government spending. Lombardo argued that his administration had increased education funding, expanded workforce development and worked to diversify Nevada’s economy beyond tourism and gaming.

A BLUE WAVE IN GOVERNORS' MANSIONS COULD HURT FAMILIES MORE THAN A BLUE CONGRESS

Lombardo also accused Ford of proposing costly new government programs without explaining how they would be financed. His campaign pointed to a campaign analysis estimating that fully implementing Ford’s platform could cost billions of dollars over four years.

Ford rejected that analysis, arguing that Lombardo’s administration had included spending mechanisms and assumptions that were not part of his actual proposals. Ford said his agenda could be accomplished through a combination of existing state resources, federal funding and policy changes.

Housing affordability was one of the defining issues of the campaign. Nevada has faced a shortage of affordable homes, particularly in the Las Vegas and Reno areas, while rising rents and mortgage rates have placed pressure on working- and middle-class residents.

The candidates also clashed over energy costs, public education, crime, abortion, immigration and the state’s reliance on tourism and gaming.

Nevada’s growing energy demands, including those connected to data centers and other large industrial projects, became another major campaign issue. Lombardo promoted efforts to attract businesses and investment, while Ford argued that economic development should not result in higher costs for residents or additional pressure on the state’s infrastructure.

Ford will now face pressure to deliver on his campaign promises while governing a state with significant budget, housing, education and infrastructure challenges.

As attorney general, Ford frequently challenged Trump administration policies in court. His election is likely to make Nevada a more prominent Democratic counterweight to the federal government as the state moves toward the 2028 presidential election.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/dem-ag-pulls-off-upset-sitting-republican-governor-blistering-campaign-key-swing-state

posts.title: LAURA INGRAHAM: Richer, safer and stronger: Why the Trump agenda deserves to keep going
posts.excerpt: Critics keep declaring Trumpism dead, but Laura Ingraham argues that the economic, geopolitical and cultural record tells a very different story about MAGA's durability.
posts.content:
"This is the end of Trumpism!" "Conservative Populism, RIP." "Goodbye, MAGA!"

If these pronouncements sound familiar, it’s because they are. The same people predicting this now in op-eds, online and in podcasts predicted the same after Trump’s first impeachment, after the 2020 election, after January 6, after the second impeachment and after every criminal indictment filed against him.

Their wishful thinking is as dim-witted now as it was then.

TRUMP HIGHLIGHTS THE 'POWER OF VETO' AS DEMS EXPECTED TO TAKE HOUSE, SENATE

Any fair-minded political analyst would admit that over the past decade, Donald Trump has been the most consequential leader in the world, and that he has accomplished more than any Republican president in at least the past 100 years. His record should not be judged on midterm results but on what it has delivered. And if the question on the table is "Should Trump’s policies continue?" the record says yes — politically, economically, geopolitically and culturally.

Critics predicted Trump would destroy the Republican Party and set back American conservatism. The opposite happened. Across the West, the right has either collapsed or made its peace with the governing consensus. Canada hasn't had a conservative prime minister since 2015. Britain's Conservatives hold just 118 of 650 seats in the House of Commons. Marine Le Pen has never cleared 42% of the vote in a French presidential election. Germany's conservatives govern in coalition with the Social Democrats, and in Italy, The Economist recently praised Giorgia Meloni for "tacking to the middle."

Only in America has the right governed on low taxes, lighter regulation, social conservatism and a strong military — and kept winning. Democrats had little trouble beating moderate Republicans like John McCain and Mitt Romney. Trump has confounded them for most of a decade. No other leader on the Western right can say that.

We were told populism would wreck the economy. It hasn't.

Trump worked with Congress to cut taxes and roll back regulation, and he has trimmed a bloated bureaucracy: Between December 2024 and June 2026, the federal workforce shrank by 255,000 employees, or 12%, according to The Washington Post.

Ordinary families have benefited. Real median household income rose from $77,230 in 2016 to a record $87,460 last year, both measured in 2025 dollars. Those figures are adjusted for inflation and describe the household squarely in the middle. Nostalgia for the '80s and '90s is understandable, but the American middle class has never been richer than it is today.

FOX NEWS POLL: COST-OF-LIVING CONCERNS WEIGH ON GOP IN MIDTERMS

Inflation, the defining failure of the Biden years, has been tamed. Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, peaked at 6.6% in September 2022 and was still 3.3% in November 2024. This September it stood at 2.6%. Headline inflation of 3.7% is in line with the eurozone's 3.8% and Britain's 3.5%. Americans are not uniquely squeezed.

Growth is outpacing our peers. In September, the OECD projected U.S. real GDP growth of 2.2% for 2026, the highest in the G7. The latest data are stronger still: the economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, compared with 0.5% for the EU and roughly 1.3% for Canada.

The upshot is that Americans are by far the wealthiest people of any major economy. The IMF projects 2026 GDP per capita of $95,212 in the United States, against $65,699 in Germany, $61,108 in Britain, $60,105 in Canada, $51,448 in France, $35,400 in Japan and $15,371 in China. The United States is not merely the richest major country on earth; it is pulling away from the rest of the West.

Critics warned that Trump's foreign policy would leave America isolated and weak. Instead, he is charting a course to victory over China, our only serious geopolitical rival.

WHY TRUMP ZEROED IN ON GREENLAND, THE WORLD’S LARGEST ISLAND, MOSTLY COVERED IN ICE — IN 3 CHARTS

Before Trump, Washington's establishment insisted that China's rise was good for America, a view the Obama administration voiced as late as 2012. Trump took a more realistic view. His tariffs kept state-subsidized Chinese cars from gutting our auto industry. His moves on the Panama Canal and Greenland denied Beijing footholds in our hemisphere. He is rebuilding a military that had grown dangerously weak and distracted by ideology. And our economic lead keeps widening: in 2016, U.S. GDP exceeded China's by $7.3 trillion; last year, the gap was $11.3 trillion.

In the Middle East, Trump has severely degraded an Iranian military that threatened the entire region. Critics predicted the Strait of Hormuz would be closed. It hasn't been: The Wall Street Journal reports that Persian Gulf oil exports, counting both Hormuz shipments and alternative routes, now exceed prewar levels. All of this has been achieved without an invasion or boots on the ground. With a stronger military and a booming economy, American leverage abroad is likely the greatest it has been since the early 2000s.

LIZ PEEK: GUARANTEED — DEMOCRAT MIDTERM WIN WOULD DELIVER CHAOS NOT 'AFFORDABILITY'

Some warned social conservatives that Trump didn't really share their priorities and that they would regret backing him. Consider what he delivered.

For four decades, Republican leaders promised to do something about Roe v. Wade. Trump kept that promise, and Roe is gone. Unlike past Republican presidents, he has not appointed justices who drift left, and on most key constitutional questions the Supreme Court now has a solid conservative majority for the first time since the early 1930s.

TRUMP DHS HITS 16 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH 0 RELEASES AT THE BORDER

The border is closed to illegal immigration — another decades-old Republican promise that only Trump fulfilled. We were told this would devastate the economy. The data above say otherwise.

By any serious measure, the Trump movement ranks among the most successful in American history, and the country is better off for it — compared both with where we were and with our peers abroad.

Tellingly, Democrats aren't seriously arguing that they would deliver a stronger economy, a firmer foreign policy or safer streets. Voters can see what their approach produces by looking at Canada and Western Europe. Instead, their campaign rests on a single promise: to go after Trump and everyone who has worked with him. It is a campaign of retribution, not prosperity.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Of course, voters, including this one, are frustrated with the Iran conflict, and they want lower gas prices. Others are simply tired of politics, and some may hope a Democratic win would at least bring some calm to America. But remember what President Reagan said: "Freedom is never more than one generation from extinction." Freedom does not come cheap. Americans today are stronger, richer, safer and freer than we have been in decades, and those who want to see this country humbled, even humiliated, know it. The socialists, Marxists and even run-of-the-mill Democrats did not run this year to make your life better. They ran to punish you for wanting more than the scraps the political establishment used to toss you.

Do not fall for it. Can you imagine Republicans abandoning Reagan because he lost eight Senate seats in 1986? Did the Democrats abandon Obama after he lost nine Senate seats in 2014? Of course not.

We know which policies work. We know which policies have been a disaster. We know how to build a better country for ourselves and our children. We know how Democrats almost destroyed America and what they intend to do to our Constitution if they get the chance.

We may not have everything we want — we probably never will — but we have already made huge progress, and we just need to keep relentlessly fighting for the type of country we want.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM LAURA INGRAHAM

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/laura-ingraham-richer-safer-stronger-why-trump-agenda-deserves-keep-going

posts.excerpt: Italian newspapers describe the penalty kick awarded to Manchester United against Roma as ‘very soft’...
posts.content:
Italian newspapers describe the penalty kick awarded to Manchester United against Roma as ‘very soft’ and argue that Harry Maguire deserved a red card in the second half.

Roma suffered a 3-2 loss to Manchester United on Tuesday in the Champions League.

Spanish referee Jesús Gil Manzano drew criticism from Italian media, mostly for two controversial second-half decisions.

Italian sports papers Corriere dello Sport, Tuttosport and Gazzetta dello Sport wrote that the penalty awarded to the Red Devils, converted by Bruno Fernandes, was ‘very soft.’

It came when Matheus Cunha’s left foot met Gianluca Mancini’s right knee inside the Giallorossi box and, according to Corriere, Manzano punished the Italian defender for negligence.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 03: Michael Carrick, Manager of Manchester United, looks on during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 03, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)“However – wrote the newspaper – the opposite interpretation is also perfectly reasonable, as Cunha lifted his foot, catching Mancini’s knee.”

READ MORE – Cristante: Roma ‘must improve’ but Man United penalty ‘very doubtful’

Fernandes missed the penalty, but the referee allowed a retake as Bryan Cristante had encroached into the penalty area.

It was a close call, a matter of centimeters, as Cristante’s foot was on the edge of the box when Bruno struck the ball. The Italian midfielder cleared it after Devis Vasquez saved it, so a retake was inevitable.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 03: Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United has his penalty saved by Devis Stiven Vasquez Llach of AS Roma during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 03, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images)Both Corriere and Gazzetta rated Gil Manzano 4/10. Gazzetta wrote that the Spaniard ‘got everything wrong’ in the second half.

The other controversial incident came later in the game, when United had already equalised.

Maguire, already on a yellow card, deliberately brought Santiago Castro to the ground, appearing to strike him in a sensitive area. As Corriere dello Sport points out, the English defender should have seen a second yellow card for unsporting behaviour.
