posts.title: Cristante: Roma ‘must improve’ but Man United penalty ‘very doubtful’
posts.excerpt: Roma midfielder Bryan Cristante insists the Giallorossi must ‘learn and improve’ after suffering another comeback...
posts.content:
Roma midfielder Bryan Cristante insists the Giallorossi must ‘learn and improve’ after suffering another comeback defeat, but feels the penalty awarded to Manchester United was ‘very doubtful.’

The Giallorossi wasted a two-goal lead at Old Trafford on Tuesday. They went 2-0 in the first 18 minutes, but conceded three times after the break, eventually falling to a 3-2 loss.

“We played great in the first half. We could have scored more than two goals, but obviously, the opponents are strong, too. Sometimes, when they push, it’s hard to contain them. Surely we had to do more, especially since we had already been there,” Cristante told Sky Sport Italia.

ISTANBUL, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 10: Bryan Cristante of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s first goal with teammate Mario Hermoso during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Fenerbahce SK and AS Roma at Fenerbahce Sükrü Saracoglu Spor Kompleksi on September 10, 2026 in Istanbul, Turkey. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images) READ MORE – Man United mock Roma with brutal tweet after comeback victory

It was their second defeat across all competitions this season. The previous one had come in a similar fashion in a home Champions League match against Real Madrid in October.

Even then, Roma wasted a two-goal lead, and the Merengues scored three goals in the dying minutes to secure a 4-3 victory at the Stadio Olimpico.

Manchester United bounced back early in the second half when Gianluca Mancini fouled Matheus Cunha, earning a penalty kick.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 03: Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United has his penalty saved by Devis Stiven Vasquez Llach of AS Roma during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 03, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images)“I didn’t see the penalty [replay], but from the field it seemed very doubtful to me,” Cristante said.

“When they are pumped up, they get really strong, so it’s hard to limit them. We have to look at it carefully and understand what we are getting wrong because it’s happening too frequently.”

The reporter suggested that one of Roma’s weaknesses might be their tendency to become less effective when they try to lower the game’s intensity.

“It could be. Surely we must be more focused at the back, as a full team,” Cristante argued.

NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Rasmus Hojlund of SSC Napoli battles for possession with Bryan Cristante of AS Roma during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)“We were leading 2-0 today. Sometimes you can drop deep and manage the game, leave the ball to the others, but without conceding goals.

“The first half in a stadium like this, against a strong team, is a positive thing,” the Italian midfielder concluded.

“They are not at their best, but they have strong players. We must learn that not everything is positive. We know we must improve in this. We’ll work on this and try to understand what we are getting wrong.”

Como have three unavailable players: Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah and Assane Diao.

posts.title: $15 Million Godzilla Movie Finds Sudden Resurgence on Digital Streaming
posts.excerpt: Takashi Yamazaki’s $15 million monster movie is quietly climbing digital charts again three years after its original release. Audiences are rushing to rent and stream the Oscar-winning film ahead of i
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Warner Bros. Pictures Takashi Yamazaki’s $15 million monster movie is quietly climbing digital charts again three years after its original release. Audiences are rushing to rent and stream the Oscar-winning film ahead of its highly anticipated upcoming sequel.

Godzilla Minus One is back on digital charts ahead of sequel

Takashi Yamazaki’s Godzilla Minus One has surged back on digital charts. The 2023 kaiju film currently sits at No. 4 on the iTunes Top Movies chart, according to PopVortex. Audiences are renting and purchasing the film to catch up ahead of its upcoming sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero.

Toho announced the sequel on November 3, 2025, with Yamazaki returning to write, direct, and handle visual effects. The studio has targeted a 2026 release window for the follow-up. Yamazaki confirmed at the 23rd Visual Effects Society Awards that storyboarding and scripting are already in progress.

The original film carried a reported budget of $15 million. It went on to gross $116 million worldwide, dethroning Shin Godzilla as the highest-grossing Japanese Godzilla film ever. The movie also became the highest-grossing Japanese-language film in U.S. box office history.

Godzilla Minus One won Best Visual Effects at the 96th Academy Awards. It became the first non-English language film to win in that category. The achievement was especially notable given the small visual effects team of just 35 artists at Shirogumi’s Chofu studio. Steven Spielberg praised the film and told Yamazaki he watched it multiple times across different formats.

The film stars Ryunosuke Kamiki as a former kamikaze pilot in postwar Japan. It earned a 99% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from 213 critics’ reviews. American audiences gave it an “A” CinemaScore grade during its theatrical run. The film also won eight awards at the 47th Japan Academy Film Prize, including Best Picture. Its digital resurgence now reflects sustained audience interest as anticipation builds for Godzilla Minus Zero.

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/2217643-godzilla-minus-one-dominating-on-digital-streaming-charts

posts.title: New $400M Horror Blockbuster Is Already No. 1 on Digital Streaming
posts.excerpt: A $400 million horror blockbuster just jumped to No. 1 on digital barely two weeks after leaving theaters. The video game adaptation claimed the top spot on iTunes’ movie rankings following its recent
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Sony Pictures Releasing A $400 million horror blockbuster just jumped to No. 1 on digital barely two weeks after leaving theaters. The video game adaptation claimed the top spot on iTunes’ movie rankings following its recent streaming debut.

Resident Evil is topping iTunes’ digital movie chart

Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil currently sits at No. 1 on the iTunes Top Movies chart. The horror reboot hit digital storefronts on November 3, following its theatrical run that began on September 18. According to PopVortex, the film’s iTunes rental price stands at $19.99, with a purchase price of $24.99.

The film stars Austin Abrams as Bryan, a medical courier who stumbles into a viral outbreak in Raccoon City. Kali Reis, Zach Cherry and Paul Walter Hauser round out the supporting cast. Constantin Film, PlayStation Productions and Vertigo Entertainment produced the project, with Sony Pictures handling distribution.

Resident Evil earned $60 million in its domestic opening weekend and has grossed $400 million worldwide against a $75 million budget. The debut set franchise records and marked Cregger’s highest-grossing film to date. It also became the highest-grossing entry in the entire Resident Evil film series.

Critics responded warmly to the reboot, making it the highest-rated video game adaptation on both Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic. Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film a B+ grade, the highest ever for a Resident Evil movie. The positive reception helped sustain the film’s commercial momentum through its theatrical window.

Cregger drew inspiration from the original games rather than previous film adaptations. He compared the project’s tone to Evil Dead II and called it a “love letter to the games.” The director created new characters instead of adapting existing ones from the franchise.

The crew shot the film in Prague between October 2025 and January 2026, with Dariusz Wolski handling cinematography. The digital release now gives the reboot a second commercial window beyond its theatrical run.

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/2217633-resident-evil-zach-cregger-digital-no-1-streaming-movie

posts.title: Corvus Glaive’s Weapon, Lisa’s Comics Form, & More VisionQuest Easter Eggs in Episode 7
posts.excerpt: VisionQuest episode 7 just dropped its biggest Avengers callback yet, and fans almost missed it. Here are all the major MCU Easter eggs, comic book references, and hidden details in the show’s penulti
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Marvel VisionQuest episode 7 just dropped its biggest Avengers callback yet, and fans almost missed it. Here are all the major MCU Easter eggs, comic book references, and hidden details in the show’s penultimate episode.

List of all major easter eggs from VisionQuest

VisionQuest episode 7, titled “Immolation,” delivers several major MCU callbacks and comic book references. The penultimate episode connects Vision’s present journey to key moments across the franchise’s history.

A Weapon From Wakanda’s Vault

Paladin reveals he possesses Corvus Glaive’s glaive at his hideout. Vision was impaled with this weapon at the start of Avengers: Infinity War. The Wakandans had kept the weapon since the events of that film, and Paladin stole it from them.

The Android’s Triple Identity

Paul Bettany plays three characters in this episode. He portrays Vision, inventor Phineas Horton, and Horton’s first AI creation, Jim Hammond. The reveal suggests Horton’s likeness influenced Vision’s appearance.

Hammond’s Fiery Fate Reimagined

The show changes Jim Hammond’s story from Marvel Comics. Hammond caught fire because he found love, which became his downfall. His creator, Phineas Horton, died alongside him in this version.

Horton’s Haunting Words

Phineas Horton tells Vision he will never know the consequence of love. He describes it as “sorrow, pain and valeting out for someone who can no longer hear you.” This echoes Vision’s famous line about grief being love persevering.

Ultron Channels His Inner Puppet Master

Ultron references Pinocchio again, continuing a pattern from earlier episodes. He tells Vision that Horton has “made you a real boy.” This adds to his previous “no strings” quips throughout the series.

A Letter to Tommy

Vision leaves Tommy a heartfelt message about his real past. He gives Tommy WandaVision to watch and references Wanda Maximoff’s iconic line. Wanda said in her series finale that “a family is forever.”

Lisa’s Robotic Arms Return

Lisa manifests robotic arms once again, echoing her transformation in episode 6. Her comic counterpart, Coat of Arms, gains four extra arms through the mystical Coat of Tiboro. The show replaces that magical origin with a technology-driven version.

The Butcher Bird Quotes Poe

Jocasta quotes “The Raven” by Edgar Allan Poe while revealing her nano-bot plan. Marvel Comics once published a mini-series adapting Poe’s works. A HYDRA character also shares the poet’s name in the comics.

A Comic-Accurate Upgrade

Vision suits up in a new costume during the episode. The suit features a comic-accurate collar and significantly more gold detailing than previous versions.

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/tv/news/2217625-visionquest-lisa-molinari-corvus-glaive-episode-7-easter-eggs

posts.title: Why Nancy Fuller Isn’t in Holiday Baking Championship: Replacement Rumors Explained
posts.excerpt: Viewers are curious to know why Nancy Fuller didn’t return to Holiday Baking Championship, a show she has been a part of since 12 seasons. Ongoing rumors suggest that she was quietly removed for two m
posts.content:
Photo Credit: @FoodNetwork / YouTube Viewers are curious to know why Nancy Fuller didn’t return to Holiday Baking Championship, a show she has been a part of since 12 seasons. Ongoing rumors suggest that she was quietly removed for two major reasons: financial considerations and fresh talent. Apart from this show, Fuller is also known as a judge on Clash of the Grandmas, Farmhouse Rules, and Spring Baking Championship.

Was Nancy Fuller replaced from Holiday Baking Championship?

Fuller has been replaced by Chef Molly Yeh as a judge on Holiday Baking Championship Season 13, which premiered November 2. The U.S. Sun addressed the alleged reason why Fuller abruptly left the show after being a judge for so many years. As per the report, Fuller’s hefty paycheck allegedly led to this decision as the executives look to hire younger replacements with lesser salary.

An insider said, “Letting Nancy go was partly the network’s decision, but Nancy understood. She is at the age where she needs to take care of herself and spend time with family.” They further mentioned that at present, Fuller is focused on her health and spending time with her loved ones. They touched upon how everyone at the network is appreciative of Nancy and how she has built a strong reputation over the years. However, they noted that this decision was “strictly business.”

“Nancy, being the amazing veteran judge that she is, is costly. The network wanted to find someone cheaper and younger. Cliche, but that’s how Hollywood still works. And they were able to find that with Molly [Yeh],” the insider further added.

Ahead of the new season’s premiere, Fuller took to Instagram to share how she’s celebrating her Halloween, posting a quick snap of the treats. She asked viewers how their Halloween was, as many took to the comment section to say they missed Fuller on the show while sharing thoughts about their celebrations.

posts.title: “The Legacy Continues”: 2Baba Announces New Album ‘Oldest Young Man’
posts.excerpt: 2Baba has announced his upcoming studio album, 'Oldest Young Man', scheduled for release on 27 November 2026. The project marks his first full-length album in six years since 2020's Warriors. The post
posts.content:
2Baba wearing a hooded black pleated drape and sunglasses to announce his studio album, Oldest Young Man.

Afrobeats icon 2Baba is officially returning with a full-length body of work, and November 27 is the date to mark in your calendars!

The legendary singer and songwriter—formerly known as 2Face Idibia—took to Instagram to announce his upcoming studio album, titled Oldest Young Man.

Taking to social media to share the exciting release date, the Afropop veteran captioned his post:

The legacy continues. OLDEST YOUNG MAN drops 27.11.26. Timeless music, no expiration date.

The announcement marks a huge moment for African music fans. Oldest Young Man is 2Baba’s first studio album in over six years, following his critically acclaimed 2020 project, Warriors, which featured heavyweights like Burna Boy, Wizkid, and Olamide.

While he hasn’t dropped a full-length album since then, the Nigerian music pioneer has remained active with steady releases, most recently dropping singles like “Mental” in September 2026 and “Ifesinachi” earlier in the year.

With over two decades at the top of the game—stretching from his days with Plantashun Boiz to solo anthems like “African Queen“—the legend is set to prove once again why his sound stands the test of time.

Oldest Young Man arrives on all streaming platforms on 27 November 2026.

2Baba posing in a draped black pleated outfit and black sunglasses ahead of his upcoming album, Oldest Young Man.

posts.title: Funke Akindele, Waje & Shoday’s London Looks Belong in Our Style Notes | See Photos
posts.excerpt: Funke Akindele, Waje, and Shoday stepped out in London in coordinated buba and iro sets and custom embroidery to announce the historic UK premiere of The Four: No One Fights Alone at ODEON Luxe Leices
posts.content:
Funke Akindele, Shoday, and Waje smiling during their London promotional walk ahead of The Four UK premiere.

Upon seeing these photos of Funke Akindele, Shoday and Waje, we had no choice but to pull out our notes, ready for some styling lessons. Did you see how they coordinated their looks for their London outing? Funke and Waje gave us matching buba and iro sets with colourful floral details, while Shoday arrived with a custom embroidered blazer that made its own case for a place in our style notes.

The trio were in the UK for the promotional campaign of The Four: No One Fights Alone, and the outing came with another exciting update. Funke Akindele Network and FilmOne Entertainment have announced that the film will have its UK premiere on 29 November at ODEON Luxe Leicester Square in London, ahead of its worldwide cinema release on 11 December.

Now, if you’re wondering how Funke and Waje managed to wear matching outfits without looking identical, the answer is in the details. Both looks started with off-white textured cotton, but the floral appliqués gave each one a distinct finish. Funke’s outfit features crimson-red roses with spiral stitching across the bodice and bell sleeves, while yellow sunflowers and leafy green stems run down her wrapper. She completed the look with a golden-yellow head wrap, layered gold necklaces, a broad cuff bracelet and metallic red platform sandals.

Funke Akindele Buba and Iro Outfit for The Four London Promo

Waje went for lavender roses across the neckline and sleeves of her blouse, with large green floral appliqués decorating the hem of her wrapper. She kept the colour story going with a matching lavender-trimmed scarf, a gold necklace accented with turquoise stones, coordinating earrings and multi-coloured platform heels. Same base colour, different floral story. We love that.

Waje outdoors in London promoting The Four: No One Fights Alone in a lavender floral buba and iro set.

And Shoday? He clearly had no plans to be the odd one out. His single-breasted blazer featured bold chevron embroidery in turquoise, yellow, red and blue, worn over a beige mesh-knit top and cream wide-leg trousers. Stacked silver Cuban-link chains and dark dress shoes completed the look, giving the colourful jacket room to do its thing.

Shoday in a custom geometric chevron-embroidered blazer during The Four promotional tour in London.

With the fashion notes taken, we’re also looking forward to seeing what the cast has in store for the London premiere. The Four: No One Fights Alone features Funke Akindele, Waje, Chioma Akpotha, Bisola Aiyeola, Richard Mofe-Damijo, Lateef Adedimeji, Timini Egbuson and Uzor Arukwe, among others. The film premieres at ODEON Luxe Leicester Square on 29 November before its global cinema release on 11 December.

Funke Akindele, Waje, and Shoday stepping out in London in coordinated buba and iro and custom tailoring ahead of The Four UK premiere at ODEON Luxe Leicester Square.

Waje, Shoday, and Funke Akindele on the streets of London during the promotional tour for The Four: No One Fights Alone.

posts.title: Toluwanisings: Oyo Police summon wife, father, friends as parties sign peace deal
posts.excerpt: The Oyo State Police Command has brokered peace between the family and associates of late Nigerian singer Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, following disagreements over his bur
posts.content:
The Oyo State Police Command has brokered peace between the family and associates of late Nigerian singer Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, following disagreements over his burial arrangements.

The intervention comes amid allegations of conspiracy, defamation of character and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace, which reportedly generated public exchanges between parties on social media and other communication platforms.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Command said the Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, received information about the dispute on October 28, 2026, and subsequently directed the parties to appear at the Command Headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, for an intervention.

The police said the meeting, which was held on November 3, resulted in the parties signing a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police.

Those involved included the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as his personal assistant and other representatives.

According to the statement, the parties agreed to maintain peace, exhibit good behaviour and refrain from actions capable of escalating tensions surrounding the singer’s death and burial arrangements.

The statement reads, “Consequently, at the conclusion of the engagement held today, 3rd November 2026, all parties, comprising the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; his friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as the deceased’s personal assistant and other representatives, entered into and signed a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police.

“Under the terms of the undertaking, all parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace, and discontinue public exchanges, interviews and discussions capable of inflaming tensions or aggravating the existing disagreement surrounding the unfortunate demise of the singer and related issues.

“Furthermore, the parties expressly undertook to discontinue the dissemination of information, narratives, allegations and publications relating to the matter through social media platforms, print media, radio, blogs and other communication channels, including publications made through their respective proxies, agents, associates and representatives. They equally agreed not to grant interviews, provide access or facilitate engagements with individuals or media platforms for the purpose of further disseminating such narratives. In addition, each party undertook to direct their respective proxies and associates to desist from making, sponsoring, amplifying or circulating publications capable of reigniting the disagreement or undermining the peace agreement.

“In reinforcing the terms of the undertaking, the Commissioner of Police warned that the agreement must be respected by all parties and extended to their proxies, agents, associates and representatives. He cautioned that no individual should take advantage of the unfortunate circumstances surrounding the singer’s demise to instigate hostility, promote unsubstantiated allegations or engage in conduct capable of disrupting public peace. Any person whose actions constitute an offence under applicable laws will be arrested and prosecuted accordingly.”

The Command also appealed to members of the public, bloggers and media practitioners to exercise restraint and avoid amplifying unverified information capable of reigniting tensions.

It urged all concerned to respect the commitments made during the peace meeting, adding that any conduct independently amounting to a criminal offence would be addressed in accordance with the law.

posts.title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri Unveils REVERIE, Its Spring/Summer 2027 Collection, Celebrating Reinvention in African Luxury

posts.content:
Ejiro Amos Tafiri, a Pan-African luxury fashion house founded in Lagos in 2010, has unveiled REVERIE, its Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, at an exclusive private showcase in Lagos on Sunday, October 25, 2026, held alongside Lagos Fashion Week.

The showcase brought together distinguished guests, fashion industry leaders, patrons and representatives of the British Council Nigeria, including chef and media personality Hilda Baci, for a presentation of the house’s latest collection.

REVERIE explores renewal and reinvention through contemporary African luxury. Bringing together expressive silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and a refined colour palette, the collection presents a visual statement that celebrates the evolving language of African fashion.

Through considered design and craftsmanship, REVERIE reflects the house’s continued exploration of contemporary African aesthetics, presenting pieces that balance creative expression with the distinctive design sensibility for which Ejiro Amos Tafiri is known.

Founded by designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri, known for her signature Drapes, the fashion house has spent 16 years developing a distinctive identity within the luxury fashion landscape. Its design language is characterized by expressive drapery, fluid tailoring and the thoughtful use of indigenous textiles, bringing African craftsmanship into contemporary fashion.

The Lagos unveiling followed the third edition of Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the British Council in Ikoyi, Lagos. The conference brought together designers, stylists, retail professionals and emerging creatives to discuss building sustainable careers and creating lasting impact within the fashion industry.

Together, the events reflect Ejiro Amos Tafiri’s continued engagement with the broader creative ecosystem, connecting fashion, education, craftsmanship and the development of emerging talent.

The REVERIE presentation forms part of the house’s 16-year milestone and will be followed by an exclusive showcase in Abuja on November 21, 2026. The forthcoming event will bring together members of the diplomatic community, government officials, fashion patrons and invited guests for a further presentation of the house’s work.

As Ejiro Amos Tafiri looks towards its next chapter, REVERIE embodies an ongoing exploration of renewal and reinvention, reinforcing the house’s commitment to advancing contemporary African luxury through expressive design and intricate craftsmanship.

posts.title: Pan-African School Games 2026: Celebrating Young Talent, School Pride and New Opportunities
posts.excerpt: The Pan-African School Games 2026 brought together young athletes from schools across Lagos for three days of swimming, athletics and football, celebrating sporting talent, school pride and the opport
posts.content:
The Pan-African School Games 2026 brought together young athletes from schools across Lagos for three days of swimming, athletics and football, celebrating sporting talent, school pride and the opportunities that organized competition can create for children and young people.

Held at James Hope College, Lekki, from 16 to 18 October, the second edition of the Games featured the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. Students competed for individual honours and school points while gaining valuable experience in a structured, multi-sport environment.

The competition also welcomed sporting stakeholders and scouts, reinforcing the wider ambition of the Pan-African School Games: to give young athletes a platform where their abilities can be demonstrated, recognized and developed.

Building on the Inaugural Games

The second edition of the Pan-African School Games built on the foundation established by the inaugural Games in 2025, continuing the vision of creating meaningful sporting opportunities for young athletes.

The 2026 edition welcomed schools and student-athletes for three days of swimming, athletics and football, providing a platform for competition, talent development and school pride.

Beyond the sporting results, the Games continued to advance a broader ambition: to connect schools, athletes, sporting stakeholders and educational institutions while creating opportunities for young people to develop their abilities and explore future pathways through sport.

Day One: Swimming Opens the Games

Swimming opened the competition, bringing young swimmers together for races across the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories.

The opening day set the pace for the Games as athletes took to the pool to test their abilities, pursue strong performances and earn points for their schools. The races highlighted the preparation, discipline and technique required to compete, while providing young swimmers with valuable experience in a formal sporting environment.

For many of the students, the opportunity to compete alongside athletes from other schools added to the significance of the experience. Each race contributed to the overall competition, with schools beginning their campaigns for medals and category honours.

Day Two: Athletics Puts Young Athletes to the Test

Athletics took centre stage on the second day, with track and field events testing the speed, strength, coordination and technique of the young competitors.

Athletes competed in running, jumping and throwing events, earning points for their schools as the standings developed. Each discipline presented a different challenge, giving students opportunities to demonstrate their abilities and compete for individual and team honours.

The athletics programme added another dimension to the Games, highlighting the variety of talent within the participating schools and the value of giving young athletes opportunities to develop through competition.

Day Three: Football and the Closing Ceremony

Football completed the sporting programme on the final day, with school teams competing for their last honours across the age categories.

The matches brought the three-day competition to its conclusion, with the closing ceremony recognizing the achievements of the participating schools and their athletes.

One of the major highlights was the presentation of a brand-new school bus to Grange School, sponsored by Mikano Changan Motors. The prize recognised Grange School’s overall victories in the U-13 and U-15 categories and represented a significant reward for the school’s performance across the Games.

The presentation was a memorable part of the closing ceremony, giving the competition a lasting highlight beyond the medals and results.

Recognizing the Schools and Their Achievements

The final results reflected strong performances across swimming, athletics and football.

Grange School secured the overall titles in the U-13 and U-15 categories, while St. Saviour’s School, Ikoyi, won the overall U-11 title.

Grange School’s performances across the U13 category earned it the overall prize sponsored by Mikano Changan Motors. St. Saviour’s School’s success in the U-11 category also highlighted the competitive strength of the younger athletes.

The results reflected the contributions of students across the participating schools, many of whom competed in multiple events and disciplines. They also reinforced the importance of consistent preparation, teamwork and participation in structured sporting activities.

School representatives celebrate their achievements at the Pan-African School Games 2026 closing ceremony.

Scouts and Opportunities Beyond Competition

A particularly important aspect of the 2026 Games was the presence of scouts, brought to the event by Plumptre Advisory.

Their attendance strengthened the talent-identification dimension of the competition, creating opportunities for promising young athletes to be observed in a competitive setting. For students with sporting potential, being seen by relevant stakeholders can be an important step in exploring future development opportunities.

The involvement of Plumptre Advisory also reflects the broader ambition of the Pan-African School Games to connect school sport with educational and developmental pathways. Through its links with international schools and its work around educational opportunities, Plumptre Advisory contributes to conversations about how young people can pursue their academic goals while continuing to develop their sporting abilities.

Participation in the Games does not automatically guarantee selection, scholarships or placements. However, bringing scouts and education-focused stakeholders into the same environment as young athletes creates valuable opportunities for promising talent to be recognized and for further conversations to begin.

This is an important part of the long-term vision for the Pan-African School Games. The competition is intended to provide more than a few days of sporting activity; it is being developed as a platform that can help young people discover their abilities, build confidence and explore possibilities for their future.

A Lasting Prize for Grange School

The presentation of a new school bus to Grange School was among the defining moments of the 2026 edition.

Sponsored by Mikano Changan Motors, the bus was awarded in recognition of Grange School’s overall victories in the U-13 category. Its practical value to the school community made the award particularly significant, extending the impact of the competition beyond the event itself.

The prize also demonstrated how corporate support can contribute to school communities in tangible ways. In this instance, the sponsorship recognized sporting achievement while providing a resource that could support the school’s wider activities.

Grange School received a new school bus sponsored by Mikano Changan Motors after winning the overall U-13 and U-15 titles at the Pan-African School Games 2026.

Bringing the Competition to a Wider Audience

Team 33 Productions supported the Games through live streaming and event coverage, helping audiences follow the competition and preserving key moments from the three days.

The coverage made the sporting action more accessible to people who could not attend in person. It also created a record of the performances, school participation and award presentations that defined the 2026 edition.

Media coverage plays an important role in building awareness of school sport. It allows the achievements of young athletes to reach a wider audience and gives schools, families and other stakeholders an opportunity to revisit and share the experience.

Team 33 Productions’ contribution helped document the Games and communicate the scale and energy of the competition beyond the venue.

The Partners Supporting the Games

Delivering a multi-sport competition involving schools, young athletes, coaches, officials and spectators requires the support of organisations that believe in the value of youth sport.

The Pan-African School Games 2026 was supported by Plumptre Advisory, Kantar, Flutterwave, Flytime, Nigerian Exchange Group, Mikano Changan Motors, Logic City, Prime Atlantic, Team 33 Productions, UAC Foods and Zenith Bank.

Their support formed part of the wider effort to deliver the competition and strengthen its development as a platform for school sport.

The Games also received support from the Lagos State Government and the Lagos State Sports Commission, reflecting the importance of collaboration among organisers, businesses and public-sector stakeholders in creating opportunities for young athletes.

The contributions of these partners supported the event’s delivery and helped sustain the ambition of growing the Pan-African School Games over time.

The People Behind the Pan-African School Games

The Pan-African School Games is led by co-founders Dr. Seun Akinbohun, Dr. Busola Tejumola and Aderoju Ope-Ajayi, whose work continues to advance the vision of a stronger platform for school sport.

The co-founders of the Pan-African School Games: Dr. Busola Tejumola, Dr. Seun Akinbohun and Aderoju Ope-Ajayi.

Their work centres on creating meaningful sporting opportunities for young people and strengthening the connections between schools, athletes and the wider sporting community.

Looking Ahead

The Pan-African School Games 2026 brought together competition, school pride, talent identification and support from a broad network of partners. The presence of scouts, the recognition of outstanding school performances and the presentation of the sponsored school bus all contributed to the story of an event seeking to create opportunities beyond the playing field.

As the Games continue to develop, the ambition is to welcome more schools and athletes, expand participation and strengthen pathways for young people who want to pursue their sporting potential.

The 2026 edition reinforced the importance of giving young athletes a platform where they can compete, grow and be recognized. It also demonstrated the value of collaboration among schools, sponsors, sporting stakeholders and the wider community.

The next chapter of the Pan-African School Games will build on this foundation, with a continued focus on young talent and the role school sport can play in shaping future opportunities.

posts.title: Afrique Femme & CANEX WKND 2026 Partner to Celebrate Francophone Fashion, Culture, and Female Leadership in Lagos
posts.excerpt: From November 5 to 8, 2026, Lagos will become the epicenter of African creativity as Afrique Femme brings the 6th edition of the Brunch des AfricanWoman2.0 to CANEX WKND 2026 at the iconic Wole Soyink
posts.content:
From November 5 to 8, 2026, Lagos will become the epicenter of African creativity as Afrique Femme brings the 6th edition of the Brunch des AfricanWoman2.0 to CANEX WKND 2026 at the iconic Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture & Creative Arts.

Organized by Afreximbank in collaboration with the African Union and the AfCFTA Secretariat, Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX WKND) is Africa’s premier event celebrating the continent’s creative and cultural industries. Under the overarching theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World: From FESTAC ’77 to CANEX ’27,” this year’s gathering will connect thousands of creative entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers, and cultural icons from across Global Africa and the diaspora.

Spotlighting Francophone Luxury & Made-in-Africa Fashion

As part of this landmark event, Afrique Femme is hosting a dedicated Exhibition Pavilion designed to bridge Francophone and Anglophone creative ecosystems. The pavilion will feature curated showcases, pop-ups, and private sales from leading West and Central African designers. Attendees will experience exclusive collections from celebrated brands including Makeda by AYA Konan,, KUMI, KWELAKU, and Galipette Atelier, highlighting the richness, craftsmanship, and global potential of Francophone fashion.

The African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch

A core highlight of the week will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026, with the African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch. Bringing together 200 to 250 influential women leaders, policymakers, innovators, and international dignitaries, the high-level gathering will feature keynote addresses, strategic panels, and structured B2B networking aimed at fostering female leadership and economic empowerment across the continent.

posts.title: ‘I’m sorry for my words’ — Blessing CEO begs Nigerians for forgiveness
posts.excerpt: Nigerian social media personality, Blessing CEO, has apologised to Nigerians over her past comments and actions, saying she regrets speaking about other people’s pain without understanding what they w
posts.content:
Nigerian social media personality, Blessing CEO, has apologised to Nigerians over her past comments and actions, saying she regrets speaking about other people’s pain without understanding what they were going through.

The influencer broke down in tears in a video shared on Tuesday, November 3, days after regaining her freedom from detention and following the death of her son, Brian.

In the emotional video she posted on her IG page, she described herself as broken and exhausted, admitting that she had learnt her lessons the hard way.

“I’m so sorry for speaking about the pain I’ve never felt. I’m realising that talk is cheap. Action speaks louder than voice,” she said.

Blessing’s apology comes amid renewed scrutiny of her controversial public statements, including her comments during the domestic violence dispute involving late Bimbo Ogbonna and her husband, IVD, as well as her repeated criticism of May Edochie during her marital crisis.

She also faced widespread backlash in 2026 after claiming she had stage four breast cancer and soliciting donations from the public. The fundraising appeal became controversial after questions were raised about the medical report she presented. She later clarified that she did not have a confirmed stage four diagnosis.

In the video, Blessing also remembered her late son, whom she affectionately called “Doom Doom”, saying she missed him and was determined to make amends.

“I miss you, Brian. I miss you so much, and I promise to correct every wrong,” she said.

She further disclosed that her mother had been struggling with the loss, revealing that they sometimes hid from each other to cry.

Describing her apology as a decision to retrace her steps, Blessing likened herself to the biblical prodigal son, saying she was ready to return home and start afresh.

“I’m not ashamed of coming back home. I just want to find my way back,” she added.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/im-sorry-for-my-words-blessing-ceo-begs-nigerians-for-forgiveness/

posts.title: Video: ‘Let Toluwanisings have a befitting burial’ – Woli Arole makes appeal
posts.excerpt: Comedian and preacher Woli Arole has appealed to those involved in the burial dispute surrounding late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, to allow him a befitting
posts.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Comedian and preacher Woli Arole has appealed to those involved in the burial dispute surrounding late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, to allow him a befitting burial, urging them to end what he described as unnecessary public arguments.

Arole made the appeal in a video shared on Instagram on Monday, describing the late singer as a great talent whose death had left friends and colleagues grieving.

“I want to speak on behalf of Toluwanisings’ demise, and this is what God asked me to say. We’ve lost a great guy, a great gift to a generation. Even we, his friends and colleagues, have not recovered. For some of us, he is so close to us, and his death is really painful. A big elephant has gone,” he said.

He also criticised people he accused of using the controversy to attract attention on social media, saying public discussion should instead focus on Toluwanisings’ wife and children.

“It’s saddening and sad that a lot of people are now beginning to want to start to use it as a means for social media traction. You are m***. I have a right to say it. A young man had died in almost his prime, and the discussion is not even about the wife left behind and two kids? No. What you want to start doing is unlicensed, ungoverned, unnecessary talk, interviews and nonsense. A lot of people speaking about him this way never spoke about him while he was alive, about his music, please, please,” Arole said.

He urged those involved to let the burial arrangements proceed and allow the singer to be laid to rest with dignity.

“This is why it is a burden in my spirit, and I have to speak, and this is what the Lord is laying in my heart. The Bible says: Let the dead bury their dead. Whatever process, anything that needs to be done within that corner, let it be done. Let the young man be given a befitting burial,” he said.

View this post on Instagram

Woli Arole added that the burial dispute could not erase the singer’s musical legacy and called on the public to support his family and preserve his work through his children.

“Nobody can ruin his legacy; he lived a good life, please. He sang songs that are eternal; his songs rang in our hearts. Whichever way he is buried, Toluwanisings is in our hearts forever; his sound is forever. So, please, I want to beg us in the name of Jesus, you should focus our energy on what is left: how his legacy will be preserved in his children and the wife,” he said.

He concluded: “God bless Toluwanisings’ legacy, God bless his wife and his children, let the noise and unnecessary nonsense die down in the name of Jesus.”

Toluwanisings’ family announced that the singer died in the early hours of October 14, 2026, but did not disclose the cause of death.

The singer’s burial arrangements have drawn public attention following disagreements over where he should be laid to rest.

Vanguard previously reported that a family representative rejected a cemetery burial and threatened to exhume the singer’s remains if he were buried there. His paternal grandmother also said she opposed a cemetery burial and wanted him buried at his home.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/video-let-toluwanisings-have-a-befitting-burial-woli-arole-tells-family/

posts.title: ‘Give Regina breathing space,’ Ned Nwoko appeals to fans, threatens legal action
posts.excerpt: Senator Ned Nwoko has appealed to the public, particularly fans and friends of his estranged wife, Nollywood actress Regina Daniels, to give her space to recover, warning that those spreading false re
posts.content:
Senator Ned Nwoko has appealed to the public, particularly fans and friends of his estranged wife, Nollywood actress Regina Daniels, to give her space to recover, warning that those spreading false reports about her could face legal action.

Nwoko made the appeal in a statement shared on his Instagram page, expressing concern over what he described as the circulation of fabricated death announcements, misleading reports and hurtful content about the actress.

He said the appeal was not only for Daniels but also for their children, who, according to him, deserve to see their mother supported and given every opportunity to recover.

“I want to make a sincere appeal to the public, particularly Regina’s fans, friends, bloggers and social media commentators, to please give Regina some breathing space,” he said.

The senator said Daniels had been through a lot and needed love, support and an opportunity to heal rather than public criticism.

“Regina has been through a lot, more than many people may realise, and right now, what she needs most is love, support and the opportunity to recover.”

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Senator Prince Ned Nwoko (@princenednwoko)

He also referenced a video Daniels shared on her birthday, saying it offered a glimpse into some of the health challenges she had been dealing with.

According to him, her situation should not be an opportunity for people to judge or vilify her.

Nwoko further said her well-being had always been important to him, adding that concerns about her welfare contributed to the decision to bring aspects of their private situation into the public domain.

He expressed particular concern over reports falsely announcing the actress’s death and other claims about her health and personal circumstances.

“These things are not harmless social media engagement. Regina sees many of these posts, and they are deeply distressing. They do nothing to support her recovery, rather, they add to the burden she is already carrying,” he said.

The lawmaker urged the actress’s supporters to discourage the spread of such reports rather than amplify them.

He also warned bloggers and social media users against deliberately publishing false information about Daniels, particularly claims concerning her death, health and personal life.

“We are documenting these publications, and anyone found responsible will be held accountable through the appropriate legal channels,” he said.

Nwoko added that Daniels deserved the opportunity to recover without being subjected to fabricated reports and renewed public scrutiny.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/give-regina-breathing-space-ned-nwoko-appeals-to-fans-threatens-legal-action/

posts.title: ‘Tinubu Must Go’ chant rings out at ADC rally in Sokoto
posts.excerpt: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The slogan, “Tinubu Must Go,” reverberated across the venue of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto on Wednesday, as supporters of
posts.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

The slogan, “Tinubu Must Go,” reverberated across the venue of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto on Wednesday, as supporters of the opposition party expressed opposition to President Bola Tinubu’s administration ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The chant echoed repeatedly among supporters gathered along Illorin Road in Sokoto metropolis, where the party’s presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, was expected to address the rally.

Many of the supporters, who reportedly travelled from different parts of the state, chanted the slogan in calls for political change and an end to the current administration.

The protest slogan also reflected the grievances expressed by some opposition supporters over the economic challenges and security concerns confronting the country.

The rally provided a platform for the ADC to mobilise its supporters and communicate its political message as opposition parties intensify activities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The development also highlighted the party’s efforts to expand its grassroots support in Sokoto State and challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

However, as of the time of filing this report, the ADC presidential campaign train was yet to arrive at the rally venue from the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto, reportedly due to the large crowd that had gathered along the route.

The party’s campaign flag-off is part of its nationwide mobilisation ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinubu-must-go-chant-rings-out-at-adc-rally-in-sokoto/

posts.title: 2027: No coalition needed in Ondo, APC elders declare
posts.excerpt: Target one million votes for Tinubu, 80% turnout By Dayo Johnson, Akure The PBAT Mandate Elders Forum (PMF), Ondo State chapter, has declared that there is no need for a coalition arrangement in the s
posts.content:
Target one million votes for Tinubu, 80% turnout

By Dayo Johnson, Akure

The PBAT Mandate Elders Forum (PMF), Ondo State chapter, has declared that there is no need for a coalition arrangement in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the All Progressives Congress (APC) is strong enough to win all elective positions.

The Forum also set a target of at least one million votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, alongside an 80 per cent voter turnout in the state.

The position was made known at a meeting of the Forum in Akure, the state capital, where its chairman, Hon. Demola Ijabiyi, said the APC’s dominance in the state made any arrangement requiring it to surrender candidates or constituencies unnecessary.

Ijabiyi said the Forum recognised the importance of cooperation among political parties with shared political objectives but maintained that such arrangements must reflect the political realities of individual states.

“In Ondo State, the APC is the dominant political party, controlling government at both the state and local government levels,” he said.

He said the Forum welcomed support from other political parties for Tinubu’s re-election but would not accept any arrangement that required APC candidates to step down.

“Support for the President need not depend on displacing APC candidates. We have confidence in our candidates and their prospects of victory,” he said.

According to him, coalition arrangements are more appropriate in states where political parties have limited electoral strength and need to combine forces to overcome their weaknesses.

He explained that parties could support stronger candidates in constituencies where they lacked sufficient electoral strength in exchange for reciprocal support elsewhere.

“But we don’t have that kind of circumstance in Ondo State. There is no constituency that we cannot win. There is no constituency that we do not want to contest. We are going to win all. That is the bottom line,” he said.

The Forum chairman also cited the declining political strength of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), which he described as the major opposition party in the state in the past, as another reason the APC should not surrender its electoral interests.

On mobilisation, Ijabiyi said the Forum was working towards extending its structures to every ward and polling unit to mobilise voters and secure victory for Tinubu and all APC candidates.

He said Ondo State’s more than two million registered voters ahead of the 2027 governorship election presented a significant electoral opportunity, adding that the challenge was to translate the figure into actual voter participation.

“We have therefore set a voter turnout target of at least 80 per cent. The PMF will work towards this through sustained mobilisation and voter education. Alongside this, we must earn sufficient support to deliver at least one million votes for the President,” he said.

Ijabiyi directed the Forum’s chapters to develop practical grassroots mobilisation plans, assign responsibilities and provide regular reports on their activities.

He said meetings and political endorsements must translate into measurable engagement with voters in communities across the state.

The chairman also urged APC National and State Assembly candidates to intensify their campaigns, identify areas of weak mobilisation and work with local party leaders to strengthen support at the polling-unit level.

He said candidates should engage voters directly, explain their legislative priorities and demonstrate how their election would advance the interests of their constituencies.

Ijabiyi further urged the candidates to promote Tinubu’s re-election and support the campaigns of other APC candidates, stressing that victory would depend on effective coordination among party structures and support groups.

The Forum reaffirmed its commitment to Tinubu’s re-election and the victory of all APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

It also pledged to collaborate with the party leadership, candidates, the Campaign Council and other support groups to mobilise support for the President ahead of his planned reception in the state on November 11.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027-no-coalition-needed-in-ondo-apc-elders-declare/

posts.title: US Midterm Voters Deliver Brutal Verdict On Trump
posts.excerpt: The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept into his Republican heartland, boosted by anger at soaring energy costs and his costly, dragging war with Ira
posts.content:
Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape on Wednesday after US voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to his presidency.

The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept into his Republican heartland, boosted by anger at soaring energy costs and his costly, dragging war with Iran.

The Democratic capture of both the Senate and the House of Representatives signals an end to Trump’s stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, launch investigations into Trump’s administration and thwart his appointments.

The results reflected deep frustration over the cost of living, tariffs and Trump’s war with Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president.

“This is so incredibly exciting. We can get our country back,” Kathy Jackoway said in Texas, celebrating a win by Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico.

Trump struck a conciliatory tone despite his history of rejecting election defeats, telling The New York Times he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results.

“I think the Democrats did a good job,” the 80-year-old told Fox News, in rare praise for his political opponents. “They fought hard.”

Combo image of Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (r) and President of the U.S Donald Trump (l)

But he sought to distance himself from his party’s poor showing, adding: “I don’t view it as a hit on me.”

He acknowledged that the Iran conflict had contributed to the result but defended the military campaign, and he suggested the rival parties could find common ground on immigration.

Republican Heartland

Democrats flipped seats that had long been held by Republicans, scoring breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine.

In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins.

In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932.

Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008.

In Texas, Democrats won not only a Senate seat but also the governor’s race, ending decades of Republican rule.

Democrats protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire.

In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curveball when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers.

In the House, Democrats made gains in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had carried comfortably in 2024.

Democrats also won Georgia’s governorship, electing former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms as the first Black woman governor in US history.

Republicans had some consolation in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds became the state’s first Black governor and Ashley Moody retained a Senate seat.

But the night was “a big wipeout and a strong repudiation of Donald Trump and his policies,” George Washington University professor Todd Belt told AFP.

Trump On Defensive

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries declared Trump’s MAGA movement “on the run.”

Jeffries could become the first Black speaker of the House when the new Congress convenes in January.

Trump insisted on social media that Republicans would have won “IN A LANDSLIDE” if he had been running, though he had repeatedly urged supporters throughout the campaign to “pretend I’m on the ballot.”

He also repeated his threat to use the presidential veto on Democrat-passed bills, posting a picture on social media of a red baseball cap reading just: “VETO.”

On the international front, Russia said it hoped Trump will continue his “peacemaking efforts” and China said it would “continue working” with the United States.

Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said he did not expect the election results to bring about a shift in US policy.

AFP

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/11/04/us-midterm-voters-deliver-brutal-verdict-on-trump/

posts.title: Police warn politicians against destroying campaign materials
posts.excerpt: …IGP orders commissioners to arrest, prosecute offenders By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has warned politicians, political thugs and other individuals against the destruction or defacemen
posts.content:
…IGP orders commissioners to arrest, prosecute offenders

By Kingsley Omonobi

The Nigeria Police Force has warned politicians, political thugs and other individuals against the destruction or defacement of campaign posters, banners and billboards belonging to candidates and political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Force said offenders would be arrested and prosecuted, warning that political differences or loyalty to a particular party did not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s campaign materials.

Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, saying the police had observed with concern growing incidents of deliberate tearing, defacement and destruction of campaign materials across the country.

The statement read: “The Nigeria Police Force strongly condemns this act of political intolerance and warns political thugs, hoodlums and other mischief-makers involved to desist immediately.

“For the avoidance of doubt, destroying, defacing or unlawfully removing another candidate’s campaign posters and billboards may constitute malicious damage, which is a criminal offence under applicable criminal laws, including Section 451 of the Criminal Code Act and Section 326 of the Penal Code Law, which defines the offence of mischief.

“Political differences or loyalty to a particular party do not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s property or infringe on their right to campaign freely.

“The Force reiterates that all political parties and candidates, irrespective of their affiliation or status, are entitled to equal protection under the law.

“No individual or group has the right to determine whose campaign materials should be displayed or destroyed.”

The police said the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, had directed commissioners of police in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to take proactive measures to prevent such incidents.

He also directed them to investigate reported cases and ensure that anyone found culpable was arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law.

The statement added that political sponsors and individuals who recruited, encouraged or facilitated the destruction of campaign materials would also be held accountable where evidence established their involvement.

The Force urged political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct their campaigns peacefully and respect the rights of others.

It warned that political intolerance, intimidation and criminal conduct must not be allowed to undermine the democratic process.

“The Nigeria Police Force will not allow political thugs and troublemakers to turn the nation’s political environment into a theatre of lawlessness. Those who choose to break the law will face the full consequences of their actions. “Be warned. Respect the law. Let democracy thrive,” the statement added.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/police-warn-politicians-against-destroying-campaign-materials/

posts.title: Police confirm death of girl allegedly pushed from two-storey building
posts.excerpt: … Suspect to face murder charge By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — The Imo State Police Command has confirmed the death of 17-year-old Chiamaka Chukwuokore, who was allegedly pushed from a two-storey building
posts.content:
… Suspect to face murder charge

By Chidi Nkwopara

OWERRI — The Imo State Police Command has confirmed the death of 17-year-old Chiamaka Chukwuokore, who was allegedly pushed from a two-storey building in Owerri.

The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), Mr Henry Okoye, confirmed the development in a statement yesterday, disclosing that the 26-year-old suspect, Ifeanyi Chukwu Joseph, would now face a murder allegation following the victim’s death.

Okoye said the incident occurred on November 1, 2026, along Mbonu Ejike Street, Ikeneagbu, Owerri.

He said the suspect remained in police custody as investigations continued to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

“Following the victim’s death, the suspect is now facing a murder allegation. He remains in police custody as investigations continue to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that justice is served,” he said.

The police spokesman said the Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, commiserated with the family of the deceased and assured that a thorough investigation was ongoing.

The Command also urged members of the public to remain calm, avoid spreading unverified information and allow the police to carry out their duties professionally.

Vanguard recalls that in an earlier statement following the incident, Okoye said the victim sustained serious injuries and was rushed to a nearby hospital, where she was receiving treatment in critical condition.

He also disclosed that an angry mob had attempted to lynch the suspect but police operatives intervened and rescued him before taking him into custody.

posts.title: State Police Bill to reach Tinubu for assent today — Reps
posts.excerpt: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The State Police Bill, seeking to decentralise policing responsibilities between the Federal and state governments, will be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu on
posts.content:
By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja

ABUJA — The State Police Bill, seeking to decentralise policing responsibilities between the Federal and state governments, will be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday for assent.

The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, disclosed this while presiding over plenary, following the approval of the proposed constitutional amendment by 29 of the 36 State Houses of Assembly.

Kalu expressed excitement over the endorsement of the proposed police reform by more than two-thirds of the state legislatures, describing the development as a major step towards the establishment of state police in Nigeria.

“The State Police Bill has received the backing of 29 State Assemblies. Later today, the Clerk to the National Assembly will transmit it to the President for assent,” he said.

The approval by the state assemblies marks a significant milestone in efforts to amend the Constitution to allow states to establish and manage their own police forces alongside the Nigeria Police Force.

The proposed reform is aimed at addressing concerns over Nigeria’s centralised policing structure, which critics argue limits the capacity of security agencies to respond effectively to local security challenges.

Under the proposed arrangement, state governments would have greater responsibility for policing within their jurisdictions, while the Federal Government would retain its own police structure.

The reform is expected to allow states to develop policing strategies tailored to their security needs, with the aim of strengthening intelligence gathering, community-based security and responses to crime.

The transmission of the bill to the President marks the next stage in the constitutional amendment process, following its passage by the National Assembly and approval by the required number of state legislatures.

The proposed establishment of state police has remained a major issue in Nigeria’s security reform debate, with supporters advocating decentralised policing as a means of improving security management across the country.

posts.title: Army rewards soldier N500,000 for rejecting kidnap suspect’s bribe
posts.excerpt: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The General Officer Commanding (GOC), 3 Division of the Nigerian Army and Commander of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), Major General Maxwell Dangana, has rewarded a soldier, Pri
posts.content:
By Golok Nanmwa

JOS — The General Officer Commanding (GOC), 3 Division of the Nigerian Army and Commander of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), Major General Maxwell Dangana, has rewarded a soldier, Private Utim Terwase, with N500,000 for rejecting an alleged bribe offered by a suspected notorious kidnapper.

Military sources said Terwase apprehended the suspect following an attempted escape but rejected money allegedly offered in exchange for his release and subsequently handed him over to the appropriate authorities.

Confirming the development, the spokesman for Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, said the reward was presented on behalf of the GOC by the Commander of Sector 6, Colonel Philimon Malgwi.

Oteh said Dangana, who spoke through Malgwi during the presentation, commended the soldier for demonstrating honesty, discipline and professionalism.

He said: “The soldier’s conduct reflects the highest standards of military professionalism, loyalty and commitment to duty expected of personnel of the Nigerian Army.

“Rather than compromise his responsibility for personal gain, he upheld the values of honesty, accountability and selfless service by discharging his duties responsibly.”

The GOC said the N500,000 reward was in recognition of the soldier’s integrity and commitment to duty, adding that the amount was equivalent to the bribe he reportedly rejected.

“Operation Enduring Peace therefore considers Private Terwase’s action worthy of commendation and encourages all personnel to emulate his exemplary conduct,” he said.

Dangana added that the recognition reinforced the operation’s commitment to promoting accountability, ethical conduct and professionalism among its personnel.

He said the military would continue to encourage personnel to discharge their constitutional responsibilities with integrity, discipline and dedication.

Crude oil and condensate production stood at 1.70 million barrels per day, while natural gas output reached 7,789 million standard cubic feet per day.

On Wednesday afternoon, NNPCL retail outlets in Abuja reduced fuel pump price to N1,315 per litre from between N1,370 and N1,405.

posts.title: 2027: Police warn politicians, supporters against destroying campaign posters, billboards
posts.excerpt: The Nigeria Police Force has warned politicians, political supporters and suspected thugs against the destruction, defacement or unlawful removal of campaign posters, banners and billboards belonging
posts.content:
The Nigeria Police Force has warned politicians, political supporters and suspected thugs against the destruction, defacement or unlawful removal of campaign posters, banners and billboards belonging to rival candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The police said incidents of deliberate damage to campaign materials were becoming a growing concern across the country, describing the practice as an act of political intolerance capable of undermining peaceful political participation.

In a statement issued by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, the police condemned the activities of political thugs, hoodlums and other individuals involved in destroying campaign materials, urging them to desist immediately.

The Force stressed that political disagreements or allegiance to a particular party do not give anyone the right to damage another candidate's property or prevent opponents from exercising their democratic rights.

It explained that the destruction, defacement or unlawful removal of campaign materials could amount to malicious damage, a criminal offence punishable under applicable laws.

The police specifically referenced Section 451 of the Criminal Code Act and Section 326 of the Penal Code Law, which provide for offences relating to malicious damage and mischief.

According to the statement, all political parties and candidates, regardless of their political affiliations or status, are entitled to equal protection under the law.

The Force maintained that no individual or group has the authority to decide which candidate's campaign materials should be displayed or removed through unlawful means.

The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has consequently directed Commissioners of Police across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to take proactive steps to prevent further incidents.

The IGP also ordered the police commissioners to investigate reported cases and ensure that anyone found responsible is arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law.

The police further warned that political sponsors and individuals who recruit, encourage or provide support for those involved in destroying campaign materials would also face accountability if evidence establishes their involvement.

The Force urged political parties, candidates and their supporters to embrace peaceful campaigns and respect the rights of political opponents as preparations for the 2027 general elections gather momentum.

It warned that political intolerance, intimidation and other criminal activities would not be allowed to threaten the country's democratic process.

Reaffirming its determination to maintain law and order, the police declared that political thugs and troublemakers would not be allowed to turn the nation's political environment into a theatre of lawlessness.

The statement concluded with a warning that anyone who violates the law would face the full consequences of their actions.

The troops subsequently proceeded to the Kumala checkpoint and continued their security operations.

No casualty was recorded during the operation.
