posts.excerpt: FOX Corporation is partnering with U.S.VETS for the "Make Camo Your Cause" campaign for the sixth straight year to help end veteran homelessness.
posts.content:
Fox News Channel viewers can once again expect to see a lot of camouflage through Veterans Day on Nov. 11.

Fox Corporation is partnering with U.S.VETS for the "Make Camo Your Cause" campaign for the sixth straight year to help end veteran homelessness because too many American heroes who bravely served our country find themselves sleeping on the streets they swore to protect.

The "Make Camo Your Cause" campaign is dedicated to ending veteran homelessness in the United States because "veterans" and "homelessness" should never be uttered in the same sentence.

Fox News Channel hosts and anchors will wear camo to show appreciation and gratitude for veterans and their military service while raising awareness and funds to propel U.S.VETS' mission. Viewers can pick up Fox News-branded camo gear in the online store and wear it proudly on Veterans Day to show support for U.S. veterans.

DONATE TO ‘MAKE CAMO YOUR CAUSE’ HERE

FOX is the founding media sponsor of the campaign, which aims to bring visibility and awareness to the tragic issue in the United States while transforming what it means to wear camo here at home. The past five years have been wildly successful and resulted in significant donations to U.S.VETS and greater awareness of the critical work it does.

Viewers can make camo their cause by donating or shopping online here because veterans deserve every opportunity to live with dignity and independence, not on the streets.

The "Make Camo Your Cause" campaign offers a variety of camouflage products — from hats and T-shirts to mugs and duffel bags — designed to create awareness of the U.S.VETS Mission.

Every purchase helps veterans and their families successfully transition to civilian life by providing housing, counseling, career development and other critical support.

DONATE TO ‘MAKE CAMO YOUR CAUSE’ HERE

"Make Camo Your Cause" will also appear in on-screen graphics and across Fox News social media platforms and Fox News Digital.

Founded in 1993, U.S.VETS is now the largest nonprofit with boots on the ground fighting America’s veteran homelessness crisis. It provides housing, counseling, supportive services and career programs, in addition to supportive services for veterans to rebuild and thrive.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/media/fox-usvets-renew-make-camo-your-cause-campaign-dedicated-ending-veteran-homelessness

posts.title: Republicans turn on Trump after devastating midterm losses hand Democrats control of Congress
posts.excerpt: GOP insiders blame Trump after Election Night's blue tsunami flipped both chambers, with Democrats scoring seven Senate and 27 House pickups.
posts.content:
Seismic political change is coming to Washington, D.C., and as Republicans sift through the wreckage that was Election Night, fingers are pointing in several directions over who’s to blame.

The blue tsunami Tuesday tore the GOP’s coalition asunder, flipping the balance of power in both chambers heading into the final two years of the Trump administration. And as Republicans search for where things went awry, GOP operatives and insiders told Fox News Digital that it starts at the top with President Donald Trump.

"Look, first and foremost, this is a Trump loss," Dan Eberhart, an oil drilling chief executive officer and prominent Republican donor, told Fox News Digital. "He wanted to be — he wanted people to consider him on the ballot. And unfortunately, as a Republican, that's what we got."

LIZ PEEK: THERE MAY BE A SILVER LINING IN TRUMP'S BRUTAL MIDTERM DEFEAT

In the Senate, Democrats scored seven pickups on Election Night, with outstanding races in Alaska and Mississippi still waiting to be called. And in the House, Democrats roared back into power with 27 pickups, and with several races still outstanding.

The Iran war, ignoring the economic hurt squeezing voters, attacking sitting Republicans and more are on the list of grievances from Republicans reeling in the days after.

The Senate map, in particular, was at one point favorable for Republicans and viewed as an uphill battle for Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and Democrats to put a dent in the GOP’s thin, 53-seat majority.

But Trump’s decision to go on a "primary revenge tour and antagonizing senators," a GOP aide told Fox News Digital, among several other issues, opened up the field for Democrats to pounce.

Indeed, Trump’s handpicked candidates were pummeled in races that were once safe bets for Republicans.

DEM FLIPS KEY SENATE SEAT IN BATTLEGROUND NORTH CAROLINA AS COOPER DEFEATS TRUMP ALLY

His backing of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., and fight with Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., last year that ultimately led to his retirement and created an opening for Democrats in the Tar Heel State, proved fatal for the GOP, coupled with stunning losses in Maine, Kansas, Ohio and Iowa, kneecapped any chances Republicans had of keeping power in the upper chamber.

"Trump ignored affordability completely," another Republican aide told Fox News Digital. "Ousted good members a la Cornyn, Tillis who knew how to win tough races, and poisoned the base’s opinion of our majority with his SAVE Act/filibuster bull----."

"We had a great map, and he hijacked [it]," they continued.

In the House, where Democrats are on pace to potentially win upward of 250 seats, Fox News Power Rankings projected that Trump’s tariffs and the war in Iran were significant drivers for voting blocs leaving the GOP.

TRUMP'S GAMBLE ON KEN PAXTON BACKFIRES AS DEMOCRAT PULLS OFF HISTORIC TEXAS SENATE UPSET

One House Republican complained that GOP leaders were too focused on "bluster" rather than "doing the job," though they did not mention Trump by name.

"All the name changes were so unnecessary — Gulf of America, Lake of America, Department of War," the GOP lawmaker said.

A second House Republican rattled off a lengthy list of shortcomings, including the quality and character of "certain candidates," Trump’s immigration enforcement, tariffs, general affordability issues, historic midterm headwinds, and "departure from traditional conservatism in favor of populism."

Meanwhile, people in Trump’s orbit blamed the candidates themselves.

Trump outside advisor Alex Bruesewitz posted on X that "most Republican candidates this cycle were uninspiring, lazy, and thoroughly ineffective communicators."

"I’m not all that surprised by some of these outcomes," he said.

Meanwhile, some are expecting a massive shift in Trump’s base of support in Congress as he heads toward a lame duck likely punctuated by investigations and stalled agendas.

"I think Trump being a lame duck starts today," Eberhart said. "You know, if I'm up in the [2028] cycle, I'm waking up today, I'm against the arch. I'm against the ballroom. I want space from Trump."

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/republicans-turn-trump-after-devastating-midterm-losses-hand-democrats-control-congress

posts.title: MEHEK COOKE: Republicans failed the affordability test. This is how to win voters back
posts.excerpt: Republicans lost Tuesday's elections because voters graded the GOP on groceries, gasoline, housing and health care affordability, not ideology.
posts.content:
Republicans lost Tuesday because we forgot the oldest lesson in politics: It is the economy, stupid. Americans did not suddenly embrace socialism or bigger government. Instead, they graded the GOP on a pocketbook scorecard of groceries, gasoline, housing and health care, then punished Republicans for failing to deliver financial relief they could feel.

Democrats captured both chambers of Congress, flipped governor’s offices and won statewide races across the country, including in Ohio, which President Donald Trump carried by double digits two years ago. Republicans must recognize that this election was a performance review and not simply the product of media bias, poor turnout or an ideological transformation of the country. The warning was clear before a single vote was counted. A Fox News poll found that 60% of voters considered the cost of living their greatest economic concern, 74% rated the economy negatively and only 18% said their families were better off than two years earlier.

Election Day was not a repudiation of every Republican principle. Voters still trusted the GOP more on crime, border security and immigration, but those advantages did not close the affordability gap.

TRUMP PLEDGES TO VETO 'INSANE' DEM BILLS, PINPOINTS ISSUE PARTIALLY TO BLAME FOR REPUBLICAN LOSSES

Republicans won the White House and both chambers in 2024 by promising economic relief, and voters judged the delivery of that promise through their bank accounts. Abandoning conservative principles would deliver more victories to Democrats and dismissing the losses as nothing more than anti-Trump anger would ignore the financial plea voters made. President Trump delivered tax relief, but Republicans failed to make broader affordability gains arrive quickly enough for families to feel them.

Democrats respond to government failure by demanding more government. They point to unaffordable housing and medical bills, invoke affordability and then call for larger budgets, new programs and expanded federal authority. Republicans cannot respond with abstract defenses of limited government while existing institutions remain expensive and unreliable.

The next Republican revolution must be a competence revolution focused on lowering the cost of living and putting American interests first. That requires government to perform its essential duties, enforce the law and remove barriers preventing families and businesses from succeeding. While Democrats measure government by how much it spends, Republicans must measure it by what families save.

The clearest opportunity to close the delivery gap is health care. A post-election KFF analysis of the national Voter Poll found that voters trusted Democrats over Republicans by 19 points on the issue. More than half said Trump administration policies had made their own health care costs worse, while only 10% said those costs had improved. Health care is a major pocketbook issue and voters judged Republicans by how much they are paying for their medical bills. More promises won’t change that sentiment, but a plan that enforces price transparency, exposes hidden middleman markups, increases competition and requires timely explanations of coverage denials. That is competent government because it gives patients information and choices without creating a larger federal health care system.

Democratic control of both chambers of Congress still leaves President Trump with the power of the veto pen even as he pledges to work with Democrats. This gives him significant negotiating leverage because Democrats need his signature to enact legislation unless they secure two-thirds support in both chambers. President Trump’s power to say no allows him to reject legislation that makes life more expensive while demanding affordability provisions that provide measurable relief for families. Democrats are now on notice. They must show voters whether they really stand for affordability or just a larger spending agenda.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Congressional Republicans face the same affordability mandate. Every spending bill, regulatory proposal and policy should be measured by whether it lowers health care costs, removes barriers to building housing, reduces government waste and allows families to keep more of what they earn. The Trump administration and Republican governors should publish scorecards that measure permit processing times, taxpayer dollars protected from fraud and whether government programs deliver what they promised. Before spending more money on a failing program, Republicans should also require an audit explaining what went wrong, where the existing money went and what taxpayers would receive from any additional spending. The test is not whether a proposal is red or blue, but whether it leaves more green in Americans’ wallets.

Democrats failed to offer a coherent governing strategy beyond blaming President Trump, and they are already mistaking Tuesday’s victory for an endorsement of socialism, permission to expand government and a blank check to spend two years investigating the president. That mistake gives Republicans a clear opportunity to prove that conservative principles can make life more affordable. Tuesday was a warning that principles without competent delivery will not earn another majority.

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM MEHEK COOKE

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/mehek-cooke-republicans-failed-affordability-test-how-win-voters-back

posts.title: One week, new loan’: NDC tackles Tinubu over fresh N10.79trn borrowing
posts.excerpt: The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has strongly criticised President Bola Tinubu over his request to the National Assembly for approval of a fresh $7.7bn (approximately ₦
posts.content:
By Henry Umoru, Abuja

The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has strongly criticised President Bola Tinubu over his request to the National Assembly for approval of a fresh $7.7bn (approximately ₦10.79tn) external borrowing plan to partly finance the 2026 budget deficit.

According to the NDC, the latest request has made it a case of a one-week new loan.

In a statement on Thursday by the spokesperson of the National Presidential Campaign Council of the NDC, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, she called on Nigerians to turn out in massive numbers in the 2027 elections and use their votes to demand accountability, fiscal responsibility and a government that puts the people’s interests first.

According to her, the country’s growing debt burden, in light of new loan requests by President Bola Tinubu, and the obligations being passed on to future generations make this election too important for citizens to sit out, just as the party appealed to Nigerians to turn out massively and vote for Mr Peter Obi and Eng. Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso on January 16, 2027.

According to her, Nigerians should emulate Americans, whom she described as champions of democratic participation, by coming out in their millions to vote for Obi and Kwankwaso, saying, “Americans demonstrated the power of the ballot in their November 4, 2026 elections.”

She further said, “President Bola Tinubu has again asked the National Assembly to approve a new external borrowing plan of $7.7 billion (approximately ₦10.79 trillion) to help finance the 2026 budget deficit, making this a case of a one-week, new loan.”

She observed that Americans, like Nigerians, are grappling with the high cost of living and economic hardship. Rather than merely grumbling or resigning themselves to their circumstances, she said, Americans turned out to exercise their democratic rights, demonstrating that the power to change government ultimately rests with the electorate.

Dr Ikokwu said, “Truly, it seems that right now, we cannot stop President Tinubu from his One Week! New Loan! One Week! New loan! Borrowing spree, which is already hitting the roof, because, regrettably, he has pocketed the National Assembly. We seem to have a rubber-stamp legislature that before a loan request formally gets to its desk, it has already been endorsed.

“But Nigerians should not despair. The ballot remains our most powerful instrument of change. We appeal to citizens to use their votes to rescue the country from this debt trap and entrust its future to a government committed to transparency, accountability and prudent management of public resources.”

The NDC reiterated that the country’s economic future must not be mortgaged by unsustainable borrowing and the mismanagement of public resources.

ENDS

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/one-week-new-loan-ndc-tackles-tinubu-over-fresh-n10-79trn-borrowing/

posts.title: LEE CARTER: The biggest winner of this election is not who you think
posts.excerpt: This election proved persuasion still works in American democracy, showing that voters aren't permanently locked into political teams or tribal loyalties.
posts.content:
Whether you’re celebrating this week's midterm elections or sniffling into your morning coffee, I have some good news.

And no, it has nothing to do with which party won.

For years, we’ve been told that America is hopelessly divided. That our politics are tribal. That our opinions are fixed, our loyalties inherited, and our minds about as open as a bank on Christmas.

AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI

Democrats vote for Democrats. Republicans vote for Republicans. Independents insist they’re independent while somehow managing to vote for the same party every November.

Persuasion? Forget it.

Why bother making an argument when everyone has already made up their mind?

LEE CARTER: THE SUMMER POLLS MISSED THE POINT: VOTERS ARE MOVING — AND THE MIDTERMS BEGIN

Well, guess what?

They haven’t.

And that may be the most encouraging thing to come out of this election.

I’m a researcher and strategist. I spend my life studying what people believe, why they believe it, and what, if anything, might change their minds. I even wrote a book called" Persuasion," which lately has been beginning to sound like a work of historical fiction.

JASON CHAFFETZ: FIVE TIMELESS POLITICAL LESSONS THAT GOT LOST IN 2026

But I’ll admit something. Watching our politics harden over the past decade, even I began to wonder just how persuadable America really was.

We seemed to have reached a point where facts were filtered through party affiliation, arguments were judged by who made them, and changing your mind was treated less like intellectual growth and more like treason.

We’ve stopped debating and started diagnosing. Anyone who disagrees with us must be stupid, evil, brainwashed, or watching the wrong cable news channel.

Then voters did something wonderfully inconvenient.

They reminded us that they are human beings, not permanent members of political teams.

Look at Michigan. Look at Texas. Look at Kansas.

EVERYONE IS WATCHING TEXAS AND MICHIGAN. AS A POLLSTER, I KNOW WHERE THE REAL STORY IS

Different states. Different political traditions. Different electorates. But each offers a reason to question the assumption that political identity is destiny.

Candidates can still reach people who weren’t necessarily inclined to listen. An argument can still break through. A message that speaks to something voters genuinely care about can still make them reconsider what they thought they knew.

Of course, an election result alone doesn’t tell us precisely how many voters changed their minds and how many different voters simply showed up. As a researcher, I feel compelled to point that out, even at the risk of ruining a perfectly good argument.

But the larger lesson remains.

INDEPENDENT VOTERS AREN’T PICKING A POLITICAL TEAM, THEY JUST FEEL PICKED ON

Political coalitions are not permanent. And voters are not property.

That’s not a flaw in democracy. That’s democracy working.

We’ve spent so much time talking about polarization that we’ve started treating it as a permanent condition. As though Americans arrived at the voting booth with their opinions tattooed on their foreheads.

But Americans are more complicated than their party registrations.

They can be conservative about spending and liberal about health care. Frustrated with immigration and worried about government overreach. Loyal to a president and disappointed in his party. Angry at Washington and hopeful about their hometown.

They can hold two seemingly contradictory ideas at once.

Imagine that.

THE HISPANIC VOTE IS UP FOR GRABS IN 2026. CANDIDATES WHO IGNORE IT WILL LOSE

And most importantly, they can change their minds.

Not necessarily because someone shouted louder. Not because a campaign spent another $50 million telling them the other guy was terrible. And certainly not because a celebrity told them what to think.

But because someone made an argument that connected with their lives.

That is what persuasion actually is.

It’s not tricking people. It’s not manipulating them. It’s not finding the magic words that make people abandon their values.

It’s finding the truth in your argument that connects with the truth in someone else’s life.

And when that happens, something remarkable becomes possible.

I'M JESSICA TARLOV, AND SOMETIMES I GET IT WRONG. ACCEPTING THAT IS THE FIRST STEP TOWARDS BETTER DEBATES

A voter can cross a party line. A lifelong loyalist can reconsider. Someone who has tuned out politics altogether can decide that this time, something is worth paying attention to.

None of this means America is suddenly united. Far from it.

We still disagree, often fiercely. We still retreat into our corners. We still have a remarkable talent for assuming the worst about people who vote differently from us.

And Thanksgiving dinner is still going to require a seating chart and possibly a referee.

But disagreement is not the same thing as permanence.

And division is not the same thing as hopelessness.

The Founders didn’t build a country on the assumption that everyone would agree. They built one in which disagreement could be argued, debated, challenged, and ultimately resolved, at least temporarily, by the people.

A country of ideas and ideals.

A country where arguments are supposed to matter.

Where leaders have to earn support rather than simply inherit it.

Where no party owns a voter forever.

And where the best ideas have a chance to win, provided someone can make the case for them.

That’s the part I hope we don’t miss in all the post-election analysis.

Because if minds can change, then our future isn’t predetermined by our divisions.

If voters can be persuaded, politicians have a reason to listen.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

If people are willing to reconsider what they believe, the rest of us have a reason to keep talking to one another.

And if an election can surprise us, perhaps our neighbors can, too.

So, whether your candidates won or lost, whether you’re popping champagne or reaching for the tissues, take a little comfort in this:

America isn’t as stuck as we thought.

People are still listening. Arguments still matter. Ideas can still change minds.

And in a country that has spent years being told it’s hopelessly divided, that might be the most hopeful election result of all.

As someone who wrote a book about persuasion, I have to admit I’m particularly relieved.

I really wasn’t looking forward to writing the sequel, "Nobody’s Listening."

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM LEE CARTER

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/lee-carter-biggest-winner-election-not-who-you-think

posts.title: Race for 2028 heats up after US midterms firestorm
posts.excerpt: President Donald Trump's stunning midterms defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election -- the race to replace him in the White House in 2028. The post Race for 2028 heats up after US midte
posts.content:
President Donald Trump’s stunning midterms defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028.

The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss.

But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars like Georgia senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful vibe has already drawn comparisons to former president Barack Obama.

– Republicans in turmoil –

The MAGA coalition that shot Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday’s midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb.

Long seen as the odds-on favorite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterms campaigns with rallies in swing states.

The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump’s unpopular war on Iran in a long thesis posted on X on Wednesday.

But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump.

It’s a familiar problem for US vice presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice president Kamala Harris suffered from a similar problem in 2024 when she said that “there’s not a thing that comes to mind” when asked how she’d differentiate herself from Joe Biden.

“The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice presidents seldom win the presidency,” James Lindsay of the Council for Foreign Relations, said.

Trump’s Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s name has also been bandied about.

Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms but any top official in Trump’s administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war.

The Republicans’ midterm disaster could, however, be a boost for other possible candidates.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal.

He described the Democratic sweep as “the political equivalent of a meteor strike” — and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off.

Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats’ stunning senate and governor wins in the midterms in his state.

– Democrats on a high –

The Democratic field is crowded but the midterms have given some likely candidates a boost.

Ossoff’s reelection as Georgia Senator has fueled speculation about a 2028 run by a telegenic politician who has already gained attention for mocking Trump’s relationship with a young staffer.

The 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for president” but his swiftly-declared win in Georgia — and his victory speech — have bolstered his status in the party.

Before the midterms Kamala Harris, 62, had been the favorite for the nomination, but there are many in the party who would prefer to have someone without a losing track record.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, 53, who was interviewed by Harris to be her running mate in 2024, had a good night on Tuesday as he stormed back to reelection in the key battleground state.

Outgoing California Governor Gavin Newsom, 59, is another big name who has repeatedly taken on Trump. He predicted in an interview with AFP in September Trump’s presidency “as we know it would be over after the midterms.

But Newsom, like Harris, may be seen as more of an old guard figure in a party that is looking to its rising stars.

A prominent but potentially divisive choice would be left-wing New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who said in September that she was weighing a run, musing about whether a Latina could win in a country that rejected female nominees in 2016 and 2024.

Other possible contenders include former Chicago mayor Rahm Emmanuel, JB Pritzker, the billionaire Illinois governor who set out a lengthy national agenda after winning a third term on Tuesday, Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, and Arizona senator and former astronaut Mark Kelly.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/race-for-2028-heats-up-after-us-midterms-firestorm/

posts.title: ‘I’m PDP member but Wike is not my leader’ — Oyinlola
posts.excerpt: Oyinlola also suggested that Wike was young enough to be his political subordinate, citing their different stages of life when he served as military governor of Lagos State between 1993 and 1996. The
posts.content:
Former Osun State Governor, Olagunsoye Oyinlola, has dissociated himself from the Peoples Democratic Party leadership purportedly under the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, saying the minister is not his leader.

Oyinlola, a retired general, stated this on Wednesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today programme.

When asked whether Wike was his leader in the PDP, the former governor said, “No, not my leader. You don’t say that kind of thing.”

He added, “Yes, I am a member of the PDP, but he’s not my leader.”

Oyinlola also suggested that Wike was young enough to be his political subordinate, citing their different stages of life when he served as military governor of Lagos State between 1993 and 1996.

Asked whether Wike was his boy, he said, “He qualifies to be. When I was governor in Lagos, where was he? In school.”

Wike, a PDP member, was appointed FCT minister by President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC). He subsequently established the Rainbow coalition, a political structure backing Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

The coalition has attracted criticism from some PDP members who accuse Wike of working against the party’s interests by supporting the president.

Oyinlola, who governed Osun from 2003 to 2010, also blamed the crisis rocking the opposition party on internal forces working against efforts to restore its unity.

Speaking about former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s efforts to rebuild the party, Oyinlola said the former president had been working to re-engineer its structure, but some members were frustrating the process.

“He’s been trying to ensure that the party is re-engineered. But those who don’t want it are working against it within the party. That’s the much I can say,” he said.

Oyinlola maintained that the PDP remained capable of recovering from its internal crisis, noting that it had structures across the country.

“The PDP is not dead. The bone will rise again,” he said.

He added that the party had a presence in all 774 local government areas and could regain its strength if members resolved their differences.

“If we get our acts together, it’s a thing we can achieve, but the forces making sure we don’t get there are there. They are not sleeping,” Oyinlola said.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/im-pdp-member-but-wike-is-not-my-leader-oyinlola/

posts.title: Okpebholo Hails Flamingos World Cup Qualification, Hands Relief Materials To Fire Victims
posts.excerpt: He assured the team that Nigerians, including the people of Edo State, are firmly behind them and will be cheering them on as they pursue their first-ever FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup title The post Ok
posts.content:
Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, on their historic qualification for the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

The governor described the team’s 3-1 victory over Brazil as a remarkable achievement, applauding the players for their determination, tactical discipline, teamwork, and fighting spirit throughout the competition.

Governor Okpebholo said the Flamingos had demonstrated the resilience and competitive spirit that Nigerians are proud of, noting that their achievement has brought joy and renewed hope to football fans across the country

Flamingos players celebrate a goal against Brazil. Photo credit: Fifa.com

He particularly commended the goal scorers, Queen Joseph and Awawu Bashiru, for their outstanding contributions to the victory while praising the entire squad and technical crew for their commitment and dedication.

The governor urged the players to remain focused, disciplined, and determined as they prepared to face Japan in Saturday’s final, expressing confidence in their ability to go all the way and bring the trophy home.

He assured the team that Nigerians, including the people of Edo State, are firmly behind them and will be cheering them on as they pursue their first-ever FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup title

Governor Okpebholo wished the Flamingos success in the final, urging them to seize the historic opportunity and make Nigeria proud.

Meanwhile, the Governor has handed over relief materials to affected traders at the recent Oluku Market fire disaster, with a promise to build the market to a modern standard.

Speaking on Wednesday while presenting relief materials from the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and the Edo State Emergency Management Agency (EDOSEMA), he assured traders who lost goods and shops that the state government will not abandon them.

“This has demonstrated how much we care about you. We love you, we feel your pain, and we have come with these little things to share among you. We know you are not happy, but no matter what you receive from us, we will always appreciate it. It is better to show little concern than not to show concern at all”, the governor said.

He added: “The day we finish this market, you will know that you have a market. We are going to build a standard market for you. When you go to the market, you will be proud of your place of business.

“If you had a standard market, the fire might not have destroyed your goods the way it did. We are going to build with concrete so that your goods will be safe. When you lock your shops, your items will remain safe,” the governor said.

He disclosed that he had briefed President Bola Tinubu on the fire, and that the President directed that the affected shops be rebuilt.

Promising further support for the victims while asking them to manage their expectations said: “We are also going to support you. We will not leave you to suffer. We will give you some form of assistance, and it may not be bigger than what you lost”.

Governor Okpebholo urged residents to keep praying for President Tinubu, noting that part of the development now taking place in Edo State followed the President’s directives.

Earlier, the Executive Secretary of EDOSEMA, Jerry Idahosa, said the agency would work with NEMA and other stakeholders to monitor the recovery of the affected traders. He urged the beneficiaries to use the relief materials wisely.

Idahosa also warned members of the public against scooping fuel from fallen or leaking tankers, citing the dangers of the practice.

Some of the traders thanked the governor and other stakeholders for coming to their aid. They said the materials would ease their hardship and restore some hope after the disaster.

One of them, Ann Ogbowman, said she lost everything in the fire. She nonetheless expressed gratitude to the governor and the agencies, saying the items would help her cope.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/11/05/okpebholo-hails-flamingos-world-cup-qualification-hands-relief-materials-to-fire-victims/

posts.title: WATCH: Bodycam captures chaotic response to deadly Citibank shooting in Florida
posts.excerpt: Body camera footage shows Hillsborough County deputies rushing into the Florida Citibank campus as frantic 911 calls capture the deadly chaos.
posts.content:
Newly released body camera footage captures the chaotic moments as Hillsborough County deputies rushed into a Citibank campus in Tampa, Florida, during a deadly shooting Wednesday, searching for the gunman before an officer announced, "Shooter is down."

The Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office released edited bodycam footage and 911 calls showing the law enforcement response to the shooting at the Sabal Center in Tampa, where a woman was killed, and the gunman was fatally shot by an armed security guard.

According to authorities, the suspect drove through a fence at the Sabal Park Office Development, crashed into an outdoor seating area and fatally shot a woman before opening fire inside the building's cafeteria.

In the footage, a deputy is heard asking bystanders for a description of the suspect as officers arrive at the sprawling business campus.

BODYCAM FOOTAGE CAPTURES MOMENTS AFTER ICE SHOOTING OF VENEZUELAN MIGRANT IN AUSTIN

The deputy then reports that a vehicle had crashed into the property and that the suspect was inside the cafeteria.

"Shooter is down," an officer later announces, before the video shows deputies escorting people out of the building.

The newly released 911 audio captures a caller reporting gunfire at Citibank as authorities coordinate their response, including plans to enter the building.

BODYCAM SHOWS LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEPUTY STABBED SECONDS AFTER ARRIVING AT KNIFE ATTACK

According to the sheriff's office, dispatchers began receiving calls about shots fired at 12:11 p.m., and deputies arrived within one minute.

Authorities praised an armed Citibank security guard who shot the suspect during an exchange of gunfire. The gunman was later pronounced dead at Tampa General Hospital.

The sheriff's office said more than 3,200 people were on campus when the shooting unfolded, and over 400 law enforcement personnel responded, including 367 sheriff's deputies.

"Thanks to the brave actions by the security team on-site and more than 365 deputies, this unhinged suspect was stopped before he could harm anyone else," Sheriff Chad Chronister said in a statement.

posts.title: Hamzat: The Man, His Vision and Agenda for Lagos
posts.excerpt: With a 100-point development blueprint outlining his vision for the Centre of Excellence, the All Progressives Congress’ governorship candidate, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, has placed accountability, co
posts.content:
With a 100-point development blueprint outlining his vision for the Centre of Excellence, the All Progressives Congress’ governorship candidate, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, has placed accountability, continuity and inclusive development at the centre of his campaign, challenging residents to hold him responsible for every unfulfilled promise. Wale Igbintade reports.

The atmosphere at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos, on Friday, October 30, was unmistakably political, cultural and symbolic.

Thousands of party faithful, residents, political stakeholders and invited guests gathered to witness the unveiling of the manifesto of the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat. Others followed the proceedings through live broadcasts, extending the event’s reach beyond the venue.

The colourful cultural performances celebrating Lagos’ rich heritage, coupled with the presence of prominent political leaders, traditional rulers, religious figures and captains of industry, underscored the significance of the occasion.

Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, who attended as special guest of honour with his wife, Dr Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, was joined by former Governor Babatunde Fashola, members of the National Assembly, Lagos State House of Assembly, the Governance Advisory Council, traditional rulers and other political leaders.

But beyond the impressive gathering, the central attraction was Hamzat’s attempt to define the next chapter of Lagos’ development journey.

His manifesto, titled ‘The Lagos Promise (Ileri Eko)’, is structured around seven pillars and 100 pledges covering healthcare, education, infrastructure, transportation, economic development, employment, security, housing, environmental sustainability and institutional accountability.

Its central philosophy was captured in a simple but weighty declaration: A promise is a debt.

In what emerged as the strongest political statement of the occasion, Hamzat challenged Lagosians to hold him accountable for every commitment contained in the document.

“I stand before you today not simply to ask for your vote, but to earn your trust, to share my vision for Lagos, to explain what I believe that we must do differently, and to demonstrate why I am prepared to serve you,” he declared.

The Man Behind the Mission

Hamzat’s presentation was not restricted to policy proposals. He offered glimpses into the personal experiences and values that, according to him, have shaped his understanding of public service.

He recalled encountering the late sage, Chief Obafemi Awolowo when he was 14 years old and a student at Olivet Baptist High School, Oyo. Awolowo’s campaign procession had passed along the road in front of his school, giving him an opportunity to see the legendary progressive politician at close range.

The experience, he said, left an enduring impression on him, particularly the philosophy that a nation progresses when people of honour and ability choose to serve.

His political consciousness was also shaped by his father, Alhaji Mufutau Olatunji Hamzat, a banker who later became involved in progressive politics. Elected into the Lagos State House of Assembly in 1979, his father subsequently served as Commissioner for Public Transportation under the administration of the late Governor, Alhaji Lateef Jakande.

Hamzat also recalled his childhood in Mushin, where he attended Odu-Abore Memorial Primary School. Those early experiences, he explained, exposed him to the everyday challenges confronting ordinary Lagos residents.

“Mushin taught me many things. I learned what a clear drain means to a street during the rainy season. I learned what steady light means to a trader at four in the afternoon,” he said.

For him, development is not merely about constructing impressive infrastructure or announcing ambitious programmes. It must improve the everyday lives of residents.

He illustrated this with the story of a 10-year-old boy he encountered under a bridge at Oshodi at about 2 a.m. The child, who had reportedly run away from home in another state because his environment was unsafe, had found sleeping under a bridge preferable to returning home.

The experience reinforced Hamzat’s conviction that government must protect vulnerable children through functioning schools, healthcare facilities, social welfare institutions and effective community support.

“If you are a child and you live in Lagos, then you are a child of Lagos. Lagos will know you are here, Lagos will work for you, Lagos will protect you,” he declared.

He said his parents had instilled three principles in him: respect, work and truth. Respect means treating citizens with dignity; work requires delivery before publicity; while truth demands honesty about government performance.

Seven Pillars, 100 Pledges

The manifesto’s seven pillars are People First, Renewal, Opportunity, Machinery of Government, Inclusion, Security and Resilience, and Everyday Excellence.

A notable feature is its classification of the 100 commitments into 87 firm pledges within the powers of the Lagos State Government and 13 aspirations requiring wider consultations, cooperation with the Federal Government or judicial intervention.

To strengthen accountability, Hamzat promised to establish a Lagos State Service Delivery Office through an executive order, with himself as chairman.

An independent Performance Council would assess government performance, while service charters would be introduced across public offices.

Under the proposed arrangement, complaints would be acknowledged within 48 hours, answered within seven days and resolved within 30 days. Annual performance reports and public scorecards would also disclose achievements, outstanding commitments and reasons for any failures.

He promised that the accountability framework would commence within his first 100 days in office.

Healthcare and education occupy prominent positions in the blueprint. Hamzat promised to increase maternal and child centres from 10 to 15 and expand the Ilera Eko health insurance programme from nearly two million beneficiaries to more than three million.

He also pledged to complete the 150-bed Massey Children’s Hospital, the 280-bed Ojo General Hospital and the 150-bed Somolu General Hospital, providing 580 additional beds. Two more general hospitals are proposed for Ogombo and Ibeju-Lekki, alongside the upgrading of 100 primary healthcare centres.

On education, he promised to strengthen public schools through improved teacher training, professional development and better learning outcomes. He highlighted EKOEXCEL and the Eko Learn initiative, which provides 320 lessons online and on television.

He also proposed establishing a University of Medicine and Health Sciences to expand tertiary education opportunities and strengthen the state’s healthcare workforce.

Jobs, Infrastructure and Economic Growth

Recognising the importance of small businesses and entrepreneurship to Lagos’ economy, Hamzat argued that government cannot create all the jobs required by the state’s growing population. Rather, it must provide an environment in which businesses can expand and employ more people.

He cited the Lagos State Employment Trust Fund’s support for businesses through financing, training and mentorship, promising to expand opportunities for entrepreneurs, artisans and young people.

Among his proposals is a single schedule of lawful government charges to eliminate uncertainty for businesses. He also promised to reserve a defined proportion of state procurement opportunities for qualified Lagos businesses.

Under a proposed apprenticeship programme, students would spend between six and 12 months working with employers, with the state paying 40 per cent of their stipends. Artisans would also receive free professional certification based on their existing practical skills.

For young people, he pledged to expand opportunities in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics, blockchain and other emerging technologies.

Transportation, one of Lagos’ most pressing challenges, received considerable attention.

Hamzat promised to increase the public bus fleet from approximately 1,000 to 4,000 buses, with the capacity to transport one million passengers daily.

He also pledged to extend the Blue Line to Okokomaiko, advance the Green Line from Marina to the Lekki Free Trade Zone and improve connections between the existing rail corridors.

Other proposed projects include the Fourth Mainland Bridge, the Regional Road along the Lekki-Epe axis and Phase II of the Opebi-Mende Link Bridge.

On water transportation, he promised to dredge an additional 140 kilometres of waterways, refurbish 25 ferry terminals and jetties, optimise 15 ferry routes and procure 75 additional electric vessels.

Housing is another major component. Hamzat promised to complete ongoing housing projects, expand Lagos HOMS and introduce more accessible mortgage arrangements.

One proposal is a mortgage scheme requiring a 10 per cent deposit, single-digit interest rates and longer repayment periods, potentially improving access to home ownership for middle and lower-income earners.

On security, he pledged to extend the Lagos State Neighbourhood Safety Agency to all wards across the state’s 20 local government areas and 37 Local Council Development Areas.

He also proposed installing streetlights and CCTV cameras in communities and establishing a State Intelligence Fusion Centre to strengthen responses to organised crime, cybercrime and other security threats.

Water supply and environmental sustainability also featured prominently.

Hamzat promised to complete the Adiyan Phase Two water project, designed to produce 70 million gallons daily and provide water to an additional six million Lagos residents.

He also pledged to rehabilitate 24 micro and mini waterworks and achieve 95 per cent waste collection coverage, alongside the completion of waste transfer stations and a waste-to-energy facility.

On inclusion, he promised to strengthen programmes such as Obirin Eko for women, Omo Eko for young people and Iyi Eko for persons with disabilities, maintaining that Lagos must work for everyone, irrespective of ethnic, religious or geographical background.

First 100 Days

Hamzat identified three immediate priorities for his proposed administration.

The first is the establishment of a Child Protection and Nutrition Agency to ensure that every child below 18 is either in school or learning a trade and receives adequate nutrition.

The second is the Lagos State Service Delivery Office, which would monitor government commitments and provide measurable assessments of performance.

The third is the advancement of a State Wealth Fund, with an independent board and published accounts, to preserve Lagos’ wealth for future generations.

Together, the proposals reflect the manifesto’s emphasis on child welfare, institutional accountability and long-term economic sustainability.

Sanwo-Olu’s Endorsement and Politics of Continuity

While Hamzat presented the policy direction, Sanwo-Olu’s address supplied much of the political and emotional weight of the occasion.

In a deeply personal endorsement, the governor recalled how Hamzat had stepped aside for him during the 2018 governorship contest after party leaders intervened and asked him to withdraw from the race.

Sanwo-Olu said Hamzat had considerable experience and every reason to pursue his ambition, having served in public office for years. However, he accepted the party’s decision and subsequently agreed to become his running mate.

“I did not come here to be polite. I came here to testify,” the governor declared.

He said his endorsement was based on seven years of working closely with Hamzat, particularly during challenging periods such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the October 2020 crisis and the execution of major infrastructure projects.

He described his deputy as a dependable partner who was involved in the technical discussions, planning and negotiations behind government projects.

Sanwo-Olu’s strongest argument for Hamzat’s candidacy was built around the metaphor of a relay race.

He described Lagos governance as a continuous journey in which successive administrations must prepare to receive the baton before the outgoing government completes its tenure.

According to him, President Bola Tinubu ran the first leg, passing the baton to Fashola in 2007. Fashola handed it to Akinwunmi Ambode in 2015, while Sanwo-Olu received it in 2019.

Hamzat, he argued, had been running alongside the administration since 2019 and was therefore well positioned to continue the journey.

“Lagosians have never before been offered a man who ran this long, this close, beside the governor he hopes to succeed,” he said.

The governor also recalled Hamzat’s earlier service as Commissioner for Science and Technology under Tinubu and Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure under Fashola.

He argued that these experiences gave the APC candidate an understanding of the state’s administrative machinery and development priorities.

Acknowledging criticism that Lagos had consistently produced governors from within the same political establishment, Sanwo-Olu defended the state’s succession model.

“Lagos trains its people. There is a difference,” he said.

He maintained that continuity was necessary to complete major projects, including the Fourth Mainland Bridge, the proposed Lekki-Epe International Airport and ongoing rail expansions.

But he was careful to distinguish continuity from complacency.

“Continuity does not mean repeating ourselves. It means finishing what was started, fixing what is not working, and starting what comes next, in that order, with a plan,” he declared.

In an emotional reflection on the approaching transition, Sanwo-Olu said his greatest achievement might be Lagos changing governors without a political quarrel.

“Lagos is going to change governors without a quarrel,” he said.

His endorsement effectively presented Hamzat’s candidacy as an opportunity to consolidate the political and developmental tradition established by successive administrations.

The Test Beyond the Manifesto

For all its ambition, the ultimate significance of Hamzat’s manifesto will not be determined by the grandeur of its presentation or the applause that greeted its unveiling. It will be measured by implementation.

Increasing the bus fleet to 4,000, extending potable water to six million additional residents, expanding health insurance, constructing hospitals and improving affordable housing will require substantial financial resources, administrative discipline and effective coordination.

The proposed single-digit mortgage arrangement will depend on sustainable financing structures, while the expansion of public transportation will require efficient maintenance and integration of road, rail and water networks.

The proposed State Wealth Fund will equally require transparent governance and safeguards against political interference.

More importantly, the promised accountability framework will only be meaningful if the government is prepared to publish unfavourable performance assessments when it falls short of its commitments.

For ordinary Lagosians, the real test will be whether commuting becomes easier, healthcare more accessible, public schools more effective, businesses face fewer obstacles and children enjoy greater protection.

The trader at Alaba, the artisan in Ebute Metta, the commuter travelling from Badagry to Lagos Island, the office worker commuting daily from Berger to Tafawa Balewa Square (TBS), and the family struggling to secure affordable accommodation will ultimately judge the proposed administration by the difference it makes to their everyday lives.

As the October 30 gathering drew to a close, Hamzat’s message was unmistakable: public service must be anchored on respect, work and truth, while political promises must carry the weight of obligation.

His personal journey, administrative experience and Sanwo-Olu’s endorsement formed the foundation of the argument for continuity. But the electorate will have the final say..

The manifesto has placed an ambitious development blueprint before Lagosians and offered a proposed mechanism through which they can monitor its implementation.

Whether those promises become measurable achievements will depend on the electoral process and, ultimately, the performance of the next administration.

For Hamzat, the challenge is to prove that the promise presented at the historic Wole Soyinka Centre can withstand the demands of governing one of Africa’s most complex megacities.

Lagos has heard the promise. The next test is delivery.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/05/hamzat-the-man-his-vision-and-agenda-for-lagos/

posts.title: Tinubu in Akwa Ibom: Lessons from History
posts.excerpt: As President Bola Tinubu visits Akwa Ibom State on Friday, November 6, Etim Etim takes a look at the lessons learnt since Tinubu first visited the State 12 years ago.
posts.content:
As President Bola Tinubu visits Akwa Ibom State on Friday, November 6, Etim Etim takes a look at the lessons learnt since Tinubu first visited the State 12 years ago.

There’s excitement in the air as Akwa Ibom State expects the arrival of President Bola Tinubu on Friday, November 6, 2026 for a working visit. It’s a proud moment for Governor Umo Eno who has a lot to show off. Some landmark projects have been lined up for inauguration by the President. Among them are the world-class terminal airport building which many have been talking about and the iconic Arise Palm Resort, a recreation and tourism facility built on a reclaimed parcel of land that was previously ravaged by gully erosion.

It would be the third time that Asiwaju Tinubu would set foot on Akwa Ibom soil, the first being November 27, 2014 when Tinubu, then APC National Leader, visited the state to receive defecting Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) members into his party. Leading the defectors then was Obong Umana Okon Umana, who was a few months before the Secretary to the State Government in the Akpabio administration and a key ally of the governor. Umana moved with 10,000 PDP members initially, but later grew to over 30,000 as more people joined the party. They included no fewer than 10 serving House of Assembly and House of Representatives members.

Among those who were received into the party by Asiwaju were former minister of Petroleum, Chief Don Etiebet; the late Ime Umana (Lagos based businessman who lived next door to Asiwaju in Lagos); Dr. Chris Ekong (now Professor and Vice Chancellor of University of Uyo); Engr. Alphonsus Ekon; the late Akanimo Edet; former Deputy Speaker of the State House of Assembly, the late Okon Uwah; another former deputy speaker, Hon Uwem Udomah and Chief Ita Awak. There were also Chief Sunny Udom; Dr. John Harry; Chief Sunny Anyang; Chief Perry Ntuk; former Minister Rita Akpan; late Dr. Maurice Ebong; Chief Sunny Jackson and Dr. Ita Udosen.

I remember also former minister, Dr. Ime Okopido; Mrs Geraldine Ita Etuk; Obong Cyril Ekiko; former Akwa Ibom First Lady, Imo Isemin (now late); Dr. Emem Wills; Chief Sam Frank; Chief Victor Iyanam and many others. Most of them were commissioners and officials in the administrations of Obong Attah and Akpabio, while others were former ministers, Permanent Secretaries and top government officials.

That afternoon, I went to the airport with Obong Umana to receive Asiwaju and his delegation, while the crowd was waiting at Asan Ibibio. As a member of his media team, Obong Umana found me useful for many assignments: protocol, PR, intelligence gathering, monitoring and of course, our core duties: media and publicity. I had just retired from banking and I found the whole political process rambunctiously exciting.

Dressed in a simple grey kaftan, Asiwaju arrived in a private jet with Chief Bisi Akande, Chief Niyi Adebayo, former Ekiti governor; Chief Lai Mohammed and some others. It was a few months to the 2015 general election, and so, many of the party’s presidential aspirants, notably Muhammadu Buhari; Atiku Abubarkar; Rabiu Musa Kwakwanso and the late Sam Nda-Isaiha, then publisher of Leadership newspaper, also came – separately in private jets – mainly to court the new members, some of whom would be delegates in the national convention that was coming up just a month away. Akwa Ibom airport was filled with airplanes of different models and sizes. It was, undoubtedly, the busiest day in the life of the airport which began operations five years prior.

We all moved in buses to Asan Ibibio, venue of the reception rally, where the defectors were formally received into APC. On the drive from the airport, the long motorcade turned into Shelter Afrique estate and headed for the residence of former governor, Victor Attah, to pay a courtesy visit on him. Umanah had served as Attah’s Commissioner for Finance in his second term (2003 – 2007), and the two had maintained good personal relationships since. Now, with Umanah and Attah not in good terms with Akpabio – the outgoing governor who was fighting had to impose a successor – Attah and Umana became politically closer.

Attah welcomed Asiwaju and the delegation warmly and told them that Umana was the most qualified to be the next governor. It was an audacious endorsement for Umana who had just been forced out of PDP because of his governorship ambition, and was about joining another party. Attah himself had not formally joined the APC by then, but it was clear to everyone that he had a soft spot for the party. His frosty relationship with Akpabio created big psychological and political challenges to the old man. Akwa Ibom was tense and divided along ethnic lines.

It was getting to around 4pm, and we quickly left Attah’s residence and sped to Asan Ibibio. The attendance of so many bigwigs from different parts of the country at the rally and the sheer size of the new joiners was quite an intimidating sight. It was probably the biggest APC event since the founding of the party in February, 2013. Although I was part of the organizers, I didn’t expect that crowd size. Asiwaju was visibly excited to see such a crowd of senior politicians. He warmly welcomed us into the party and promised to create a level-playing field for all contenders. Gov. Akpabio was unusually humbled by the event and the caliber of the attendees. Both Umana and Akpabio had served as commissioners in the Attah administration and had forged close friendship. Umana’s support for Akpabio to become governor was legendary. His falling out with Akpabio and subsequent defection to the APC occurred at dizzying speed and blindsided many a pundit.

The following month (December 2014), Umana won the governorship primary held at the Uyo township stadium and Buhari won the Presidential primary held at Teslim Balogun Statdium, Surulere, Lagos. I attended both events and saw history unfold. The governorship campaigns of that year and the ensuing violence literally shook the state to its foundations. I should not forget to add that four years earlier, Senator John James Akpanudoedehe had defected from the PDP to Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN), one of the four legacy parties that merged to form the APC. It was the first cataclysmic shift in the texture of opposition politics in the state, and had prepared the people for more of such events that came later.

Now, we have President Tinubu arriving for a working visit this Friday, 12 years after he first came as an opposition leader to receive us into his party. Then, he had touched down in a hostile environment, but warmly received by brave new supporters. Now, the whole state – government and the people – are all for him; supporting and rooting for him.

What lessons can we glean from this?

First, Akwa Ibom State was an early contributor to the growth of APC as a party. APC members in Akwa Ibom State were the first in the South-South to turn the party’s platform into a formidable and strong opposition party. Since then, APC has grown in leaps and bounds in the state, culminating in Governor Eno emptying the whole PDP into it last year. Akwa Ibom state should therefore not be treated as a mere footnote in the scheme of things in the party.

Umana himself was quite reflective when I called to ask him for his recollections and thoughts. He chose his words carefully, as he’s wont to do: ‘’Looking back, we can see how politics can be dynamic. By then, we were dubbed traitors for leaving PDP, which was said to be a religion in the state…we were called different names for supporting a Northerner… for not supporting Jonathan, the son of the South-South. But all that we did was rooted in local politics of the time. “We were waging a struggle against an incumbent who had so much resources… it took a lot of courage. We were fighting against an unjust system because were not satisfied with the internal processes within the PDP by that time. Many of our supporters were induced, but a lot were not persuaded to go back…’’

Talking about the injustices and unfair internal processes in PDP took my mind to what has eventually happened to that party. Are we learning?

Senator Akpabio himself joined APC in August 2018 – four years after Umana – in what was then the most stunning political upset in the National Assembly. His defection helped stabilize the Buhari Presidency which was by then tormented by the then-Senate President, Dr Bukola Saraki. It is therefore important that the President remembers his earlier pledge to support the state build a deep sea port. The state government has already invested so much in the preliminary works, including producing a feasibility report, but the backing of the federal government is essential to bring it to fruition.

Governor Eno has staked his political capital on the President’s willingness to help us achieve our dream project. The people will therefore be listening keenly to the President’s pronouncement on this when he visits. If he fails to live up to his words to support the state, Akwa Ibom people will feel a terrible sense of letdown, the political implications of which is difficult to fathom.

The second time Asiwaju visited Akwa Ibom was in 2023 when he came for Presidential campaign rally.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/05/tinubu-in-akwa-ibom-lessons-from-history/

posts.title: Tinubu: I Drove Taxi, Did Different Odd Jobs to Survive at the University in America
posts.excerpt: • Returns to Abuja after Umrah •Tasks Nigerians to tell him about things not working well in their areas, promises to fix identified problems • Insists nation’s journey from reform
posts.content:
• Returns to Abuja after Umrah

•Tasks Nigerians to tell him about things not working well in their areas, promises to fix identified problems

• Insists nation’s journey from reform to shared prosperity must begin with education, justifies introduction of NELFUND

•APC lists Tinubu’s education milestone, highlights $552 million for basic education, technical colleges’ expansion

• Recalls FG budgeted record N3.52 trillion for education in 2026

Deji Elumoye and Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, reminisced on his student days in the United States, and recalled how he drove taxi and did different odd jobs to pay his bills while his university education lasted.

In a post on X, @OfficialPBAT, Tinubu also challenged Nigerians to give him feedback about things that were not working properly in their areas, pledging to fix identified problems.

The president departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, on Wednesday for Nigeria’s capital, Abuja, after the successful completion of his Umrah (Lesser Hajj) in the Holy city of Makkah.

In the post on X, he justified the introduction of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) through which over N372 billion had been disbursed as students’ loans to young Nigerians, and spoke extensively about his student days

He told Nigerians, “If something is not working as it should in your community, I want to hear about it. Your feedback will help us identify problems and address them.”

Focussing on his economic reforms, Tinubu said Nigeria’s journey from reform to shared prosperity must begin with education.

In the lengthy post on why no Nigerian should be denied education due to lack of fund, Tinubu stated, “When I first arrived in the United States as a young man, I drove a taxi to earn money for my education. I even had to postpone starting school for several months to save enough.

“When I eventually got to Chicago, I worked different jobs to support myself and pay my way through university. I know what it means to worry about tuition, accommodation, and how to make ends meet while pursuing an education.

“Those experiences have stayed with me. I know what education made possible in my own life, and I believe every Nigerian child deserves that same opportunity, regardless of where they are born or what their parents can afford.

“This is one reason education remains a major priority of our Renewed Hope administration. Through NELFUND, we have provided over N372 billion in student loans for institutional fees and upkeep, helping young Nigerians remain in school and pursue their education.”

Tinubu also stated, “Our technical and vocational education programme has attracted over 2.8 million applications. We have rehabilitated 38 technical colleges, while students in federal and selected state technical colleges now benefit from free school fees, boarding, textbooks, and uniforms.”

He announced, “We have reached a new agreement with ASUU, providing for a 40 per cent increase in academic staff remuneration and measures to improve stability in our universities.

“A four-year course must take four years. Our young people deserve to complete their education on time and get on with their lives. Promise made, Promise Kept!”

Tinubu said, “In medical education, we are investing N110 billion in rehabilitating 24 medical schools. Annual nursing enrolment has increased from 28,000 to 115,000, while medical and dental enrolment has risen from 5,000 to 12,000.

“Nigeria needs more doctors, nurses, and other healthcare professionals, and we must build the capacity to train them here at home.”

He also spoke to the out-of-school children issue, saying, “Over one million children who were previously out of school have been returned to learning. We are investing in teacher development, expanding educational opportunities for girls, and implementing a new national curriculum that restores Nigerian History to our classrooms.

“Our children must know where we have come from, understand the country they belong to, and be prepared to take responsibility for its future.

“I commend the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa @DrTunjiAlausa, Minister of State, Professor Suwaiba Sa’id Ahmad @Suwaiba_Said, and the entire education team @NigEducation for their dedication to this important work.

“I am particularly pleased that the team has developed an interactive A–Z of the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI), bringing together the reforms, programmes, achievements and opportunities across our education system.”

The president said, “I invite every Nigerian to visit edu4pbat.ng and explore the A–Z of NESRI. If you are a parent, find out what opportunities are available for your children. If you are a student, explore the programmes you can benefit from. If you are a teacher, see what support is available.

“And if something is not working as it should in your community, I want to hear about it. Your feedback will help us identify problems and address them. Our journey from reform to opportunities and shared prosperity must begin with education.

“The circumstances of a child’s birth should never determine the limits of their ambition. Our responsibility is to give every Nigerian child a fair chance to fulfil their potential. We have more work to do, and I am determined to see it through.”

Further rolling out his scorecard in the education sector in the last three and a half years, the president said his government had expanded access to learning, improved teachers’ welfare, and stabilised the academic calendar across higher institutions in the country.

Spokesperson of All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC), Dele Aleke, who disclosed the president’s record in a release, stated that the government’s interventions covered basic and secondary education, technical and vocational training, and tertiary education.

Alake, who quoted from the 2026 Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI) report of the Federal Ministry of Education, explained that the reforms focused on six priority areas, namely technical and vocational education, science and medical sciences, out-of-school children, girl-child education, digitalisation, and education quality assurance.

According to the NESRI report, the federal government allocated a record N3.52 trillion to education in the 2026 budget and secured $552 million for the HOPE-EDU programme, which targets 29 million children, over 500,000 teachers, and 65,000 public schools.

The report said the BESDA programme had returned over one million out-of-school children to learning, trained 1,400 Tsangaya teachers, and established 200 bilingual centres across 17 northern states.

It added that the AGILE programme had reached 7.19 million girls, with 3.7 million enrolled in secondary schools, while over 10,000 schools had benefited from improved facilities.

The NESRI index indicated that the administration had introduced a revised national curriculum that reintroduced Nigerian History and strengthened Civic and Heritage Studies.

The National Learning Assessment, for instance, had been restored to monitor pupils’ performance and identify learning gaps.

Under EduRevamp, 53,553 teachers had registered, while 51,794 joined the first cohort of the Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway (ATPP), a six-month programme offering professional qualifications, certification and licensing.

Backed by N2 billion, the programme targets 250,000 teachers by 2027. Also, the Inspire Live initiative provides online lessons from Primary One to Senior Secondary School Three, supported by certified teachers and AI-assisted learning.

Under Tinubu’s government, the statement stated, the TVET scheme had attracted over 2.8 million applications, with 156,446 verified trainees receiving free training, monthly stipends and start-up support.

The statement said, “More than N65.7 billion have already been disbursed to trainees, while another sum of N30.2 billion has gone to training centres. The government has also rehabilitated 38 technical colleges and introduced free technical education covering tuition, boarding, textbooks, and uniforms.

“Also, NELFUND, a flagship programme of the Tinubu administration in the education sector, has processed 1,659,853 student loan applications and disbursed N372.62 billion, comprising N192.89 billion for tuition and N179.73 billion for upkeep allowances across 319 tertiary institutions.”

The administration, according to the report, has resolved the age-long dispute between the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and government, and implemented the agreement that provided for 40 per cent increase in academic staff remuneration and improved welfare benefits.

Additionally, the Tertiary Institutions Staff Support Fund has disbursed N28 billion to 15,000 workers across 153 public institutions, offering eligible staff loans of up to N10 million for housing, healthcare, transportation and education.

The report added that the federal government was investing N110 billion in the rehabilitation of 18 federal medical schools across the six geopolitical zones.

Nursing enrolment rose from 81,480 in 2023 to 114,300 in 2025, while 20 STEM-focused tertiary institutions had been approved and 12 engineering and technology faculties were targeted for rehabilitation.

The federal government also provided N365 million annually for research and innovation through the National Laureate Prize, while the Student Venture Capital Grant disbursed over N2.5 billion to 45 student entrepreneurs, the report said. It added that each beneficiary could access up to N50 million in equity-free funding.

It said entrepreneurship certification was currently ongoing in 14 federal universities, while the Diaspora BRIDGE initiative had registered 1,141 Nigerian experts abroad, reaching 16,675 students across 107 tertiary institutions.

Still on the achievements recorded so far in the education sector, Alake, who is also Minister of Solid Minerals Development, quoted

Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, as saying the success of Tinubu-led education reforms would be measured by their impact on students, teachers, and institutions, rather than the amount of money allocated or the number of programmes introduced.

Alausa stated, “Our measure of success is not merely the amount of money allocated to education or the number of programmes introduced. It is the difference these interventions make in the lives of our children, students, teachers and institutions.”

Meanwhile, Tinubu departed Jeddah for Abuja on Wednesday after the successful completion of his Umrah, lesser Hajj, in the Holy city of Makkah.

The president’s plane, according to a release by presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, took off at the Royal Terminal of the King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, at 5:13pm Saudi time.

Deputy Governor of the Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin MISHAL bin Abdulaziz Al Saud; Nigerian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Ambassador Yakubu Gambo; and Hon. Consul-General, Ambassador Muazam Ibrahim Nayaya, accompanied the president to the airport.

Before departure, Tinubu had a brief meeting with the deputy governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace at the airport.

On arrival in Saudi Arabia last Thursday, the president led his delegation to perform the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah.

Last Sunday, Tinubu was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure, where he and members of his delegation performed the two raka’at prayers.

Inside the Holy Ka’abah, the president offered special supplications to Almighty Allah for lasting peace, security, unity, and prosperity in Nigeria, while seeking divine guidance, wisdom, and strength to continue to serve the Nigerian people.

Tinubu also prayed for Allah’s continued blessings upon Nigeria, its leaders, and citizens, expressing hope that the country’s diversity would be transformed into a source of strength, national cohesion, and shared prosperity.

The president’s visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia provided an opportunity for spiritual reflection, thanksgiving, and prayers for Nigeria, as well as renewed commitment to the national task of building a peaceful, united, and prosperous nation.

Tinubu expressed appreciation to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, for the special courtesies and hospitality extended to him and his delegation, particularly the privilege of accessing the Holy Ka’abah to offer prayers.
