posts.title: ADC: Learn from Americans, Reject APC; Atiku Overwhelmed by Massive Crowd at Sokoto Rally
posts.excerpt: Chuks Okocha in Abuja and Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on Nigerians to draw lessons from Tuesday’s midterm elections in the United States, where the
posts.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja and Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on Nigerians to draw lessons from Tuesday’s midterm elections in the United States, where the people voted against the ruling Republican Party, in what is considered a decisive rebuke of the ruling party’s leadership and unpopular economic policies.

In a statement by ADC National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party said the US election outcome demonstrated that the greatest power in any democracy belonged not to the president or the ruling party, but to ordinary citizens armed with their votes.

Meanwhile, ADC Presidential Campaign Council described the reception accorded its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, yesterday in Sokoto as a powerful expression of public anger against the President Bola Tinubu administration and the growing support for ADC’s promise to make life affordable again.

ADC stated, “Americans have shown that when politicians become arrogant, when policies punish ordinary people, and when those in power mistake popularity for a permanent licence to govern, the ballot box remains the ultimate instrument of accountability.

“American voters understand something Nigerians must also learn: elections are about the welfare of the citizens, not sentiments, political loyalties or personality cults. No leader is bigger than the people, and no political party is entitled to power forever.”

ADC stated that Nigerians had endured years of unprecedented economic hardship, worsening insecurity, and disappearing opportunities under the Tinubu-led APC government, yet they were being asked to reward the same party with another mandate.

The party said, in the statement, “We cannot continue to complain about the cost of living while voting for a president who has made life unaffordable. We cannot demand security while rewarding failure. We cannot earnestly yearn for change while sustaining the very political system responsible for our collective impoverishment.

“History beckons in 2027. Our voters’ cards must become instruments of change, not souvenirs of citizenship. Nigerians must turn out massively and vote for their own interests.

“The ADC and its candidates are offering Nigerians a clear alternative: Make Nigeria Affordable Again. Make Nigeria Safe Again. Give Nigerians Jobs Again.

“If Americans can use their votes to demand better, Nigerians can do the same. In 2027, let our votes speak louder than the APC-induced suffering.”

Atiku Overwhelmed by Sokoto Rally Crowd

ADC Presidential Campaign Council described the reception accorded Atiku in Sokoto as a powerful expression of public anger against the Tinubu administration and growing support for the party.

The ADC campaign was flagged off in Sokoto before a mammoth crowd that lined the route from Sultan Muhammad III International Airport to the party’s state secretariat.

According to a statement by Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the motorcade took three and a half hours to reach the rally venue as men and women, young and old, including mothers, gathered to welcome and accompany Atiku.

Shaibu said in several parts of the city, work came to a standstill, people left their offices and abandoned their daily activities to join the procession and attend the rally.

He said that was not a crowd assembled by inducement. It was a spontaneous turnout by Nigerians struggling with the cost of food, transport, fuel, and other basic necessities, he said.

Shaibu explained that attempts to frustrate the rally only deepened public resentment against the APC-controlled Sokoto State government, which he said denied ADC access to public facilities requested for the campaign flag-off, and placed obstacles in the path of the party’s legitimate campaign activities.

He said the federal government and its APC allies should understand that denying people a venue could not suppress their political choices.

Shaibu stated that in Sokoto, those efforts backfired because the people came out in even greater numbers and made their voices heard.

He explained that at the rally, Atiku reaffirmed his commitment to tackling the cost-of-living crisis and restoring hope to households and businesses.

Shaibu said the ADC presidential candidate’s plan included a targeted, production-based subsidy for qualifying petroleum products refined in Nigeria. By tying support to domestic production, the policy will help bring down the cost of fuel and ease the pressure that high transport and energy costs place on food prices and family budgets, he said.

Shaibu stated, ‘’The ADC message is clear: Nigerians deserve a government that makes life more affordable, supports local production and responds to the hardship people face every day.

“When you have a message that connects with the people, you do not need to rent a crowd. The people show up on their own.”

Tension as Community Guards Allegedly Shoot Two ADC Supporters En Route to Rally

Two persons believed to be supporters of ADC were, allegedly, shot by operatives of Sokoto State Community Guards along the Sokoto–Wurno Road, amid heightened political tension before the party’s presidential campaign rally in the state.

The incident, reportedly, occurred when the operatives barricaded the road linking Sokoto metropolis with the eastern part of the state, forcing vehicles conveying supporters to the rally venue to turn back.

The victims were said to be among those going to attend the campaign rally for the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku, in Sokoto.

Eyewitnesses alleged that the shooting followed an altercation between occupants of a vehicle conveying the supporters and the guards.

The operatives were accused of opening fire during the confrontation, leaving two persons with gunshot injuries. The victims were subsequently rushed to a hospital for medical attention.

A source said it took the intervention of the Civilian JTF in the convoy of Senator Ibrahim Lamido, coordinator of the Sokoto State ADC Presidential Campaign Council, before vehicles were allowed to move through the checkpoint.

The community guards had previously been accused of attacking the ADC governorship candidate, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto.

The latest allegation further heightened concerns over the conduct of security personnel and the need to ensure that political activities were conducted without intimidation or violence.

Sokoto State Police Command Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmad Rufai, when contacted, said the command had yet to receive information about the alleged shooting, and as such, could not confirm the incident.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/05/adc-learn-from-americans-reject-apc-atiku-overwhelmed-by-massive-crowd-at-sokoto-rally/

posts.title: 2027: Makinde Unveils Manifesto, Prioritises Microeconomic Reforms for Citizens’ Welfare
posts.excerpt: Chuks Okocha in Abuja The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, yesterday unveiled his RESET NIGERIA manifesto stating that his microeconomic
posts.content:
Restates four years transitional government of national unity

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, yesterday unveiled his RESET NIGERIA manifesto stating that his microeconomic reforms would lead to the overall welfare of Nigerians and not the present poverty and hunger in the country. He also hinted at overhauling the present political system to address the social challenges in the country. He explained that this was why his four-year tenure, if elected, would be transitional to reset the polity, but added that, as a serving President, “I will not be a beneficiary.”

Addressing party chieftains in Abuja, Makinde said, “For us, macroeconomic reforms must translate into improvements in people’s lives. “I think it was one Kanu Adamu who, in a post about two days ago, said that microeconomic stability should mean having access to affordable food. What does macroeconomic stability mean if it does not improve the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians? “Macroeconomic stability must have a direct impact on the people through job creation, improved incomes and a lower cost of living. These are issues we cannot shy away from,” he stressed.

According to the APM presidential candidate, “The second concern is that government must take responsibility for results or the lack of them. “I have been trying to explain particularly that we dare not reinforce the system that produced the current situation. Let us leave that discussion until 2027. “In 2027, within the first two weeks, we will begin to address the issues and set the process in motion.

“Nigeria has the resources and the capacity to achieve greatness. Nigeria is rich in natural resources and human resources, but our leaders are poor in ideas. “Thirdly, our institutions must work across our differences rather than allowing division and bribery to obstruct national development. “It should not matter which political party you belong to or who you know. What should matter is national development and the commitment to improving the lives of our people,” he stated.

According to Governor Makinde, “We want a situation where some of the ideas contained in our manifesto will be brought into the open and discussed. “However, I would like to emphasise that we did not come up with these ideas on our own. They are the outcome of extensive consultations. We held town hall meetings across all the geopolitical zones of Nigeria and listened to the people. We asked them: What would you like to see? What kind of Nigeria are you thinking about?

“The outcome of those consultations informed our agenda. I remember that, somewhere in the North-East, somebody asked me: Can you give us the Tafawa Balewa of our time? Are you going to be the Awolowo of our time or the Azikiwe of our time?

“I remember the passion with which that question was asked and the expectations it carried. It made me realise the weight of the responsibility before us. Therefore, we must take this responsibility seriously. We must not disappoint Nigeria,” he stressed.

He said that these ideas were not his alone, as they were the ideas of Nigeria’s founding fathers.

According to him, “Somewhere along the line, in the way a relay race is conducted, one person runs the first lap before handing over the baton to another runner. I think we dropped the baton somewhere along the line. Therefore, we must now return to rebuilding the Nigeria our founding fathers envisioned.” Talking about the Nigeria of his dream, Governor Makinde said, “We want a Nigeria that works for every Nigerian, irrespective of the part of the country they come from, their religious background or their ethnic identity.

“Our founding fathers understood that we had differences and rivalries in this country. That was why they organised constitutional conferences and engaged in discussions about the future of Nigeria. I believe our founding fathers were undoubtedly among the best this country had to offer at that time. “When you go to the universities, you see students graduating at the top of their classes. In the past, many of those who excelled academically went into the public service.

“Today, however, the best of the best no longer want to work in the public sector. They prefer to work in the private sector because of the financial opportunities available there.

“You cannot blame them for that because it is a simple proposition. I do not want to complicate things. I do not want a situation where I start using big grammar such as price modulation to explain issues that should be straightforward.”

In view of this, he said, “My simple proposition is that government must make life easier for the people. That is all.

“We must develop people’s abilities and expand their access to opportunities. We must also have institutions that work.

“Concrete promises alone are not enough. Every promise must be linked to a responsible institution, a delivery plan and measurable results that citizens can verify. It is not enough to say we have this or that and then engage in arguments. What matters is that citizens can verify the results. That is the standard behind our Reset Agenda.

“There are four major concerns that have shaped my decision to seek the presidency. I did not just wake up one day and suddenly decide to become President of Nigeria. There are four fundamental issues driving my decision, and they form the basis of the Reset Agenda.

“As the vice-presidential candidate said, we held discussions despite coming from completely different backgrounds and different parts of Nigeria. I am Yoruba, from the South-West, while he is Hausa.

“Let me also use this opportunity to appreciate our national leaders from the different parts of the country. During the process, they made contributions and sacrifices, even when it meant having to lose sleep at night.

“Our leaders from the North-East and the North-Central also contributed immensely to the process.

“The first concern is the emphasis on macroeconomic reforms to the detriment of broad-based economic growth.

“It is almost like someone saying, ‘This family has a lot of money in its savings account,’ without considering the welfare of the people who make up that family,” he stated.

On the need for political realignment, Makinde said, “Political parties will come and go, but our national development plans and the things we must do for our people must remain constant. We must continue to implement them, irrespective of the political party in power.

“Fourthly, more than half of Nigeria’s population lives in poverty. These people must be at the centre of government decisions. They should never be treated as an afterthought.

“All four issues I have mentioned are interconnected, and they require a coordinated response. This is why Nigeria needs a Reset Agenda.” According to the APM presidential candidate, “So, let us get to the heart of the Reset Agenda.

“Our economic agenda focuses on reducing the structural cost of living. We must lower the cost of production and enable Nigerian businesses to become competitive.

“For instance, no matter how hard I try, a manufacturer who relies on generators powered by diesel will continue to incur high production costs. We must make it possible for manufacturers to connect to the national electricity grid and access electricity at a lower cost.

“Of course, the cost of energy remains a major burden on businesses. We export plastics and many other products to the Republic of Benin. Today, some businesses are leaving Nigeria because our operating environment is not competitive enough.

“So, what do we mean by the structural cost of living? We are talking about avoidable costs that make essential goods and services more expensive for you and me.”

On the Tuesday US midterm elections, he said, “By the way, this week, I was watching developments in the United States when I left the house, and what I saw irritated me. In the US, one political party can gain control of Congress, the Senate and the House of Representatives. That is the kind of democracy we want to practise.

“However, because of developments affecting democracy in the United States, oil prices declined by about one per cent. For most of last week, crude oil traded at about $100 per barrel.

“As the price of crude oil rises in the international market, more money is taken from the pockets of Nigerians and transferred into the Federation Account. “I know how this works because, for several years now, I have participated in the process of federal allocations. Every month, state commissioners of finance come to Abuja for the allocation process.

“In fact, someone once said that state allocations were given to us by the Federal Government. That is not the case. The money is paid into the Federation Account and must constitutionally be shared among the different tiers of government.

“Therefore, nobody should say that the President gave you this money or that money. These are revenues belonging to the Federation and are shared in accordance with the Constitution.

“So, when crude oil sells at a higher price in the international market, what happens? More money is taken from the pockets of ordinary Nigerians and transferred into the Federation Account.

“Therefore, as part of our Reset Agenda, we must ask an important question: How will this additional revenue be used to benefit the majority of Nigerians? “What value does every Nigerian derive from the increase in oil prices, particularly considering that we are not yet a sufficiently productive country?” On the subsidy regime, he said, “Yes, there has been a lot of political debate about petroleum subsidy, but under our Reset Agenda, we have a clear pathway to deliver value to Nigerians.

“I am particularly passionate about this because the oil and gas industry is one I have worked in for almost all my life.

“This is part of the Nigerian dream. I left Ibadan in early October 1990 with just a bag containing a few belongings, perhaps two pairs of trousers, three or four shirts and a book. The only thing I had was the fare to travel to Kaduna with my degree.

“I travelled across the country, searched for opportunities and eventually secured a job. I got married, had children and built my life in that environment. I also established my business there, working and growing through the opportunities available to me.

“Therefore, when people talk about value creation and value distribution, these are things I experienced and practised in those days.

“I know what it means to create value, and I believe Nigerians must derive value from the increase in the price of crude oil in the international market. “The government has been talking about price modulation and the Presidential CNG Initiative. Some of these interventions may provide short-term solutions, but we must also consider the long-term approach.

“There are certain things that Nigerians, including ordinary people on the streets, already understand about the current administration.

“For instance, when it comes to the federal government’s budget, there is a lack of transparency. Today, Nigerians do not have a clear understanding of the projects being implemented and the actual performance of the budget,” Makinde stressed.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/05/2027-makinde-unveils-manifesto-prioritises-microeconomic-reforms-for-citizens-welfare/

posts.title: Jameson Backs the Businesses Behind the Business
posts.excerpt: Jameson Wholesale Offer Recognizes Trade Partners with Trucks, Generators and Other Rewards Pernod Ricard Nigeria, through its Jameson brand, is investing in its wholesale channel through the Jameson
posts.content:
Jameson Wholesale Offer Recognizes Trade Partners with Trucks, Generators and Other Rewards

Pernod Ricard Nigeria, through its Jameson brand, is investing in its wholesale channel through the Jameson Wholesale Offer 2026, a trade initiative designed to recognize wholesalers’ contributions to the company’s distribution network and provide business assets that can support their day-to-day operations.

Running from 14 September to 13 December 2026, the offer features a range of rewards for qualifying wholesalers, including 30 delivery trucks comprising 10 five-tonne trucks and 20 1.5-tonne trucks. Other rewards include 100 units each of 7.5KVA petrol generators, side-by-side refrigerators and 75-inch televisions, alongside thousands of additional items such as tabletop gas cookers, rechargeable fans and air fryers.

The scale and variety of these rewards reflect the important role wholesalers play in moving products through the distribution network. Beyond purchasing and reselling products, wholesalers manage inventory, coordinate deliveries, respond to retailer demand and help ensure products remain available across different outlets.

For businesses operating in this part of the value chain, access to reliable delivery vehicles and essential business equipment can support daily operations and help them respond to the demands of their customers. Through the Jameson Wholesale Offer, Pernod Ricard Nigeria is providing qualifying trade partners with rewards that extend beyond the products they purchase.

Emmanuel Ehikioya Musa, Head of Trade Marketing Nigeria, said: “Our wholesale partners play an important role in ensuring our products reach retailers and other businesses. We recognise the work that goes into managing stock, meeting customer demand and keeping products moving. Through the Jameson Wholesale Offer, we want to acknowledge their contribution with rewards that can support their businesses and day-to-day operations.”

The offer also includes a sell-out component that allows wholesalers to access additional items to give to their retailers. These include tabletop gas cookers, rechargeable fans and air fryers, providing another way for wholesalers to recognise their customers and support their business relationships.

For Pernod Ricard Nigeria, strengthening the wholesale channel is an important part of maintaining relationships with the businesses that help connect its portfolio to retailers. The Jameson Wholesale Offer provides a practical way to recognise these partners while offering rewards that have potential value beyond the immediate transaction.

Ikechukwu Agu, Commercial Director, Pernod Ricard Nigeria, said: “Our trade partners are an important part of how we do business, and we value the role they play in making our products available to customers. Through initiatives like the Jameson Wholesale Offer, we are recognising their contribution and reinforcing our commitment to building strong, long-term relationships across the distribution network.”

The Jameson Wholesale Offer 2026 runs until 13 December 2026. Participation is subject to the programme’s terms and conditions.

About Pernod Ricard Nigeria

Established in 2012, Pernod Ricard Nigeria is a member of the Pernod Ricard Group, a worldwide leader in the spirits and champagne industry, combining traditional craftsmanship, state-of-the-art brand building and global distribution technologies. Our prestigious portfolio of premium to luxury brands includes Absolut vodka, Ricard pastis, Ballantine’s, Chivas Regal, Royal Salute, and The Glenlivet Scotch whiskies, Jameson Irish whiskey, Martell cognac, Havana Club rum, Beefeater gin, Malibu liqueur and Mumm and Perrier-Jouët champagnes. Our mission is to ensure the long-term development of our brands with full respect for people and the environment, while empowering our employees to be ambassadors of our purposeful, inclusive and responsible culture of authentic conviviality.

About Jameson Irish Whiskey

Founded in 1780 by John Jameson, Jameson is the best-selling Irish whiskey in the world. Produced in the distillery in Midleton, County Cork, from malted and unmalted Irish barley, Jameson’s blended whiskeys are triple-distilled, resulting in exceptional smoothness.

posts.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
posts.excerpt: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would
posts.content:
I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me.

Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century.

Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life

And the cars! Oh, the cars!

Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different.

I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse.

I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion.

I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought.

Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary.

Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money!

That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. The country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso (CUC), and the Cuban peso (CUP). I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors. The notes I had just rejected were CUP notes, used by the locals.

I was relieved, slightly embarrassed and suddenly very curious. How had I been in Cuba for four days without understanding something so fundamental to paying for things?

The top notes (CUC) have monuments and are for tourists. The bottom notes (CUP) have national heroes and are for locals.

Suddenly, I began wondering how much I had already spent and how I had been paying far more than necessary. I recalled tipping a tour guide 10 CUC. He had been delighted, even asking me whether I was sure I wanted to give him that much. At the time, I thought I was simply being generous. But after learning that the commonly used conversion was around 25 CUP to 1 CUC, I understood why he might have been so pleased. My tip was equivalent to about 250 CUP. I did not regret rewarding someone for good service, but I was beginning to understand how easily a visitor could spend money without appreciating its value.

Then came the experience that really opened my eyes. I had been eating at a particular local food joint and paying 5 CUC for my meal because the menu read $5. I always enjoyed the food and always handed over 5 CUC because 1 USD was equivalent to 1 CUC. But now that I knew about CUP, curiosity got the better of me.

On my next visit, I decided to observe before ordering. A local customer arrived ahead of me. I waited and watched what he ordered, how much he paid and which notes he handed to the cashier.

Five CUP.

Five CUP?

I watched him complete his transaction and leave. Then I stepped forward and ordered the same meal.

When the time came to pay, I brought out my newly acquired CUP notes and handed over 5 CUP. The cashier raised an eyebrow. I pointed to the menu and explained that I had just watched the customer before me order the same meal and pay the same amount. I was not guessing. I got my meal for 5 CUP as against the 5 CUC I had always paid.

At the commonly used conversion rate of 25 CUP to 1 CUC, my previous payment of 5 CUC was equivalent to 125 CUP. I had been paying 125 CUP for a meal that I had just watched a local buy for a mere 5 CUP

Twenty-five times the price!

I was stunned. Part of me wanted to laugh at the absurdity of it all; another part wondered how many other times I had paid without understanding the difference. I had been so confident, so comfortable reaching into my purse and handing over my money. Yet I had missed a detail that could make a significant difference to my spending. That local joint visit became one of my most memorable Cuban experiences. Not because of the food, but because of the lesson I had been taught.

Of course, my story is about Cuba in 2019. The currency system has since changed. On 1 January 2021, Cuba discontinued the CUC as part of a currency reform, leaving the Cuban peso (CUP) as the sole official currency. The two-currency arrangement that caught me off guard belongs to that chapter of the country’s history.

What remains with me, however, is not just the currency confusion. I remember Cuba’s faded pastel buildings, the vintage cars gleaming beneath the sun, the music in the streets and the thrill of driving along the coast in that neon-green convertible. The country was vibrant, beautiful and full of contrasts.

But whenever I travel somewhere new, I remind myself to ask questions, understand the local currency, and never assume I know how things work.

Source: https://www.bellanaija.com/2026/11/dayo-akinbode-what-travelling-to-cuba-taught-me-about-money/

posts.title: Logan’s Dafne Keen Was Offered Cocaine When She Was 11
posts.excerpt: Dafne Keen says she was offered cocaine at wrap parties as a child. The actor was around 11 to 13 and says she refused. During a recent podcast appearance, Keen explained that seeing adults drink and
posts.content:
Photo Credit: 20th Century Fox Dafne Keen says she was offered cocaine at wrap parties as a child. The actor was around 11 to 13 and says she refused. During a recent podcast appearance, Keen explained that seeing adults drink and use drugs helped her avoid both.

Dafne Keen details witnessing cocaine and drinking culture

Dafne Keen, now 21, discussed her choices during an appearance on Michael Rosenbaum’s Inside of You podcast. She told the host that she has “never been drunk enough to even have a hangover,” describing herself as a “control freak” about drinking. Seeing that culture as a child made her wary of trying it herself.

When Rosenbaum asked about the drinking she had witnessed, Keen revealed that she was “getting offered coke at wrap parties.” She said she turned it down, and joked that she was not getting involved at such a young age. Rosenbaum reacted with surprise at the idea of a child encountering drugs so early. “11 or 12? Man, I didn’t start that early,” he said.

Staying sober has not stopped Keen from enjoying nights out, she explained. She likes music, dancing and spending time with people, and said she can stay out until 6 a.m. without drinking or taking anything.

The actress described herself as a fun time and said she simply does not need substances to enjoy herself. As a teenager, she sometimes claimed she was already high to avoid pressure from others. In reality, she said, she would be drinking soda and pretending to be high.

Keen also spoke warmly about Hugh Jackman, her costar in Logan, in which she played Laura, also known as X-23. She described him as the “best on-screen dad” who offered encouragement and advice. Jackman, she said, made sure “that no one was abusing my hours.” Jackman also helped her enjoy the set and shielded her from tensions behind the scenes.

Sydney Sweeney shares new video as Cindy Lou Who for Syrn

Sydney Sweeney’s lingerie brand SYRN shared a new video on Instagram promoting its holiday collection. The brand’s caption read, “Our gift to you: early access to All I Want Is Plaid, available NOW.” The video continues the Cindy Lou Who-inspired campaign from How the Grinch Stole Christmas.

View this post on Instagram

Sweeney rocks red-and-black plaid lingerie pieces with oversized bows in the new promotional video. She also pairs the look with a white fur-trimmed cape and thigh-high stockings. Meanwhile, decorated Christmas trees, wrapped gifts, and Christmas lights round out the festive setting.

Sweeney first unveiled the Cindy Lou Who-inspired look on October 21. The original advertisement featured her wearing plaid pajamas and a festive cape while carrying gifts. Additionally, another scene showed her decorating a Christmas tree in a Corpse Bride-inspired outfit.

However, the campaign drew online criticism after its initial launch. Many commenters pointed out that Cindy Lou Who is traditionally portrayed as a young child. Despite the backlash, the brand has now released five additional photos and videos for the collection.

Notably, this is not the first time a Sweeney advertisement has stirred controversy. Her 2025 American Eagle campaign faced significant online backlash. Furthermore, her Novig ads also attracted criticism, including from Euphoria co-star Sharon Stone. Stone called out the broader issue of women in gambling advertising at the time.

SYRN’s latest post has already racked up over 9,600 likes and 78 comments in just 14 hours. Fan responses range from compliments to suggestions for future products. One commenter even pitched the idea of Sweeney starring in a Grinch remake alongside Jim Carrey. The brand continues to push forward with the holiday campaign despite the ongoing discourse around the Cindy Lou Who imagery.

posts.title: Longtime ABC & CBS Affiliate Anchor Harold Greene Dies
posts.excerpt: Harold Greene, a familiar presence in Los Angeles living rooms for decades, has passed away at 82. The veteran broadcaster, who anchored news at both ABC and CBS affiliates in the city, died Tuesday n
posts.content:
Photo Credit: @ABC7 | YouTube Harold Greene, a familiar presence in Los Angeles living rooms for decades, has passed away at 82. The veteran broadcaster, who anchored news at both ABC and CBS affiliates in the city, died Tuesday night, his family confirmed.

LA anchor Harold Greene dies at 82

Courtney Greene, the anchor’s daughter, shared the news on Wednesday on Facebook. She said her father “signed off for the last time” on Tuesday and that both she and her mother were at his bedside. “We have a feeling he’s already settling into the great newsroom in the sky, no doubt with a few suggestions on how things should be run,” Courtney Greene wrote. “He was so very loved, and we know he will be missed by many.”

Greene’s broadcasting journey began behind the scenes in Los Angeles, where he worked as a reporter and producer for KABC. He soon headed south to San Diego, helping launch KCST-TV’s (now KNSD) news operation before co-anchoring at KGTV. By 1978, the anchor had returned to Los Angeles, sharing the desk with Eyewitness News icon Jerry Dunphy.

Four years later, he partnered with Joanne Ishimine on ABC7’s weekend broadcasts. When Dunphy departed, Greene stepped into the weeknight 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. chairs, later adding the 5 p.m. and 11 p.m. editions. He also fronted lighter local fare, including Hollywood Close-Up and A.M. Los Angeles.

In 2001, Harold Greene shifted to CBS 2, where he joined Ann Martin and sportscaster Jim Hill. Laura Diaz and weatherman Johnny Mountain eventually came aboard, bringing former KABC colleagues back together. KCBS/KCAL let Greene and Martin go in 2008.

Moreover, over his career, Greene amassed 10 Golden Mike awards, two Emmys, three Edward R. Murrow Awards, twelve L.A. Press Club Awards and the Columbia Graduate School of Journalism Award. He also earned a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

A memorial service is planned for after the holidays.

posts.title: 2Baba ends six-year album wait, announces ‘Oldest Young Man’ release date
posts.excerpt: Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has announced November 27, 2026, as the release date for his forthcoming album, ‘Oldest Young Man’, his first studio project in six year
posts.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has announced November 27, 2026, as the release date for his forthcoming album, ‘Oldest Young Man’, his first studio project in six years.

The singer announced the date in a post on his Instagram handle on Tuesday, describing the project as timeless music.

“The legacy continues. OLDEST YOUNG MAN drops 27.11.26. Timeless music, no expiration date,” he wrote.

View this post on Instagram

The announcement comes after months of teasing the album on social media, with 2Baba repeatedly using its title in his Instagram captions.

In August, he wrote: “I’ve lived it, I’ve seen it, I’m still here. My new album, Oldest Young Man, soon come.”

On his birthday, the singer also described himself as the “forever the oldest young man”.

The upcoming project will be his first album since ‘Warriors’, released in 2020, which was his eighth studio album.

2Baba first rose to prominence in the 1990s, composing jingles before co-founding the music group Plantashun Boiz with Blackface and Faze in 1996.

He later established himself as one of the pioneers of Afropop, influencing generations of Nigerian artistes with his music.

His album releases include ‘Face 2 Face’ (2004), ‘Grass 2 Grace’ (2006), ‘The Unstoppable’ (2009), ‘The Unstoppable International Edition’ (2010), ‘Away and Beyond’ (2012), ‘The Ascension’, ‘Rewind, Select, Update’ (2015) and ‘Warriors’ (2020).

posts.title: Politano: ‘Napoli cannot have this attitude, only Italians take responsibility’
posts.excerpt: Matteo Politano seemed to launch a broadside at his Napoli teammates after the 4-1 defeat...
posts.content:
Matteo Politano seemed to launch a broadside at his Napoli teammates after the 4-1 defeat to FC Porto, noting it was ‘just us Italians’ who took responsibility for their difficulties.

The Partenopei had started quite strong at the Estadio do Dragao this evening, despite having a decimated squad with 10 players out between injury and ineligibility, leaving only three senior outfield figures on the bench.

The Jan Bednarek header on a corner was cancelled out by Scott McTominay, but they crumbled in the final 20 minutes to Gabriel Veiga’s counter-attack, another free header from Jakub Kiwior and the late Samu penalty with Rafa Marin red card.

Politano upset with Napoli teammates

ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Matteo Politano of SSC Napoli celebrates after scoring team’s second goal during the Serie A match between AC Monza and SSC Napoli at U-Power Stadium on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images)When Politano was the first to speak after the match, Sky Sport Italia noted it was ‘always you’ who comes to represent the squad in the media room.

“It would be nice if a few other teammates came here to give an explanation and not just us Italians, but never mind,” replied Politano with what could only be described as a bitter laugh.

“I never hide my face.”

Napoli had hoped for better after the 2-0 Serie A defeat to Juventus at the weekend, but have now lost three out of four Champions League matches.

PORTO, PORTUGAL – NOVEMBER 04: Players of SSC Napoli pose for a team photograph before the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Porto and SSC Napoli at Estadio do Dragao on November 04, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images)“We didn’t see the progress we wanted. The first half had been a good approach, we had equalised and created a few more chances that we could’ve done better, but we conceded two goals from corners and they hit the crossbar twice, all from the same situations, so there’s not a lot to say there,” added Politano.

“The attitude is one that a team like ours cannot have at this level.”

Considering his comment about only the Italians stepping up, does Politano feel there is a lack of unity at Napoli, or that Max Allegri is losing control of the side?

“I was not attacking anyone, we have a squad that is struggling, but we need to come together and think about this next game before the break for international duty. Hopefully we can recover a few players during that spell and then our season can really begin.”

PORTO, PORTUGAL – NOVEMBER 04: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of SSC Napoli, reacts during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Porto and SSC Napoli at Estadio do Dragao on November 04, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images)It is a recurring theme that Napoli tend to crumble in the last 30 minutes of matches, both in Serie A and Europe, so is it purely a physical problem?

“I don’t know, we have asked ourselves that too. At times, it is not even a tactical issue, as we are all behind the ball, but we lack the determination and sharpness, we don’t read situations well or sense danger,” added Politano.

“In the Champions League and Serie A, the moment you leave the slightest bit of space, they punish you.”

Speaking to Amazon Prime Video Italia, Politano also added that “losing 2-1 and losing 4-1 is a big difference. We melted at the second goal and we need to take a good look at ourselves.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/politano-napoli-only-italians-responsibility/

posts.title: Allegri: ‘Napoli have limitations, these mistakes cost you matches’
posts.excerpt: Max Allegri admits Napoli have ‘limitations’ after a 4-1 defeat to FC Porto, as their...
posts.content:
Max Allegri admits Napoli have ‘limitations’ after a 4-1 defeat to FC Porto, as their Champions League campaign hangs by a thread. ‘These are the mistakes that cost you matches.’

The Partenopei were truly decimated going into the Estadio do Dragao, as they were missing 10 players between injuries and ineligibility, leaving only three senior outfield figures on the bench.

In the circumstances, they still got to half-time with the score at 1-1, Scott McTominay cancelling out the free header from Jan Bednarek.

However, they crumbled in the final 20 minutes with a Gabriel Veiga counter-attack, identical Jakub Kiwior header on a corner, and Samu’s penalty after a Rafa Marin red card offence.

Allegri sees Napoli running on empty

PORTO, PORTUGAL – NOVEMBER 04: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of SSC Napoli, looks on before the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Porto and SSC Napoli at Estadio do Dragao on November 04, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images)“We made mistakes on two set plays, the team had in my view a good performance up to the 70th minute,” Allegri told Sky Sport Italia.

“It was an aggressive performance, we went man for man, but then conceded this second goal on a bouncing ball and with fatigue we didn’t push up in time for the offside.

“These are errors that unfortunately can happen when you are tired. The tempo is high in the Champions League, and in those final minutes we were struggling, as they hit the crossbar twice just before the goal and were cutting through us fairly easily.”

Allegri is now under serious pressure after a series of defeats in big games, and they lost three of the first four Champions League fixtures, so can he turn this around?

“We have a game on Sunday against Lazio and need to recuperate, because these are the only players we’ve got,” he replied.

“You win and lose matches on details, not the big things, but the small ones. The team fought and chased Porto around man for man as long as they could, but then we ran out of fuel.

“It’s like a Cup Final for us against Lazio and then hopefully we can recover some players during the break for international duty.”

PORTO, PORTUGAL – NOVEMBER 04: Scott McTominay of SSC Napoli celebrates scoring his team’s first goal with Kevin De Bruyne during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Porto and SSC Napoli at Estadio do Dragao on November 04, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images)This is going to be an extremely tough campaign for Allegri and Napoli, who are falling behind in Serie A and in Europe.

“I had a similar season at Juventus, I’ve been through this before, the only thing we must do is keep working, fix a few things, have that extra metre and extra bit of concentration in certain moments.

“This evening was a better performance than the one we saw on Sunday in Turin, certainly.”

PORTO, PORTUGAL – NOVEMBER 04: Players of SSC Napoli pose for a team photograph before the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Porto and SSC Napoli at Estadio do Dragao on November 04, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images)Due to the vast shortage of players, Allegri changed his system to a 3-5-1-1 with Kevin De Bruyne in support of Rasmus Hojlund upfront, so is this the way forward or is it just an emergency?

“I decided to play this way tonight because it was the only way. It went well for over an hour, but Porto made five substitutions, they had fresh legs, and we didn’t have anyone left to introduce.

“If you want to play this way, aggressive and high press, you need to have fresh legs off the bench. It’s either that or you defend in front of your penalty area, but we struggle to do that, so it was the only way.

“Unfortunately, we conceded the second goal on our own clearance.”

— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 4, 2026

Sky Sport Italia pundit Fabio Capello asked Allegri if there was anyone who could lead the Napoli defence when they were so visibly disorganised.

“You are perfectly right, but if you look at the bounce of the ball, Beukema just pushed up straight, but when the ball is bouncing around, then he has to mark the man. It was a distraction, he might’ve been tired, but these are details and it was the same thing in Turin.

“There too, there seemed to be no sign of danger, but then we made a mistake, that time it was Marianucci who turned the wrong way. These are mistakes that make you lose games,” replied the Napoli coach.

PORTO, PORTUGAL – NOVEMBER 04: Andre Silva of FC Porto is challenged by Amir Rrahmani of SSC Napoli during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Porto and SSC Napoli at Estadio do Dragao on November 04, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images)Allegri then seemed to suggest this was not just down to the current injury crisis, but rather his lack of faith in the side.

“I know the limitations of this squad. In the first game with Genoa, I was accused of having a bad first half, but it was because we needed to control the tempo. Lately, we’ve had good first halves, but then fall away in the second half, it’s because we have a limited squad.

“If the same lot play every three days, the tempo is high, by the 70th minute it becomes a different match. You can only control that if you have eight or nine players on the bench. Now we’ve got one more game to play with Lazio, then we’ll see what happens when more return.”

posts.title: Hotel accommodation: ‘This is not democracy, APC should allow parties to campaign without hindrance’ — NDC
posts.excerpt: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of attempting to restrict the democratic space and frustrate opposition activities, alleging that hotels in
posts.content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of attempting to restrict the democratic space and frustrate opposition activities, alleging that hotels in Abuja have denied the party access to their facilities for meetings.

The party made the allegations in a statement posted on its X platform on Thursday, calling on the APC to allow all political parties to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general election.

The NDC alleged that it had faced discrimination from some hotels in Abuja, despite meeting the requirements for the use of their facilities.

According to the party, a hotel (name withheld) cancelled agreements for the use of its facilities on two occasions, including arrangements for its second National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting in June 2026.

It alleged that the hotel recently declined another request for its facilities, claiming that the decision was based on an instruction from an undisclosed authority.

The party also accused an other hotel of refusing to make its facilities available for a meeting despite its compliance with the conditions stipulated by the hotel.

The NDC further alleged that its recent unveiling of the National Campaign Council was nearly disrupted after the host venue reportedly asked the party to collect a refund of its payment, saying it was no longer willing to make its facilities available.

It, however, said its insistence on using the facility, for which it had already paid, eventually compelled the hotel to honour the arrangement.

Describing the alleged incidents as undemocratic, the party said the development represented an attempt to frustrate opposition activities and restrict political participation.

“This is not democracy. The APC should allow all parties to campaign without let or hindrance, and give Nigerians the opportunity to make their choice on who governs them,” the statement said.

The party also called on Nigerians and supporters of democracy to condemn what it described as anti-people and anti-democratic actions by these hotels.

The statement was signed by the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, who reaffirmed the NDC’s commitment to serving Nigerians with passion and patriotism.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/hotel-accommodation-this-is-not-democracy-apc-should-allow-parties-to-campaign-without-hindrance-ndc/

posts.title: City Boy Movement Plans 100,000-man Solidarity Walk For Tinubu, Others In Borno
posts.excerpt: The City Boy Movement, Borno State chapter, has announced a 100,000-man solidarity walk scheduled to take place in Maiduguri on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, to express the organisation’s full support
posts.content:
The City Boy Movement, Borno State chapter, has announced a 100,000-man solidarity walk scheduled to take place in Maiduguri on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, to express the organisation’s full support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima.

Ahead of the 2027 general election, the organisation said the 100,000-man Solidarity Walk is in solidarity with the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in the state, Alhaji Mustapha Gubio, and other candidates of the party.

Director of the state chapter of the City Boy Movement, Comrade Mahmud Muhammad, explained that the solidarity walk is aimed at bringing together youths, women, political stakeholders, community mobilisers and supporters from across the 27 local government areas of Borno State to demonstrate their support for the Tinubu-Shettima administration, the Renewed Hope Agenda and the APC.

In a statement issued on Thursday, Mahmud, who is also the Personal Assistant to the President on Domestic Affairs (North-east) (Office of the Vice-President), said the event will also provide an opportunity for participants to demonstrate their commitment to peaceful political participation, democratic engagement and collective civic expression.

He noted that the march will commence at 8:00am from the Shehu’s Palace, Maiduguri and proceed to the Borno State Government House, where the organisers intend to present a solidarity message.

The statement read in part: “The City Boy Movement invites youths, women, APC stakeholders, community leaders and supporters from across Borno State to participate in the event and be part of this public expression of solidarity.

“The movement calls on all participants to maintain peace, demonstrate discipline and conduct themselves responsibly throughout the exercise. Participants are expected to respect public order, cooperate with relevant security personnel and avoid any actions capable of disrupting the peace.”

Mahmud further said that The City Boy Movement, Borno State Chapter, was looking forward to “a peaceful and orderly event that reflects the spirit of responsible civic participation”.

posts.title: 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike
posts.excerpt: The FCT minister acknowledged Kwankwaso’s popularity but questioned whether his political influence extended beyond Kano State, where he won the 2023 presidential election. The post 2027: Obi’s wave d
posts.content:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has dismissed the political support behind Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying the wave that propelled him in the 2023 election no longer exists.

Wike also described Obi as a dramatist, insisting that the former Anambra State governor had nothing to offer Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election.

The minister spoke on Thursday during his monthly media chat in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where he questioned the prospects of the NDC presidential ticket featuring Obi and former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.

“All this so-called Obi kererenke doesn’t exist again. I have killed it,” Wike said.

He argued that the political circumstances that helped Obi secure significant support in the 2023 presidential election had changed.

“Nigerians know that Obi has nothing to offer, he is a dramatist. You were there when Soludo exposed him,” the minister said.

Wike also criticised the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, saying Nigerians had already given him and other politicians opportunities to govern.

“Nigerians know that Atiku and co have been given the opportunity, but they did not do anything. Nigerians know that the former governor of Rivers State looted our state,” he said.

The FCT minister acknowledged Kwankwaso’s popularity but questioned whether his political influence extended beyond Kano State, where he won the 2023 presidential election.

“I agree that Kwankwaso is very popular, but he ran in 2023 and won in Kano, fine, but what about the other northern states? What about the North-Central, what will happen there?” he asked.

Wike further questioned whether Obi still enjoyed the level of financial and popular support associated with his 2023 presidential campaign.

“The Obi wave is dead and buried. How many people are contributing money for Obi today?” he said.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027-obis-wave-doesnt-exist-again-he-has-nothing-to-offer-wike/

posts.title: ADC crisis: Bala Gombe reacts as court sacks David Mark, nullifies Atiku's emergence as presidential candidate
posts.excerpt: Factional National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Bala Gombe, has reacted to the court judgement that sacked David Mark's faction of the party and nullified Atiku Abubakar's candida
posts.content:
Factional National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Bala Gombe, has reacted to the court judgement that sacked David Mark's faction of the party and nullified Atiku Abubakar's candidacy for the 2027 presidential election.

Gombe commended the Federal High Court and the trial judge for what he described as the independent, impartial and intellectually rigorous manner in which the matter was handled and determined.

He said his commendation, as a citizen and stakeholder in the nation's democracy, was that of someone who recognised that when a court speaks with clarity, courage and fidelity to the law, the public must also respond with gratitude.

"By every measure, this was a politically sensitive, highly charged and nationally watched dispute. It touched on party autonomy, internal democracy, constitutional supremacy within political associations, and the proper role of the Independent National Electoral Commission as regulator," Gombe said in a statement reacting to the judgement.

"It is precisely in such cases that judicial independence is most tested, and most needed.

"By subjecting the question of leadership emergence to constitutional and statutory scrutiny, rather than to political expediency, His Lordship affirmed a foundational principle of Nigerian jurisprudence as provided in Sections 1, 6, 228 and 223(1) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria: political parties are not above their own constitutions, and the Electoral Act is not a mere suggestion.

"Where a party's constitution prescribes a procedure for succession and leadership must be obeyed. Where a political party fails to comply with the rules, procedures, and constitutional provisions laid down for its own governance, the court is duty-bound to intervene in order to safeguard democracy, uphold the rule of law, and prevent anarchy, as no man is above the law, and no man is below it.

"This commendation is not merely about one litigant succeeding and another losing. It is about what the judgement represents for Nigerians and for the African Democratic Congress:

"It restores public confidence that a judge can still decide on the law and the facts alone, uninfluenced by political pressure, media commentary, or the weight of personalities involved in the suit.

"It affirms that leadership must emerge through lawful process, not through imposition, and that aggrieved members have a legitimate right to seek redress in court rather than resort to self-help.

"It reassures ordinary Nigerians that the court remains the last hope of the common man, and indeed, of every man.

"As the Supreme Court has repeatedly held, 'justice must not only be done, but must manifestly and undoubtedly be seen to be done.' His Lordship's conduct in this suit embodies that principle.

"I therefore respectfully commend His Lordship for upholding the independence of the judiciary and the sanctity of the judicial oath to do right to all manner of people without fear or favour, affection or ill-will; demonstrating patience, erudition, and firmness in a matter of immense political sensitivity; and delivering a judgement that strengthens the rule of law, party discipline, and constitutional democracy in Nigeria.

"May His Lordship's example continue to inspire the Bench and the Bar, and may the Federal High Court continue to stand as a bastion of impartial justice.

"I also wish to place on record my profound commendation to our team of lawyers for their exceptional diligence, intellectual rigour, and unwavering commitment to the cause of justice. Their professionalism, perseverance, and fidelity to the rule of law were instrumental in ensuring that justice was not only sought, but seen to be done.

"I further extend my heartfelt gratitude to our teeming supporters across the length and breadth of this country for their steadfastness, loyalty, and fervent prayers throughout this process. Your faith and solidarity have been a source of immense strength and encouragement."

posts.excerpt: Presidential aide Daniel Bwala has criticised the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), accusing it of taking over the party’s leadership without due process. Bwala made
posts.content:
Presidential aide Daniel Bwala has criticised the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), accusing it of taking over the party’s leadership without due process.

Bwala made the remarks in a post on his X platform on Thursday, following the controversy surrounding the leadership of the opposition party.

He said a political party seeking to govern Nigeria must uphold the principles of due process, equity and justice, accusing the Mark-led executive of disregarding those principles in its emergence.

“A political party that wants to govern Nigeria must be a party of due process, equity and justice.

“You descended on ADC like a thief in the night, took over its leadership undemocratically and hoped that all is well,” he wrote.

Bwala further accused the leadership of violating the party’s constitution and guidelines, as well as the Nigerian Constitution and the provisions of the Electoral Act and guidelines of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

He said the alleged violations amounted to a disregard for Nigerians, accusing the party leadership of assuming that the public could be misled over the circumstances surrounding its emergence.

Bwala also took a swipe at individuals lobbying on behalf of the party leadership, suggesting that they were expecting financial rewards.

The comments came amid the dispute over the ADC leadership and a court ruling affecting the Mark-led executive committee.

posts.title: 2027 Polls: Tinubu storms Akwa Ibom, Rivers for presidential campaign
posts.excerpt: PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu will depart Abuja on Friday, November 6, for a two-state visit to Akwa Ibom and Rivers. The post 2027 Polls: Tinubu storms Akwa Ibom, Rivers for presidential campaign appeared fi
posts.content:
—To commission projects in Uyo

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA –PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu will depart Abuja on Friday, November 6, for a two-state visit to Akwa Ibom and Rivers.

The President will first visit Uyo, the Akwa Ibom State capital, to commission landmark projects completed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration and attend a political rally.

Governor Eno, the host, has declared Friday a work-free day in the state to give the President a rousing reception.

Among the projects President Tinubu scheduled for commissioning in Uyo are the new International Terminal Building, the International Airport Hospital, and the Ibom Aviation Village, all located at the Victor Attah International Airport.

President Tinubu will also commission the Airport-Okopedi Road in Nsit Atai and Okobo Local Government Areas and Ring Road 3, linking Idoro Road to Ikot Ekpene Road through Uyo and Ibiono Ibom.

Other projects include the AKWA-GIS Office Complex, the Command and Control Centre and the ARISE Palm Resort.

On Saturday, President Tinubu will leave for Port Harcourt, Rivers State, to take part in the All Progressives Congress rally.

The rally will be his third, since he flagged off the re-election campaign in Kaduna last month.

The visits will also give President Tinubu opportunities to engage with political stakeholders, party members, and supporters while emphasising unity, political stability, and a shared commitment to national progress.

posts.title: ADC: 'They took over like thief in the night' - Presidency reacts to court verdict sacking David Mark, others
posts.excerpt: The Presidency has reacted to the Federal High Court judgement nullifying the candidacy of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. DAILY POST reports that the cou
posts.content:
The Presidency has reacted to the Federal High Court judgement nullifying the candidacy of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar.

DAILY POST reports that the court on Thursday sacked the David Mark-led leadership of the party and invalidated all decisions taken by its National Working Committee, including the primary election that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate.

The judgement has sparked reactions from politicians across the country, with opposition figures warning against any attempt to undermine democracy.

Reacting, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, justified the court's decision, alleging that the David Mark-led faction took over the party like a thief in the night.

In a post on his official X handle, Bwala said, "A political party that wants to govern Nigeria must be a party of due process, equity and justice.

"You descended on ADC like a thief in the night, took over its leadership undemocratically and hoped that all is well.

"You desecrated the party’s constitution and guidelines, you trampled on Nigeria’s constitution and “poopooed” on INEC’s Act and guidelines; and by so doing you lifted a middle finger on Nigerians and think that you would gaslight everyone;

"I am sure by now your cash-out lobbyists will be dancing, waiting for a payout."

ADC: 'They took over like thief in the night' - Presidency reacts to court verdict sacking David Mark, others

posts.title: Atiku, Obi, SDP, CUPP, ADC kick as court sacks Mark-led ADC exco
posts.excerpt: "The survival of democracy requires a political environment in which opposition parties are allowed to operate, organise and compete without persecution" The post Atiku, Obi, SDP, CUPP, ADC kick as co
posts.content:
By Nwafor Sunday, Henry Umoru, Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Luminous Jannamike, & John Alechelu

The Federal High Court in Abuja’s decision to sack the Senator David Mark-led executive committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and nullify all actions taken by it has drawn criticism from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate Peter Obi; the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and the Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP.

While Atiku accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of using the judgment to frustrate his presidential ambition and weaken his support base in the North, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive.

The court, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu, declared the Mark-led ADC caretaker committee illegal and invalidated all actions taken by it, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general election.

The judgment followed a suit instituted by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the ADC (North-East), who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party.

Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the leadership of the party.

The court upheld his claims and granted the reliefs sought.

The ruling has raised questions about the status of Atiku’s candidacy, coming barely 24 hours after he held a campaign rally in Sokoto State.

Atiku alleges plot to weaken Northern support

Reacting to the judgment, Atiku accused the APC of using the court ruling to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the ADC’s growing political influence ahead of the 2027 elections.

Atiku said the ruling came barely 24 hours after thousands of supporters welcomed him to Sokoto for the launch of the ADC campaign, alleging that the development was part of a strategy to weaken his Northern support base and halt the spread of his campaign beyond the region.

In a statement issued on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former Vice-President insisted that the judgment would neither derail the party’s campaign nor diminish its appeal across the country.

He said the reception in Sokoto reflected Nigerians’ growing frustration with economic hardship and their desire for a change of government.

“The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward,” he said.

Rejecting attempts to portray his candidacy as a Northern project, Atiku said the economic crisis confronting Nigerians had made his political message relevant across regional boundaries.

“My roots are in Northern Nigeria, but my candidacy belongs to all Nigerians. There is a difference between being from the North and being a candidate only for the North. Hunger and hardship do not respect regional boundaries. Nigerians across the country are suffering under this government, and they deserve a leader with a credible plan to make life affordable again,” he said.

Atiku alleged that the judgment was intended to disrupt the momentum of his campaign and weaken the opposition’s growing political reach.

“The timing of this judgment is no coincidence. It is part of a strategy to weaken my support in the North and frustrate a campaign whose message is resonating across the country. But the ruling party’s greatest miscalculation is to assume that my support ends in the North. What we saw in Sokoto, what we will see in Kebbi and across the country, is the strength of a national movement,” he said.

On the legal implications, Atiku questioned why the leadership dispute was reopened despite an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the Federal High Court, Abuja, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025.

He said the court had dismissed the challenge to the David Mark-led leadership after upholding objections bordering on jurisdiction, standing and failure to exhaust internal party remedies, adding that the substantive issues were also resolved in favour of the defendants.

“Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute? This is a calculated attempt to circumvent a subsisting judgment. We will challenge this judicial manoeuvre at the Court of Appeal,” he said.

The former Vice-President urged ADC supporters to remain peaceful and law-abiding, insisting that the ruling would not interrupt the party’s mobilisation.

“Our journey to rescue Nigeria from the hardship imposed by the APC government is a long one. Our Affordable Life campaign will continue because Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis,” he said.

With the campaign train already in Kebbi, Atiku urged supporters to take the party’s message from house to house and door to door, declaring, “There is no shaking.”

Obi warns against undermining democracy

Also reacting to the development, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive.

Obi, who expressed shock over the judgment, said the development had created uncertainty in the country’s political landscape, particularly with the 2027 general election approaching.

He disclosed this in a statement posted on his X platform on Thursday.

The former Anambra State governor said although he respected the court’s authority to determine disputes in accordance with the law, the timing of the judgment raised concerns about electoral certainty.

“I do not challenge the ruling of the court. The court of law is constituted to determine disputes according to the law. My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty,” he said.

Obi argued that uncertainty over political parties and their candidates close to an election could undermine the electoral process and restrict the space for opposition campaigns.

He alleged that the ruling party was engineering instability within opposition parties, claiming that similar developments had affected him in the Labour Party.

He also alleged that opposition campaigns had been subjected to violence, describing the developments as part of what he called efforts to shrink the civic space and weaken opposition politics.

Emphasising the importance of voters in a democracy, Obi said the choice of political leaders should ultimately rest with the electorate.

“One mark of democracy is that at all times, it is voters and not courts that choose leaders. I trust in the judiciary. As a public officer, I have shown deep respect for the judiciary,” he said.

He appealed to the judiciary and other stakeholders to protect democratic institutions and ensure that candidates were allowed to participate freely in electoral contests.

Obi further warned against weakening opposition politics, citing the spread of military rule in parts of West Africa as a reason Nigeria should strengthen its democratic institutions.

According to him, the survival of democracy requires a political environment in which opposition parties are allowed to operate, organise and compete without persecution.

He said he had consistently maintained that, if elected president, he would give special attention to ensuring that opposition parties remained stable and viable.

Obi added that his administration would protect opposition candidates from being pushed out of electoral contests.

“This is a time to strengthen our democracy by allowing the opposition to thrive,” he said.

CUPP accuses APC of pursuing one-party state

Similarly, the Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP) criticised the judgment, alleging that it could weaken opposition parties and undermine political competition in the country.

In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday through its Office of the Spokesperson, the coalition accused the ruling APC of benefiting from what it described as a systematic effort to weaken opposition parties.

CUPP alleged that the judgment was part of a broader attempt to undermine opposition political structures and create conditions for a one-party state.

The coalition also expressed concern over the role of the judiciary, arguing that the ruling raised questions about the courts’ responsibility to protect democratic rights and political participation.

“CUPP views this controversial judgment not as an isolated legal dispute, but as part of a well-choreographed, state-sponsored onslaught aimed at wiping out viable opposition parties and turning Nigeria into a one-party state,” the statement read.

It further alleged that sections of the judiciary had failed to adequately protect the interests of citizens and the electoral process.

CUPP also accused the APC-led government of relying on legal technicalities to challenge opposition candidates and party leadership structures, saying such developments could restrict political competition and undermine public confidence in the electoral system.

“The judiciary must remember that its allegiance belongs to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, not to the political actors of the day. When the courts become a tool for political liquidation, the very survival of our democracy is at stake,” the statement added.

The coalition declared solidarity with the ADC and other opposition groups, saying it would continue to defend democratic participation and political pluralism.

SDP condemns alleged move to disqualify Atiku

Meanwhile, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) condemned alleged attempts to disqualify Atiku from the 2027 presidential election, insisting that political parties should be allowed to freely present candidates.

The SDP National Chairman, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, stated this on Thursday in Abuja while addressing journalists after a meeting with the party’s nine governorship candidates from different states.

Gombe called on the judiciary, security agencies and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remain impartial and protect the country’s democratic process.

He also accused the APC of allegedly plotting to infiltrate opposition parties and weaken their ranks ahead of the elections.

The SDP chairman alleged that the ruling party, having lost the confidence of Nigerians over its governance record, was using the proposed Rainbow Coalition to woo opposition members and undermine their unity.

He, however, said the SDP was working with other opposition parties towards building a coalition of Nigerians committed to credible elections, including joint training of party agents and the establishment of common situation rooms to protect votes at polling units.

Gombe reaffirmed the party’s commitment to presenting what he described as credible alternatives to Nigerians, naming its presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and vice-presidential candidate, Prof. Usman Bugaje.

“I want to assure you that SDP, as a political party, has nothing to do with anything called Rainbow Coalition.

“We are with other political parties in the opposition, doing everything possible to rescue our dear country through a coalition of the Nigerian people.

“We are not into any Rainbow Coalition where we will have candidates here and profess support for the APC presidency. We are SDP and we are for SDP candidates,” he said.

He said the party had resolved to discipline any member who participated in the proposed arrangement without its authorisation.

The SDP chairman also expressed concern over the alleged failure of INEC to publish the names of some of the party’s candidates, saying the matter was already before the court.

He accused the commission of failing to recognise the candidates despite what he described as the party’s compliance with the Electoral Act, the Constitution and its internal nomination procedures.

Gombe further raised concerns about the voters’ register and the creation of polling units, warning against actions capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process.

SDP candidates strategise ahead of 2027

Earlier, the Chairman of the SDP Governors’ Forum and Nasarawa governorship candidate, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, said the meeting was aimed at developing strategies to secure victory in the presidential, governorship and legislative elections.

Adamu said the candidates shared experiences from their respective states and discussed ways to address organisational gaps ahead of the polls.

The meeting brought together the party’s nine governorship candidates and members of its National Working Committee as part of efforts to strengthen its structures ahead of the 2027 general elections.

ADC vows to appeal judgment

The ADC has vowed to appeal the judgment. Its National Welfare Secretary, Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was joined as an interested party in the case, said the party would challenge the verdict at the appellate court.

Vanguard Newspaper

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/atiku-obi-sdp-cupp-adc-kick-as-court-sacks-mark-led-adc-exco/
