posts.title: Jewish leaders in Michigan prepare to work with Abdul El-Sayed despite lingering concerns
posts.excerpt: Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan Senate win divides Jewish leaders as AJC Detroit calls his anti-Israel rhetoric a stain on the historic milestone.
posts.content:
Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed's victory in Michigan has drawn mixed reactions from Jewish leaders and Jewish Democrats, with some expressing optimism and a willingness to work with him, while others say their concerns remain.

"We congratulate all the winners, and we will work with all the winners," Jewish Federation of Detroit CEO Steven Ingber told Fox News Digital. "The Jewish voice and Jewish vote is not monolithic, meaning, we have people who voted on every side of the aisle on all the races up and down the ballot. And the beauty of being a 501(c)(3) is we don't get to take an opinion and we just get to work with whoever then is elected."

The Jewish Federation is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit, meaning it cannot endorse political candidates or participate in political campaigns on behalf of or in opposition to candidates. Instead, it works with elected officials from across the political spectrum to support Jewish communities.

UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN STUDENTS RALLY BEHIND ABDUL EL-SAYED AFTER HIS SENATE WIN OVER MIKE ROGERS

For Ingber, the key is understanding that people have varying reactions to elections, something he said has happened before and will likely happen again.

"I think it's all about unity," he told Fox News Digital. "There'll be an election again in two years. There was an election two years ago. People were upset then, people were happy then. And I think that's the beauty of our system right now is — America will go on."

Throughout his campaign, El-Sayed faced criticism from Jewish leaders and voters who were concerned about his stance on Israel and ties to controversial figures. One remark in particular that struck many Jews the wrong way was El-Sayed's response to the March 2026 attack on Temple Israel in West Bloomfield, Mich.

According to the FBI, Ayman Mohamad Ghazali drove a truck containing commercial-grade fireworks and containers of flammable liquid into Temple Israel on March 12. Ghazali died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound during an exchange of gunfire with synagogue security personnel, investigators said. Following the attack, El-Sayed said, "Hurt people, hurt people," drawing criticism. He later apologized and told Fox News Digital that his comments "might have been misconstrued to be justifying something I did not intend to justify."

EL-SAYED’S HASAN PIKER PROBLEM FOLLOWS HIM TO DEM CONVENTION AS JEWISH VOTERS BREAK RANKS

Democratic strategist Julian Epstein told Fox News Digital that Democrats have been inconsistent when opposing bigotry, particularly when Jews are the targets.

"If you believe in civil rights, right? If you believe [in] pluralism, if you believe in dignity for all, if you're against bigotry, then you don't do it for one group, but not for another, or accept it for another or capitulate on it for others. Because then you really don't believe in the civil rights. You just believe in group preferences at that point," Epstein said.

Epstein predicted that El-Sayed's victory could mean a broader shift among Jewish voters, who have long been a reliable Democratic base.

"I think there's no question that Jewish voters are going to start leaving the Democratic Party," Epstein told Fox News Digital. "They should. I mean, why would you stick with a party that openly tolerates hate directed at you?"

The American Jewish Committee's Detroit chapter (AJC Detroit) acknowledged the historic significance of El-Sayed's election as the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate but expressed concern about his public statements.

ABDUL EL-SAYED DELIVERS MAJOR BLOW TO GOP IN MICHIGAN AFTER BRUISING SENATE RACE

"We recognize the historic significance of Dr. El-Sayed becoming the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, a milestone that reflects the promise of American democracy. As a Jewish organization, we understand the profound importance of seeing one’s community represented in government," AJC Detroit's statement read. "Unfortunately, this historic moment has been tarnished by the Senator-elect’s continued anti-Israel rhetoric that alienates countless Jewish Michiganders and other supporters of the State of Israel, and endangers American Jews."

"As a U.S. Senator, El-Sayed will have the responsibility to represent all Michiganders. The Senator-elect proclaimed that America is 'big enough for all of us' but his obsessive hostility toward Israel yet again in his victory speech told many Jewish Michiganders and countless others who support Israel that they are not included," AJC Detroit added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Despite the concerns expressed by some Jewish leaders, Ingber urged community leaders to continue calling out antisemitism regardless of which party is responsible.

"We have antisemitism coming at us from both sides, from the far-left, from the far-right. Neither is better, neither is worse," he told Fox News Digital. "Antisemitism isn't a Jewish problem, it's an American problem."

He said Jewish Americans should not retreat from public Jewish life because of rising antisemitism or political divisions.

"Antisemitism and people who don’t want us to succeed in life are not going to stop us from being who we are," Ingber said.

The El-Sayed campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Fox News Digital's Paul Steinhauser and Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/media/jewish-leaders-michigan-prepare-work-abdul-el-sayed-despite-lingering-concerns

posts.title: Republican state lawmakers reported Omar to the IRS in 2019
posts.excerpt: Years before Omar's latest federal probe, Minnesota Republicans flagged her controversial tax filings to the IRS, according to newly obtained correspondence.
posts.content:
EXCLUSIVE: A group of Minnesota Republican state lawmakers asked the IRS in August 2019 to "conduct a detailed reexamination" of tax filings by Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., based on a report from a state board suggesting she filed joint tax returns in 2014 and 2015 with a man she was not legally married to, according to a letter obtained by Fox News Digital.

The letter was sent after the Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board issued a report on June 6, 2019, indicating that Omar had filed joint tax returns in 2014 and 2015 with Ahmed Hirsi, despite being legally married to another man, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, at the time.

The joint tax returns came up during the Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board’s examination of a $1,500 expense associated with Omar’s campaign committee. The board was investigating whether the expenditure was a legitimate campaign-related expense or whether campaign funds had been used to pay for services that benefited Omar personally. The payment was part of a larger $2,250 reimbursement to the Kjellberg Law Office for legal and other services.

ILHAN OMAR ISSUES STUNNING ADMISSION WHEN CONFRONTED WITH BROTHER MARRIAGE RUMORS

In response to the board’s questions, Omar’s campaign committee explained that the Kjellberg Law Office had retained the accounting firm Frederick & Rosen to obtain and review financial records as part of the campaign committee’s efforts to respond to allegations surrounding Omar’s marital history. According to the committee’s explanation, Frederick & Rosen prepared releases for Omar and Ahmed Hirsi to sign, so the firm could obtain copies of their filed joint federal income tax returns for 2014 and 2015 from the IRS.

The board concluded that the committee had not demonstrated that the $1,500 expense benefited the campaign and required Omar to reimburse the committee.

JD VANCE SAYS DOJ LOOKING INTO IF ILHAN OMAR COMMITTED IMMIGRATION FRAUD AMID BROTHER-MARRIAGE ALLEGATIONS

Omar married Hirsi in 2002 in their Muslim faith tradition and that they ended their relationship in that tradition in 2008, Newsweek reported. She then legally married Ahmed Nur Said Elmi in February 2009, according to public records, as reported by Newsweek.

According to divorce documents obtained by Fox News Digital, Omar legally divorced Elmi in December 2017.

Carla Kjellberg, a lawyer for Omar and her campaign committee, stated during the board proceedings that Frederick & Rosen’s services provided "some personal benefit to Rep. Omar," because "there was an issue with her tax returns that needed to be corrected regardless of her status as a candidate," according to the board’s report.

In a letter to then-IRS Commissioner Charles Rettig dated Aug. 6, 2019, the state lawmakers asked the IRS to undertake a review in light of the Minnesota Campaign Finance Board report.

"Due to recent developments, I believe probable cause exists for an investigation into Rep. Omar's tax filings," read the letter, signed by Minnesota state Reps. Steve Drazkowski, Linda Runbeck, Glenn Gruenhagen, Shane Mekeland, John Poston, Eric Lucero, Duane Quam, Tim Miller, Cal Bahr and Jeremy Munson.

Drazkowski told Fox News Digital that the IRS never responded to the request.

The IRS did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Fox News Digital could not confirm whether the IRS followed through with the lawmakers’ request.

Federal tax confidentiality rules generally restrict what the agency can disclose about individual taxpayers. The Minnesota Campaign Finance and Public Disclosure Board issued its findings on June 6, 2019, following two complaints filed by Drazkowski. Although the board required Omar to repay the $1,500 that her campaign had paid the Kjellberg Law Firm for Frederick & Rosen’s services related to the tax returns, it rejected the allegation that this money was payment for Omar’s personal divorce proceeding, in which Kjellberg also represented her.

The board also required Omar to repay campaign funds used for certain travel expenses, including trips to Boston, New York and Washington, D.C.

Following the board's 2019 findings, Omar said she was "glad" the process was complete and welcomed the board's determination regarding allegations that she had improperly used campaign funds for personal expenses. However, she did not address the portion of the board’s report concerning the joint tax returns she submitted with Hirsi.

Omar did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

In a separate letter obtained by Fox News Digital, the Republican state lawmakers, led by Drazkowski, asked Cynthia Bauerly, then-commissioner of the Minnesota Department of Revenue, in August 2019 to review Omar's joint tax filings.

Drazkowski said neither Bauerly nor the Minnesota Department of Revenue responded to the lawmakers' request.

The Minnesota Department of Revenue did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The letter from the lawmakers urging the state and federal tax reporting agencies to investigate Omar’s joint tax filings came two months after Drazkowski urged Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., to refer his concerns about Omar's tax filings to the House Ethics Committee.

As previously reported by Fox News Digital, Craig told Drazkowski in a letter that he could submit information himself to the Office of Congressional Ethics (OCE), which was renamed to the Office of Congressional Conduct in 2021.

The congressional ethics process allows members of the public and lawmakers to submit information concerning alleged misconduct, although the independent ethics office and the House Committee on Ethics have separate procedures.

In late October, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on Fox News that the federal investigation into Omar regarding potential immigration and marriage fraud had been referred to the Department of Justice (DOJ) as a "large case" that targets multiple individuals rather than just one person.

The DHS did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment on whether the investigation is looking into the 2014 and 2015 joint tax filings flagged by the state lawmakers in 2019.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/republican-state-lawmakers-reported-omar-irs-2019

posts.title: Popular drinks linked to heart attacks, cardiac arrest in young adults, study finds
posts.excerpt: Energy drinks with caffeine and stimulants were linked to cardiac arrest reports 11 times more often than non-stimulant products, per AHA research.
posts.content:
Energy drinks and stimulant-containing supplements have been linked to the risk of serious heart problems, including cardiac arrest and heart attacks, particularly among young adults.

That’s according to new research released by the American Heart Association, which will be presented at the AHA Scientific Sessions in Chicago, November 6–9, 2026.

A retrospective observational analysis looked at more than 28,000 reports submitted to the FDA of cardiovascular events, including cardiac arrest, myocardial infarction (heart attack), ventricular arrhythmias (abnormal rhythms), palpitations, tachycardia (rapid heart rate), chest pain and syncope (fainting).

EVEN OCCASIONAL MARIJUANA USE LINKED TO HIGHER STROKE RISK, STUDY FINDS

Cardiac arrest appeared in reports involving caffeine- and stimulant-containing products about 11 times as often as in reports involving products without those ingredients.

Heart attacks were reported about 4.5 times as often, while ventricular arrhythmias (abnormal heart rhythms) or palpitations were reported about four times as often, according to the AHA.

Elevated heart rate, chest pain and fainting were also increased among the group consuming those substances.

Approximately 45% of reported cardiovascular events associated with stimulant products involved adults ages 18 to 34.

The stimulants included in the study were caffeine, methylxanthines, guarana, yerba mate, synephrine, yohimbine and other compounds. They were consumed in products such as soft drinks, meal replacement shakes, protein bars, smoothies and vitamins.

Colin Kane, M.D., pediatric cardiologist and service chief at Children's Health and professor at UT Southwestern Medical Center, said the findings build on earlier case reports about potential heart risks from high caffeine intake.

"We've known through case reports and anecdotal evidence that caffeine in high amounts can be potentially dangerous to people with underlying heart conditions and even those who have normal hearts," Kane, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital.

WHY STACKING SUPPLEMENTS WITHOUT A BLOOD TEST FIRST CAN DO MORE HARM THAN GOOD

It is generally safe for adults to consume up to 400 mg of caffeine per day, which equates to up to five 8-ounce cups of regular black caffeinated coffee, according to a 2026 American Heart Association Scientific Statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease.

"Some energy drinks have up to three times more caffeine per fluid ounce than brewed coffee, and some pre-workout supplements have more than 12 times as much," senior study author Dr. Pamela Benavidez, a cardiothoracic anesthesiologist at Fairfield Medical Center in Lancaster, Ohio, told Fox News Digital.

"This means one small serving can easily surpass the advised daily limit or more."

Benavidez also warned that these products often include other stimulants like synephrine, yohimbine and methylhexanamine.

"These can interact with caffeine in ways that are not fully understood, especially in young, healthy people," she said.

YOUR DAILY COFFEE HABIT MAY AFFECT YOUR BRAIN AND MOOD IN UNEXPECTED WAYS, STUDY FINDS

The researchers recommend that young people carefully monitor their consumption of caffeine and watch for heart-related symptoms, such as palpitations, chest pain or tightness, lightheadedness, fainting, or a racing or irregular heartbeat during or after use of these products.

"If you notice any of these symptoms, seek medical help right away," Benavidez advised. "If you have a known heart condition, a family history of sudden cardiac events, or take medications that are classified as stimulants or can affect your heart rate/rhythm, you should talk to your doctor before using these products at all."

Kane identified people with underlying heart conditions, particularly those with potentially dangerous heart rhythms and older adults with coronary artery disease, as groups needing particular awareness.

"And there's a whole group of people who may have an underlying heart condition that they're not diagnosed with yet," he added.

The findings are preliminary and have not yet been published as a full peer-reviewed manuscript.

As the study was observational, it could only show an association and could not prove that the products caused the cardiac events.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"We don't know how many people consumed these drinks and didn't report symptoms or those who maybe had symptoms and didn’t report them," Kane said.

Also, as the FDA reports were voluntary, they may contain incomplete, inconsistent or selectively submitted data.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

It is possible that other factors, such as alcohol or drug use, strenuous exercise and undiagnosed heart conditions, may have contributed to the cardiovascular events.

"Anytime you're mixing stimulants and other substances or medications, it can certainly bring up a potential for harm," Kane said.

The American Beverage Association, based in Washington, D.C., sent the below statement to Fox News Digital in response to the study.

"Energy drinks have been enjoyed by billions of people around the world for more than 30 years and are recognized as safe by government food safety agencies worldwide. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Health Canada, the European Food Safety Authority all relied on the highest quality science when they determined that a moderate daily intake of 400 milligrams of caffeine from all sources is safe for adults."

"Energy drinks have less caffeine than coffeehouse coffee and no regulatory agency has found that their other ingredients interact harmfully with caffeine," the statement concluded.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Andrea Wong, chief science officer of the Council for Responsible Nutrition in Washington, D.C., also reacted to the study’s findings.

"Because the analysis does not account for how many consumers actually used these products, whether they were overused or misused, or even the amount of caffeine (or other ingredients) per serving, it cannot determine the incidence of cardiovascular events or quantify the associated risk," she told Fox News Digital.

"Importantly, the reported 11-fold difference in cardiac arrest reporting does not mean consumers are 11 times more likely to experience cardiac arrest."

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/health/popular-drinks-linked-heart-attacks-cardiac-arrest-young-adults-study-finds

posts.title: NDC to Tinubu: Obi-Kwankwaso ticket targets erosion of Nigeria’s wealth
posts.excerpt: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has said its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, are committed to addressing what it described as the erosion of Nigeria’s
posts.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has said its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, are committed to addressing what it described as the erosion of Nigeria’s commonwealth through excessive borrowing and alleged poor management of public resources.

The party made the position known in a statement by the Spokesperson of its National Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, in reaction to President Bola Tinubu’s criticism of Obi over the erosion menace in Anambra State.

The NDC said the mission of the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket went beyond tackling environmental erosion in Anambra to addressing the country’s fiscal challenges, including rising public debt, inadequate budgetary funding and the management of revenues accruing from the removal of petrol subsidy.

It questioned the benefits Nigerians had received from subsidy removal, particularly in view of the Federal Government’s continued borrowing, increased revenue generation and the country’s debt-service-to-revenue ratio.

The party also expressed concern over what it described as inadequate funding of critical public services, particularly healthcare and education, despite increased government revenues.

It said the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket would prioritise prudent management of public resources, accountability, productive investments and improvements in citizens’ welfare.

To support its argument, the NDC cited the financial records of Obi and Tinubu during their respective tenures as governors of Anambra and Lagos states.

According to the party, Obi left behind investments valued at the equivalent of $500 million, alongside local and foreign currency assets, including $156 million in dollar-denominated bonds, when he left office in 2014.

It also cited figures from the Debt Management Office, which it said put Lagos State’s external debt at approximately $190.43 million at the end of 2007, when Tinubu left office.

The NDC further criticised the pension law enacted during Tinubu’s administration in Lagos, which provided lifetime benefits for former governors and their deputies.

It listed the benefits as pensions equivalent to 100 per cent of the incumbent governor’s basic salary, houses in Lagos and Abuja, vehicles, furniture and utility allowances, entertainment allowances, free medical care and provisions for domestic staff.

The party contrasted the Lagos arrangement with Anambra, claiming that Obi did not establish a pension scheme for former governors during his tenure.

On environmental erosion, the NDC defended Obi’s record in Anambra, saying he helped attract and launch the World Bank-assisted Nigeria Erosion and Watershed Management Project (NEWMAP).

It also said his administration introduced drainage requirements for new state roads, ensuring that drainage systems were connected to safe discharge points, while undertaking local flood-control projects in communities including Adazi Nnukwu, Amawbia and Umuoji.

The party added that Obi regularly engaged the Federal Government on the need for ecological intervention funds and accountability in their utilisation.

Describing excessive borrowing without corresponding economic benefits as a threat to the country’s financial stability, the NDC cited historical examples of countries that had experienced economic difficulties associated with unsustainable debt and poor fiscal management.

It warned that Nigeria could face similar challenges if the trend was not addressed.

The party said its proposed economic approach would focus on responsible borrowing, accountability and investments capable of creating opportunities for Nigerians and improving the welfare of future generations.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/ndc-to-tinubu-obi-kwankwaso-ticket-targets-erosion-of-nigerias-wealth/

posts.title: Chainsaw robot looks terrifying but has a real job
posts.excerpt: JR East's towering ZIZAI ZX-3 chainsaw robot tackles dangerous branch-cutting along Japan's Koumi Line while a trained operator controls it remotely.
posts.content:
If you saw a humanoid robot holding a chainsaw next to train tracks, you'd probably do a double take. I know I would. But that's exactly what's happening in Japan, where a towering chainsaw robot is cutting back branches that could interfere with passing trains. It's a little intimidating to watch, especially when you see how high this machine can reach. Still, there's a pretty good reason railway crews are putting it to work.

Japan's JR East railway company is using the chainsaw robot to handle dangerous maintenance jobs that would normally require workers to operate heavy cutting equipment high above the ground. The robot does the physical work while a person controls its movements from a safer location. I find that reassuring, especially when a chainsaw is involved. So how does this unusual machine actually work, and could it change the way dangerous maintenance jobs get done?

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover five ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay and downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

HUMANOID ROBOTS PERFORM LIVE SURGERY IN WORLD FIRST

The robot has been put to work along JR East's Koumi Line in central Japan, where overgrown branches can create problems for passing trains. What's interesting is how the machine actually handles the cutting. One mechanical arm grips a branch while the other operates the chainsaw. The robot's upper body extends from a boom mounted on a specialized maintenance vehicle, allowing it to reach high above the tracks. That means workers can tackle branches that would normally require someone to operate cutting equipment at height.

The robot even has a name, ZIZAI ZX-3. Japanese manufacturer Nippon Signal announced its delivery to JR East earlier this year. The machine began full-scale maintenance work along the Koumi Line in October. And this technology already has some experience behind it. JR West started using a related robotic system in July 2024. What's especially appealing about this approach is that the machine takes on the dangerous physical work while a trained operator stays at a safer distance.

Now, before you start worrying about robots running around with chainsaws, the ZX-3 is actually controlled by a person. A trained operator guides the robot remotely, deciding where to position its arms and when to start cutting. That's important because working near railway tracks requires careful attention. One wrong move could damage equipment or put someone in danger. So while the robot handles the heavy lifting, a human still makes the decisions.

Nippon Signal designed the ZX-3 to make it easier for workers to control the robot's movements. Right now, its main job is cutting back trees and branches that grow too close to railway lines. However, the company hopes to give it additional tools so it can handle other maintenance work in the future. And here's what I find interesting. Workers still need the skills to do the job, but now they can operate the equipment from a safer location. That's a pretty big change when you're talking about working high above train tracks with a chainsaw.

Keeping train tracks clear takes more work than you might realize. Branches can grow close enough to interfere with passing trains, and cutting them back sometimes means sending workers high above the tracks with heavy equipment. That brings some serious safety risks, especially when crews are working near electrical infrastructure. Japan is also dealing with a shortage of skilled workers, so JR East is looking for ways to make these jobs safer and less physically demanding.

That's where the chainsaw robot comes in. It can reach areas that would be difficult or dangerous for workers to access while the operator stays at a safer distance. JR East is also changing when some of this work gets done. Since 2022, the company has been moving certain maintenance jobs along the Koumi Line into daytime hours instead of having crews work overnight. That sometimes means temporarily canceling trains, which I'm sure passengers aren't thrilled about. But it also gives workers better conditions and more manageable schedules. And when you combine that with a robot that can handle dangerous cutting work, you can see why JR East is investing in this technology.

NEW AI BRAIN LETS ROBOTS MOVE LIKE HUMANS

Now this is where I start having a few more questions. JR East has been investing in artificial intelligence and robotics across its railway operations. The company is exploring ways to use AI for equipment inspections and other maintenance activities. Its broader technology plans include robots that can help inspect infrastructure. That raises an interesting possibility. Could a future version of this chainsaw robot identify an overgrown branch and cut it without someone guiding every movement?

It's certainly a direction robotics developers could explore. AI-powered image analysis could help identify vegetation that threatens railway operations. More advanced systems might eventually assist with some of the decisions an operator makes today. But there's an important difference between what might be possible and what JR East has actually announced.

The ZX-3 currently relies on human control, and JR East has not announced a timeline for making its chainsaw operation fully autonomous. Personally, I think that's worth emphasizing. Giving a robot greater independence sounds impressive until you consider what happens if it misidentifies an object or someone enters its working area. We recently covered how humanoid robots are getting new workplace safety systems. Those safeguards will become even more important as machines take on jobs involving powerful tools.

You may never see this particular chainsaw robot working near your local train station. However, the technology behind it could eventually change how infrastructure gets maintained closer to home. If you ride commuter trains, you already know how frustrating delays can be. Overgrown vegetation can contribute to service disruptions, and railway companies spend considerable time keeping tracks clear. Equipment that helps crews perform those jobs safely and efficiently could eventually benefit passengers. There are potential applications beyond railways, too. Utility companies regularly need to trim vegetation around power lines. Construction crews also handle dangerous work in areas that are difficult to reach. Remotely operated machines could help reduce some of those risks.

Of course, there's another side to this. As robots become more capable, companies will need workers who know how to operate and maintain them. That could create opportunities for new skills while changing the way traditional maintenance jobs are performed. And while robots can reduce certain dangers, they bring their own safety concerns. A machine handling a chainsaw still needs reliable controls and proper oversight. For now, the ZX-3 shows how robotics can help people perform hazardous work without placing them directly in the path of danger.

ONE OF THE WORLD'S HOTTEST INDUSTRIES IS SPARKING A BLUE-COLLAR JOBS BOOM

I've seen plenty of humanoid robots doing backflips and showing off what they can do. But there's something different about watching one actually earn its keep. Seeing this robot handle a chainsaw high above the tracks makes me think about the risks workers face doing that job themselves. And if it can help keep railway workers out of dangerous situations, I am all for it. What I especially like is that there's still a person making the decisions. The operator brings the experience while the machine takes on the physically demanding work. That seems like a sensible way to introduce robotics into jobs where mistakes can have serious consequences. What I'll be watching is how quickly companies push these machines toward greater independence. AI is advancing, and I suspect we'll see more robots taking on jobs that once seemed impossible to automate. But when the tool in a robot's hand is a chainsaw, I want to know someone is paying very close attention.

Would you trust a fully autonomous robot to operate a chainsaw near the trains you ride? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

posts.title: Obienyem faults Tinubu over claim Obi ignored erosion in Anambra
posts.excerpt: Valentine Obienyem, a media aide to former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, has faulted President Bola Tinubu over his claim that Obi did nothing to tackle erosion during his tenure as governor. Obie
posts.content:
Valentine Obienyem, a media aide to former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, has faulted President Bola Tinubu over his claim that Obi did nothing to tackle erosion during his tenure as governor.

Obienyem, in an opinion article sent to Vanguard on Saturday, described the allegation as unfair and contradicted by historical records, citing several erosion-control projects undertaken by the former governor and his role in securing regional and international support to address the problem.

The reaction followed Tinubu’s visit to Akwa Ibom State, where he reportedly promised to develop the state’s deep seaport and accused Obi of failing to address erosion in Anambra during his administration.

Obienyem linked the development to Obi’s recent remarks on the need to develop seaports across Nigeria’s coastal states, including the Calabar Port and Ibom Deep Seaport.

He recalled that Obi had advocated the development of multiple ports across the country’s littoral states, citing Egypt, with about 15 ports, and South Africa, with about eight, as examples of countries that had diversified their maritime infrastructure to promote balanced economic development.

On the erosion challenge in Anambra, Obienyem said the state had more than 1,000 active erosion sites, including the devastating Nanka-Agulu erosion complex, but maintained that Obi gave the problem considerable attention while in office.

He cited two incidents to illustrate the former governor’s personal involvement in emergency interventions.

According to him, Obi once arrived at Umuchiani, Ekwulobia, as early as 6 a.m. after receiving reports of advancing erosion threatening the Ekwulobia-Oko road and nearby buildings.

He said some residents had begun dismantling parts of their houses to salvage their belongings before Obi intervened and directed that work should commence immediately.

Obienyem said the erosion was subsequently arrested and stabilised, saving the road and protecting the threatened buildings from further destruction.

He also recalled a similar intervention along the Nkpor-Onitsha dual carriageway, around the Omagba axis, where Obi reportedly responded to a distress call and helped prevent an endangered building from being swallowed by erosion.

Beyond the emergency interventions, Obienyem said Obi, as Chairman of the South-East Governors’ Forum, advocated declaring the region an ecological disaster zone to attract urgent government attention and international assistance.

He credited the former governor’s advocacy with helping to advance the Nigeria Erosion and Watershed Management Project (NEWMAP), a World Bank-assisted programme designed to tackle erosion and watershed degradation.

To support the claim, he cited the remarks of former Minister of Environment, John Odey, who reportedly acknowledged Obi’s contribution during the project’s official launch in Abuja.

According to Obienyem, Odey recalled that Obi had almost single-handedly pushed for the initiative despite initial reservations among some of his colleagues.

He also cited the commendation by the World Bank’s then Country Director, Marie-Françoise Marie-Nelly, who praised Obi for being the first governor to pay the state’s N500 million counterpart contribution to the programme.

The project covered Anambra, Imo, Ebonyi, Enugu, Abia, Edo and Cross River states.

Obienyem further claimed that Obi had worked on nearly 40 erosion-control and storm-water management sites across Anambra State before leaving office, with most completed and work continuing on others.

Among the locations he listed were Umuchiana, Ekwulobia; Mbaukwu; Mbanabo-Umuogba/Bishop Uzodike Road, Nnewichi, Nnewi; Umunze-Uga; Umudiana, Adazi-Nnukwu; Nsugbe; and Utu/Osumenyi in Nnewi South.

Other locations included Okpuno, Uwani Village, Ebenebe, Inyaba Umudim, Nnewi, Umuchu, Iyiagu floodplain in Awka, St Patrick’s Catholic Church, Awka, New Tarzan Junction, Agulu Avenue, Okpuno-Umuota, Obosi, and New Era Girls’ Secondary School, Onitsha.

He also listed drainage and waterway interventions, including the dredging of the Nwangene River in Onitsha, desilting of the Okpoko/Obodouwku road channels and Okpoko Creek, as well as desilting of the Sacamori channels in Fegge and Housing Estate, Onitsha.

According to him, other erosion-control projects were undertaken at several communities, churches, schools and public institutions across the state, including Obosi, Oraifite, Ebenator, Okpuno, Nimo and Agulu.

Obienyem argued that the projects demonstrated that erosion control was a major component of Obi’s administration’s development agenda and not an afterthought.

He said the former governor’s interventions went beyond saving roads and buildings to protecting livelihoods, communities and the economic future of residents.

The writer urged that governance should be assessed based on problems identified, initiatives undertaken and results achieved rather than political propaganda.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/obienyem-faults-tinubu-over-claim-obi-ignored-erosion-in-anambra/

posts.title: Explainer: Who won 2023 presidential 2023 in Kaduna, Katsina – the 161,829 votes difference
posts.excerpt: Kwankwaso of NNPP came third with 69,386 votes. Peter Obi, who ran on the Labour Party, LP, ticket, had just 6,376 votes The post Explainer: Who won 2023 presidential 2023 in Kaduna, Katsina – the 161
posts.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA

Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, won Katsina State in the February 25, 2023 presidential election by only 6,762 votes over Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC.

Read Also:

*Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal

*How Buhari promised me APC presidential ticket in 2022; I regret listening to him – Amaechi

He also won neighbouring Kaduna State, where his lead was far wider.

Katsina: a margin of 6,762 votes

Atiku polled 489,045 votes in Katsina, against Tinubu’s 482,283. Out of 1,058,673 valid votes, that is a gap of about 0.64 of a percentage point.

Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, came third with 69,386 votes. Peter Obi, who ran on the Labour Party, LP, ticket, had just 6,376 votes.

Katsina had 3,516,719 registered voters. The 1,058,673 valid votes represent about 30 per cent of that figure.

Kaduna: a lead of 155,067 votes

Kaduna was not close. Atiku scored 554,360 votes to Tinubu’s 399,293, a lead of 155,067.

Obi came third in Kaduna with 294,494 votes, and Kwankwaso was fourth with 92,969.

The state had 4,335,208 registered voters, of whom 1,418,046 were accredited. INEC recorded 1,360,153 valid votes and 41,223 rejected votes, making 1,401,376 votes cast in total.

Where the two states differ

Obi’s vote shows the sharpest contrast. He polled 294,494 votes in Kaduna. But he got only 6,376 in Katsina, where he finished fourth behind Kwankwaso.

Across both states, Atiku polled 1,043,405 votes and Tinubu 881,576, giving Atiku a combined lead of 161,829. Obi had 300,870 votes and Kwankwaso 162,355.

Nearly all of Atiku’s combined lead came from Kaduna. Katsina added only 6,762 votes to it.

posts.title: Turkey: Osimhen undergoes successful knee surgery, faces three weeks on sidelines
posts.excerpt: Galatasaray have confirmed that Super Eagles striker, Victor Osimhen has successfully undergone surgery after sustaining a knee injury during the club's UEFA Champions League encounter against VfB Stu
posts.content:
Galatasaray have confirmed that Super Eagles striker, Victor Osimhen has successfully undergone surgery after sustaining a knee injury during the club's UEFA Champions League encounter against VfB Stuttgart.

The Nigerian international picked up a sprain in his left knee following the match, but further medical examinations, including an MRI scan, uncovered a loose fragment in the affected area, making surgery necessary.

In an official statement released on Saturday morning, the Turkish champions disclosed that the procedure was carried out at Maslak Acıbadem Hospital by the club's team doctor, Yener İnce.

The Istanbul-based club added that Osimhen would undergo daily medical evaluations, with his recovery and treatment continuing under the close supervision of the medical department.

Galatasaray also wished the 27-year-old striker a quick recovery, expressing optimism that he would return to the pitch as soon as his condition allows.

Meanwhile, Turkish sports newspaper Fanatik reports that Osimhen is expected to miss Galatasaray's upcoming league fixtures against Amedspor and Samsunspor.

The publication further estimates that the former African Footballer of the Year could spend approximately three weeks recovering and undergoing rehabilitation.

Should his recovery progress as expected, Osimhen could be available for Galatasaray's UEFA Champions League clash against Aston Villa on November 24.

The injury also represents a major concern for Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle, who would have been counting on the striker's availability for Nigeria's forthcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying fixtures against Tanzania.

Osimhen's absence could therefore pose a selection headache for the Nigerian tactician as he prepares his squad for the crucial international assignment.

posts.title: Kalu urges Igbo leaders to unite, engage in Nigerian politics
posts.excerpt: Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has urged Igbo elders, leaders and stakeholders to unite and take a more active role in Nigeria’s politics, warning that disunity and pol
posts.content:
Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has urged Igbo elders, leaders and stakeholders to unite and take a more active role in Nigeria’s politics, warning that disunity and political apathy have weakened the South-East’s influence in national affairs.

The call was contained in a statement issued on Saturday by his Chief Press Secretary, Levinus Nwabughiogu.

Kalu also called for a change of mindset among Igbo people, particularly those who have traditionally focused on developing their communities while keeping away from national politics.

He made the call on Friday at the South-East Stakeholders’ Convergence, also known as the South-East Elders and Stakeholders Meeting, held at the Imo State Government House, Owerri.

The meeting, convened to discuss unity, peace and development in Igbo land, was chaired by a former Military Governor of Imo State and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Senator Ike Nwachukwu.

Kalu, who represents Bende Federal Constituency of Abia State, said unity was essential to the political relevance and development of the South-East, stressing that the region could achieve more if its leaders and people worked towards common goals.

“Unity is strength. We will achieve more when we are united. The need for unity cannot be overemphasised. Peace leads to the development of communities,” he said.

Commending the elders and stakeholders for attending the meeting despite their individual engagements, the Deputy Speaker described their gathering as an expression of patriotism and commitment to the progress of Igbo land.

He said their example would encourage younger generations to sustain the quest for unity and development, likening leadership to a relay race in which older generations hand over the baton to their successors.

Kalu, however, warned that the Igbo people risked losing their heritage and political direction if they continued to operate in isolation.

On the region’s political influence, he said the numerical strength of the Igbo was not adequately reflected in the political fortunes of the five South-East states, partly because many people from the region lived in other parts of the country.

He argued that a common political agenda would enable the Igbo to consolidate their strength and make their voices more influential in national decision-making.

“The number of votes of Ndi Igbo is not what we are getting across the five states because we are scattered around the country. If we take a position now and say, Igbo, this is our agenda, this is what we want to do, I can assure you, the whole of Nigeria will feel our impact,” he said.

The Deputy Speaker also urged the people to abandon what he described as the post-civil war mindset of avoiding national politics and concentrating solely on developing their communities.

According to him, the approach has not yielded the desired political results, making it necessary for the region to become more actively involved in Nigeria’s governance.

“After the war, we had believed we will work it out on our own and develop our place. We say we are not interested in politics. It is not our business. We have tried to develop on our own. It is about time we changed that mindset.

“The politics and governance of Nigeria should be our concern. We should get involved and play an active role because if we are not in the room, we can’t be part of the decision. We need to be part of the decision-making process,” he said.

Kalu called on Igbo leaders to agree on a common position and pursue it collectively, insisting that the region would command greater respect and achieve better results through political cooperation.

The meeting was attended by Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, traditional rulers, representatives of religious organisations, women and youth groups from the five South-East states, as well as prominent figures from politics, business and academia.

Among those present were former Senate President and Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator Anyim Pius Anyim; former Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University of Technology, Owerri, Prof. Nnenna Oti; former Chairman of the Police Service Commission, Chief Simeon Okeke; and former President-General of Ohanaeze Ndigbo, Nze Ozichukwu Chukwu.

Others included Chief Tony Chukwu, Ambassador Greg Mbadiwe, Prof. Osita Ogbu, Mazi Sam Ohuabunwa and Ambassador Okey Emuche.

posts.title: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal
posts.excerpt: Lagos produced the closest of the three contests. Obi polled 582,454 votes (45.81 per cent), while Tinubu, the APC candidate, followed with 572,606 votes (45.04 per cent) The post Explainer: What INEC
posts.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA

Lagos, Oyo and Osun states each backed a different candidate in the February 25, 2023 presidential election, according to the results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC.

Read Also: How Buhari promised me APC presidential ticket in 2022; I regret listening to him – Amaechi

Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, won Lagos; Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, won Oyo, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, won Osun.

What happened in Lagos?

Lagos produced the closest of the three contests. Obi polled 582,454 votes (45.81 per cent), while Tinubu, the APC candidate, followed with 572,606 votes (45.04 per cent).

The gap was 9,848 votes, less than one percentage point. Atiku trailed far behind with 75,750 votes (5.96 per cent), and Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, had 8,442 votes (0.66 per cent).

What happened in Oyo?

Oyo was not close. Tinubu polled 449,884 votes (55.58 per cent), well ahead of Atiku’s 182,977 votes (22.60 per cent).

His lead of 266,907 votes was the widest of the three states. Obi came third in Oyo with 99,110 votes (12.24 per cent), and Kwankwaso had 4,095 votes (0.51 per cent).

What happened in Osun?

Osun was nearly as tight as Lagos. Atiku won with 354,366 votes (46.88 per cent), while Tinubu had 343,945 votes (45.50 per cent), a difference of 10,421 votes.

Obi finished third with 23,283 votes, and Kwankwaso had 713 votes (0.09 per cent).

What the combined figures show

Added together, the results tell a story that the three winners alone do not. Tinubu won only one of the states, yet he finished first or second in all three and polled 1,366,435 votes across them.

Obi, who topped the Lagos poll, totalled 704,847 votes across the three states because he fell to third in both Oyo and Osun. Atiku polled 613,093 votes, and Kwankwaso finished fourth in each state, with 13,250 votes combined.

Put differently, Obi’s win came by the thinnest of margins in the most populous of the three states. But Tinubu’s lead in Oyo was large enough to leave him comfortably ahead of both rivals on the combined tally.

Vanguard News

posts.title: Pursue Unity, Peace, Play Active Role in Nigerian Politics, Deputy Speaker Kalu Urges Igbo Elites, Leaders
posts.excerpt: Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu has called on Igbo elders, leaders and stakeholders to close ranks and speak with one voice in politics,
posts.content:
Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu has called on Igbo elders, leaders and stakeholders to close ranks and speak with one voice in politics, cautioning that disunity has continued to weaken the political strength and heritage of Ndi Igbo of the South East region.

He also urged them to pay more than passive attention to socio-economic issues and get deeply involved into the national politics of Nigeria.

Kalu made the call at the South East Stakeholders’ Convergence (SESC), also described as the South East Elders and Stakeholders Meeting, convened in Owerri, the Imo State capital on Friday to discuss unity, progress and peace in Igbo land.

Addressing the gathering chaired by the former Military Governor of Imo State and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Senator (Gen) Ike Nwachukwu (Rtd), the Deputy Speaker said unity remains the foundation for development, stressing that peace in Igbo communities would only come when leaders reason together in harmony.

He said: “Unity is strength. We will achieve more when we are united. The need for unity cannot be overemphasized. Peace leads to the development of communities”.

Kalu who represents Bende Federal Constituency of Abia State at the National Assembly commended the elders for setting aside their personal engagements to attend the meeting, describing their action as patriotism and genuine love for Igbo land.

“I salute you all, my elders and stakeholders for this thoughtfulness, this great idea to come together and discuss the unity, progress and peace of Igbo land. This is patriotism. You all have what you are doing but for you to leave it and come here to discuss the development of our place, it means you love Igbo land. It shall be well with you all,” he said.

The Deputy Speaker said the upcoming and the contemporary younger generation are encouraged by the elders’ example, likening leadership to a relay race in which one generation hands the baton to the next.

“Some of us who are coming up are encouraged by this unity and patriotism you display. We are glad to see our elders sit together to discuss the future of Igbo land. This is like a relay race, where you run and later hand over the baton to the next person and the next generation. We are coming behind you so that whenever you hand us the baton, we collect it from you and continue with the race of progress and development,” he said.

Kalu however said that without unity, Ndi Igbo risk losing their direction and heritage.

“But if we are not in unity, we will miss our bearing and lose our heritage. But when we reason together in unity and harmony, we achieve greatness,” he said.

Speaking about Nigeria’s political structure, the Deputy Speaker noted that Igbo as one of the major tribes in Nigeria is not standing strong in the national politics.

He further argued that the political numbers of Ndi Igbo are not fully reflected across the five South East states because the people are scattered across the country.

To encourage active political participation, the Deputy Speaker urged a change of mindset, saying the post-war decision by many Igbo people to focus only on personal development and stay away from national politics had not served the region well.

“And it will not be good we shake and be left out in the scheme of things. Please, let’s come together. Let’s unite. When we unite, we gain more respect as a people. But when we work in isolation and silos, we lose our heritage.

“The number of votes of Ndi Igbo is not what we are getting across the five states because we are scattered around the country. If we take a position now and say, Igbo this is our agenda, this is what we want to do, I can assure you, the whole of Nigeria will feel our impact.

“But if we work in silos, every man to himself, to your tent O Israel, it is not encouraging at all. It yields no positive result. It reduces our number.

“After the war, we had believed we will work it out on our own and develop our place. We say we are not interested in politics. It is not our business. We have tried to develop on our own. It is about time we changed that mindset. The politics and governance of Nigeria should be our concern. We should get involved and play an active role because if we are not in the room, we can’t be part of the decision. We need to be part of the decision making process,” he said.

Kalu therefore called for a common position to help Ndi Igbo to deliver with one mind.

“There is no wisdom in saying we are not interested in the politics of Nigeria. It should be our business. Let us say one thing and stick to it with one mind, then, we will see the result of our togetherness. God bless you,” he said.

The stakeholders meeting held in Imo State Government House attracted the presence of Governor Hope Uzodinma as the chief host, some traditional rulers, representatives of religous leaders, women and youth groups from the five eastern States, other prominent Igbo sons and daughters in politics and governance, business, academia amongst whom are former Senate President/Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator Anyim Pius Anyim; immediate past Vice Chancellor of Federal University of Technology, Owerri (FUTO); Prof. Nnenna Oti; former chairman, Police Service Commission, Chief Simeon Okeke; former President-General, Ohaneze Ndigbo, Nze Ozichukwu Chukwu; Chief Tony Chukwu; Amb. Greg Mbadiwe; Prof. Osita Ogbu; Mazi Sam Ohuabunwa and Amb. Okey Emuche.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/07/pursue-unity-peace-play-active-role-in-nigerian-politics-deputy-speaker-kalu-urges-igbo-elites-leaders/

posts.title: Champion Breweries, Bature Brewery Partner to Take Nigerian Craft Beer Nationwide
posts.excerpt: Champion Breweries Plc has entered into an agreement with Thistlerock Enterprises Limited, owner of Bature Brewery, to manufacture and distribute Bature’s craft beers across Nigeria. The agreement als
posts.content:
Champion Breweries Plc has entered into an agreement with Thistlerock Enterprises Limited, owner of Bature Brewery, to manufacture and distribute Bature’s craft beers across Nigeria.

The agreement also grants Champion Breweries an option to acquire three Bature brands, subject to agreed sales performance milestone.

Under the agreement, Champion will brew, package and distribute Bature’s core beers, Lagos Lager, Black Gold Stout and Harmattan Haze, at its brewery in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, leveraging its national distribution network to expand their availability across Nigeria.

Bature will license the brands to Champion Breweries for manufacturing and distribution in Nigeria, retaining ownership and control of product development, brand strategy and consumer engagement, while still serving its Lagos hospitality accounts directly.

The acquisition option, which covers the brands’ trademarks, recipes and goodwill, would be exercised once annual sales reach 40,000 hectolitres, at a pre-agreed, performance-linked valuation, subject to the necessary corporate and regulatory approvals.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Champion Breweries, Malolan Sampath, said: “Our ambition is to build a diversified beverage business that creates value through the brands we own, the capabilities we develop and the partnerships we establish. We see significant opportunities to leverage our manufacturing expertise and distribution network to help distinctive Nigerian brands reach more consumers.

“Bature is a strong example of that opportunity. It has built a reputation for quality, creativity and innovation, and we believe that combining its brand strengths with Champion’s operational capabilities will help bring its award-winning beers to consumers across Nigeria. This partnership reflects our confidence in the long-term potential of Nigeria’s beverage industry and our commitment to playing a meaningful role in its growth.”

Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Bature Brewery, Kevin Conroy, said: “When we started Bature, we believed Nigeria could produce world-class craft beers with a character and identity entirely their own. What has been most rewarding is seeing people embrace that vision and build a community around our beers. We are incredibly proud of what we have created in Lagos, but we have always believed Bature could go much further.

“This partnership marks an exciting new chapter for us. It means more Nigerians will have the opportunity to discover and enjoy our beers, while we stay true to the creativity, originality and passion that made Bature what it is today.”

The beers will be rolled out nationally in phases, beginning with Lagos Lager, which is targeted for launch at the Calabar Festival in December 2026, one of the largest consumer gatherings in the Nigerian calendar.

Harmattan Haze is expected to follow in the first quarter of 2027, with Black Gold Stout later in 2027.
