posts.title: Institutional Memory, Professional Knowledge and the CORFEPS Journal
posts.excerpt: By Tunji Olaopa The Council of Retired Federal Permanent Secretaries (CORFEPS) is an association of patriotic former public servants that embodies administrative experiences, institutional memories an
posts.content:
By Tunji Olaopa

The Council of Retired Federal Permanent Secretaries (CORFEPS) is an association of patriotic former public servants that embodies administrative experiences, institutional memories and professional knowledge that could pull a lot of political and administrative weight within the reform imperative to transform governance architecture, the civil service and its ecosystem. As a multidisciplinary body of retired public servants with vast knowledge of the workings of the system, CORFEPS possesses a huge significance in connecting the institutional and reform dots in terms of where the civil service system is coming from, where it is at the moment and where it intends to be, given the democratic imperatives and development necessities of the current Tinubu administration. It is one of the most critical stakeholders in the public administration communities of practice and service that articulates a continuing professional and institutional interest in furthering the relevance of the civil service as a significant player in the development process in Nigeria.

The necessity of such a body derives from the fact that patriotic and meritorious service does not need to end with retirement. Indeed, more can still be done in entrenching the institutional memories that retired permanent secretaries embody. CORFEPS, under the able chairmanship of Mahmud Yayale Ahmed, has been energetic in its consistent push to regain the vocational honor, professional ethos and administrative efficiency of the civil service. And in furtherance of this enthusiastic push for the significance of the civil service system as one critical cornerstone of democratic governance in Nigeria, CORFEPS has just launched an amazing initiative: the CORFEPS Journal on Pubic Policy and Governance.

This significant initiative must be situated within a larger context of the institutional reform of the civil service system, especially its status as a value-based institution founded on merit, public spiritedness and professionalism. That context facilitates a framework that allows the past and the present to initiate conversation, and for both retired and current public servants to incessantly brainstorm the future of the bureaucratic system and its capability readiness to shoulder the burden of public policy implementation. The journal, I must say, presses the advantage of escalating the fundamental significance of professional knowledge and its role in deepening institutional progress. In other words, through it, CORFEPS provides a rare forum—draw, I dare say, from the administrative history of that golden era when administrative theorists (the gown) and practitioners (the town) were in conversation—within which administrative ideas, practices and initiatives could be discussed, extended and applied.

The inaugural edition of the CORFEPS journal is indeed a full, rich and exciting package that is sufficiently exciting to signal to the communities of service and practice that something new and challenging has arrived in the administrative space. This is because the editorial board went all out to create a splash especially with the range of topics covered, and even more specially with the array of contributors and their unique specialties. As is to be expected, CORFEPS pulled strongly from within its own ranks for reflections that combine past administrative experiences with current observations from behind the scenes. The majority of the contributors are retired permanent secretaries who have served in one capacity or the other, and who have faced one crucial challenge or the other with wide ranging levels of successes.

In this regard, the CORFEPS journal, in its inaugural edition, is drawing on the immense institutional memories and professional knowledge of its members to ventilate both diagnostic, recuperative and reformative insights. And this is salutary in ways that serve to complement the mediatory role CORFEPS has been playing as a staunch and energetic stakeholder in the civil service reform project in Nigeria. We now have an opportunity to listen and take note, outside of the usual high-power meetings, of the single-minded understanding of the civil service system from those who have manned its various aspects, especially the ministries, departments and agencies. Their reflections and analyses are complemented by others, critical watchers of the civil service, whose many years of dealing with the system make them significant participants in the ongoing efforts to transform it into a value-based, public-spirited, meritocratic and high-performing world class institution.

In terms of the range of topics and themes discussed in the inaugural edition, the CORFEPS journal becomes an automatic administrative keepsake. The inaugural edition is divided into eight parts. Each of the segments, with the exception of the last two, speaks intentionally to the most dominant issues involved in assessing and transforming Nigeria’s democratic governance experiment. This is indeed a well-thought out scholarly first step by the editorial board. Part one, titled “The Nigerian Civil Service,” has four essays; part two with seven essays is concerned with governance tools; part three has just one essay dealing with Nigeria’s infrastructural development; part four has two essays surrounding leadership and management; the two essays in part five are wrapped around the theme of health and lifestyle; part six is dedicated to three book reviews; part seven signals recent appointments and tributes to distinguished former public servants; and part eight speaks to the activities of CORFEPS itself. In all, these thematic segments are all-encompassing. They are meant to lay on the table the diagnoses, prognoses and resolution frameworks for understanding the totality of Nigeria’s administrative and governance challenges and the ways forward to transcending them.

Without daring any in-depth review of each essay—which goes beyond the space of this piece—I will touch on some of the significant contributions. And of course, we start with the civil service system. This is key, even to the current advocacy responsibilities of CORFEPS itself. And the four essays in this segment did not disappoint. Their different focuses are without doubt current and contemporary—the status of the public administrator within the civil service and governance framework; the relationship between the civil service and the task of nation building; the significance of the MDAs in the achievement of state capacity; and the relationship between administrative leadership and performance management system. These are issues that are critical in reflecting on the challenges the civil service system is facing—how can we instigate the emergence of a public manager with twenty-first competences and literacies who can supervise a civil service system that is flexible, agile, technology-based and result-oriented through performance management that transforms Nigeria’s productivity?

In the second segment of the journal, containing the most essays, the contributors engaged with governance matters that richly scope the depth of the key issues. I am particularly thrilled by the essays that investigate (a) public financial management and development financing, (b) the intervention of the executive in the institutional autonomy of public institutions, (c) decentralization and local governance, (d) capacity development to achieve service delivery and (e) the significance of corporate governance in the public sector. These issues connect with the earlier one on the administrative system. Budgeting and the financial management discipline that must attend it are critical for servicing development planning. And this goes beyond merely increasing budget size to the fundamentals of ensuring transparency and accountability in financing and execution that speaks to sustainable outcomes.

I am also fascinated, as my many public interventions have demonstrated, with the place of local governance in Nigeria’s democratic governance. This also ties with the concern with the health of fiscal federalism in the Nigerian federation. Indeed, the author of the essay argues that constitutional autonomy to back the essence of local governance will be grossly less than optimal. Rather, what is needed is what he calls the “Nigeria Local Governance Reform Framework (2026-2035)” meant to reposition the local governments as key drivers of grassroots development. This is right on point. Similarly, the authors of the essay on training and capacity development attempt to recuperate training programmes “as genuine capacity-building instrument, anchored on competency-based needs assessment, transparent procurement, post-training accountability and the professionalization of Nigeria’s training institutions.”

The third and fourth segments of the journal are tied together by the relationship between leadership and sustainable development. Sound leadership is the difference between successful and failed infrastructure projects. This then directs critical reform attention to the issue of leadership training and selection, the focus of the first essay in part four. Part five would seem to be off the path of a direct focus on administrative and governance subject matters in its focus on health and lifestyle. But that is not the case. Most reform blueprints, unlike the practice during the golden era of the public service in the 1970s, fail to factor in work-life balance in human capital development. This is crucial in the sense that when the public servant is healthy, it goes a long way in affecting performance and productivity. Thus, the two chapters on breast cancer and prostate health are key factor in institutional reform.

To recapitulate: the inaugural edition of the CORFEPS journal is really a mouthful! It is like a reader on institutional and governance reform that all MDAs and key parastatals must have in their libraries. More than this, the edition already raises the bar that the editorial board cannot afford to undermine, going forward. I have a series of recommendations in this regard. One, the journal must not attempt to be academic. It must rather be styled and intended as a journal for public administration and public service professionals. This then demands that the editorial board must give deep reflection, again, to the objective of the journal and its intended audience. The fundamental question in this sense would be: What does the CORFEPS journal aim to become in the next five years within the Nigerian communities of service and practice? This question impacts the idea of style and content. For example, every edition could then be themed around some specific subject matter of administrative and institutional reform, governance challenge, democratic consolidation, leadership, financial management, civil service mentoring, etc. Contributions can then be sourced from seasoned experts, public servants, administrators, while online search can also be made for syndicated columnists with innovative ideas and initiatives that speaks to the concerns of the journals.

Indeed, special editions can be proposed on any theme for which the guest editor is renowned. Departments of public administration, as well as the MDAs, could serve as key studies for reflection on the overall health of the civil service system and public administration in Nigeria. Websites of other professional bodies will serve as veritable source of publishable materials to introduce new ideas, tools, techniques, etc. Young mentees, volunteers and analysts could also be enlisted and commissioned to write features on some current affairs that are relevant to public administration. Interviews and autobiographical notes are critical elements for understanding the progress and reform of the public service. The editorial board must therefore also think of segmenting the journals to give room for special features, from interviews to critical reform highlights in some of the MDAs.

I will end this piece with a note of deep appreciation of those who thought the idea of the journal into existence. This is no mean feat in the total scheme of things concerning institutional reform in Nigerian civil service system. Kudos, first, to Alhaji M. Yayale Ahmed, the National Chairman of CORFEPS and the distinguished publisher of the journal. And then to Ambassador Dr Godknows Igali as the chair of the editorial board. I recognize every member of the editorial board and commend the efforts that went into birthing this inaugural edition. We have commenced a journey into a legacy of reform activities.

Prof. Tunji Olaopa is a retired Federal Permanent Secretary and Chairman, Federal Civil Service Commission, Abuja

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/07/institutional-memory-professional-knowledge-and-the-corfeps-journal/

posts.title: Mutfwang Uniting Plateau For Renewed Hope, Continuity And Shared Prosperity
posts.excerpt: By Gyang Bere There is an African proverb that says, “The man who carries his people in his heart will always find a place in their hearts.” This timeless wisdom
posts.content:
By Gyang Bere

There is an African proverb that says, “The man who carries his people in his heart will always find a place in their hearts.” This timeless wisdom reflects the political philosophy of the Executive Governor of Plateau State, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, who has demonstrated a strong commitment to addressing the needs and aspirations of his people.

His quest for selfless service and purpose-driven governance speaks to the enduring relationship between his administration and the people, reminding us that the true measure of leadership lies not merely in the authority one exercises, but in the sincerity of purpose, compassion and commitment demonstrated in the service of the people.

Governor Mutfwang, who remains conscious of his social contract with the people of Plateau State, took a decisive political step on Monday, November 2, 2026, by inaugurating and setting in motion the Tinubu/Shettima and Mutfwang/Piyo Campaign Council, with the mandate of coordinating support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Governor’s re-election and the emergence of all APC candidates in the January 16 and February 6, 2027 elections.

The significant political event brought together respected men and women of integrity, drawn from across the electoral wards of Plateau State, who have served the state and the nation in various capacities.

At the helm of the campaign as Chairman is Governor Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, with the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, serving as Adviser; Deputy Governor, Ngo Josephine Piyo, as Deputy Chairperson I; State APC Chairman, Hon. Rufus Bature, as Vice Chairman II; Hon. Dr. Bernard Doro, Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, as a member; and Sir Joseph Ari as Director-General, entrusted with the responsibility of coordinating the campaign’s activities.

The inclusive Campaign Council also has former Governors, Senator Joshua Dariye and Senator Simon Lalong, as members, alongside former Deputy Governor, Dame Pauline Tallen; Senator Simon Mwadkwon; retired Air Vice Marshal Napoleon Bali, Coordinator of the Southern Zone; serving members of the National and State Assemblies; all APC candidates for the National and State Assemblies; political stakeholders, community leaders and party faithful.

Beyond the political significance of the occasion, the inauguration places an important responsibility on members of the Campaign Council to engage citizens with humility, respect and a clear understanding of the issues that matter most to them.

Governor Mutfwang believes that the campaign should transcend the mere mobilisation of political structures. Rather, it should provide an opportunity for honest conversations about governance, security, economic opportunities, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and the collective aspirations of the people of Plateau State and Nigeria.

For Governor Mutfwang, the 2027 political journey will inevitably invite public reflection on the promises made, the decisions taken, the challenges encountered and the results recorded since he assumed office in May 2023. He has acknowledged the trust, support and confidence he has enjoyed from the people of Plateau State and has appealed to them to continue the journey with him in the forthcoming election, with the aspiration of positioning the state more prominently on Nigeria’s national development landscape.

From the outset, Governor Mutfwang’s approach to governance has reflected an understanding that meaningful development must begin with the people. He has woven their concerns, aspirations and everyday challenges into his development agenda, translating these realities into practical interventions and implementing them systematically to improve lives and advance the collective prosperity of Plateau State.

For the 2027 elections, Governor Mutfwang’s message is anchored on a unification movement, built around the aspiration of bringing the people of Plateau State together under a common political direction under the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC). He has emphasised a factual, issue-based and peaceful campaign that places the people at the centre of every conversation.

The Governor’s argument for a second tenure rests on the record of his first term: the task of rescuing Plateau State from the brink of institutional and economic collapse, restoring confidence in governance, and laying a solid and enduring foundation for sustainable development across all sectors. Having undertaken the difficult work of recovery, reconstruction and repositioning, his administration is beginning to see citizens reap the benefits of these deliberate interventions.

The security of lives and property remains a central responsibility of the Mutfwang administration and a defining priority of its governance agenda. Recognising that peace and security are indispensable to development, Governor Mutfwang has approached the challenge with a strong sense of responsibility, commitment and institutional coordination.

His administration has revitalised Operation Rainbow, strengthened community-based security through the training and deployment of personnel and Forest Guards, and embraced technology by integrating modern surveillance systems into the state’s security architecture to enhance intelligence gathering, monitoring and response capabilities.

Equally significant is the Governor’s sustained engagement and harmonious working relationship with the leadership of security agencies at the national and state levels. Through cooperation, regular consultations and coordinated security interventions, he continues to strengthen the collective capacity to address security threats, protect vulnerable communities and restore public confidence.

Governor Mutfwang has prioritised strategic investments across critical sectors of the state’s economy, recognising that sustainable development must be built on infrastructure, human capital development and improved access to essential services. His administration has committed resources to transportation, healthcare, agriculture, education, water supply, energy, tourism and road infrastructure, with interventions designed to improve the quality of life of citizens and expand economic opportunities.

In transportation, the introduction of subsidised Metro bus services has made public mobility more accessible and affordable, while investments in road infrastructure are opening up communities, facilitating the movement of people and agricultural produce, and strengthening commercial activities across the state.

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s development footprint is increasingly visible in Plateau State, particularly through strategic federal infrastructure projects and humanitarian interventions aimed at improving connectivity, stimulating economic activities and enhancing the welfare of citizens.

The ongoing construction of the Akwanga–Jos Road, the rehabilitation of the Sharram–Garram–Babban Lamba Road, and the recent approval of the Mararaban Jama’a–Kanke–Langtang–Shendam–Ibi Road, extending towards Taraba State, represent significant federal infrastructure interventions.

Equally noteworthy are the humanitarian interventions of the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, through the distribution of relief materials and support to vulnerable individuals and communities. These gestures have provided meaningful assistance to beneficiaries, brought relief to households facing difficult circumstances and reinforced the importance of compassion and social protection in governance.

The Director-General of the Campaign Council, Sir Joseph Ari, has extended an invitation to over 115 support groups and the people of Plateau State to come out and receive the President on Saturday Novermber 14, 2026, while highlighting the Federal Government’s engagements and interventions in the state as evidence of its commitment to Plateau’s development.

However, as the African proverb reminds us, “Little by little, the bird builds its nest.” Great nations are not built in a day; they emerge through deliberate decisions, consistent effort, patience and enduring commitment.

This principle underscores the development aspirations of President Tinubu and Governor Mutfwang for Nigeria and Plateau State respectively: a commitment to building on existing foundations, consolidating progress and creating a more prosperous future for generations to come.

Dr. Gyang Bere, ANIPR is the Director of Press and Public Affairs to the Executive Governor of Plateau State

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/07/mutfwang-uniting-plateau-for-renewed-hope-continuity-and-shared-prosperity-2/

posts.title: Golden Morn At 40, Promoting Nigeria’s Tourism
posts.excerpt: Charles Ajunwa The Nestle Nigeria, Agbara Factory, nestled in a massive ambience in Ogun State, has become a tourism landscape which attracts educational, entrepreneurship and business excursions from
posts.content:
Charles Ajunwa

The Nestle Nigeria, Agbara Factory, nestled in a massive ambience in Ogun State, has become a tourism landscape which attracts educational, entrepreneurship and business excursions from institutions.

Golden Morn, one of the brands produced by the Nestle Nigeria Plc, on Tuesday attained 40 years.Its Agbara Factory where it all started played host to guests who witnessed the milestone.

Guests at the event, were welcomed by female dancers into a well-decorated open field, where some adult games had been arranged and winners were given tickets to buy any item of their choice from a makeshift store. Also, visitors and staff of the company were on hand, exchanged pleasantries and were served Golden Morn mixed with groundnuts, sliced apples and other fruits as music from Nigerian artistes played intermittently.

What makes Golden Morn truly Nigerian, is that all the ingredients – maize, soya and millets- are sourced and produced within Nigeria. The cereal is fortified with Vitamin A, Iron, Calcium, Protein and dietary fibre.

The Category Manager, Golden Morn, Omofasa Orhiunu, described the celebration of 40 years of Golden Morn as special.

“For 40 years, Golden Morn has been nourishing generations of Nigerian families and earning a special place at the breakfast table.

“Today, we are not only celebrating a brand, we are celebrating the people, the passion and the dedication that has kept Golden Morn going strong for four decades. And what better place to celebrate it than here at the Agbara Factory where so much of Golden Morn’s story comes to life every day. From the grains that go into every pack to the people who work tirelessly to ensure we continue to deliver the quality and nourishment families have come to know and love, this 40-year milestone belongs to all of us. Because at Golden Morn, we believe in making everyday golden. It is the fuel for the day ahead. Whether you are heading to school, going to work, caring for your family, or like many of us here, making the product that nourishes millions of homes. So today is about pausing to celebrate how far we’ve come, appreciating everyone who has contributed to this incredible journey and looking forward with excitement to what lies ahead.”

“To celebrate our consumers who’ve been loyal to Golden Morn for over 40 years, we’ll be rolling out a promotion this November where for every 900gram pack of Golden Morn our consumers buy, they get 50gram extra free. So that’s an extra bowl of Golden Morn to nourish our wonderful families in Nigeria.”

On what stands Golden Morn out, Orhiunu said “We are uniquely Nigerian and we are the only cereal that can proudly claim to have been developed in Nigeria, and to have been nourishing Nigerians for the last 40 years.

“We will continue to nourish Nigerians, we will come up with new variants which will excite Nigerians, new things that will make the breakfast table a lot more interesting and of course, we continue to fortify Nigerians because all our products are fortifying. Golden Morn is a fortifying product which is good for the health of everybody in Nigeria.

Factory Manager, Agbara, Nestle Nigeria Plc, Talla Fall, also described Golden Morn as unique Nigerian brand and only Nigeria.

Fall, a Senegalese who has lived in Nigeria for over 20 years, said Golden Morn doesn’t exist anywhere else. “Since 1986, Golden Morn has been cherished home-grown brand in Nigerian households. It has grown into a trusted choice of families, offering wholesome nourishment that fits into everyday life, whether in the morning or at any time of the day. That is the most important thing for Golden Morn. You can eat it at every time in the day.

“It is at our Agbara factory that every pack of Golden Morn is made. Golden Morn is 100 per cent Nigeria. So it has been created here in Nigeria, developed here in Nigeria, produced in Nigeria, and all the raw materials are coming from Nigeria. It is made with the goodness of maize and soya, grown by Nigerian farmers and created in Nigeria by Nigerians. Behind every pack are the farmers who grow the grains and the men and women in the factory who turn them into the nourishment that families trust. Over four decades, we have grown alongside our consumers. We began with high protein recipes in 1986, moved to a soft pack for greater affordability, adopted whole grains, fortified with iron and Vitamin A, and introduced Grainsmart. This is really a great journey.

“More recently, we modernised our packaging and pioneered the Golden Morn 3-in-1, Nigeria’s first ready-to-eat complete cereals. Throughout every changes, one thing has stayed the same, our commitment to quality and nourishment. But beyond the milestones, what truly stands out are our people, our greatest asset. Every pack that leaves Agbara carries the dedication of our colleagues across production, quality, engineering, logistics, and supply chain, and of those who came before us and led the foundations.

“Our commitments to safety, quality, and food safety is what makes this anniversary possible. Because 40 years is not one day. It means that you are really consistent and sustainable. That is what makes today special.

“Today, we also look forward to an exciting moment as we unveil the limited edition of Golden Morn 40 years anniversary pack. Our way of saying thank you to the families who have made this journey possible, because if it was not you, the consumers, we will not be there. So it will be our ways of saying thank you to our families who made this journey possible. The pack looks different, but inside it is the same. So Golden Morn you know and love with the same quality, taste, and nourishment.

“To our farmers and partners, colleagues, and every consumers who has welcomed Golden Morn into their home, we say thank you for being part of this 40 years journey. As the home of Golden Morn, we remain committed to the highest standards of quality and safety so that for the next coming years and beyond, Golden Morn continues to nourish Nigerian families and feel promising futures.

Nurse Olusolape, said that Golden Morn apart from containing the right nutrients for a healthy living, “gives you a fresh start for your day and it’s very easy to prepare.”

“As we celebrate 40 years of Golden Morn, let’s make a commitment all of us present here today and everyone out there to nourishing ourselves, prioritise our well-being, and keep showing up as our best self. Swell your day, nourish your potential, and build your future,” she added.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/07/golden-morn-at-40-promoting-nigerias-tourism-2/

posts.title: Naira Would Have Been Worthless Without Economic Reforms, Tinubu Tells Nigerians
posts.excerpt: Using the biblical account of Moses and the Israelites' departure from Egypt, he said Nigeria must continue moving forward, stating: "Nigeria will never go back to the subsidy." The post Naira Would H
posts.content:
President Bola Tinubu has defended his administration’s economic reforms, saying the naira would have become worthless if his government had failed to take decisive action to remove the fuel subsidy upon assuming office.

He made the remarks at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium.

Tinubu said his administration inherited an economy in which 27 of the country’s 36 state governors were unable to meet their salary obligations, let alone pay pensions and gratuities.

“When I took over, 27 governors out of 36 of this country were unable to pay salary obligation, not to talk of pension and gratuity. Today I stand before you able to say we are out of that tunnel. I can beat my chest to say we are out of the greatest despair, the dark tunnel of uncertainty and the calamity of possible bankruptcy.”

Tinubu speaking at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, on Friday, November 6, 2026.

Defending the decisions taken by his government, the President said: “By now, if we didn’t take a decision, the day I took over, we would use wheelbarrows to move our naira. Because it would have been valueless, nothing.”

He added that the exchange rate was about ₦1,300 to the dollar, arguing that the currency had retained some value because of the decisions his administration took.

President Tinubu insisted that his administration would not reverse its decision to end the policy.

Using the biblical account of Moses and the Israelites’ departure from Egypt, he said Nigeria must continue moving forward, stating: “Nigeria will never go back to the subsidy.”

“We are talking of $1,300 now to a dollar. Because it still has pocketable value. If we had left it, it would have been a wheelbarrow when you go to a tomato market. That is the truth.”

Tinubu also aimed at opposition figures Peter Obi and Atiku Abubakar, questioning their leadership capacity and accusing them of abandoning difficult situations.

He criticised Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), over the erosion challenges in Anambra State, while accusing Atiku, now the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, of abandoning the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) when his leadership came under challenge.

Tinubu questioned whether Nigerians could entrust the country’s leadership to people he accused of lacking responsibility and the ability to manage internal challenges.

Tinubu also highlighted his administration’s education policy, describing education as a major tool for tackling poverty.

He said funds recovered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission would be channelled into the education programme.

“I don’t know the pain of the market, but I share your pain. I share the difficulty. That’s why I decided to take away the responsibility of tuition fees away from parents.

“Equal opportunity for everybody who wants to read. Taking education as the greatest weapon against poverty. And creating opportunities for those who are still coming behind.

“From today on, as we are fighting corruption, any money recovered from EFCC is dumped into that education program. No one can reverse it.”

President Tinubu urged Akwa Ibomites to support his administration, pledging to keep his commitment to the realisation of the Ibom Deep Seaport.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/11/07/naira-would-have-been-worthless-without-economic-reforms-tinubu-tells-nigerians/

posts.title: Spain’s Puente And Africa’s Elusive ‘Political Dignity’
posts.excerpt: By Mobolaji Sanusi “The first requirement of a sound body politic is that there should be public integrity; and next, that there should be personal dignity.”—-Theodore Roosevelt (1858-1919) Oscar Puen
posts.content:
By Mobolaji Sanusi

“The first requirement of a sound body politic is that there should be public integrity; and next, that there should be personal dignity.” —-Theodore Roosevelt (1858-1919)

Oscar Puente, Spain’s Minister of Transport, was largely unknown outside his home country until a little over a week ago. He came into the international limelight after at least 69 people died and dozens more were injured in a high-speed train collision in his country. He was not the driver of the train, nor has it been officially established that he was negligent in the accident.

But six days after the collision, he took responsibility as the man in charge of the ministry and voluntarily resigned. At his appearance before his country’s Congress to give evidence about last week’s disaster near the town of Adamuz, south of the capital, Madrid, where a moving train smashed into the back of a stationary train, he announced his decision to resign.

That collision involved a train run by the state-owned operator Renfe, with 397 passengers on board, and a stationary train run by a private operator named Iryo that was carrying 147 passengers. The accident reportedly stemmed from an issue with the automatic signalling system, a computer failure that forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch. Another appointee seeking to evade responsibility would have blamed unforeseen technical glitches beyond human control.

He did not filibuster before Congress but simply resigned in a manner that exemplified a touch of patriotic courage when he declared: “A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot remain in office after two accidents of this seriousness in less than a year.” The first crash under his watch happened on the same line in January this year and left 46 people dead.

He did not just resign; he stated that he was also withdrawing his name from “the lists for the early legislative elections” scheduled for November 29. Sadly, Spain’s train crash last week was described as one of the worst rail disasters in modern European history, and the country’s worst since 2013. Rescue operations deployed heavy lifting equipment to access derailed carriages where passengers were trapped.

No wonder Puente’s position came under immediate scrutiny after the crash. The main conservative opposition People’s Party (PP) and the far-right Vox party called for his resignation. Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez admitted that public trust in the credibility of the high-speed rail system had been “broken.” But Puente resigned because he wanted to, not because of any opposition pressure, which is particularly dignified considering the incident’s closeness to an imminent election.

Puente’s act, which he described as being done for the sake of “political dignity,” is worthy of emulation. Prime Minister Sánchez was proud of him when he said that he “faced up to the situation, provided answers and solutions, and then stepped aside… out of dignity. Of his own accord. Out of respect for the victims.”

When juxtaposed with the public service attitude across the Black man’s continent, political office is largely misconstrued as a personal reward rather than a public trust. When disaster strikes, when a grid collapses, or when a flood that was clearly made worse by years of neglected drainage occurs, the routine response from the appointees in charge is not resignation, but inexcusable explanations.

Such an appointee’s responsibility is diffused until it is effaced by time, since our people are believed to have a short institutional memory. Usually, on our continent, when disasters or accidents happen, condolences are issued, a committee is set up, and the minister or other such appointees remain in office to supervise the committee investigating their own ministry or agency.

The reports of such committees are submitted only to gather dust on shelves in offices, like in the instance of the latest report of the inquiry into the deaths of miners in Niger State while in the custody of the civil defence corps. No one will eventually be sanctioned for treating the lives of (illegal) miners so shabbily. Even the current Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, sometime ago reportedly confessed in the media that NECO examination papers leaked, with no heads rolling, voluntarily or otherwise, for the poor handling of such examination papers. This is why “political dignity” remains so elusive on our continent.

Even in clear instances of underperformance, appointees in our clime find it difficult to resign voluntarily from their appointments. This administration, and even the one before it, have had to send some ministers packing. Examples abound, including Prof. Tahir Mamman, former Minister of Education, who was dismissed by President Bola Tinubu on October 23, 2024, for underperformance.

Barrister Uju Kennedy-Ohanenye, then Minister of Women Affairs, was removed on October 23, 2024, because her tenure was marred by avoidable altercations that hampered the ministry’s operations. Also, Lola Ade-John, former Minister of Tourism, was relieved of her position due to poor performance. The same applied to Dr. Jamila Bio Ibrahim, former Minister of Youth Development. Both were relieved of their duties on October 23, 2024.

In addition, Betta Edu, the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Alleviation under this administration, was suspended in January 2024 following public outcry over a controversial transfer of ₦585 million into a private account. She failed to resign voluntarily before she was suspended, after which her position was filled.

Adebayo Adelabu, former Minister of Power, despite severe criticism for repeated collapses of the national electricity grid and chronic power outages, stayed put in office until the electoral timeline for political party primaries compelled his departure.

The head of the previous administration, former President Muhammadu Buhari, sacked Sabo Nanono, his Minister of Agriculture, and Saleh Mamman, Minister of Power, on the same day in September 2021 for failing to meet the operational expectations of his administration. Despite glaring signals that they were performing below par, the aforementioned appointees failed to throw in the towel voluntarily.

Under the same Buhari administration, Adamu Adamu, the Minister of Education, served out the tenure of that government despite his inept handling of protracted strikes by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) that paralysed the tertiary education system. His subsequent confession at the end of his tenure that he knew nothing about education-sector management and had refused to resign confirmed the alien nature of voluntary resignation among political appointees in this part of the world.

However, Puente could voluntarily resign because, in Spain, the system allowed him to. His prime minister could accept his resignation without it looking like a confession of guilt for the entire government, while a credible press of that country treated the victims as more important than the minister’s political future. No cover-up. Resignation under such institutional circumstances should be understood for what it is: it should not be seen as a criminal admission but as an acceptance of political responsibility. On our continent, including in Nigeria, these conditions barely exist because loyalty is largely personal with no iota of consideration for institutional sanctity.

A minister on our continent owes their appointment to a political godfather or a president, not to the public. To resign voluntarily is therefore read as disloyalty or betrayal, and most of the time with serious communal consequences for toeing the path of honour.

So, clinging to office is perceived as a form of self-defence. For example, Hope Uzodimma, incumbent governor of Imo state, and others perceive the National Assembly as a retirement home because there are no institutional checks for overstaying in power even without commensurate achievements. The only consequence is that the public is temporarily outraged, while the opposition remains largely disunited and institutional pressure remains persistently weak due to corruption and affinity for impunity.

Men like Puente are in short supply on the African continent, and the few available ones are always afraid to act for the sake of institutional growth because our system punishes honour and rewards graft. The bar of public service overseas is high but not because the whites are from a different planet. The Europeans who colonised and committed the worst atrocities against Black people and mankind are not more moral than we are. It is just that their culture promotes political dignity and a political culture that largely embodies institutional dignity.

In their clime, public office is seen as stewardship, where the parliament actually checks power, the judiciary truly resolves conflicts impartially, and stepping aside out of respect for victims is understood as strength, not a weakness. Such resignations on our continent should be made normal by developing a political culture that makes loyalty to the public outweigh loyalty to the appointing authority. As rightly pointed out by the 26th President of the United States, Theodore Roosevelt, attaining a sound body politic requires “public integrity… and personal dignity.” And despite the riotous political quagmire that Roosevelt’s country is currently experiencing under President Donald Trump, there are inbuilt institutional checks to correct such.

Until we separate political responsibility from criminal guilt on our continent as well, we will continue to watch from afar as others show us what “I take responsibility” truly means. I hereby rest my case for this week.

•Sanusi, former MD/CEO of the Lagos State Signage and Advertisement Agency, is currently Managing Partner at AMS RELIABLE SOLICITORS. (WhatsApp only: 07011117777)

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/07/spains-puente-and-africas-elusive-political-dignity/

Roma have Manu Koné back in the squad for tonight’s Serie A match with Sassuolo, but Gianluca Mancini, Pierluigi Gollini, Mile Svilar, Paulo Dybala and more are still out.

It kicks off at the Stadio Olimpico at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s four Serie A games on the Liveblog.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 03: Gian Piero Gasperini, Manager of AS Roma, reacts during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 03, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)The Giallorossi are still unbeaten in Serie A, but smarting from their latest Champions League collapse, this time surrendering a 2-0 lead at Old Trafford for a 3-2 defeat to Manchester United.

There was added bad news from that midweek round, because Devyne Rensch limped off with a muscular problem and is out of action here.

Gianluca Mancini also sustained a flexor issue in the right thigh and is not even in the squad this evening.

(Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)Goalkeeper Svilar has been out for over a month, and his understudy Gollini sustained a back injury ahead of the Manchester United match, so third choice Devis Vasquez had to make his club debut.

Neither Svilar nor Gollini are in the Roma squad tonight either, so it is again a choice between Vasquez and USA Under-20 international Giorgio De Marzi.

Long-term absentees include Dybala and Lorenzo Pellegrini.

ROME, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 19: Manu Kone of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the Serie A match between AS Roma and FC Internazionale at Stadio Olimpico on September 19, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)Roma squad for Sassuolo

posts.title: Di Canio was ‘certain’ Milan would struggle against Bournemouth, 5-6 of their players would start for Inter’
posts.excerpt: Paolo Di Canio believes that Milan need more leadership in their side and says that...
posts.content:
Paolo Di Canio believes that Milan need more leadership in their side and says that it is not a surprise to see Ruben Amorim’s side struggling in the Europa League this season: ‘I was certain they’d struggle against Bournemouth, five or six of their players would be starters for Inter’.

Di Canio: ‘Who are the leaders in this Milan side? Not Rabiot or Modric’

Milan were defeated 2-0 at home by underdogs Ferencvaros in the Europa League on Thursday evening: Their third defeat in four matches in Europe this season and one that leaves them at risk of missing out on qualification for the knock-out rounds.

ITALY – NOVEMBER 05: Lenny Joseph of Ferencvarosi TC scores his team’s second goal under pressure from Mario Gila of AC Milan during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AC Milan and Ferencvarosi TC at Stadio San Siro on November 05, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)The Rossoneri have also lost at home to Benfica and away against Bournemouth in the Europa League this season.

Di Canio, speaking in an interview with La Repubblica, says he always thought that Milan would find it difficult in the Europa League this season.

“They are no longer what they were 15 years ago,” said Di Canio, who represented the Rossoneri between 1994 and 1996.

“It makes me think about those who claimed they should be winning the Europa League. Look at the competition. I was certain that Milan would struggle against Bournemouth. Five or six of their players would be starters for Inter.”

BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 22: Players of Bournemouth pose for a team photograph before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AFC Bournemouth and AC Milan at Bournemouth Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images)Di Canio went on to question the leadership in the current Milan squad.

“Who is the leader in this Milan side? Rabiot doesn’t seem like it to me. Modric leads by example, not by temperament. In my days, if you did something wrong, there would be Baresi glaring at you and the others would grin as if to say ‘he’ll take care of it’. It wouldn’t even be down to Capello.

“The starting XI is not bad, but it’s not a team that wins the derby and is then immediately capable of winning the Scudetto.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/di-canio-certain-milan-struggle-vs-bournemouth/

posts.title: Gattuso: ‘Pressure isn’t on Lazio, I hope to achieve 1/4 of what Allegri did in his career’
posts.excerpt: Gennaro Gattuso admits that the loss of Mattia Zaccagni is a big blow for Lazio,...
posts.content:
Gennaro Gattuso admits that the loss of Mattia Zaccagni is a big blow for Lazio, but insists that the pressure is not on his side approaching their Serie A clash against Napoli this weekend.

Lazio sit alone at the top of the Serie A table with 28 points after the first 10 league matches of the 2026-27 season. They have dropped points just once so far in the league this season and are one of only two sides in the division who remain unbeaten.

Up next for the in-form Biancocelesti is an away trip to face one of Gattuso’s former clubs, Napoli, who have lost half of their competitive matches since Massimiliano Allegri took charge over the summer. Encouragingly for Lazio, they have won all five of their away matches in Serie A so far this season.

Gattuso’s pre-match press conference ahead of Napoli vs. Lazio

REGGIO NELL’EMILIA, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: SS Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso during the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and SS Lazio at Mapei Stadium – Citta’ del Tricolore on October 27, 2026 in Reggio nell’Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)Speaking at his pre-match press conference on Saturday, Gattuso insisted that there is far more pressure on the struggling Napoli than there is on the table-topping Lazio.

“It depends on how you look at it. We don’t have any pressure, especially tomorrow. We’re aware of the fact that we will go to play in a tough stadium against a strong team that is going through a difficult period. It will take humility and for us to be at our best,” said Gattuso (via TMW).

“We have to think game by game, there are 12 points left for us to get and once we’ve hit 40 points, we’ll have a big celebration for reaching our first goal.

“Our journey consists of hard work, we shouldn’t be reading into anything else. People are rightly congratulating us at the moment, but when that day comes, we will be back under it.”

ROME, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Fisayo Dele-Bashiru and Andrea Pinamonti of S.S. Lazio celebrate after the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on November 01, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)Napoli are coming off a 4-1 hammering against Porto in the Champions League. Despite the scoreline, Gattuso feels that the Partenopei had a solid game for the first hour or so.

“We need to be aware of the first 70 minutes they played in Porto. They held their own in difficult circumstances. They also weren’t really able to make any changes. I expect my players to want to suffer and fight back blow for blow. We have nothing to lose.”

Sunday’s game will bring a reunion between Gattuso and Allegri

“Max was my captain in Serie B [with Perugia] and then my coach [with Milan]. History says that I’ve never won against him. I hope to achieve a quarter of what he’s achieved in his career. Knowing him, I know that he does not suffer from stress, in moments of difficulty he always finds the right things to do.

PARMA, ITALY – MARCH 17: AC Milan manager Massimiliano Allegri shouts to his players during the Serie A match between Parma FC and AC Milan at Stadio Ennio Tardini on March 17, 2012 in Parma, Italy. Gennaro Gattuso pictured in the background. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)“It will be a final for us too, playing at the Maradona is always a special feeling. We will have to get there with the right spirit and mentality.”

Gattuso won the 2019-20 Coppa Italia title during his time as coach of Napoli.

“I had a great time in Napoli and won a trophy. For me, it was an honour to coach that club,” he recalled. “There are still several people who work there and whom I still have a relationship with. Incredible people who live life the way I want to. It was an honour and a privilege.”

As for the team news, Lazio will be without star attacker Mattia Zaccagni for several weeks following an injury to his thigh. There is a chance that Nuno Tavares returns against Napoli, though.

ROME, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 12: Mattia Zaccagni of SS Lazio kicks the ball during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and AC Milan at Stadio Olimpico on September 12, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)“Nuno trained today and we’ll evaluate him tomorrow. I won’t lie, I still have some doubts. The loss of our captain is a big one, we hope it will be less than six weeks. He’s been working twice a day for the last three days in the pool to get back to his best condition as soon as possible. We hope there will be positive updates.

“Gudmundsson will not go off on international duty. We’ll have a friendly next week and the goal is for him to play 35-40 minutes. Rovella and Marusic are with us tomorrow, we’re feeling good.”

There could be an opportunity in attack for Andrea Pinamonti in the absence of Zaccagni.

“We are showing our identity. Those who came off the bench last Sunday changed the game. It’s a shame to have lost Zaccagni, but we will have to be ready and prepared to play without him. Pinamonti is doing better now. He’s a player who helps you attack spaces. He and Noslin are different types of players, but he can lend us a big hand as well.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/gattuso-the-pressure-isnt-on-lazio/

posts.title: FIFA reduce Molina ban after Argentina brawl during 2026 World Cup final
posts.excerpt: Roma full-back Nahuel Molina has seen his international ban reduced by FIFA after an appeal...
posts.content:
Roma full-back Nahuel Molina has seen his international ban reduced by FIFA after an appeal from the Argentine Federation following the post-match brawl that broke out at the end of the 2026 World Cup final.

FIFA reduce Molina’s international ban

Molina had originally been handed a seven-game ban and his teammate, former Roma and Juventus midfielder Leoandro Paredes was given a 10-match ban for his involvement in the World Cup final brawl in the summer. Molina was also handed a fine of $77,000 and his teammate $90,000.

Following an appeal from the AFA, Molina’s ban has been reduced from seven matches to four and his fine reduced from $77,000 to $60,000. Paredes’s 10-match ban and $90,000 has been upheld.

EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY – JULY 19: Nahuel Moiina #26 of Argentina and Rodri #16 of Spain square off after the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)Molina has already served three games of his suspension: Argentina having beaten Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin in a series of friendlies in October since the World Cup final in July.

He was not part of the Argentina national team squad that was announced earlier this week ahead of a pair of international friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica coming up in November.

PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – MARCH 22: Lionel Scaloni Head Coach of Argentina at the start of the International Friendly match against El Salvador at Lincoln Financial Field on March 22, 2024 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Ira L. Black/Getty Images)Seven other Serie A players were, including three of Molina’s Roma teammates in Leonardo Balerdi, Matias Soule and Santiago Castro, plus Como pair Nico Paz and Maxi Perrone, as well as Parma’s Mariano Troilo and Fiorentina’s Franco Mastantuono.

posts.title: Juventus suffer Cambiaso blow but could recover two players for Fiorentina
posts.excerpt: Andrea Cambiaso is set for a spell on the sidelines and will not be available...
posts.content:
Andrea Cambiaso is set for a spell on the sidelines and will not be available to face Fiorentina in Serie A this weekend, but Luciano Spalletti could potentially recover two more Juventus players for Sunday’s trip to Florence.

Cambiaso ruled out of Fiorentina vs. Juventus, McKennie and Celik could return

According to the latest reports from Gianluca Di Marzio, Cambiaso is struggling with muscular fatigue, which will rule him out of Sunday’s Serie A match against Fiorentina.

VIGO, SPAIN – OCTOBER 15: Andrea Cambiaso of Juventus reacts during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Real Club Celta and Juventus at Estadio Balaidos on October 15, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)The 26-year-old had lined up as a starter for Juve’s 2-1 victory away against AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League on Thursday evening. He was not one of the 31 players called up by Roberto Mancini to the most recent Italy national team squad, which was also announced on Thursday night.

Cambiaso has already missed four matches this season, skipping the weeks leading up to the September-October international break with a sprained ankle.

TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Weston McKennie of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)In more encouraging news for the Old Lady, Weston McKennie is expected to be available for selection for the Fiorentina match after missing out on the AZ Alkmaar match with a minor adductor issue.

Zeki Celik is also pushing for a spot on the bench against Fiorentina, but this is less of a certainty than McKennie’s return. The reintroduction of Francisco Conceicao this weekend has been described as ‘more complicated’.

posts.excerpt: Written by American Cola Nigeria The post ‘Make Dem See’: American Cola Club Talent Returns for Season Two appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
posts.content:
Let’s talk about something plenty of us know too well. It is rarely the talent that is missing. You have been dancing since secondary school. You have been on the decks for years. You have been painting walls that people stop to photograph. The talent is there.

What is missing is the room. The one where somebody with reach finally looks up and goes, oh.

American Cola Club Talent is back for season two, and this year the theme says the quiet part out loud: Make Dem See. Entries open 6th November, 2026.

But first, can we talk about last season?

If you were following in 2025, you’ll remember Show Your Flow. Five weeks. Talents from rap, dance, street art, disc jockeying, basketball, skating and BMX. Ten finalists. One winner.

That winner was DJ Mafdee Bitrus Moses Bugama. Fourteen years of showing up, reading crowds and moving people before a platform like this came along. He went home with ₦1.5 million, a year of music streaming, a year’s supply of American Cola, media interviews, and a community impact project that American Cola funded completely.

Temz BusyTm (@temz_the_dj) came in as first runner-up, and dancer Adetutu (@_therealadetutu) took second place.

And when the voting got tough? He went outside and asked people for votes one by one, because the rules allowed one vote per day. That is the kind of hustle and determination we love to see.

So what does “Make Dem See” actually mean?

Season one asked you to show your flow. Lovely. Season two goes one step further.

Make Dem See starts from the assumption that you are already good — and turns the attention to the people who haven’t noticed yet. The campaign film features four creators across dance, skating, DJing and street art, all of them talented, all of them tired of waiting to be discovered.

Sound familiar? Then this is your sign.

Now, the rewards (we know you scrolled here first)

₦2,000,000 in cold, hard cash

A community impact project in your own city, fully funded by American Cola (Another 2 million naira)

Media features and interviews on national platforms

A full year’s supply of American Cola

Awards, medals and other gift items

Runners-up won’t go home empty-handed either — 200,000 naira in cash prizes and gift items.

How to enter American Cola Club Talent 2026

It is genuinely this simple:

Film yourself doing your thing. Vertical, under 40-60 seconds.

Post it on Instagram, Facebook, or TikTok and tag American Cola in your video. Use the hashtags #MakeDemSee and #AmericanColaClubTalent.

Get your people ready for voting

Follow @americancolanigeria for details

No manager needed. No follower count needed. No connections needed. Just you and whatever you are great at.

Why we are rooting for this one

Nigeria is not short of gifted young people. What we have always been short of are platforms willing to put real money and real structure behind them — and then keep showing up after the announcement post.

So if you have been waiting for a sign to finally put your talent in front of people, this is it.

Go and make dem see.

posts.title: Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult emerge as new James Bond favourites
posts.excerpt: The two actors are reportedly among five candidates to have screen-tested for the role, alongside Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor The post Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult emerge as ne
posts.content:
Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult have emerged as surprise new contenders to become the next James Bond, with both actors reportedly having screen-tested for the role.

READ MORE: ‘Primetime’ review: Robert Pattinson and Phoebe Bridgers team up to catch a predator

According to a new report from The Hollywood Reporter, Pattinson, 40, took part in auditions for the coveted role over the weekend of October 24, joining previously identified candidates Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor.

Hoult, 36, has also reportedly been identified as one of the mystery candidates, with TheWrap corroborating the reports that both actors were among the hopefuls.

Pattinson’s inclusion comes as a surprise given that he is already one of Hollywood’s most established leading men, and is currently starring as Bruce Wayne in The Batman franchise.

The actor is in the midst of a particularly busy year, having appeared alongside Zendaya in The Drama, played Antinous in Christopher Nolan‘s The Odyssey, and starred as television presenter Chris Hansen in the A24 drama Primetime.

He has also been working on The Batman Part II, with the Bond screen tests reportedly taking place in London.

Crucially, Pattinson has already worked with the director of the next Bond film, Denis Villeneuve, on the forthcoming Dune: Part Three, which is due for release on December 18. Their collaboration is said to have gone well, potentially giving the actor an advantage in the casting process.

Hoult, meanwhile, has extensive experience in major franchises, having played Beast in the X-Men films and Lex Luthor in Superman, alongside an acclaimed performance in Nosferatu.

Interestingly, Hoult was previously a runner-up to Pattinson for the role of Batman in the 2022 film.

The latest reports add another twist to the lengthy search for Daniel Craig‘s successor, which officially began in May.

Earlier this week, Bond experts suggested that Turner had already secured the role, after he was reportedly spotted attending a screen test at Bray Studios in Berkshire.

Meanwhile, a separate rumour claimed that O’Connor had been cast as 007, based on an account allegedly given by a colleague from his recent West End production of Golden Boy.

No official announcement has been made, however, and Amazon MGM Studios has declined to comment on the latest casting reports.

The next Bond film will be the first since Amazon assumed creative control of the franchise from longtime custodians Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson in February 2025.

Villeneuve will direct the 26th instalment from a script by Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight, with Amy Pascal and David Heyman serving as producers.

Pascal has previously indicated that the new Bond will be announced before the end of 2026.

“We are being really, really methodical,” she explained. “I mean, Daniel Craig is a hard act to follow. And it’s got to be something really different that is stirring, exciting and different.”

Craig was announced as Bond in October 2005 and went on to play the character in five films, beginning with 2006’s Casino Royale and concluding with No Time To Die in 2021.

posts.title: Manics honour Richey Edwards as Suede look to the future at London co-headline show
posts.excerpt: Check out photos, footage, the setlist and more from what went down as the almighty double header rolled into The O2 The post Manics honour Richey Edwards as Suede look to the future at London co-head
posts.content:
Manic Street Preachers honoured Richey Edwards while Suede aired new material and looked to the future as their UK co-headline tour rolled into The O2 in London last night (Friday November 6). Check out photos, footage, the setlists and what went down below.

Earlier this spring the two bands confirmed that they would be joining forces once again – having first hit the road together in 1994, and later embarking on a run of joint North American shows in 2022 and a UK trek in 2024.

With the running order alternating throughout the tour, the Manics hit the stage first as the tour hit the capital, opening with the bittersweet euphoria of ‘Motorcycle Emptiness’ – the first of four songs from ‘Generation Terrorists’ as the band continue to tease an upcoming announcement to mark their debut album’s 35th anniversary.

Nicky Wire of Manic Street Preachers at their co-headlining tour with Suede at The O2 on November 6, 2026 in London (Photo by James Klug/Redferns) Pumped up to be playing in “fucking London Town on a Friday night”, the Welsh rock veterans leant heavily into their treasure trove of ’90s hit singles and took the time to pay tribute to missing former lyricist and guitarist Richey Edwards. Bassist Nicky Wire introduced early single ‘Little Baby Nothing’ as “one of Richey’s best lyrics”, recalling fond memories of penning the song at the Askew Road home of late manager Philip Hall.

Another tribute came when Wire remembered the band’s first ever London gig at The Horse & Groom pub in London, telling the crowd that “there are three of us tonight, but are always fucking four”. They then marked the recent release of their ‘The Holy Bible’ live album by performing the post-punk-noir ‘Die In The Summertime’ as a trio, without live backing musicians Wayne Murray and Dave Eringa.

Frontman James Dean Bradfield introduced Wire to the crowd as the man “in the red, white and green corner, in the title fight between him and the rest of the world” as he took over lead vocals for ‘Hiding In Plain Sight’ from latest album ‘Critical Thinking‘, including a brief cover of Echo & The Bunnymen‘s ‘Bring on the Dancing Horses’. “It’s nights like this I wish I was back on the booze,” joked Wire.

READ MORE: Manic Street Preachers tell us about their “vicious” ‘The Holy Bible’ live album and plans for the future

‘Everything Must Go’ highlight ‘No Surface All Feeling’ came with a brief snippet of ‘Total Eclipse Of The Heart’ by the late Bonnie Tyler before the mid-gig peak of former set closer ‘A Design For Life’ led into Bradfield asking the crowd to choose between which of of “two of Richey Edwards’ best lyrics” he would perform acoustic, with the audience cheering for ‘This Is Yesterday’ over ‘Kevin Carter’. One member of the crowd called for the ‘Gold Against The Soul’ opener ‘Sleepflower’ (infamously maligned by the band) to which Bradfield replied: “Fuck off, with the greatest respect” wishing him a “happy Christmas and a happy new year”.

The set concluded with the crowd uniting to clap-along to the band’s first Number One single ‘If You Tolerate This Your Children Will Be Next’.

View this post on Instagram

Suede made an explosive opening with the one-two punch of new album highlights ‘Disintegrate’ and ‘Antidepressants’ before the glam-punk rush of the iconic ‘Trash’, ‘Animal Nitrate’ and ‘We Are The Pigs’ ignited The O2 as the animated and elastic frontman Brett Anderson squared up to the front rows and performed some astounding acrobatics by swinging his mic around to Olympic standards.

“Welcome to Suede World,” Anderson told the crowd, describing their universe of chain-link fences and gritty gutter poetry. Keen to please their hardcore faithful, the band surprised fans with the tour debut of fan-favourite B-side ‘Killing Of A Flashboy’.

Other surprises came with the tour debuts of ‘Everything Will Flow’ and ‘Still Life’ – the latter delivered stripped back with just Anderson on vocals and guitarist Neil Codling on piano, introduced as a fond look to the past despite being an “anti-nostalgia band”. That sentiment was echoed as they aired the punk-driven new song ‘Tribe’.

“I just want to dedicate this song to this lot down here,” said Anderson, addressing the front row. “This song’s for the insatiable ones, for the mild ones, for the quiet ones, for the wild ones, for the beautiful ones, you are my tribe”.

Speaking to NME last month, Anderson explained that their next record deals heavily in “tribes and belonging”.

“So the record we’re making now is the third in the trilogy,” he told us. “It’s going to be another punk-based record. I don’t quite know what I’m going to call it yet – well actually, I do know what I’m going to call it – but I don’t know how I’m going to define it yet. The first one [‘Autofiction’] I said was our ‘punk record’, the second one [‘Antidepressants’] I said was our post-punk record, the third one I’m going to call our ‘something’ punk record.”

READ MORE: Suede tell us about progress on their new “anarcho-punk” album: “These are songs of tribes and belonging”

He continued: “When we started writing it, it was a bit like anarcho-punk actually. That’s what I thought was the parallel, but I don’t know yet. I think it’s important to message very broadly and say that it’s a genre because it helps people understand these things. When you’re talking about a record, when you’re messaging a record, it’s got to be in very simplistic terms. It’s a very broad brush, it’s a very blunt instrument..

“Obviously we didn’t just make a punk record, obviously we didn’t just make a post-punk record, obviously this won’t be an anarcho-punk record, but it’s a broad place for people to position it.”

Other set highlights came with the epic ‘She Still Leads Me On’ being dedicated to all the mothers and sons in the audience, along with the huge sing-along closing of ‘Metal Mickey’ into ‘Beautiful Ones’.

Brett Anderson of Suede performs at The O2 on November 6, 2026 in London (Photo by Jo Hale/Redferns)

Speaking to NME ahead of their North American tour with Suede in 2022, the Manics’ James Dean Bradfield recalled their joint 1994 trek, when the Manics were promoting their seminal third album ‘The Holy Bible’, and said that the collaboration worked as the two bands “shared the same DNA”.

Last year, Suede frontman Anderson told NME: “The Manics are lovely boys and I’m very, very fond of them. They’re a fantastic band and it was a wonderful tour. There’s something very complimentary about the bands and their fans. We tessellate quite beautifully, but at the same time it doesn’t feel like some kind of nostalgic ‘90s Britpop party. We occupy similar territory, but different enough to be complimentary.”

As well as talking to NME about revisiting ‘The Holy Bible’ last month, Manics also told us about plans for new material and what they’ve been working on in the studio.

“It is a fine batch of songs: ‘Threshold’, ‘Don’t Be Afraid To Be Afraid’, ‘Recrudescence’… I’m just trying to find a thread to them at the moment that makes sense. We don’t have any problem with inspiration for songs, it’s just that the wherewithal to put it all together and release it gets harder,” said Wire.

“This is our 16th album, and that’s a lot of records! I don’t know any one of our contemporaries that has got close to that.”

posts.title: U2 on the Ed Sheeran Macklemore row: “No billionaire, no promoter, no owner has the right to censor anybody”
posts.excerpt: The Edge has defended Macklemore's right to speak out, while insisting that Sheeran should not be vilified over the controversy The post U2 on the Ed Sheeran Macklemore row: “No billionaire, no promot
posts.content:
U2 have spoken out about the controversy surrounding Macklemore‘s removal from Ed Sheeran‘s US tour, insisting that billionaire venue owners have no right to censor musicians.

READ MORE: U2 live in Las Vegas: a dazzling opening night at the $2 billion Sphere

The Irish band discussed the row in a new interview with BBC News, with guitarist The Edge voicing his support for Macklemore while defending Sheeran against criticism.

“We totally support Macklemore’s right as an artist to say what he wanted to say,” he explained.

“I don’t think Ed should be vilified,” he added, acknowledging the difficult position the singer had faced.

The Edge also praised the younger musicians who withdrew from Sheeran’s tour in solidarity with Macklemore, arguing that they had taken a stand in defence of another artist’s freedom of expression, which he considered the overriding issue in the dispute.

Drummer Larry Mullen Jr. was similarly emphatic, adding: “Artists can choose whether they want to be, um, politically active or not. It’s a human right”.

View this post on Instagram

“But we as a band will fight for the right to speak your mind as long as it doesn’t incite violence. And even if we disagree with it or don’t like it, nobody has a right – no billionaire, no promoter, no owner has the right to censor anybody. Um, but they will definitely not be censoring us ever.”

Their comments relate to the controversy that erupted in September when Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran’s US ‘Loop Tour’.

During two concerts at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium, the rapper called for the protection of Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank before declaring “Free Palestine” and performing his protest song ‘Hind’s Hall’.

The remarks prompted criticism from the Israeli-American Council and billionaire Robert Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, who objected to Macklemore performing at Sheeran’s subsequent concerts.

Promoters subsequently removed the rapper from the tour, prompting Sheeran’s backing band and remaining support acts, including Finneas, Lukas Graham and Beoga, to withdraw in solidarity.

Sheeran later denied being complicit in the decision, explaining that he wanted his concerts to remain places of safety and sanctuary rather than political forums.

View this post on Instagram

The interview follows U2’s previous comments on the controversy last month, when Bono revealed that Sheeran had been reluctant to become involved in politics when collaborating with U2 on their new song ‘Yours Eternally’.

“You’re not going to get me into politics, are you?” Bono recalled Sheeran asking him during the recording process.

According to Bono, Sheeran subsequently explained: “Yeah, but I just want to keep my thing free.”

Meanwhile, Macklemore recently completed three sold-out ‘Free Palestine’ benefit concerts in Dublin, Paris and London.

The shows featured guests including Hozier, Kneecap, Aurora, Greta Thunberg and Paloma Faith, with proceeds supporting organisations working with Palestinians.

Macklemore has since claimed that nine major US arenas refused to host further benefit concerts, accusing venue owners of withdrawing available dates once they learned the purpose of the shows.

Meanwhile, U2 are preparing to release their 16th studio album ‘Carnaval De Luz’ on November 13, ahead of their return to full-scale touring in 2027.

posts.title: Nick Cave announces North American ‘Conversations’ tour for 2027
posts.excerpt: The singer will answer questions directly from audiences and give solo piano performances: "What could possibly go wrong?" The post Nick Cave announces North American ‘Conversations’ tour for 2027 app
posts.content:
Nick Cave has announced a North American tour for 2027 that will see him answer questions from fans and perform stripped-back versions of his songs on the piano.

READ MORE: Nick Cave live at Tennessee Performing Arts Centre, Nashville: extraordinary honesty and coruscating one-liners

The singer-songwriter is reviving his ‘Conversations With Nick Cave: An Evening Of Talk And Music’ series, which will begin in Vancouver on April 9 and conclude in New Orleans on May 21.

The intimate shows will feature Cave fielding unvetted questions from the audience on any subject, interspersed with solo piano performances of songs from throughout his career.

The format was first introduced in 2018 and subsequently expanded into a wider tour in 2019, when Cave said he wanted to establish a more direct and personal connection with his fans.

Announcing the new dates, he reflected on how the original shows had helped him process his grief following the death of his son Arthur in 2015.

He described the unconventional format as “a strange, almost desperate idea”, but said that the evenings had become “deeply healing” for him.

Cave explained that his regular correspondence with fans through The Red Hand Files, which launched in 2018, had further encouraged him to return to the format.

Reflecting on how the country has changed in the intervening years, Cave said he was looking forward to returning with his piano, playing songs and answering questions.

“What could possibly go wrong?” he joked.

View this post on Instagram

During the original North American tour in October 2019, NME attended a show in Nashville, where Cave answered questions about grief, religion, songwriting and his career alongside stripped-back piano performances.

In 2022, he explained how performing live had become part of his grieving process, describing the mutual support between himself and fans as a source of strength.

He also spoke to NME in 2023 about the importance of maintaining open conversations with people whose perspectives differed from his own.

Meanwhile, Cave has had a busy year with The Bad Seeds, touring their acclaimed 2024 album ‘Wild God’.

In July, the band played a huge homecoming show at Brighton’s Preston Park, where Kylie Minogue joined them for a performance of their 1995 collaboration ‘Where The Wild Roses Grow’. The concert attracted nearly 50,000 people and was reportedly the largest ticketed event in Brighton’s history.

Earlier in May, Cave also revealed that The Bad Seeds had been working together in the studio, with the possibility of recording a follow-up to ‘Wild God’.
