posts.title: How Was 2026 For You? Come Tell Us All About Your Year With the #BN2026Epilogues
posts.excerpt: Like the flick of a finger, 2026 is coming to an end. It all feels like an hour ago when we wished each other “Happy New Year” and “Welcome to 2026.” Each month flew by, days folding into weeks, weeks
posts.content:
Like the flick of a finger, 2026 is coming to an end. It all feels like an hour ago when we wished each other “Happy New Year” and “Welcome to 2026.” Each month flew by, days folding into weeks, weeks folding into months, and here we are in November, preparing for December, Christmas, January, and a brand new year: 2027.

As it is tradition, the best way to close out the year is through reflection. A lot has happened this year, and with the few days remaining this year, a lot will still happen. Despite the many faces of 2026, the ups and downs, Nigerians and Africans showed up on big stages to express their creativity and talent. It was this year that Nora Awolowo and Damilola Osikoya broke the Guinness World Record for the largest attendance at a film screening with the screening of Black Market: The Movie. It was in 2026 that Ogaga Ifowodo won the $100,000 Nigeria Prize for Literature. It was in 2026 that Kayinsola Ajayi broke Nigeria’s 100m record. And many many more.

At BellaNaija, it was an even greater and more remarkable year. We celebrated our 20th anniversary with a Grand Red Carpet Experience. It was a beautiful evening that marked and solidified BellaNaija’s contribution as one of the culture shapers in Africa. Beyond the red carpet experience, it was the year of stories. We told stories of Africans and Nigerians achieving incredible feats at home and abroad. We told stories of educational success, stories of love, of Africans across the world. We did only what we are meant to do, and what we know best to do.

So we want to hear from you too. We want to know how 2026 has been for you. Did you start a new job? Did you find love? Did you start a new hobby or routine? Did you buy something you’ve always wanted? How were your finances? What experience from the year stood out for you? What did you manage to achieve? What did you fail to achieve? Share any experiences that brought you down, but also taught you how to pick yourself back up.

We want to hear about it all. We want you to write all about it.

Reflect on moments when you wished you had made different choices. Share instances where you chose to trust your intuition. Tell us about the beautiful experiences you had this year. We invite you to share your victories and setbacks, as well as your joys and sorrows, with us.

You have a lot to get a lot off your chest, and we are also ready to read, so share with us.

Guidelines:

Send your #BN2026Epilogues stories to features@bellanaija.com

Include 2026 Epilogues in the subject of your email.

Stories can be between 400 and 1,500 words.

Submissions will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and publication begins December 1st. So send your submissions as early as possible.

Don’t be shy, send us your photos too (and as many as you can).

Deadline: Submissions are open until the 15th of December, 2025. You can read previous entries here.

You matter. Your story matters, and you never know, you might help someone feel seen by sharing.

We cannot wait to hear from you.

posts.title: Macklemore says nine US arenas rejected his ‘Free Palestine’ tour: “We will build our own stages”
posts.excerpt: Madison Square Garden has responded to the rapper's allegations, claiming he is "not an arena-level act" The post Macklemore says nine US arenas rejected his ‘Free Palestine’ tour: “We will build our
posts.content:
Macklemore has claimed nine American arenas refused to host his ‘Free Palestine’ tour, accusing venue owners of attempting to silence his support for Palestinians.

READ MORE: “What am I willing to risk?”: Macklemore on Trump, gun control and why ‘Same Love’ remains vital

The rapper shared a lengthy statement on Instagram yesterday (November 6), explaining that he had intended to bring the tour to the US following three sold-out concerts in Dublin, Paris and London last month.

However, he said his team had been turned away by nine venues, despite initially having being offered available dates before the end of the year.

“From the beginning, our plan was to bring this tour home to the U.S.,” he wrote. “But after weeks of reaching out, nine major American arenas have turned us down.”

He named New York’s Madison Square Garden, Newark’s Prudential Center, Brooklyn’s Barclays Center, Long Island’s UBS Arena, Los Angeles venues Intuit Dome, Kia Forum and Crypto.com Arena, San Francisco’s Chase Center and Seattle’s Climate Pledge Arena.

“By mid-September, we received available dates at these arenas through the end of the year,” Macklemore claimed. “But once they found out these were my benefit shows for Palestine, those dates were suddenly off the table.”

“The doors were closed. The conversations were all different, but the result was the same. The shows were not going to be allowed to happen in these venues.”

He added: “In over twenty years of touring, I’ve never experienced anything like this.”

View this post on Instagram

Madison Square Garden has since responded to the allegations, disputing the suggestion that its decision was politically motivated.

An MSG Entertainment spokesperson told TMZ: “We have some of the busiest venues in the world with extremely limited availability and he’s not an arena level act.”

In his statement, Macklemore argued that the difficulties he had encountered were part of a wider pattern of pressure against performers who publicly support Palestinians.

“Looking back over the last three years, the only real regret I have is not speaking publicly when Zionists were kicking me under the table,” he wrote. “At the time, I didn’t believe that centering what was happening to me was worth taking any attention away from the genocide in Palestine.”

He continued: “But the intimidation, manipulation and suppression I experienced are part of how those in power keep entertainers quiet. It’s their main tactic to keep us in line. Shut up and dribble, or you will be punished.”

The rapper went on to criticise wealthy venue owners and their business relationships with Israel, arguing that financial power should not determine which political causes artists can support.

“We live in a country that prides itself on freedom of speech,” he wrote. “Yet we’ve reached a point where a handful of billionaires can decide which causes are acceptable, which voices are welcome and which human lives are worth defending.”

He added: “To these owners, the words Free Palestine represent a threat. Not because they endanger anyone, but because those words challenge the systems of power they have built their fortunes on.”

Macklemore said he remained committed to organising further benefit concerts, even if that meant abandoning plans to perform at conventional arenas.

“There will be more shows for Palestine,” he wrote. “We’ll keep working with other artists and organizers, continuing where we left off in Europe. We’ll probably just take that shit outside where it belonged in the first place.”

He concluded: “We will build our own stages. They may own the arenas. But they do not own the people who fill them. And they never will.”

View this post on Instagram

The latest dispute follows Macklemore’s removal from Ed Sheeran’s US ‘Loop Tour’ in September, after he made speeches in support of Palestinians during concerts at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium.

The rapper faced criticism from billionaire Robert Kraft, the owner of Gillette Stadium, who said he would not permit Macklemore to perform at the venue because of concerns about the messaging of his set.

Sheeran subsequently said the decision to remove Macklemore was made by promoters and venue owners, rather than himself, adding that he had attempted to find a resolution. The controversy also prompted several support acts, including Finneas, Beoga and Lukas Graham, to withdraw from Sheeran’s tour in solidarity with Macklemore.

Following his dismissal, the rapper pledged his entire $1million earnings from the tour to six organisations supporting Palestinians.

He then launched the ‘Free Palestine Tour’, holding the opening concert in Dublin on October 26 alongside Hozier and Kneecap.

The tour subsequently visited Paris, where Aurora, Pomme and Portugal. The Man were among the performers, before concluding in London with appearances from Greta Thunberg, Paloma Faith and Nemahsis.

posts.title: Daddy Showkey: Vanguard Award will be the biggest of my lifetime
posts.excerpt: "At 13, in 1983, I started following Danladi Bako of NTA. I was always at his office on Lagos Island. He would give me a voucher to go and eat, and made me comfortable in his office" The post Daddy Sh
posts.content:
By Clifford Ndujihe & Benjamin Njoku

Chief John Odafe Asiemo, 57, popularly known as Daddy Showkey, is a household name in Nigerian music scene. He is the creator of ‘Galala’ music, which sound helped define Nigeria’s street music in the 90s.

Read Also: Nostalgia, glitz as icons reunite for Daddy Showkey’s 50th anniversary celebration

Daddy Showkey is a nominee for Vanguard Newspaper’s 2026 Entertainment Icon of the year award.

Speaking with ululation after being presented with the letter of nomination, on Tuesday at his Lagos residence, he said: “They say a prophet is not recognised by his own people. But I am a prophet who is being recognised by the people who built me. This is the greatest awards I have ever received in my life because it is coming from Vanguard. Vanguard is the first newspaper in Nigeria that wrote about me, when I was nothing. This is Vanguard, and I cherish it a lot.

“Apart from that, Vanguard played a big role in pushing me to the limelight.

“So, a recognition award coming from Vanguard, I must cherish it. It is like my own people saying it is high time. Sometimes, when I see Vanguard giving people awards, I always say in my mind, when is it going to be my turn?

“Now, it is my turn to receive the award and I am very grateful.”

Reminiscing on his early days, Daddy Showkey, who celebrated 50 years on the stage recently, continued: “For years, I kept coming to Vanguard head office, but I never met the publisher, Uncle Sam, in person.

After my secondary education, I hit the streets. From childhood, I had made up my mind to follow music.

At 13, in 1983, I started following Danladi Bako of NTA. I was always at his office on Lagos Island. He would give me a voucher to go and eat, and made me comfortable in his office.

My first song, “Big Belle”, was released in 1990 in Nawfia, Njikoka, Enugu-Ukwu, Anambra State.

I cannot forget the late Amadi Ogbonna(former Vanguard Entertainment Editor). He was one of the earliest journalists to write about me and played a huge role in my career. Before Ogbonnaya wrote about me, we used to walk from Kirikiri to Olodi areas, passing Vanguard. I remember saying one day while walking past Vanguard ‘this newspaper will one day write about me.’ It came to pass when Ogbonnaya wrote about me for the first time.

The second was Smart Irewudo, a former Champion Newspaper reporter, now based in the United States.

Before I started recording, during the June 12 crisis, I led Ajegunle boys who blocked roads and extorted money from motorists. Smart took my picture and published it in the Daily Champion. In his mind, he thought he had done me a great favour. He didn’t know the police would come after me.

Luckily, one of the policemen from Area F showed my picture to Amadi Ogbonna. He recognised me immediately and called me. When I showed up, Ogbonna took me to the police station and told them I wasn’t a bad boy, they should release me and focus on arresting real criminals.

That same week in 1999, Dr Obiefula Nwankwo offered to record my songs. On the day I signed as his artiste, Amadi Ogbonna and Smart Irewudo accompanied me. After signing the deal, we ended up at the Vanguard Canal. That’s where we celebrated it.

Ogbonna kept encouraging me, supporting my career financially and otherwise.

If Vanguard decides to honour me today, I would say I merit it. It is Vanguard honouring their own, recognising their own pikin. And it will be the biggest award I will ever receive in my lifetime.”

Vanguard News

posts.title: Flo Milli Wins Dismissal of Copyright Lawsuit Over ‘Never Lose Me’ Beat Sample
posts.excerpt: A judge ruled that the man who brought the claims did not technically own a beat sampled in the 2023 hit.
posts.content:
A judge threw out copyright claims over Flo Milli’s 2023 hit “Never Lose Me” after ruling that the man bringing the lawsuit does not technically own a beat sampled in the track.

The Friday (Nov. 6) court ruling, obtained and first reported by Billboard, dismissed the lawsuit without any opportunity to amend. But the case is not over for good; an attorney for the plaintiff said they intend to appeal.

Related

Flo Milli Hit With Copyright Lawsuit Over Hit Single ‘Never Lose Me’

Michael Sanft, Attorney Who Represented Keffe D in 2Pac Murder Trial, Dies at 54

Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71

The case was brought last year by Shamar Deal, a Baltimore-based artist who purchased a beat called “Youu” on the rap instrumental marketplace Traktrain in 2019. Deal said that after he paid $200 for a 10-year exclusive license, producer Gerreaux Katana wrongly turned around and relicensed the beat to Babyface Ray and 42 Dugg for their 2023 song “Ron Artest.” Flo Milli then sampled “Ron Artest” on “Never Lose Me,” which peaked at No. 15 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Deal sued all three rappers for copyright infringement. On Friday, however, Judge André Birotte Jr. found that Deal does not actually own the rights to “Youu.” That’s because copyright law requires all exclusive licenses to be signed by both parties — and Traktrain never got Katana’s signature to sell the beat to Deal.

According to Deal, the fact that Katana uploaded the beat to Traktrain and accepted his $200 should be enough to validate the license. But Judge Birotte said there’s no room for ambiguity here. He quoted a decades-old appellate ruling on the topic: “The rule is really quite simple: If the copyright holder agrees to transfer ownership to another party, that party must get the copyright holder to sign a piece of paper saying so.”

Related

Buying Beats Online Is Common, Convenient and Risky

The ruling highlights a potential pitfall of online instrumental marketplaces, which have become a common source of beats for aspiring rappers in recent years. As experts have previously told Billboard, casual licensing arrangements can later come back to haunt artists and producers in a business that relies on proper legal paperwork.

Deal’s attorney, Larry Zerner, cited the prevalence of the online beat economy when telling Billboard on Friday that they “respectfully disagree” with Judge Birotte’s decision and plan to appeal it.

“Shamar Deal paid for an exclusive license to this beat,” said Zerner. “The producer listed it for sale as an exclusive, set the price, took the money, and confirmed the sale in his own emails. Shamar also has a contract with the producer that confirms all of these facts. That’s how thousands of independent artists buy beats online every single day, and they deserve to know that the licenses they pay for will hold up. We’re confident the Ninth Circuit will see it that way.”

David Given, a lawyer representing Babyface Ray and his distributor EMPIRE, told Billboard on Friday, “Our clients are grateful for the court’s carefully reasoned decision dismissing the case for copyright infringement against them.”

Reps for Flo Milli and 42 Dugg did not immediately return requests for comment on the ruling.

posts.title: After years away, Charles Okafor ‘The Primate’ roars back in ‘Issakaba Sequel’
posts.excerpt: By Benjamin Njoku True legends never really leave. They stay etched in our hearts, commanding respect, admiration and timeless relevance. That is how filmmaker Lancelot Imasuen describes Charles Okafo
posts.content:
By Benjamin Njoku

True legends never really leave. They stay etched in our hearts, commanding respect, admiration and timeless relevance. That is how filmmaker Lancelot Imasuen describes Charles Okafor, affectionately known as The Primate.

Okafor, who dominated Nollywood screens in the 90s and early 2000s as one of the industry’s most prolific and popular stars, is set for a grand comeback on Wednesday, November 11, when the highly anticipated action-thriller “Issakaba: The Return” hits cinemas.

The premiere promises a new dawn for Nollywood, and the return of a screen icon who has been away for several years.

Announcing Okafor’s return, Lancelot said his appearance on the promotional poster was a powerful reminder of the enduring legacy of a man whose talent, commanding screen presence, versatility and remarkable contribution to Nollywood have earned him a special place in Nigerian entertainment history.

“The Primate is not just an actor; he is an institution, a symbol of excellence and a distinguished custodian of a generation of Nigerian storytelling,” Lancelot said.

“His remarkable ability to bring characters to life, coupled with his unmistakable presence, has left an indelible impression on audiences across generations.

“Seeing him return in ”Issakaba: The Return” evokes nostalgia, excitement and admiration. It is a beautiful convergence of legacy and renewed relevance, a testament to the fact that genuine talent does not grow old, and true legends never go out of fashion. The legend returns, but the legacy never leaves!”

Okafor, famed for movies like “Computer Girls (2003)”, “Sting (2006)” and “Ocean Deep (2007)”, was long rumoured to have quit acting to win souls for God. In reality, he says his long absence from the screen was simply about his preference for quality movies over quantity.

posts.title: CAFA urges unified policies to grow Africa’s fashion economy to $500bn
posts.excerpt: By Benjamin Njoku The Confederation of African Fashion,CAFA, has called on African countries to harmonise their fashion policies, strengthen intellectual property protection and invest in local manufa
posts.content:
By Benjamin Njoku

The Confederation of African Fashion,CAFA, has called on African countries to harmonise their fashion policies, strengthen intellectual property protection and invest in local manufacturing as part of efforts to grow the continent’s fashion economy to $500 billion. The President of CAFA, Professor Lai Labode, made the call during the unveiling of the joint stand of the organisation and the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy at the ongoing CANEX WKND 2026. Labode said Africa had no shortage of creative talent but lacked the structures and policies needed to translate its creative potential into economic value. “In Africa, we don’t have a shortage of talent. What Africa needs is structure. Money always follows structure,” he said. He said the African Fashion Industry Growth Charter, developed by CAFA, was built around 10 pillars designed to address challenges across the fashion value chain, including policy harmonisation, raw material cultivation and processing, intellectual property protection, counterfeiting, logistics and market access. Labode stressed the need for African countries to process their raw materials locally instead of exporting them in largely unprocessed forms, arguing that local value addition would create jobs and retain more wealth within the continent. Using cotton production as an example, he compared Brazil’s reported $5.3 billion cotton exports with China’s earnings from cotton production and processing, saying Africa needed to build its own processing capacity to compete more effectively. He also identified intellectual property protection as a major priority, noting that African designers and creative businesses needed stronger systems to protect their original works from counterfeiting and unauthorised use. On market access, Labode disclosed plans to establish about 10 African fashion houses across the continent, alongside outlets in New York, Paris, Milan and London, to promote African designers and connect them with international markets. He called for common intellectual property rules and standards across African countries, warning that fragmented systems could weaken the continent’s competitiveness. The CAFA president also urged member states to support the intellectual property framework under the African Continental Free Trade Area, saying the relevant protocol annexes had been passed in February 2026 but required wider participation by African countries. Speaking in the same vein, the Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, identified private-sector partnerships, policy development and infrastructure as essential to strengthening Nigeria’s fashion industry. Musawa said the collaboration with CAFA should translate into tangible economic benefits, particularly job creation, while promoting African unity, cultural pride and soft power. She disclosed that the ministry was working towards establishing an intellectual property policy to protect fashion designers across Nigeria, irrespective of their backgrounds. “Partnerships, the policies, and hubs, it is very important to put us to capacity-building, and that can only happen through infrastructure,” she said. The minister added that the ministry was working to establish creative hubs across the country to support capacity building, stimulate economic growth and create employment opportunities. Beyond government policies and investment, discussions at the CAFA stand highlighted the need to build sustainable fashion businesses through financial literacy, proper business structures and production-cost management. Series of discussions at the event also highlighted the importance of preserving African textile heritage while adapting traditional designs to contemporary markets. Participants identified technology as an important tool for improving garment sizing, production consistency and quality standards, particularly as African designers seek to serve international markets. They also emphasised the need to document traditional textile knowledge and protect the cultural meanings associated with indigenous patterns and designs. Speaking on local patronage, Labode said Nigerians were increasingly embracing traditional fabrics such as adire and aso-oke rather than relying exclusively on Western-style clothing. He said Africa was already exporting about $15 billion worth of apparel and related products but could achieve greater economic returns by strengthening local production and consumption. He encouraged Africans to incorporate locally made clothing into their everyday dressing, saying the continent needed to place greater value on its own fashion and textile products. The four-day gathering which gathers creatives, entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers and industry stakeholders from Africa and the diaspora to explore opportunities across the creative and cultural industries will round off tomorrow, with cultural activities and a Legends football.

posts.title: CANEX WKND 2026 lights up Lagos as Davido, Fally Ipupa, Flavour headline star-studded concert tonight
posts.excerpt: By Benjamin Njoku & Tony-Okafor Favour The 2026 edition of Creative Africa Nexus Weekend, CANEX WKND, which opened at the Professor Wole Soyinka Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos on Thursday, continues this
posts.content:
By Benjamin Njoku & Tony-Okafor Favour

The 2026 edition of Creative Africa Nexus Weekend, CANEX WKND, which opened at the Professor Wole Soyinka Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos on Thursday, continues this evening with a blockbuster concert.

Headlining the night are some of Africa’s biggest music stars, including Nigeria’s Davido, Congolese sensation Fally Ipupa, Flavour, Cali-Ber Tha Grime, Sabrina Francis and Nigerian DJ duo Wanni X Handi.

The concert will bring together performers from Africa and the Caribbean for an evening of live music, rhythm and cultural celebration. The four-day gathering, themed “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World”, has brought the once moribund Arts Theatre back to life. It convened leading voices from film, music, fashion, sport, publishing, gastronomy and business to advance trade, investment and commercial opportunities across Africa’s creative economy. The opening day featured a series of masterclasses and sessions, including Building Your Brand as an Independent Artist, Podcasting for Success, Fashion Masterclass: Building Profitable Fashion Brands, and Building Sustainable Business Models in the Performing Arts. In attendance were Vice-President Kassim Shettima, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Afreximbank President and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Dr George Elombi; Nigeria’s Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole; and African Continental Free Trade Area Secretary-General, Wamkele Mene. Other dignitaries included the Minister of Arts, Culture, Tourism, and the Creative Economy for Nigeria, Hon Hannatu Musa Musawa; Mrs Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President of Intra-African Trade and Export Development at Afreximbank; Hon Ginger Moxey, Minister for Grand Bahama; Emmy Award-winning actor Uzo Aduba; filmmaker Funke Akindele; and actors Richard Mofe-Damijo and Thuso Mbedu among other dignitaries. Speaking while declaring the programme open, Shettima said the world will eventually hear about the can-do spirit of African women. He commended Afreximbank for committing $2 billion to Africa’s creative industries by 2027, noting that the industry is not just about entertainment, but also serious economic infrastructure. Shettima took the audience down memory lane, recalling almost 50 years ago when the same Arts Theatre hosted the second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture, FESTAC ’77, where the Black World declared through music, dance, literature and art that “our culture was not just a footnote to history, but the very core within it. “In 1977, we came to celebrate our culture. In 2024, we are here to capitalize it,” he said. He urged Africans to be proud of who they are without asking for anything in return.

The film’s soundtrack is executive-produced by Grammy-winning Nigerian superstar Tems, bringing together African musical talent for a major international cinematic production. Designed as an intimate yet energetic gathering, YORÙBÁ HEALER LIVE will attract a curated audience spanning Nigeria’s music, entertainment, fashion, media and creative industries, alongside Moelogo’s fans and wider creative community.

At its heart, YORÙBÁ HEALER LIVE is about bringing people together through the transformative power of music and the cultural stories that connect us. It is a celebration of artistic evolution, heritage and community, bringing the world of Yorùbá Healer to the people and place that make its cultural foundations meaningful.

On December 20, Lagos becomes the meeting point for the music, the memories, the people and the magic.

posts.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
posts.excerpt: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cy
posts.content:
With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it.

Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky.

The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes.

Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares:

“I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.”

A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK

In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production.

The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices.

Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment.

SHOW AND AVAILABILITY

Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists.

Date: November 11th, 2026

Time: 6 PM WAT

Dress Code: Banke Kuku Glam

ABOUT BANKE KUKU

Banke Kuku is a British-Nigerian designer celebrated as the Queen of Prints. Nature is at the heart of everything she creates: flowers, birds, skies, and landscapes from Nigeria, transformed into bold prints and intricate textiles. Recognised by Vogue and a recipient of the Women in Making award, she designs womenswear, menswear and home textiles that bring the beauty of the natural world into everyday life.

Follow @Bankekuku for updates, stories and behind-the-scenes moments from Earth & Sky.

posts.title: FinTribe Finance Fair 2026: Empowers Over 10,000 Women to Build Wealth and Financial Independence
posts.excerpt: Over 10,000 women gathered at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, on October 31, 2026, for the fourth edition of FinTribe Finance Fair, a growing movement dedicated to helping African w
posts.content:
Over 10,000 women gathered at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, on October 31, 2026, for the fourth edition of FinTribe Finance Fair, a growing movement dedicated to helping African women move from financial awareness to wealth creation and ownership.

Themed I CAN and powered by returning lead sponsor Sycamore, the event brought together financial experts, business leaders, entrepreneurs and influential personalities, including Funke Akindele, Omoni Oboli, BamBam, Sola Adesakin and Olufemi Shobanjo, for a day of practical financial education, inspiring conversations and meaningful opportunities.

For FinTribe founder Jennifer Awirigwe, popularly known as Financial Jennifer, the fair represents a bigger mission: helping women gain the confidence and resources to take charge of their financial futures.

“Financial education is important, but knowledge must eventually become action. We want women to leave Finance Fair knowing that they can save, invest, grow their income, build businesses and take ownership of their financial future,” she shared ahead of the event.

Beyond Finance Fair, FinTribe is building a community where women learn about money and put that knowledge into practice. With a presence across 43 countries, the organisation has reached over 20,000 women through financial education, supported more than 5,000 women with capital market training and helped members collectively save and invest millions of dollars.

Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence.

At the fair, award-winning filmmaker Omoni Oboli encouraged women to pursue their ambitions without neglecting their wellbeing, reminding them to take things one step at a time, prioritise rest and ask for help when needed.

During the Financial Clinic, Sola Adesakin challenged women to become more intentional about their finances, emphasising the importance of earning, budgeting and turning income into real assets. She also introduced the four forces of money: Earnings, Expenses, Engines and Encumbrances.

Olufemi Shobanjo of NGX Regulation Limited shared insights into capital market participation, while actress BamBam, marketing strategist and Woof Studios founder Adetutu Laditan, and Mercy Agbeti, popularly known as Christian Money Woman, contributed to conversations about building value, navigating opportunities and growing with purpose.

One of the most memorable moments came during Funke Akindele’s session when a medical doctor and founder of Raffia Fashion Africa presented the actress with a pair of handcrafted raffia earrings.

Funke immediately wore them, danced, invited the entrepreneur onto the stage, embraced her, prayed for her and publicly endorsed her business.

The entrepreneur later shared on her instagram page that “she had saved to purchase a VIP ticket to the fair and had admired Funke for years”. What began as a simple audience interaction became a powerful demonstration of how visibility, encouragement and one meaningful connection can open doors for a growing business.

Beyond the stage, women connected with financial institutions, explored investment opportunities and participated in financial education sessions. The fair also featured empowerment opportunities and giveaways, including children’s investment portfolios, stock units, a plot of land, a Zanzibar trip and getaway experiences supported by partner organisations.

Sycamore returned as lead sponsor for the second consecutive year, alongside other partners supporting FinTribe’s mission to expand women’s access to financial knowledge and opportunities.

From its first edition in 2023 to this year’s gathering, FinTribe Finance Fair has continued to demonstrate the power of bringing women together around a shared goal.

But the real work continues long after the event ends. Through education, community, partnerships and practical wealth-building initiatives, FinTribe is helping women across Africa move beyond conversations about money to making informed decisions, building assets and creating financially secure futures.

To learn more about FinTribe, explore its programmes and join its growing community, visit www.thefintribe.com or follow @thefintribe on Instagram.

posts.title: Concerts to attend in Lagos for Detty December 2026
posts.excerpt: Here are concerts in Lagos fans and music lovers can attend to this Detty December 2026 which kicks off earlier than many expected. The post Concerts to attend in Lagos for Detty December 2026 appeare
posts.content:
Here are concerts in Lagos fans and music lovers can attend to this Detty December 2026 which kicks off earlier than many expected.

Lagos is gearing up for another exciting Detty December as Nigerian and international music stars prepare to take over the city with a series of concerts, music festivals and live performances throughout December 2026.

With thousands of music lovers expected to travel to Nigeria for the festive season, this year's entertainment calendar is shaping up to be particularly busy, featuring performances from some of the biggest names in Afrobeats, hip-hop and R&B.

From Wizkid's appearance at Detty December Fest and Davido's three-night residency to BNXN's headline concert, Adekunle Gold's orchestral experience and Flytime Promotions' international lineup, there is plenty to look forward to.

Here is a breakdown of some of the major concerts scheduled to take place in Lagos in December 2026, including their dates, venues and announced performers.

ÀLÓ: Once Upon a Song – December 13

Kicking off the major live music events on the calendar is the third edition of ÀLÓ, titled Once Upon a Song, scheduled for December 13 at Shell Hall, MUSON Centre, Onikan.

The event will celebrate African folk music, indigenous sounds, storytelling and cultural heritage through live musical performances and traditional storytelling.

Scheduled to begin at 7 PM, the concert will provide a platform for celebrating African musical heritage. The organisers are yet to publish the complete list of performing artistes.

Davido's ORIADÉ: The Residency – December 17–19

Davido Already Falling Lyrics

Davido will headline a three-night concert experience titled ORIADÉ: The Residency at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly known as the National Theatre, in Iganmu.

Scheduled to run from December 17 to 19, the residency will celebrate 15 years of the singer's musical journey, bringing together songs from his extensive catalogue and music from his Oriadé project.

The three-night experience is expected to be one of the biggest Nigerian-led concerts of the festive season, giving fans an opportunity to celebrate the singer's contribution to Afrobeats.

Wizkid at Detty December Fest – December 18

A picture of Wizkid (NotjustOK.com media library)

Wizkid is set to headline the opening concert of Detty December Fest on December 18.

The Grammy-winning Afrobeats superstar will lead the opening night of the festival, which is scheduled to run until December 30.

Organised by Livespot360, the festival will feature a mixture of concerts, nightlife, food, fashion and cultural experiences, with multiple performance stages expected to accommodate established and emerging performers.

Wizkid's appearance is expected to be one of the major highlights of the opening weekend.

ICONIQ FEST – December 19–23

One of the biggest additions to Lagos' December concert calendar is ICONIQ FEST, a five-day music festival featuring individual headline concerts from five Nigerian music stars.

Scheduled to take place at The Lekki Coliseum, the festival will feature BNXN, FOLA, Oxlade, Ruger and Mr P across five consecutive nights.

The programme begins on December 19 with BNXN's Still In Charge concert, followed by FOLA's Cloud 9 on December 20.

Oxlade will take over on December 21 with Plug The Ox, while Ruger is scheduled to headline the fourth night on December 22 with his BlownBoy experience.

The festival will conclude on December 23 with Mr P's The OG Thank You Concert.

ICONIQ FEST is expected to provide a platform for the five artistes to deliver individual headline experiences rather than a conventional festival lineup.

According to the published event announcement, general admission is available through registration, with VIP and table reservations also advertised.

Brandy's House of R&B – December 20

American R&B superstar Brandy will headline Flytime Promotions' House of R&B concert on December 20 at the Eko Convention Centre, Victoria Island.

The Grammy-winning singer, widely celebrated for her contributions to contemporary R&B, will lead the event as Flytime begins its annual December concert programme.

Brandy's appearance adds another major international name to Lagos' festive entertainment calendar.

Coca-Cola Rhythm Unplugged – December 21

The international music lineup continues on December 21 with Coca-Cola Rhythm Unplugged at the Eko Convention Centre.

American rapper Lil Baby and R&B singer Kehlani are among the announced performers, alongside American rapper and television personality Yung Miami.

The concert will mark Kehlani's first live performance in Nigeria, adding another major international appearance to the December calendar.

The event is expected to attract fans of hip-hop and contemporary R&B, bringing together three American music personalities for one night.

ELITE FEST – December 21

If You Like lyrics by BNXN

Also scheduled for December 21 is ELITE FEST 2026, an Afrobeats festival organised by The Elite Collective.

The one-day event will take place at Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island, with activities scheduled to begin at 4 PM.

Although the organisers have confirmed BNXN as one of its headline acts, the date and venue, the full list of performing artistes has yet to be announced.

Flytime Fest – December 22–24

Flytime Promotions will continue its December concert programme with Flytime Fest, powered by Coca-Cola, running from December 22 to 24 at the Eko Convention Centre.

American rappers Latto, A Boogie Wit da Hoodie and Sexyy Red have been announced for the opening day, December 22.

The festival is expected to feature additional local and international performers across its three-day programme, with more names anticipated for December 23 and 24.

AfroJazz Fest: To the Roots – December 23

AfroJazz Fest returns to Lagos on December 23 with its 2026 edition, titled To the Roots.

Scheduled to take place at Amore Gardens, Lekki, the festival will celebrate African musical heritage through a combination of jazz expression, indigenous sounds and contemporary African music.

The Cavemen and Lagbaja feature in the festival's artist-reveal section, with further announcements expected as the organisers finalise the programme.

Adekunle Gold's The Greatest Showman – December 26

Adekunle Gold

Adekunle Gold will headline the second edition of The Greatest Showman on December 26 at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Theatre, in Iganmu.

Scheduled to run from 6 PM to 11 PM, the concert will feature the singer alongside the MUSON Orchestra and The 79th Element.

The event will adopt an orchestral presentation, bringing Adekunle Gold's music to life through a live musical arrangement. It will also feature a black-tie dress code, giving the concert a more theatrical and formal experience.

Victony's The Bonfire Experience – December 26

Victony 2FRESH Lyrics

Victony is also scheduled to bring his The Bonfire Experience to Lagos on December 26 as part of a multi-city concert programme.

The experience is designed to bring fans closer to the singer through an intimate live music setting.

The Lagos performance follows previously advertised dates in Abuja on December 4 and Port Harcourt on December 5.

However, the Lagos venue remains subject to confirmation from the organisers.

Other December Concerts and Live Music Events

Beyond the major headline concerts, several other live music events have been listed for Lagos throughout the festive period.

These include Waje's The Unexpected Christmas, scheduled for December 20 at the National Theatre, and SPINALL's Èkó Groove, also listed for December 20 at the J. Randle Centre.

Juma Jux is also listed for a December 18 performance at Ilubirin, while Laolu Gbenjo's Gratitude Concert 2026 is scheduled for December 28 at The Podium, Lekki.

Additionally, Snazzyrogue's L!ve Forever 26 has been listed for December 28 at Landmark Centre.

Some of these additional listings require further confirmation of their full programmes and ticketing details.

A Busy Detty December for Lagos

With concerts spread across different parts of the city, December 2026 is shaping up to be another major period for Lagos' live music and entertainment industry.

The combination of Nigerian headline performances from Davido, Wizkid, BNXN, FOLA, Oxlade, Ruger, Mr P, Adekunle Gold and Victony, alongside international appearances from Brandy, Lil Baby, Kehlani, Yung Miami, Latto, A Boogie Wit da Hoodie and Sexyy Red, reflects the growing appeal of Lagos as a destination for festive-season entertainment.

With several organisers still expected to announce additional performers and event details, the December concert calendar could become even more extensive in the coming weeks.

For music lovers planning to spend the festive season in Lagos, there will be plenty of live performances and musical experiences to choose from.

posts.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
posts.excerpt: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. F
posts.content:
There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world.

For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac, inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats.

The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28.

At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box.

The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent.

For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration.

“Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said.

He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.”

The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally.

The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression.

Speaking about the collaboration, Davido described his partnership with Martell as an opportunity to continue pushing African culture forward, while Prince Gyasi’s creative contribution translates the energy, confidence and movement of Afrobeats into a visual experience.

Beyond the artwork, the limited-edition XO brings together Martell’s craftsmanship and a creative story rooted in African identity and contemporary expression. The collaboration also extends into Davido’s music video for Already Falling, filmed at Château de Chanteloup, Martell’s historic estate in Cognac, where the limited-edition collection makes an appearance.

The Nigerian unveiling on November 6 will be marked by an intimate dinner with Davido and Prince Gyasi, bringing together invited guests to experience the collaboration firsthand.

As Afrobeats continues to influence music, fashion, art and popular culture, the Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO is another reminder of how far the movement has travelled and the creative possibilities it continues to inspire. Through Davido’s music and Prince Gyasi’s visual storytelling, Martell celebrates a genre that continues to shape how African creativity is experienced around the world.

About Pernod Ricard Nigeria

Established in 2012, Pernod Ricard Nigeria is a member of the Pernod Ricard Group, a worldwide leader in the spirits and champagne industry, blending traditional craftsmanship, state-of-the-art brand-building, and global distribution technologies.

Our prestigious portfolio of premium to luxury brands includes Inverroche Gin, Absolut vodka, Ricard pastis, Ballantine’s, Chivas Regal, Royal Salute, and The Glenlivet Scotch whiskies, Jameson Irish whiskey, Martell cognac, Havana Club rum, Beefeater Gin, Malibu liqueur, Mumm and Perrier-Jouët champagnes.

Our mission is to ensure the long-term development of our brands with full respect for people and the environment while empowering our employees around the world to be ambassadors of our purposeful, inclusive, and responsible culture of authentic conviviality.

About Martell

Founded in 1715 by Jean Martell, Maison Martelll is the oldest of the great cognac houses and a symbol of audacity, mastery, and refinement. For over three centuries, Martell has celebrated those who dare to move differently, guided by curiosity, courage, and the pursuit of excellence. At the heart of the House stands The Swift, Martell’s timeless emblem of freedom, vision, and forward motion. It represents a spirit that never stands still, a commitment to rise above convention and redefine what refinement means in every era.

From the iconic Martell XO to the boundary-breaking Martell Blue Swift, every creation reflects a legacy of craftsmanship and an invitation to live boldly, purposefully, and with audacity. For more information, visit martell.com or follow @martellofficialnigeria

posts.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
posts.excerpt: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi, is a qualified social wor
posts.content:
OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi, is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone.

The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma.

Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families.

During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included.

The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support.

For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported.

OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible.

The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included.

About The Founder

OBIMI founder Helen Ewumi at the Nigeria outreach in Lagos. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma.

The incident happened during the first judging round. Atlanta-based pastry chef Curtis Lamar Scott presented his dessert. He prepared a spice cake with eggnog mousse. The dessert also featured white chocolate eggnog snow.

Brown initially appeared to enjoy the cake. However, one particular component changed her reaction. After taking a bite, she spit it into her napkin. “I’m sorry Curtis,” Brown told the contestant. She then explained what went wrong with the dessert: “It was great up until I tried the snow.”

Scott later admitted that the experience felt disappointing. He also recalled Brown comparing the snow to chemicals. The moment quickly sparked discussions among fans online. Several fans criticized Brown’s reaction on Reddit. One fan called the moment particularly rude.

“OK, Kardea was so rude spitting out the cake! Come on, no one else thought it was that bad!” the fan wrote. Another fan also questioned her reaction. “I liked Duff’s homage to Nancy’s ‘hand dance.’ It made me miss Nancy. So far, it’s good. I’m glad the teams are only in place for two weeks. I agree that Kardea was a bit over-dramatic spitting out the cake, though.”

A third fan shared similar criticism. They felt Brown made the moment unnecessarily dramatic. However, some fans defended the judge’s actions. One Reddit user noticed Duff Goldman and Molly Yeh struggling.

They also pointed out Brown apologized beforehand. The commenter added that judges sometimes spit out food. This also happens on other Food Network competitions. Worst Cooks in America regularly features such moments.

The incident comes during a season of changes. Brown and Goldman now judge alongside Molly Yeh. Yeh replaced longtime judge Nancy Fuller for Season 13. The new judging lineup continues to attract attention, but this brief incident has sparked debate among fans.

posts.title: Ryan Gosling’s Hilarious R-Rated Comedy Suddenly Becomes No. 1 on Streaming
posts.excerpt: Ryan Gosling’s R-rated comedy has found a fresh audience years after its theatrical run. The film is now drawing attention on Apple TV, where it has climbed past several better-known titles. Its renew
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Warner Bros. Pictures / Bloom Ryan Gosling’s R-rated comedy has found a fresh audience years after its theatrical run. The film is now drawing attention on Apple TV, where it has climbed past several better-known titles. Its renewed popularity also puts the spotlight back on a crime comedy that struggled to become a box-office hit.

The Nice Guys is getting the love it deserves on Apple TV

Ryan Gosling’s The Nice Guys topped Apple TV’s U.S. movie chart, according to FlixPatrol. It moved ahead of Prisoners, A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving, It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown and newer titles such as Matchbox, Tenzing and Mayday. Interstellar and F1 also made the list.

Directed by Shane Black, the R-rated comedy follows two unlikely partners in 1970s Los Angeles. Gosling plays Holland March, a struggling private eye, while Russell Crowe is Jackson Healy, a hired enforcer.

They team up to make sense of a young woman disappearance and investigate a porn star’s suspicious death. Angourie Rice plays March’s daughter Holly. Margaret Qualley, Matt Bomer, Kim Basinger and Yaya DaCosta also star. The movie runs for 116 minutes and fuses action, mystery and dark humor.

Black co-wrote the script with Anthony Bagarozzi while Joel Silver produced the film. Warner Bros. released it, with Silver Pictures, Waypoint Entertainment and RatPac-Dune Entertainment among its production companies.

Reviews were strong. Rotten Tomatoes gives the film a 91% Tomatometer score from more than 320 reviews and a 79% Popcornmeter score from more than 50,000 audience ratings. IMDb rates it 7.4/10.

Fans were hooked by the script and the electric chemistry between Gosling and Crowe. Their scenes delivered plenty of laughs, thanks to their perfectly timed banter. Gosling was a particular standout, winning fans over with his hilarious expressions and comic timing.

The box office was less impressive. Released in theaters on May 20, 2016, the film earned about $71.2 million worldwide against an estimated $50 million production budget. Its total included $36.2 million in the United States and Canada.

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/2219136-the-nice-guys-ryan-gosling-apple-tv-streaming-no-1

posts.title: Inde Navarrette Names Obsession’s Scariest Scene: ‘I Refuse to Watch’
posts.excerpt: Inde Navarrette may have delivered one of the year’s most unsettling horror performances in Obsession. But even the actor has trouble watching some of the film’s most disturbing moments. During a conv
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Focus Features Inde Navarrette may have delivered one of the year’s most unsettling horror performances in Obsession. But even the actor has trouble watching some of the film’s most disturbing moments.

During a conversation with Allure, Navarrette pointed at one particular sequence as the scariest part of Curry Barker’s supernatural horror movie.

“This is the scariest part of the film. I refuse to watch this scene, so I was looking at the corner … I was like, ‘I know what we’re talking about,’” Navarrette said while watching the sequence.

The scene takes place when Bear, played by Michael Johnston, wakes up to find Nikki standing over him in the middle of the night. She slowly retreats into the dark corners of the bedroom, crying and questioning whether Bear loves her. Her behavior becomes increasingly unnatural as the supernatural wish that forced her to love him takes its toll.

What has Inde Navarrette been cast in since Obsession’s release?

Navarrette’s performance in Obsession has helped turn her into one of the year’s most talked-about rising actors. The horror film follows Bear, who makes a supernatural wish for his childhood friend Nikki to love him. The wish comes true, but Nikki loses her ability to choose how she feels, turning Bear’s desire into a disturbing nightmare.

The actor has several major projects ahead, including Marvel Studios’ upcoming X-Men reboot. Navarrette has been cast as Rogue, one of the franchise’s best-known mutants. Directed by Jake Schreier, the film is scheduled to arrive in theaters on May 5, 2028.

She is also set to lead Apple TV+’s upcoming movie The Waffle House Index. Navarrette plays a waitress whose overnight shift takes an increasingly bizarre and dangerous turn. The project does not yet have a confirmed release date.

Another potential opportunity is the upcoming Call of Duty movie. Taylor Sheridan is writing the screenplay with director Peter Berg, and Navarrette has openly expressed interest in joining the adaptation.

Navarrette has also joined the cast of Vertigo, a thriller about teenagers trapped hundreds of feet in the air after a roller coaster system fails. Her current projects span horror, superhero films, and action.

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/2219800-inde-navarrette-obsession-scariest-scene-refuse-watch

posts.title: Jimmy Kimmel Sees a Possible Early Exit in Donald Trump’s Oval Office Plan
posts.excerpt: Jimmy Kimmel has some thoughts to share on Donald Trump's Oval Office plan. The post Jimmy Kimmel Sees a Possible Early Exit in Donald Trump’s Oval Office Plan appeared first on ComingSoon.net - Movie
posts.content:
Credits: ABC Jimmy Kimmel has some thoughts to share on Donald Trump‘s Oval Office plan. The comedian, who has never once hesitated to take a jab at the president over his antics, recently implied a possible early exit in Trump’s decision to declare the Oval Office a national monument.

In his opening monologue on the November 5 episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live!, the talk show host played a clip of the president signing a proclamation to turn the Oval Office into a national monument, calling it an effort to make sure “no future president can remove any of his crap.”

Kimmel quipped, “That’s right. His historic Diet Coke button will be preserved for many generations to come. I guess ‘Tacky-o’ really wants to make sure nobody lays a finger on all the beautiful new sconces and knickknacks he had spray-painted gold. He turned the Oval Office into the gift shop at the Liberace Museum.”

“Why do this now? Why do this right after the midterms? Maybe he’s planning to leave sooner than we think?” he continued.

Calling the new Oval Office a “landmark and a skid mark,” Kimmel then gave Trump a reality check, saying, “Let me tell you something, buddy: On January 20, 2029, we are gonna yank that crap down and throw it out faster than Melania moves back to New York.”

Trump’s midterm setback adds to Kimmel’s latest White House jabs

While Kimmel mocked Trump for changes to the Oval Office, he also put due emphasis on the president’s midterm setback. The talk show host said that, after numerous Trump-backed Republican candidates lost in the recent midterm election on Tuesday, the president appeared to be preoccupied with the wrong thing.

He also played a clip of Trump signing the document, in which the president was heard saying, “I’m going to be signing a document, which will make them into a landmark for the ages. It won’t be able to be taken down, destroyed, touched, or anything else.”

For context, the midterm elections resulted in a bruising “bloodbath” for the GOP, as Americans overwhelmingly elected Democratic candidates and flipped control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. However, Trump has since dismissed concerns about a potential impeachment effort from the newly Democratic Congress, saying he was “not even a little bit concerned” about the possibility, per Parade.

The political fallout was dissected sharply on The View as well, where co-host and former Trump administration staffer Alyssa Farah Griffin delivered a scathing review (via Entertainment Weekly).

Griffin described the sweeping Democratic victories as a “total and complete repudiation of Donald Trump’s presidency and his policies.” She went on to declare the election results the “beginning of the end of the MAGA movement,” rendering Trump an official “lame duck president.”

posts.title: Simon Pegg Joins Oscar-Winning Actor in Horror Movie With Similar Plot to Hot Fuzz
posts.excerpt: Simon Pegg is returning to the horror genre with a new project that shares great similarities with one of his most iconic films. The upcoming movie follows an American visitor who finds himself caught
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Focus Features Simon Pegg is returning to the horror genre with a new project that shares great similarities with one of his most iconic films. The upcoming movie follows an American visitor who finds himself caught up in the dark secrets of a strange English town, a premise that will instantly remind fans of Pegg’s 2007 cult classic Hot Fuzz.

According to a report from Deadline, Pegg has joined two-time Oscar nominee Paul Giamatti in the upcoming horror-thriller Boutique. Although specific details regarding Pegg’s character name remain under wraps, he will portray a “reclusive author.” The film will be written and directed by Jim Gavin.

The official story of Boutique follows Calvin, an American tourist who travels to an eerie English seaside town that inspired the work of his favorite reclusive author. However, his visit takes a disturbing turn when he becomes entangled with a murderous secret society operating throughout the town.

Apart from Hot Fuzz, Pegg’s acting credits also include The World’s End, Shaun of the Dead, Star Trek, The Undeclared War, and The Boys.

The new horror film brings together a notable mix of talent

Unlike Hot Fuzz, Pegg will not lead the upcoming horror movie. Instead, it will be led by the two-time Oscar nominee, Giamatti. The actor gained widespread recognition for his performance in movies like The Holdovers and Sideways. He also starred in the horror film Morgan and the horror comedy John Dies at the End. He will next be seen in Jesse Eisenberg’s The Debut and Tom McCarthy’s A Statement.

Meanwhile, Boutique will mark Gavin’s feature directorial debut after creating Lodge 49, an AMC comedy series that starred Wyatt Russell. In addition to starring in the horror movie, Giamatti will also serve as a producer. The other producers include Chris Dodds, Charlie Alderman, Greg Field, James Harris, and Mark Lane, while Jacob Jaffke is attached as an executive producer.

Additional casting and an official release date have yet to be announced as the project continues early production.

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/2219754-simon-pegg-paul-giamatti-hot-fuzz-horror-movie

posts.title: Danny McBride & Bradley Cooper’s G.I. Joe Movie Sets Release Date
posts.excerpt: Paramount is bringing the G.I. Joe franchise back to theaters. The post Danny McBride & Bradley Cooper’s G.I. Joe Movie Sets Release Date appeared first on ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Stream
posts.content:
Credits: Warner Bros. Paramount is bringing the G.I. Joe franchise back to theaters with a new live-action movie. The upcoming project will feature Bradley Cooper in a leading role, with Danny McBride directing. The film will introduce a fresh take on the long-running Hasbro property, which has struggled to maintain its theatrical success despite its popularity across toys, comics, and animated shows.

The studio has announced that the untitled movie will hit theaters on October 20, 2028. Cooper will portray Duke, a popular member of the G.I. Joe team. McBride is directing and co-writing the screenplay alongside Jeff Fradley and John Carcieri. Lorenzo di Bonaventura, Mark Vahradian, and Zev Foreman are producing the project.

The upcoming installment will offer a fresh take on the franchise instead of continuing the previously discussed G.I. Joe and Transformers crossover. Although the studio has not disclosed the official plot, McBride reportedly revealed on the Happy Sad Confused podcast that it will be centered on Duke and other members of the team. They will be investigating Springfield, a town secretly controlled by Cobra. Further details about the story and additional cast members remain under wraps.

G.I. Joe has struggled to find success on the big screen despite its longtime popularity

The franchise’s history in theaters began with G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra in 2009. Directed by Stephen Sommers, the film starred Channing Tatum as Duke and earned approximately $302 million worldwide. Following its release, Paramount brought G.I. Joe: Retaliation to theaters in 2013, which introduced Dwayne Johnson as Roadblock. The sequel collected over $375 million worldwide.

Despite the improvement, the franchise struggled to maintain its box-office momentum. Paramount released Snake Eyes in 2021, with Henry Golding playing the titular character. The standalone origin story explored the character’s beginnings but failed to attract a large theatrical audience. It earned approximately $40 million worldwide.

Paramount is now giving the property another chance to find its audience. With Cooper taking on the role of Duke and McBride directing, the upcoming film will bring a different creative approach to the franchise.

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/2219724-gi-joe-movie-release-date-danny-mcbride-bradley-cooper

posts.title: Matt Rhule says Nebraska was due for 'a change' after coaching staff shakeup following loss to Illinois
posts.excerpt: Matt Rhule fired Dana Holgorsen just five days after calling him one of the best offensive minds, as Nebraska scored only 54 points in four losses.
posts.content:
Nebraska coach Matt Rhule wants to see the Cornhuskers’ offense move in a different direction.

The fourth-year Nebraska head coach removed Dana Holgorsen from his role as offensive coordinator, a move that was confirmed shortly after the Cornhuskers’ 24-13 loss to Illinois on Friday. The shakeup comes five days after Rhule called Holgorsen "one of the best offensive minds of our generation."

Co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Glenn Thomas will take over play-calling duties for the Huskers, who have scored just 54 points while dropping four straight games.

"Like so many of you, I am angry, I am disappointed and I am frustrated with our results this season," Rhule said in a statement. "As the head coach, I am ultimately responsible for every aspect of our program — including wins and losses — and it is my responsibility to make changes when they are warranted."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Rhule added that while he still respects Holgorsen’s coaching ability and leadership, the team's offense had reached a point where he believed change was necessary.

"While there are many areas that need improvement, our offensive plan and execution is simply not working. Earlier today, I relieved offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen of his duties. As I have recently shared, Dana has a fantastic offensive mind, he is a strong leader, and he has done great work here at Nebraska. But simply, we need a change."

OHIO STATE'S COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF HOPES TAKE BIG HIT WITH LOSS TO OREGON, JEREMIAH SMITH SHOWS FRUSTRATION

Holgorsen was widely criticized for abandoning the running game and having quarterback Anthony Colandrea attempt 44 passes in a 17-10 loss to Washington. "Dana Holgorsen is one of the best offensive minds of our generation," Rhule said earlier this week.

The Huskers were again plagued by penalties, missed field goals and questionable play-calling in the loss to Illinois. Nebraska scored on just two of its nine possessions against the Illini. Over the last four games, the Huskers have scored on nine of 46 possessions.

"I will continue to evaluate our program through the season and certainly at its conclusion and make additional changes where I believe they will help us win," Rhule said. "The Nebraska fan base has high expectations and I embrace them, and I also know of their passionate support of the young men in our program. I hope they will continue to be there for our players with very important games still ahead. Our entire program is determined to finish this season strong."

Holgorsen was in his second full season as Nebraska’s offensive coordinator. He left his role as an offensive consultant at TCU in November 2024 to join the Cornhuskers in the same capacity, then was promoted to offensive coordinator a week later after Rhule moved Marcus Satterfield to another role.

Nebraska travels to New Jersey next week for a matchup with Rutgers.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/outkick-sports/matt-rhule-says-nebraska-due-change-coaching-staff-shakeup-following-loss-illinois
