posts.title: Tinubu orders implementation of youth confab resolutions
posts.excerpt: President Bola Tinubu has directed the Federal Ministry of Youth Development to translate outcomes of the 2026 National Youth Conference into concrete government action, demanding measurable results a
posts.content:
President Bola Tinubu has directed the Federal Ministry of Youth Development to translate outcomes of the 2026 National Youth Conference into concrete government action, demanding measurable results and clear accountability from officials.

Tinubu gave the directive on Monday at the conference’s closing ceremony at the State House Conference Centre in Abuja.

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, represented him at the event.

The ministry said this in a statement signed by Nwachukwu Christian, Assistant Director, for the Director of Information and Public Relations, on Monday.

Tinubu directed Youth Development Minister Ayodele Olawande to work with relevant ministries, state governments, private sector organisations and development partners to prepare a framework for implementing the conference’s recommendations nationwide.

He said the framework must outline clear priorities, assigned responsibilities, realistic timelines and measurable indicators to ensure effective implementation of the conference recommendations and strengthen accountability across participating government institutions.

Tinubu also insisted that young Nigerians must participate actively in implementing and monitoring the decisions, emphasising that their involvement should extend beyond consultations to meaningful participation in actual government decision-making processes.

“The real test of this conference begins after today. I do not want the recommendations of this conference to become another report gathering dust on government shelves,” he said.

He said Nigerian youths must not merely be invited to discussions but should also occupy meaningful roles in implementing decisions affecting their future, ensuring their voices influence government policies and programmes.

Acknowledging challenges confronting young Nigerians, Tinubu identified unemployment, rising living costs, limited educational opportunities, inadequate access to finance and insecurity as major concerns requiring sustained government attention and practical interventions.

He said his administration understood their concerns, adding that ongoing reforms and investments in education, skills development, innovation and entrepreneurship were designed to expand opportunities for young Nigerians.

“These initiatives such as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, Three Million Technical Talent programme, YouthCred and Nigerian Youth Academy are interventions aimed at empowering young people,” Tinubu said.

He, however, emphasised the need to ensure that skills acquisition translated into employment, innovation attracted investments and young entrepreneurs gained improved access to financing to establish and expand sustainable businesses.

Tinubu commended the ministry’s conference planning committee and participating young Nigerians, saying they had demonstrated their capacity to contribute meaningful ideas and practical solutions towards national development.

Earlier, Olawande said the conference produced an 18-point action agenda covering six priority areas, following nationwide virtual consultations and physical deliberations involving young Nigerians.

Olawande said the conference provided an important platform for strengthening youth participation in national decision-making and ensuring their concerns informed government policies, programmes and development priorities across the country.

“For the first time in the history of this country, the youth can feel the government, see the government, and touch the government,” he said.

He said the recommendations would be pursued through relevant executive, legislative and judicial channels, while the ministry would engage stakeholders to secure the necessary institutional support.

The minister appreciated Tinubu for providing the platform, describing the conference as an opportunity for young Nigerians to move beyond expressing concerns and contribute directly to solutions.

Delivering the keynote address, Finance Minister and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, urged young Nigerians to participate actively in shaping the country’s economic future through constructive engagement and innovation.

Oyedele warned that negative perceptions and distorted narratives about Nigeria could discourage investments, weaken economic confidence and undermine opportunities for employment, entrepreneurship and sustainable national development.

“A factory that is not built means jobs that are not created,” he said, urging participants to embrace constructive engagement, innovation and practical solutions to national challenges.

He emphasised the need to translate economic progress into tangible benefits through increased investments, production, job creation and shared prosperity, ensuring Nigerians experience meaningful improvements in their livelihoods.

The statement said the conference, convened by the Tinubu administration, brought together young Nigerians from across the country and the diaspora to deliberate on national issues and make recommendations.

It said the conference focused on strengthening youth participation in governance, economic development and nation-building, with its outcomes expected to guide policies and programmes affecting young Nigerians nationwide.

“With Tinubu’s directive, attention is now focused on developing an implementation framework to translate the recommendations into concrete government actions, with youths expected to participate in the process,” it said. (NAN)

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinubu-orders-implementation-of-youth-confab-resolutions/

Although the football body gave no reason for the change, the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Art Theatre, in Lagos, remains the venue for the ceremony.

The event will mark the return of the CAF Awards to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition, bringing together leading players, coaches, clubs and other personalities in African football to celebrate their achievements.

A total of 18 categories will be recognised at the ceremony, with the CAF Men’s Player of the Year and CAF Women’s Player of the Year awards among the major honours.

Other categories will recognise outstanding coaches, goalkeepers, emerging talents, clubs and national teams for their performances during the year.

Meanwhile, voting for the 2026 awards is ongoing and will run from November 5 to 20 across the men’s and women’s categories.

posts.title: Iran calls on US to meet its demands to end war
posts.excerpt: "The only solution is to adopt a language of respect, engage in diplomacy, and address Iran's demands and conditions -- which were outlined in the two-day proposal and remain on the table." The post I
posts.content:
Iran on Tuesday urged the United States to meet its demands in a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, after President Donald Trump spoke of “positive momentum” to end their eight-month war.

“The conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iran’s IRNA news agency.

“The only solution is to adopt a language of respect, engage in diplomacy, and address Iran’s demands and conditions — which were outlined in the two-day proposal and remain on the table.”

Tehran has proposed reopening Hormuz, which it has blockaded since the start of the war, within two days in return for Washington meeting a raft of conditions.

These include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Trump, whose Republican party last week lost midterm elections in part due to the war, said on Monday that there was “positive momentum” towards ending the conflict after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House.

In a post on social media, Trump reiterated that the US was “locked and loaded” but said further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo”.

“We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” Trump said.

Diplomatic efforts, led by Qatar and Pakistan, are underway to find a resolution to the war, which broke out in late February when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

On Tuesday, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei urged Washington to “surrender” to the Iranian demands.

“The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler. FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks,” said Rezaei, the head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, in a post on X.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/iran-calls-on-us-to-meet-its-demands-to-end-war/

FIRST ON FOX: A Senate Republican isn’t ready to support Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., to stay as the top Republican as the GOP’s leadership elections fast approach.

Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., in an interview with Fox News Digital, argued that whoever would be the next to lead the Senate GOP and earn his vote in the process needed to lay out a plan on how Republicans would pass key agenda items heading into the lame-duck session of Congress before Senate Democrats take control in January.

Thune plans to run again for another term as the GOP leader, but Scott and a cohort of others want to delay Tuesday morning’s leadership elections to debrief after stunning losses across the board on Election Night. Whether he’ll support Thune for another term depends on his pitch.

SENATE GOP REBELS MOVE TO DELAY LEADERSHIP VOTE, DEMAND RECKONING AFTER MIDTERM DISASTER

"I don't want to put the cart before the horse," Scott said. "I mean, I think the first step is what do we want to accomplish? And then anybody, including John Thune, if they want to be that, the first thing I have to say is, ‘Do they want to do that?’"

"If that's not what they want to accomplish, then why would we elect them? But if that's what they want to accomplish, then tell us why they're the best at it," he continued.

Senate Democrats flipped the upper chamber with wins in red states across the country, clinching a 54-seat majority that could grow even more depending on the outcomes of outstanding races in Mississippi and Alaska.

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

That gives Republicans little time with a trifecta in government to ram through key remaining agenda items before Democrats officially take over.

Thune still plans on running for leader, too, despite the grumbling among Republicans. He said on Monday after lawmakers returned to Washington that he expected a "very engaged conversation" ahead of the leadership election.

"We'll see where it goes from there, but, yeah, I'm running for leader, and I think it's important that we have that discussion, and we will," Thune said.

Scott said that he wants the candidates to be "specific" on how they can balance the budget and pass a slew of legislation, including a stock trading ban for lawmakers, permitting reform, the National Defense Authorization Act and the SAVE America Act.

SCHUMER TANKS POPULAR INSIDER TRADING BAN IN DEM EFFORT TO DERAIL REPUBLICAN'S AGENDA AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

All of that, he said, would be a show that Republicans are listening to voters after getting pummeled in the midterms.

"Back home, they don't care about anything other than do we make their lives better," Scott said.

Thune is so far running unopposed for the top job — Scott reiterated that he had no interest in running again, trying twice for the gig, once against Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., in 2022, and in 2024 when Senate Republicans were searching for McConnell’s replacement.

When asked if he would like to see someone else jump into the fray, Scott said, "Oh, I wouldn't do that to anybody."

Scott and Sens. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., Ted Budd, R-N.C., John Kennedy, R-La., and Mike Lee, R-Utah, all signed onto a letter demanding that Republicans meet before holding their leadership elections and delay voting until they have a full debrief on the midterm losses and what comes next.

They’re joined by Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Dave McCormick, R-Pa., who called for the elections to be delayed but did not sign onto the letter pushing leadership for a meeting.

When asked how long he’d like to see the leadership elections delayed, Scott said, "I think this first step is how long is it gonna take us to agree on what our path should be?"

"If we can get that done quickly, then we can, you know, have elections after that," he said. "And then people that want to run with that agenda in mind, saying they believe in that agenda and will work hard to get that agenda accomplished, then that's how we would decide how we vote."

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/gop-senator-withholds-support-thune-leadership-showdown-looms

posts.title: Trump's Supreme Court majority faces looming threat after Dem Senate takeover: 'Stuck'
posts.excerpt: Justice Samuel Alito confirmed he has no plans to retire, but Democrats' Senate takeover raises stakes for the Supreme Court's conservative majority.
posts.content:
Republicans' loss of the U.S. Senate in the midterm elections could have far-reaching consequences for President Donald Trump's judicial agenda, threatening his ability to reshape the federal courts and raising new questions about the future of the Supreme Court's 6-3 conservative majority.

With Democrats set to take control of the Senate in January, Republicans face a shrinking window to confirm Trump's judicial nominees, while any future Supreme Court vacancy could leave the president dependent on Democratic support to install a replacement.

"Lawless Lawfare" author Alex Swoyer told Fox News Digital, the election results could leave the court's oldest conservative justices with a difficult decision over when to retire.

"It's likely the justices — mainly Justices Thomas and Alito — are stuck on the high court for at least six more years with Democrats taking control," Swoyer said. "Both in their late 70s, I could see why they may want to retire now, midterm."

UNDER-THE-RADAR IMPLICATION OF DEM BLUE WAVE MEANS 'ZERO' CHANCE GOP ACCOMPLISHES CRITICAL GOAL, EXPERTS WARN

Justice Clarence Thomas, 78, and Justice Samuel Alito, 76, are the court's two oldest conservatives, making their retirement decisions particularly consequential as Republicans prepare to lose control of the Senate.

Alito, however, confirmed to Fox News on Thursday that he has no plans to retire and is committed to serving through at least the current Supreme Court term, with the justices expected to wrap up their major decisions in late June or early July.

DEMS SEIZE THE SENATE AS BLUE TIDAL WAVE CRASHES DEEP INTO TRUMP COUNTRY, TOPPLES GOP STRONGHOLDS

"While Senate Republicans were able to confirm Justice Barrett in a one month timeframe in 2020, I don't think this GOP Senate has that same work ethic or ability to push a nominee through ahead of January," Swoyer said.

"I think conservatives would like to see them try; however, a judicial nominations expert told me the Senate work calendar ahead of the holidays would not afford them enough time," she added. "While a five week window seems workable, it doesn't appear like Senate Majority Leader John Thune would have the support to usher such a move at this time."

The stakes extend beyond the Supreme Court. As of Nov. 8, the federal judiciary had 28 vacancies, with 16 nominees awaiting confirmation for current and future vacancies, leaving Republicans with limited time to advance Trump's picks before Democrats take control of the Senate.

Zack Smith, a senior legal fellow for courts and the Constitution at the Heritage Foundation, said Republicans should focus on confirming Trump's remaining lower-court nominees before their majority expires.

CHUCK SCHUMER AFTER SWEEPING DEMOCRATIC MIDTERM VICTORIES: 'I'LL BE RE-ELECTED AS MAJORITY LEADER'

"The top priority for Senate Republicans right now should be confirming the lower federal court judges President Trump has already nominated. It will take all Senators showing up and doing their part. But it is possible," Smith told Fox News Digital.

"As for the Supreme Court, even if a Justice announced his or her retirement today, it could prove difficult to get a replacement confirmed before the end of the current Senate, although Senate Republican leadership has indicated a willingness to try. However, neither Justice Alito nor Justice Thomas has indicated any plan to retire."

The uncertainty surrounding Thomas and Alito echoes the debate over the late liberal Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, who resisted calls to retire before the 2014 midterms despite concerns that Republicans could take control of the Senate and complicate efforts to confirm an Obama-appointed successor.

DEMOCRATIC SENATOR CLAIMS GOP 'STOLE' TWO SCOTUS SEATS IN 2016, 2020, CALLS FOR EXPANSION

Republicans won the Senate in 2014 and, two years later, refused to consider Obama's Supreme Court nominee, Merrick Garland, following Justice Antonin Scalia's death. Trump won the 2016 election and appointed Neil Gorsuch to Scalia's seat in 2017.

Ginsburg remained on the bench until her death in September 2020, just weeks before the presidential election. Trump nominated Amy Coney Barrett to replace her, and the Republican-controlled Senate confirmed Barrett days before Election Day.

Barrett's confirmation gave conservatives a 6-3 majority on the Supreme Court, a balance that has shaped some of the nation's most consequential legal decisions, including the 2022 ruling overturning Roe v. Wade.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trumps-supreme-court-majority-faces-looming-threat-after-dem-senate-takeover-stuck

posts.title: LIZ PEEK: Here’s how Trump can rebound and become one of the presidential greats
posts.excerpt: Trump admitted on "60 Minutes" that his immigration program went too far, signaling a possible pivot toward comprehensive merit-based reform.
posts.content:
Never — ever — count President Trump out.

After begging voters to "pretend" he was on the ballot, Trump got socked with a monster rebuke, one of the worst midterm drubbings ever. But the same man who sprang up shouting "fight!" after surviving an assassin’s bullet, and who came back from political Siberia to win the popular vote in 2024, will not go quietly into the night.

President Trump wants to be one of the greatest presidents of all time, not just to his MAGA base, but to all Americans. How could he do that? By finally fixing our broken immigration system.

LIZ PEEK: THERE MAY BE A SILVER LINING IN TRUMP'S BRUTAL MIDTERM DEFEAT

To be considered great, a president must leave the U.S. permanently changed for the better. FDR created our nation’s safety net to counteract economic downturns, for instance, while Ronald Reagan ended the decades-long Cold War by driving the collapse of the Soviet Union.

Coming up with a balanced approach to immigration, an issue that has bedeviled our country for the past century or longer, is in the same league.

President Trump admitted on "60 Minutes" the other night that his immigration program had gone too far. In particular, he said that while he thought his administration got "high marks" for "getting the bad ones out", he got hurt "because we also took people that had good jobs, that — that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally."

The president is correct. Early in his second term, over half the country signaled their approval of Trump’s successful closure of our wide-open southern border and the deportation of gang members and other illegal criminals. But, as aggressive ICE raids into immigrant communities brought fear and ultimately, violence, attitudes shifted. By the time voters handed Democrats a landslide win last week, Real Clear Polling averages showed Trump’s approval on immigration underwater by more than 10 points.

As I’ve written repeatedly, the vast majority of Americans — Republicans and Democrats — support legal immigration. Most citizens came from somewhere else and applaud those who follow. That said, Americans were appalled to watch thousands of migrants cross the southern border illegally every day while Joe Biden was president; allowing millions to enter the country unvetted, unvaccinated and undocumented was criminal. Trump’s promise to secure the border was a major reason he was elected in 2024, but he took that win as a mandate to eject everyone who was in the U.S. illegally. That was not only impractical, it was a profound misreading of the country’s attitudes towards immigration.

In January of this year, I argued on Fox News that the White House’s overreach on immigration might cost Republicans the House in the midterms, and here we are. Some think that in choosing Stephen Miller, reportedly the author of Trump’s aggressive deportation program, as his chief of staff, the president is indicating that the harsh approach will continue. That could be wrong.

HOUSE GOP ERUPTS AT STEPHEN MILLER AS TRUMP ELEVATES HIM AFTER MIDTERM MASSACRE: 'MEGALOMANIAC'

Just as it took ardent anti-communist President Richard Nixon to open up China, it might take ardent anti-immigrant Stephen Miller to help President Trump fix what is broken. If the administration presented a sensible and fair program to the public, Democrats would dismiss it at their peril.

The challenge is enormous. But there is a way:

1) First, the GOP and the White House must present a program that will continue to attract the best and the brightest to our country while not putting our own citizens at a disadvantage. Instead of allowing entry based on family sponsorship (chain migration) or through the unpopular diversity visa program, which the White House has attempted to eliminate, establish a point-based merit system that prioritizes skills and capability, such as that used in Canada. In 2019, Trump proposed such an approach; it is the right way to go.

2) Second, the president must provide a path to legal status for those living in the country illegally but who have built lives here and committed no crime beyond their initial entry. Grant those people an opportunity to become registered legal aliens. Determine that they will never be citizens, but they will emerge from the shadows, work and pay taxes legally. This is not "amnesty", but the attainment of legal status which should win the support of Democrats and the country.

3) Third, since about half of undocumented people living in the U.S. have not entered illegally but instead overstayed their visas, securing the border, though essential, is not good enough. Additionally, Congress must require that all employers use E-Verify, a free government-provided service, to screen out workers in the U.S. illegally. Migrants mostly come for economic opportunity; if they cannot work, they will go home. Meanwhile, if we need more seasonal workers, increase the number of visas.

4) Fourth, we must eliminate the benefits and enticements, from free healthcare to birthright citizenship, that encourage illegal immigration. If someone attains legal status, they have a right to put their kids in school and apply for healthcare insurance; if they forego that opportunity, they should be denied such taxpayer-provided services. The Trump White House attempted to end birthright citizenship by executive order, but the Supreme Court narrowly declared the rule illegal. Congress needs to change the law.

HOUSE REPUBLICANS MOVE TO MAKE TRUMP'S BORDER POLICIES PERMANENT

5) Finally, we must stop including illegals in the census. Including undocumented people rewards politicians like those governing California and New York, who purposefully attract illegals with benefits, since it leads to more federal aid and more House seats and Electoral College votes for their states.

No immigration program can gain traction unless it is backed by a solid commitment to border security. Trump has shown that preventing illegal immigration does not require a wall; it requires a will. Reforming immigration will require much more: dedication to our country’s security and sovereignty.

President Trump should roll out a newer, better plan, and challenge the Democrats to stop it. It would be the ultimate deal.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/liz-peek-how-trump-rebound-become-one-presidential-greats

posts.title: Nigeria’s active telecom lines hit 200m as 5G share crosses 5%
posts.excerpt: Nigeria’s active telecommunications subscriptions rose to 200.3 million in September, crossing the 200 million mark for the first time since the NIN-SIM enforcement exercise led to mass line disconnec
posts.content:
…As Internet data usage falls to 1.73 terabytes in September

By Juliet Umeh

Nigeria’s active telecommunications subscriptions rose to 200.3 million in September, crossing the 200 million mark for the first time since the NIN-SIM enforcement exercise led to mass line disconnections in 2024.

Latest data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, showed that active lines increased by about 2.9 million, from 197.4 million in August.

The September figure of 200,337,097 subscriptions was up from 197,416,694 in August. Teledensity rose to 92.41 per cent from 91.07 per cent.

The NCC defines teledensity as the number of active telephone connections per 100 inhabitants. It measures subscriptions rather than unique users, as one person may have more than one line.

The data showed that 4G remained the largest share of mobile connections at 54.37 per cent in September. 2G accounted for 36.42 per cent, while 3G made up 4.16 per cent. 5G’s share increased to 5.05 per cent from 4.92 per cent in August.

Internet subscriptions also grew, rising to 160.9 million from 158.5 million in August.

Broadband subscriptions increased to 128 million in September from 126.2 million the previous month, while broadband penetration rose to 59.05 per cent from 58.22 per cent.

However, total internet data usage declined to 1.73 million terabytes in September from 1.76 million terabytes in August.

Mobile number porting increased during the month, with 1,603 subscribers switching networks, compared with 1,111 in August. MTN recorded 854 incoming ports, Airtel 580, Globacom 165 and Vitel four. T2 recorded none.

The figures also showed that the telecommunications industry’s contribution to gross domestic product, GDP, rose to 9.72 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 9.19 per cent in the first quarter.

Fixed broadband infrastructure expanded, with Fibre to the X (FTTX) subscriptions rising to 401,666 in the third quarter from 319,735 in the second quarter. The NCC’s FTTX category covers fibre connections to homes, offices, streets, hubs and other locations, including subscriptions from internet service providers and fixed or private network operators.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nigerias-active-telecom-lines-hit-200m-as-5g-share-crosses-5/

posts.title: Abacha wanted to liquidate me - Obasanjo narrates how he was arrested
posts.excerpt: Former president Olusegun Obasanjo has disclosed that the ex-military Head of State, Sani Abacha wanted him liquidated because he wanted to have his way. Obasanjo disclosed this in a video published b
posts.content:
Former president Olusegun Obasanjo has disclosed that the ex-military Head of State, Sani Abacha wanted him liquidated because he wanted to have his way.

Obasanjo disclosed this in a video published by BBC, where he narrated how he was arrested by Abacha.

The former president also disclosed going into farming after retiring from the Nigerian Army.

According to Obasanjo: "When I was leaving the government as the military Head of State I was leaving too early, I didn't join the army to retire at the age of 42.

"At the age of 42 I have become a four-star general, there was nothing I could do in the army, I had become the military Head of State, the highest political office.

"So what can I do, I decided I will go into farming, it really was going well and it went well until I was arrested.

"Abacha had decided that I must be liquidated, otherwise he won't be able to have his way, I didn't know that. I travelled and was coming back, the American ambassador in Nigeria called me and said his country has offered me political asylum because they know that I will be arrested if I return home.

"I haven't done anything, what would they arrest me for? Why would I want a political asylum? When I arrived, they seized my passport and at the gate of my farm, my security said security had surrounded the farm.

"And not up to 15 minutes this man came in with mufti, not uniform, and said I have been invited by the AIG to come and help. I said if the AIG wants me to help, he will not invite me, he will come here.

"It was my own car I drove to the police station and the AIG said, 'I have been instructed to arrest you.' I didn't know that it was Abacha's decision that some of us must not be kept free otherwise."

Abacha wanted to liquidate me - Obasanjo narrates how he was arrested

posts.title: Atiku urges World Bank to reject Tinubu’s $500m loan request
posts.excerpt: Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has condemned the Tinubu administration’s pursuit of a proposed $500 million loan from the Wor
posts.content:
Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has condemned the Tinubu administration’s pursuit of a proposed $500 million loan from the World Bank.

Atiku said President Bola Tinubu cannot borrow in the final days of his tenure and leave the incoming administration and Nigerians to repay the debt.

He argued that no outgoing president has the right to burden his successor with fresh debt days before handing over power.

Atiku made this known in a viral statement on Tuesday.

His reaction comes amid the Federal Government’s reported plan to secure a $500 million loan from the international lender.

Atiku accused Tinubu of mortgaging Nigeria’s future, insisting that the incumbent administration has no business committing the country to additional debt beyond 2027.

He urged the World Bank not to approve the Tinubu administration’s fresh $500 million loan request.

“Taking loans as if you were a drunken sailor is a road to economic bondage, a second slavery. If this government is determined to mortgage Nigeria’s future and place our country at the mercy of creditors, we will not accept it.

“According to the report, the proposed $500 million facility is scheduled for consideration on May 25, 2027, just four days before the next presidential inauguration. President Tinubu has no business committing the country to fresh debt as he prepares to leave office.

“We call on the World Bank not to approve this proposed loan on the timetable now being contemplated,” he stated.

DAILY POST reports that Nigeria’s total public debt stood at about N166.79 trillion, according to June 2026 data from the Debt Management Office, DMO.

Financial experts, including Professor Godwin Oyedokun, have called for caution over the country’s rising debt profile.

However, the Tinubu administration has maintained that Nigeria’s debt level is sustainable.

posts.title: HUGH HEWITT: Three big legal fights are looming, and Trump needs answers before January
posts.excerpt: Stephen Miller and the DOJ brace for an epic clash with Congress over executive privilege as Democrats prepare sweeping oversight inquiries.
posts.content:
United States Assistant Attorney General T. Elliott Gaiser is going to be a very busy man in 2027. Before the new Congress arrives in January, President Donald Trump should require Gaiser and his team to provide detailed answers to a few very important questions of law.

On Friday, November 6, at 3:29 p.m., Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., the incoming chairman of the House Oversight Committee, posted a threat barely disguised as advice directed at new White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller: "Steven Miller should lawyer up."

At 6:10 p.m. that same day, United States Attorney General Todd Blanche posted a response: "The Chief of Staff already has a lawyer. The Attorney General of the United States and the Department of Justice."

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

Welcome to the next two years. There is an epic clash coming between the powers of Congress under Article I of the Constitution and the powers of President Trump under Article II. The Supreme Court will referee the clash, but it will start soon, and one of the key participants will be Mr. Gaiser, the assistant attorney general for the Office of Legal Counsel (OLC).

OLC is the division of the U.S. Department of Justice that serves as the principal legal adviser to the president and the executive branch. AAG Gaiser was confirmed by the Senate on July 30, 2025. By all accounts, he is a brilliant lawyer. Gaiser helms an office of about two dozen lawyers who are collectively widely regarded as among the top legal minds in the country. The office is a mix of career and political appointees, but all are serious legal scholars.

OLC tackles questions President Trump or Attorney General Blanche require it to answer, and it can also supply answers to questions from Cabinet officers and military leaders, as time allows and the president and the AG permit. The Supreme Court does not issue advisory opinions on possible controversies that have not reached it at all or that are premature (cases that are not yet "ripe" for decision), but OLC does.

One recent example: On August 10 of this year, OLC opined that "executive privilege can apply to presidential communications with private advisers so long as the communications (1) relate to official presidential decision making, (2) involve or reflect communications with the President or his direct advisers, and (3) are confidential."

AG BLANCHE CLASHES WITH ANCHOR ASKING WHETHER IT'S HIS 'JOB' TO DEFEND THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

There is going to be a raft of additional executive privilege questions incoming, as the new Democratic majorities cannot immediately compel testimony about matters over which President Trump has asserted "executive privilege." But there are other pressing questions about "court packing," statehood for the District of Columbia and the constitutionality of the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact that can be asked and answered by OLC before the executive privilege debates begin.

Both Republican and Democratic presidents have asserted their privilege in situations that have angered Congress. Sometimes the Supreme Court or the United States Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit has sided with the president, and sometimes it has sided with Congress.

TRUMP'S MOVE FROM WILES TO MILLER SIGNALS MAJOR TACTICAL SHIFT FOR GOVERNING WITHOUT CONGRESS

President Biden, facing a demand for the audio recordings of his and his ghostwriter’s interviews with Special Counsel Robert Hur, sought and received an OLC opinion on May 15, 2024, on whether he could assert executive privilege over those recordings. OLC opined that Biden could. Lawsuits were filed challenging that opinion and President Biden’s decision not to release the recordings, and the Trump administration decided to release the recordings.

President Clinton asserted a novel Secret Service protective-function privilege as well as a White House attorney-client privilege, both of which were rejected in whole or in material part by the United States Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit. President Obama made claims of executive privilege over materials in the "Fast and Furious" investigation, and when litigation followed, a settlement was reached before a court decision was made.

MORNING GLORY: DSA DEMOCRATS' RADICAL PLAN TO RESHAPE AMERICA STARTS WITH THE SUPREME COURT

Everyone should expect President Trump to follow the examples of Presidents Clinton, Obama and Biden and play full-court defense against what have already been announced as sweeping inquiries into executive branch conduct by such members as Garcia and Congressman Jamie Raskin, D-Md., who will chair the House Judiciary Committee. Both committees have subpoena powers.

President Trump may require a legal opinion from the attorney general under 28 U.S.C. § 511, and when such a demand is made, the AG turns to OLC. Before OLC is deluged with requests from President Trump and A.G. Blanche in 2027 on the scope of executive privilege across the executive branch, the president could secure some important OLC opinions between now and January 3, when the new Congress is sworn in.

Three such questions come to mind in light of last week's sweeping Democratic wins across the country and the often very extreme positions put forward by Democrats campaigning for House or Senate seats.

JONATHAN TURLEY: MIDTERMS EMPOWER DEMOCRATS TO TARGET THE ELECTORAL COLLEGE

First and perhaps most important: Is it in fact constitutional for Congress to expand the Supreme Court to more than the current nine justices? There is a strong argument that, in the wake of the ratification of the Fourteenth Amendment and the almost immediate passage of the Judiciary Act of 1869 the following April, "court packing" is simply unconstitutional.

When Congress set the number of justices at nine in 1869 after expanding it to 10 justices in 1863, and then temporarily reducing it to seven in 1866, Congress and President Grant did so in the shadow of the new Fourteenth Amendment’s guarantee of "due process of law." OLC ought to be tasked by President Trump with weighing in on whether "court packing" violates that guarantee of due process and/or whether packing the court is an unconstitutional attempt to seize control of judicial review, which has always been implicitly vested in the federal courts by the Constitution but which was only made explicit by the Supreme Court in 1803 in the case of Marbury v. Madison, almost a decade and a half after the Constitution was ratified.

Democrats also want to make the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico states. The Twenty-Third Amendment to the U.S. Constitution deals with the District of Columbia, and OLC ought to opine on whether statehood for D.C. would require another amendment.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

George Washington University law professor and Fox News contributor Jonathan Turley has already raised another important issue: "With one-party control in states like Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin, the [Democratic] party is ready to get states to join the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact," Turley wrote recently in an op-ed for Fox News.

"Under the Compact," Turley explained, "states agree to give all their electoral votes to the presidential ticket that wins the national popular vote."

"The constitutionality of the Compact has obviously not been tested," Turley wrote.

As with "court packing," OLC has never weighed in on either statehood for D.C. or the Compact. AAG Gaiser and his team of big legal brains can study these issues and provide the first comprehensive analysis for the executive branch, including who would have "standing" to bring constitutional challenges to all three schemes and when such challenges would be ripe. Of course, OLC opinions would not bind federal courts, but they would be instrumental in shaping the debate before the courts.

posts.title: New Israel parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot seeks government
posts.excerpt: Israel's new parliament will be sworn in Tuesday, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu set to lose his majority even as rival Gadi Eisenkot still works to form a new government. The post New Israel
posts.content:
Israel’s new parliament will be sworn in Tuesday, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu set to lose his majority even as rival Gadi Eisenkot still works to form a new government.

President Isaac Herzog will deliver a speech at 4:00 pm (1400 GMT) for the swearing-in of the 120-seat parliament, in which neither Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc nor Eisenkot’s opposition will hold a majority.

The opposition hopes to use its newfound legislative power to move quickly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.

Herzog on Sunday gave Eisenkot the initial mandate to form a government, starting the clock for him to cobble together a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.

Ahead of the parliament opening, Eisenkot’s party announced progress in naming people to seek key positions.

The opposition will put forward Matan Kahana — like Eisenkot a former senior military figure — as speaker of the parliament, Eisenkot’s Yashar party said.

Avigdor Lieberman, a right-wing opposition leader who has played a key role in deciding who can enter the government, will be nominated as chair of the foreign affairs and defence committee.

The opposition’s choice for speaker would need to secure a larger number of votes than anyone backed by Netanyahu’s bloc, which has been trying to push back a vote on the speaker.

The newly formed government would need 61 votes to be approved to take office.

Eisenkot could secure the threshold with support from Arab-Israeli lawmakers, who secured a record number of seats on the back of anger in the minority community over Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

But Lieberman had been clear he would not allow Eisenkot to rely on Arab-Israelis to come to power. He has instead proposed an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, despite his years of bitter denunciations of the community for its singular priority on maintaining an exemption from mandatory military service.

Eisenkot’s core opposition bloc has fewer seats than Netanyahu at 48, but would achieve a majority if the 19 Arab-Israeli lawmakers either enter the government or, more likely, vote for it without joining.

The two ultra-Orthodox parties, with 13 seats, could also crown Eisenkot if they ditch their long alliance with Netanyahu, who backed the exemption from military service without enshrining it fully into law.

An alliance with either group would likely be fragile. Arab-Israelis are likely to object if Eisenkot carries out another major offensive in Gaza.

Eisenkot has largely backed Netanyahu’s war decisions, although he has vowed to crack down on extremist settlers in the West Bank who have been attacking and stealing from Palestinians with virtual impunity.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/new-israel-parliament-to-be-sworn-in-as-eisenkot-seeks-government/

posts.title: Obasanjo betrayed Babangida over one-term power-sharing agreement — Kalu alleges
posts.excerpt: "Well, I cannot be certain about the vice presidency, but I can tell you, yes, this was our discussion in Ota. That he would leave, he would leave for four years and give back to the North," he disclo
posts.content:
***Discloses why his relationship with Obasanjo collapsed, promises to groom younger Nigerians for leadership

***Recalls financing PDP’s formation, how party members turned against him

By Henry Umoru, Abuja

Chairman Senate Committee on South East Development Commission (SEDC), Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, APC, Abia North, has revealed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo betrayed his agreement to serve one term and to subsequently hand over to the North.

Kalu has, however, revealed an account of an alleged political understanding involving Obasanjo and former military president Ibrahim Babangida ahead of the 2003 presidential election.

The former Abia State governor, who spoke on why his once cordial relationship with Obasanjo eventually collapsed, disclosed that their disagreement was rooted partly in what he described as an agreement that Obasanjo would serve only one four-year term before power returned to the North.

According to him, the understanding was reached during a meeting involving himself, Obasanjo and Babangida at Obasanjo’s residence in Ota, Ogun State, stressing that the arrangement was intended to accommodate the political circumstances surrounding the emergence of Obasanjo in 1999, following the annulment of the June 12, 1993, presidential election.

The former Senate Whip spoke on Monday night during an exclusive appearance on Arise PrimeTime, the flagship evening current affairs programme of Arise News Television, anchored by Charles Aniagolu.

Kalu maintained that the agreement was for Obasanjo to complete one term and hand over to another political leader from the North, allowing the country’s power rotation arrangement to continue.

When asked specifically to speak about reports that Babangida was expected to succeed Obasanjo in 2003, with Kalu potentially becoming his running mate, the senator said he could not confirm the vice-presidential arrangement but stood by the agreement concerning Obasanjo’s tenure.

“Well, I cannot be certain about the vice presidency, but I can tell you, yes, this was our discussion in Ota. That he would leave, he would leave for four years and give back to the North,” he disclosed.

Providing further details, Kalu identified an individual he described as Obasanjo’s aide from Benue State, named Adobeye in the interview, as being present during the discussion.

He said, “What we discussed and agreed there were people there, there were people there, like His Boy, Obasanjo’s Boy, Adobeye from Benue State; he was sitting down there where we sat, me, Ibrahim Babangida and President Obasanjo. Where we agreed, we agreed.”

Kalu said the disagreement over the alleged arrangement was among the issues that eventually damaged his relationship with the former president, just as he accused Obasanjo of using state institutions, particularly the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), to pursue political opponents and remove elected governors through what he considered unconstitutional means.

The senator maintained that his opposition to Obasanjo was not driven by personal ambition but by his disagreement with what he considered a departure from their political understanding and constitutional principles.

‘I financed PDP’s formation; then party members turned against me’

Recalls financing PDP’s formation, says party members turned against him

Kalu, who also provided an account of his financial contributions to the formation of the PDP during the transition from military to civilian rule, dismissed suggestions that he was the only wealthy individual involved in the party’s formation, acknowledging the contributions of prominent figures, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Yomi Edu and General Theophilus Danjuma.

The former Abia State governor, who maintained that he played a significant role in financing the early meetings and logistical arrangements that facilitated the formation of the party, said, “I was the one funding the meetings, aircraft, paying honourariums to people that came for cooking food and all the rest of them. That is the truth.”

He explained that his motivation was to ensure the emergence of a formidable political platform capable of ending military rule.

“So for me, it was just a joyful thing to make sure that we had a strong party to drive away the military,” he added.

Kalu, however, expressed disappointment with how some of the party’s members treated him after he had invested considerable resources in its formation.

“I became a fool before the PDP because after bringing all the money, they turned against me,” he said.

He further claimed that he had supported Obasanjo financially after the former president’s release from prison, including funding his movements and providing aircraft for his political engagements.

‘My relationship with IBB, international figures’

The Abia North Senator also discussed his longstanding relationships with influential political figures within and outside Nigeria, attributing much of his approach to relationship-building to lessons from three individuals.

He identified former military President Ibrahim Babangida, the late Professor Jibril Aminu and businessman Gilbert Chagoury as the people who taught him the importance of maintaining relationships across different social and political backgrounds.

“Three men taught me how to cultivate this. One, still alive, is his present, Ibrahim Babangida. Two, was Professor Jubril Aminu. And the third one was Mr Gilbert Chagoury,” he said.

According to Kalu, their advice was that maintaining relationships required humility, accessibility and the willingness to interact with people regardless of their social standing.

“They told me that it’s always good to keep people and eat with people. And I maintained that, and this is what I maintained in my life,” he said.

He explained that he deliberately maintains relationships with people from different social classes and makes efforts to return missed calls and respond to messages.

“I welcome people of no status. I welcome people with status. I welcome people of the same below and above. I keep relationships,” he stated.

Kalu also acknowledged that his relationship with Babangida opened doors for him to meet influential international figures, which he subsequently leveraged to expand his business and diplomatic networks.

He recalled his friendship with the late South African President Nelson Mandela, who, according to him, introduced him to other influential South African leaders, including Thabo Mbeki and Jacob Zuma.

He also confirmed that he had maintained relationships with influential individuals in the United States, including people associated with the Democratic Party, while clarifying that his relationships with international intelligence officials did not make him an agent of any foreign government.

Asked about allegations linking him to the CIA and Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency, Kalu categorically denied working for either organisation.

“I’m not an agent,” he said.

Kalu also addressed his previous recognition by Forbes magazine as one of Africa’s wealthiest individuals, explaining why he had not featured prominently in more recent wealth rankings.

He attributed the difference to his current involvement in politics, arguing that his business profile would become more prominent if he returned fully to the private sector.

“Any day I drop out of politics, I’m sure Forbes, if I have anything to rank, they’ll rank me,” he said.

He further made a notable claim about his previous recognition by the international financial publication.

“Because in the history of Forbes, I’m the only person active in politics ever they have ranked,” he declared.

‘How Dangote reacted when I announced my intention to become governor’

Recounting his transition from business into politics, Kalu revealed that some of his closest associates initially considered his decision to contest the governorship of Abia State an unwise move.

Kalu, who specifically recalled the reaction of Africa’s foremost industrialist, Aliko Dangote, when he informed him of his intention to enter politics, said the conversation took place at his residence in the presence of other associates, including Chat Sahi and the late Mohammed Wazgiri.

He said Dangote was surprised by his decision, considering the business empire he had built and the risks associated with entering Nigerian politics.

“The day I told him I was going to run for governor, he felt I was a fool,” Kalu recalled.

Recounting Dangote’s reaction, he said:

“He said you must be very strong to think about that. He said, “You will not do that.”

Kalu explained that his decision was influenced partly by the encouragement of politicians who approached him to participate in the formation of a political movement capable of ending military rule.

He recalled that he became actively involved in financing meetings, providing aircraft and supporting the logistics required to establish the PDP ahead of the return to democratic governance in 1999.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/obasanjo-betrayed-babangida-over-one-term-power-sharing-agreement-kalu-alleges/

posts.title: Texas governor-elect's plan to freeze electricity prices raises questions over legal authority
posts.excerpt: Texas Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa plans to freeze electricity rates on Day One, but experts warn the move could trigger energy shortages.
posts.content:
On her first day in office, Texas Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa plans to freeze residential electricity rates in response to what she described as an affordability crisis.

"On Day One as governor, I’ll freeze residential electricity rates and make corporations finally pay their fair share," Hinojosa said in an interview with a local energy data group. She reiterated the plan in an interview with the Texas Tribune, stating, "Within an hour of taking the oath of office, I will declare a high-cost emergency in the state of Texas and issue an emergency executive order to … freeze electricity rates."

The plan is raising concerns that such a freeze will clash with Texas’ uniquely competitive energy sector, which relies heavily on free-market choice, and that it could inadvertently create energy shortages as suppliers are prevented from adjusting their prices.

DEMOCRAT GINA HINOJOSA STUNS ABBOTT, MAKES HISTORY AS FIRST LATINA TEXAS GOVERNOR

That’s the concern of Nick Loris, the president of C3 Solutions, a conservative coalition for climate solutions that focuses on energy, environment and agriculture policy.

He expects the emergency declaration will face legal challenges almost immediately from energy providers. In particular, he cast doubt on the scope of the emergency declaration.

"The Texas Disaster Act lets the governor declare disasters and suspend the regulatory laws and statutes that are in existence. But I think there is a high degree of skepticism, both from courts but also from state policymakers, that this warrants such a claim — and that it is such a disaster," Loris told Fox News Digital.

"I would imagine if there were legal challenges, it would come from those affected parties," he added.

Loris explained that Texas has fostered one of the most competitive energy environments in the country.

In 1999, the state passed Senate Bill 7 — a piece of legislation that opened most of the state to retail choice, allowing customer to pick their preferred retail electric providers (REPs), beginning in 2002.

"The legislature finds that the production and sale of electricity is not a monopoly warranting regulation of rates, operations, and services and that the public interest in competitive electric markets requires that, except for transmission and distribution services and for the recovery of stranded costs, electric services and their prices should be determined by customer choices and the normal forces of competition," the Texas Legislature wrote in the law.

TEXAS GOV. GREG ABBOTT EFFECTIVELY PAUSES NEW DATA CENTER PROJECTS PENDING STATEWIDE GRID AUDIT

As a result of the law, Texas largely operates its own independent energy grid and runs an energy-only wholesale market in which generators are paid primarily for the electricity they produce rather than for standing capacity.

Texas has over 100 REPs that energy consumers can pick from, each competing for consumers' business.

To Loris, the range of choices provides a remarkable amount of flexibility for consumers.

"It's like shopping at a grocery store for cereal for your retail electricity. There's so much choice that you can enter into. Short-term contracts, long-term contracts, use different fuel sources," Loris said.

However, he warned that a utilitiesrfreeze undermines that competitive environment, causing providers to shoulder the burden of fluctuating supply.

"If the electricity suppliers are not covering the costs that they incur, that's going to leave them worse off and make it more vulnerable for them to adequately provide that power," Loris said.

AI'S MASSIVE APPETITE FOR POWER, WATER IGNITES FIGHT IN HIGH-STAKES TEXAS SENATE RACE

"Price signals really kind of act like a traffic light. They tell people when to speed up, when to slow down, or when to come to a full stop," he added.

Having won her Nov. 3 gubernatorial race, Hinojosa will be sworn in on Jan. 19, 2027.

Her office did not immediately respond to requests for comment on what her response would be if the rate freezes resulted in an energy shortage.
