posts.title: As NLC Squares Up with TUC Over N70,000 Transport Allowance…
posts.excerpt: For decades, the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress have presented themselves as two pillars of one house – Organised Labour. Most times when they speak they do
posts.content:
For decades, the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress have presented themselves as two pillars of one house – Organised Labour. Most times when they speak they do so with one voice and governments are compelled to listen. But when they disagree, it’s government that gains to the disadvantage of workers, writes Onyebuchi Ezigbo.

Recently the two labour centres – the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC) disagreed over a seemingly simple issue which is should workers take N70,000 as a transport allowance for six months, or should they insist that the money be built permanently into their salaries?

What began as a difference in negotiating tactics has grown into a public rift, with statements, counter-statements and affiliate unions taking sides. Now, veteran labour leaders have stepped in, warning that the quarrel, if left unchecked, could undermine the unity, solidarity and strength that took decades to build.

Observers of the unfolding crisis of confidence within organised Labour family of the opinion that it will augur well for the workers whose interest are better protected when both labour centres join hands to confront the government and other employers of labour.

The bone of contention in this current misunderstanding was an agreement reached between the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment and NLC on October 27, 2026 with major focus on commencement date for negotiation of a new minimum wage, issues on public service welfare and adjustment of tax relief for workers.

The agreement also addressed the Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU) issues on CONHESS Palliative to cushion the effect of challenges faced by the workers, demands by Joint National Public Service Negotiation Council (JNPSNC) and reduction in petroleum pump price.

Other issues include, demand for payment of hazard allowance for Agricultural workers. According to JNPSNC, the agreement was the product of more than six hours of tough negotiation presided over by the Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Mohamed Maigari Dingyadi.

The labour team was led by NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, with participation from JNPSNC and the Joint Health Sector Union (JOHESU). A major highlight of the deal was the N70,000 transport allowance to be paid for the next six months to public servants starting November 2026, to subsidize unbearable transport costs.

It also cemented implementation of the long-overdue 40 per cent peculiar allowance reflecting the N70,000 minimum wage, which ought to have started since July 2024. The allowance will be domesticated at sub-national levels from November 2026, while arrears from May 1, 2026 will be paid in three tranches.

Other gains listed in the JNPSNC circular signed by National Secretary, Comrade Gbenga Olowoyo, include: a tripartite negotiation committee comprising government, labour and NECA to commence immediately; resolution of the 13-year-old CONHESS adjustment demand, with the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) given three weeks to conclude work; payment of 19-month arrears of health workers’ allowances in three installments from December 2026; issuance of a circular for hazard allowance to agricultural professional officers within three weeks; and a one-month window to reconvene to evaluate implementation.

On its part, the Federal Government has said it is “fully committed to ensuring that the ongoing collective bargaining agreement negotiation is concluded as soon as possible and that its implementation can bring the expected relief and improved condition of service to your members.” It gave the undertaking through the Minister of Labour Alhaji Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi at the opening of the National Executive Council meeting of the Medical and Health Workers Union in Abuja.

For NLC, the N70,000 is not the end of the struggle. NLC President, Joe Ajaero said it is a starting point, a foothold that cannot be taken away. “Whatever we got for you, nobody can take away from us. The N70,000 you are hearing is just an intervention. Like I said somewhere, when you give glucose to someone and it is inside his mouth, if you want to bring it out and you put your hand there. You know what will happen. So now that we have N70,000 on top of N70,000 you know where we are going to start from,” he told the 52nd National Executive Council meeting of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN) in Abuja. He said the agreement was negotiated with the mandate from affiliate unions, including handling of JOHESU and JNPSNC issues, and represents a landmark achievement. Already, the move has the backing of the leadership of JNPSNC which dismissed the notion that NLC is a union of junior workers, saying all its affiliates have members across Ministries, Departments and Agencies up to Directorate level.

JNPSNC scribe argued that TUC, which was not part of the negotiation, has no basis to reject what it did not negotiate, though he added it would be commendable if TUC could secure a higher amount.

“Rejection of any item by any trade union is inconsequential to implementation because wider spectrum of workers has applauded decision as right step in right direction,” the circular said.

On the other hand, TUC sees the same N70,000 through a different lens – basing it’s argument on previous lessons where government failed to religiously implement the wage award. In its communique after an emergency National Administrative Council (NAC) meeting on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, signed by Secretary General, Dr. Nuhu Toro, TUC reaffirmed its demand for a sustainable salary increase, not another wage award. Its argument is rooted in experience: the wage award palliative agreed on October 2, 2023 was to run until the new minimum wage was signed into law on July 29, 2024. Workers, TUC said, received an average of only three months out of the ten months agreed upon.

“A sustainable salary increase offers a more meaningful intervention to improve workers’ purchasing power and living standards,” the communique said, stressing that the minimum wage is a statutory floor and not a ceiling on workers’ earnings.

Secretary General of TUC, Dr. Nuhu Toro who spoke at the recent MHWUN NEC meeting, put it more plainly: “The NLC is saying pay N70,000 transport allowance. The TUC was not there when that was negotiated, and the TUC said, we think you should negotiate for the N70,000 to be component of the salary. For instance, if N70,000 is added to your housing allowance, it becomes part of your salary and will not be taken off after six months. So the TUC said no, let’s make it holistic so that they won’t take it off after six months. So that is the argument. It’s not any issue.”

TUC also acknowledged the positions of its public-sector affiliates — SSAUTHRIA, NUAHP and SSASCGOC — noting they are consistent with its earlier position.

It stressed that workers’ welfare cannot be advanced by disregarding the collective bargaining rights of affected unions. The Labour Centre further reaffirmed its mandate under ILO Conventions 87 and 98 to represent, defend and negotiate for its members, and resolved to pursue constructive, result-oriented engagement with government to implement the resolutions of its October 8 meeting, including the JOHESU agreement.

At it’s NAC meeting, TUC tasked it’s leaders to refocus efforts on securing a salary increase while refraining from public exchanges on the matter.

Intervention by Veteran labour leaders

Amid verbal exchanges by leaders of the two Labour Centres, concerned stakeholders especially former union leaders have stepped in to help broker peace and resolve this understanding between NLC and TUC.

Speaking at the NEC meeting of the Medical and Health Workers Union in Abuja, immediate past NLC President and former President of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC), Comrade Ayuba Wabba, said veteran leaders, including pioneer labour leader, Hassan Sumonu and other past presidents of NLC and TUC are intervening in the dispute

He said they have summoned both centres for dialogue and asked them to suspend further altercation in the media.

“The leaders have asked them to suspend any further altercation, we do not want to see any further statement. We the veterans have intervened”.

Wabba described most of the things trending in the media space about the disagreement as hype imported by third parties to undermine workers’ unity. He warned that the NLC was built by sweat and blood and must not be brought down.

He said: There are more important issues like inequality than those issues that are being imported by third parties to try to undermine workers’ unity, workers’ strength and workers’ solidarity. Anybody that wants to bring it down certainly we will not take it lightly. Unity is strength and all of us must advocate for unity of the working class.” Wabba explained that though the veterans have started preliminary engagement to settle the misunderstanding among the labour centres, there will be more meetings and consultations going forward to try to bring both parties to amicably work together to protect workers welfare.

In substance, both centres want the same thing: more money in workers’ pockets that government cannot easily withdraw. Whereas NLC argues that securing the allowance first creates a new baseline for the next round of negotiation, TUC’s position is that without embedding it in salary structure, the allowance will expire after six months, just as the 2023 wage award did.

Both arguments have merit. Both carry risk. Accepting a temporary allowance could become a substitute for real salary review. However rejecting it outright could leave workers with nothing while negotiations drag.

Considering the current mood of the workers, any suggestion that they should surrender the N70,000 transport allowance for another round of negotiation may not be an acceptable option. It may be that both NLC and TUC will have to present a common front to pressurise government to retain the N70,000 beyond the six months timeline and convert it into a permanent salary component in the ongoing Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiation that government says its committed to concluding soon. If they fail, the rift could deepen, with affiliates lining up behind one centre or the other, and government exploiting the division. For now, both sides have at least agreed to one thing: stop fighting in public. Whether that truce holds and whether it produces a better deal for workers will be the real test of veteran wisdom.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/as-nlc-squares-up-with-tuc-over-n70000-transport-allowance/

posts.title: Civil Society Decries Osun NLC Strike
posts.excerpt: Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo The Executive Director World Institute for Peace, Lamina Omotoyosi, yesterday warned the Osun State Government and the various labour unions on the three-day warning strike em
posts.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Executive Director World Institute for Peace, Lamina Omotoyosi, yesterday warned the Osun State Government and the various labour unions on the three-day warning strike embarked upon by the Osun State chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) over the lingering local government crisis in the state.

The executive director noted that as an organisation committed to promoting peace, stability, development and social justice, “he considered this warning strike needless, barbaric, deceptive and a deliberate attempt to ground the state’s economy and potentially trigger civil unrest.”

According to him, “We have no reservation in concluding that the strike is being embarked upon in bad faith and is politically motivated, with the intention of blackmailing the judiciary and creating a possible atmosphere of anarchy in the polity. “

Omotoyosi, who stated this at a press conference addressed in Osogbo yesterday, contended that: “This position is informed by the trajectory of the local government crisis in Osun State and the plethora of litigations surrounding local government administration in the state.

“It is our expectation that the labour movement should serve as a fountain of knowledge, the voice of workers, and by extension, the voice of the downtrodden.

“Labour unions are expected to be populated by people with sound knowledge of the law and judicial processes, and this should reflect in their approach to sensitive issues such as the ongoing local government crisis in Osun State, particularly when the matter is still pending before several courts of competent jurisdiction.

“Unfortunately, the reverse appears to be the case in Osun State. As things stand today, the labour movement in the state appears to have chosen political patronage over honesty, integrity and the general interest of workers.

“As an organisation, we are equally disturbed and seriously concerned about the protracted nature of the local government crisis and the legal impediments affecting the release of local government allocations.

“We are genuinely interested in a timely resolution of the crisis and the release of funds to improve the lives of people at the grassroots. However, ignoring existing legal obstacles amounts to mischief, dishonesty and an affront to the judiciary, particularly when such a position is being advanced by a labour movement that ought to be a custodian of public institutions, including the judiciary.”

The Executive Director, however, considered the proposed strike as mere political grandstanding, either to patronise the state government, intimidate the judiciary or blackmail the Federal Government of Nigeria.

He posited that: “The fundamental questions that the Osun State NLC should provide answers to are: Who is withholding the local government allocations? Why are the allocations allegedly being withheld? And why were the allocations released recently to the 2022 elected local government administration in Osun State?

“The straightforward answer to these questions is the court, the court, and the court.

“Therefore, if the courts are yet to reach a final determination of the matter, who has the authority to either stop or authorise the release of the allocations? Certainly, no other institution can legitimately override the judicial process. Or is the Osun NLC suggesting that the Federal Ministry of Finance or the Central Bank of Nigeria should release the funds in flagrant disregard of subsisting court orders”?

“The foregoing raises serious questions about what the Osun NLC intends to achieve through this strike. “

“What cannot be obtained through the courts cannot be secured through industrial action.”

“This is similar to the situation in which local government workers embarked on one of the longest strikes in the state’s history, lasting about 20 months, after several attempts to obtain judicial redress proved unsuccessful.”

He recalled that the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE) dragged the local government council chairmen and councillors to court but subsequently withdrew the cases after approaching several courts.

He said: “It is therefore unfortunate that the labour movement now appears to be resorting to extrajudicial means of seeking redress. Such conduct is capable of encouraging anarchy and should not be condoned in a democratic society governed by the rule of law.

“For emphasis, protests and industrial strikes are fundamental rights and privileges guaranteed by the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended. However, in the present circumstances, this warning and sympathy strike represents, in our view, a high level of dishonesty and an attempt to create an economic crisis in the state while inflicting unnecessary hardship on public and private business owners.

“The option we would have expected from the labour unions is constructive dialogue with all parties involved in the ongoing litigations. The unions should persuade the parties to either withdraw the cases or consider an out-of-court settlement that would pave the way for the resolution of the impasse surrounding local government funds in Osun State.

“Interestingly, the labour unions could have used the opportunity of their recent inclusion in the Campaign Council of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, as announced by the State Coordinator, Senator Ademola Adeleke, to engage the political parties involved in the litigations. Such engagement could help facilitate an amicable resolution and allow Osun State to breathe again over the lingering local government allocation crisis.”

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/civil-society-decries-osun-nlc-strike/

posts.title: NGF, GCNg to Host Health Innovation Exchange in Abuja
posts.excerpt: * Eight maternal, newborn and child health projects to feature as stakeholders examine pathways to adoption and scale The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) and Grand Challenges Nigeria (GCNg) are set
posts.content:
* Eight maternal, newborn and child health projects to feature as stakeholders examine pathways to adoption and scale

The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) and Grand Challenges Nigeria (GCNg) are set to convene the 2026 Annual Meeting and Innovation Exchange on Friday, November 13, in Abuja, to explore ways of translating Nigerian-led health research and innovations into practical solutions for improving healthcare delivery.

The meeting, scheduled to hold at Lake Greenfield Hotel, will bring together state governments, research teams, government institutions, development partners and financing stakeholders to examine how evidence-based health innovations can be adopted, funded and scaled across the country.

With the theme, ‘Innovation to Impact: Evidence, Adoption, Uptake and Scale for Better Health in Nigeria,’ the exchange is expected to focus on the institutional capacity, policy decisions and sustainable financing required to assess how promising innovations can progress from research towards practical use.

Eight projects supported by Grand Challenges Nigeria, focusing on maternal, newborn and child health, will feature prominently at the meeting.

The projects address critical healthcare challenges, including newborn sepsis diagnosis, umbilical cord care, community-supported digital healthcare, emergency maternal referrals, birth-defect identification, perinatal asphyxia research, digital risk support and the prediction of severe pre-eclampsia.

According to the organisers, the programme will combine research evidence and practical implementation experiences with policy discussions on adoption, replication across states, financing and the evidence and conditions required for adoption and scale.

The NGF’s involvement is expected to bring state-level implementation priorities and opportunities for peer learning into the discussions, particularly as state governments remain critical to the delivery of healthcare services.

The African University of Science and Technology will also contribute a Policy Lab focusing on the institutional decisions required to translate research into practice.

Grand Challenges Nigeria was launched in November 2024 as a national platform supporting locally led research and innovation in health and food security.

Anchored by the Nutrition Society of Nigeria, the initiative operates in partnership with the Office of the Vice-President and the Federal Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology.

It is supported by the Gates Foundation, with technical assistance from the Science for Africa Foundation, and forms part of the wider Grand Challenges family of initiatives.

The organisers said the November 13 meeting would help identify the additional evidence, institutional engagement and financing required to assess promising innovations for their next stage of development.

Participation in the exchange and inclusion in the showcase do not constitute a decision to fund or adopt an innovation. Research findings should be interpreted within their stated limitations.

Attendance at the meeting will be by invitation. Media organisations seeking interviews or coverage arrangements are invited to contact the Grand Challenges Nigeria secretariat in advance.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/ngf-gcng-to-host-health-innovation-exchange-in-abuja/

posts.title: CASER Condemns Rising Electoral Violence across Nigeria
posts.excerpt: Alex Enumah in Abuja A social rights group, the Citizens’ Advocacy for Social and Economic Rights (CASER), has condemned the rising wave of electoral violence and political intimidation across the
posts.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

A social rights group, the Citizens’ Advocacy for Social and Economic Rights (CASER), has condemned the rising wave of electoral violence and political intimidation across the country ahead of the 2027 general election.

The group noted that within days, incidents in Ado-Ekiti, Calabar and Asaba have raised urgent questions about the safety of candidates, campaign workers and ordinary citizens.

CASER in a statement issued by its Executive Director, Mr. Frank Tietie, said that Nigerians must be able to attend a rally, support a candidate or campaign for a political party without risking their lives.

“So far, one Nigerian has been killed in Asaba, while others have been severely injured in the above three locations,” CASER said while extending its condolences to the bereaved family and its solidarity to the injured.

The group, accordingly, warned that it is documenting these incidents and at the same time putting Nigeria’s political class on notice.

“We will use appropriate national, regional and international mechanisms to pursue accountability for those who carry out, order, finance, organise or knowingly facilitate electoral violence. We will press for prosecution wherever the evidence warrants it and seek compensation and other lawful remedies for victims and bereaved families.

“We will follow the evidence regardless of party affiliation, political influence or public office.

“Section 40 of the Constitution protects peaceful assembly and association. That protection applies to supporters of every political party. The police and other competent authorities must act promptly on credible threats and provide protection impartially.

“Federal, state, FCT, and local government officials must discharge their respective legal duties to protect Nigerians’ right to gather peacefully for political rallies.

“Where public officials participate in attacks, use public resources to facilitate them or breach a legal duty to protect, CASER will pursue personal liability against each one of them wherever the evidence and the law support it,” the statement read in part.

CASER, however, disclosed that it would seek joint liability where officials or institutions share legal responsibility, and vicarious liability where the relevant government or public authority is legally answerable for the conduct of its officers.

The group added that where officials received credible warnings, they will demand the records showing who received them, what measures were available and what action was taken.

“Victims and witnesses should report every incident to law enforcement and notify CASER. They are urged to lodge a formal complaint with the Nigeria Police Force, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) or any other competent law enforcement authority. They are also to notify CASER at: complaints@citizensadvocacy.org OR; citizensadvocacy@gmail.com

“Such notifications to CASER must include a contact phone number, the date and location of the electoral violence, and a brief account of the incident. Where possible, such complaints should preserve original photographs, videos, threatening messages, medical records, receipts and witness details.

“Families may also report on behalf of victims who have died or are unable to report. CASER will track how complaints are handled, press for timely investigations, and pursue appropriate claims for compensation and other redress.

“We call on the Inspector-General of Police and the relevant Commissioners of Police to preserve evidence, protect witnesses, and provide public updates on these three investigations, or any others that may occur in the future, before and after the elections.

“Political parties and candidates must condemn attacks unequivocally, cooperate with investigators and answer for the conduct of anyone they direct or sponsor. Every Nigerian must be free to campaign, assemble and vote without fear.

“CASER assures the public that electoral violence is totally unacceptable, especially at a time when Nigerians are already being traumatised by some of the worst forms of violence by kidnappers, terrorists and bandits. ‘Enough is Enough!’,” the statement added.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/caser-condemns-rising-electoral-violence-across-nigeria/

posts.title: WIM Leaders Seek Increased Access to Capital,Global Opportunities For African Women
posts.excerpt: Jonathan Eze Founder and Chairperson of Women in Management (WIM), Dr. Sulochana Segera, and Chairperson of Women in Management Africa (WIMAFRICA), Dr. Ngozi Oyewole, have called for greater economic
posts.content:
Jonathan Eze

Founder and Chairperson of Women in Management (WIM), Dr. Sulochana Segera, and Chairperson of Women in Management Africa (WIMAFRICA), Dr. Ngozi Oyewole, have called for greater economic opportunities, global recognition and increased participation of Nigerian and African women in trade, investment, entrepreneurship and leadership.

The duo made the call at a press conference in Lagos on Monday ahead of the maiden African edition of the WIM Global Economic Forum, themed “The Power Shift: Women Driving Africa’s Global Economic Influence,” scheduled for November 10–11, 2026, at the Federal Palace Hotel, Lagos.

They said the gathering would move beyond celebrating women’s achievements to creating practical opportunities for them to influence economic decisions, access capital, expand businesses, participate in international trade and establish strategic partnerships across continents.

Oyewole, who is also the founder of Commonwealth Business Women Africa, said the power shift being advocated by WIMAFRICA was about ensuring that women moved from being participants in economic activities to becoming influential decision-makers, business owners, manufacturers and investors.

She noted that African women were already sustaining local markets, building enterprises and contributing significantly to national economies, but needed greater access to finance, markets, infrastructure and leadership opportunities to maximise their potential.

“For me, the power shift is about who gets to make economic decisions. African women already build businesses, create jobs and sustain local markets. The next step is for more women to own the companies that grow, decide where capital goes and help set the terms on which Africa trades,” she said.

She explained that the conference would amplify the contributions of African women, particularly in manufacturing, agriculture, technology, trade and other productive sectors, while exploring how they could take advantage of opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

Oyewole stressed the importance of backward integration and local production, noting that women entrepreneurs could play a significant role in strengthening African supply chains by transforming locally available raw materials into finished products.

She identified access to finance as one of the biggest constraints facing women-owned businesses, arguing that many entrepreneurs have the capacity and market opportunities to expand but lack the working capital required to execute contracts and sustain production.

Drawing from her experience as a manufacturer and founder of NOXIE Limited, an office furniture manufacturing company established nearly three decades ago, she explained that businesses often struggle to finance materials, wages and production costs while waiting for customers to pay for completed contracts.

She therefore called on financial institutions to develop financing products that reflect the operational realities of women-owned enterprises, particularly manufacturers and small businesses.

Oyewole also urged government agencies and corporate organisations to make procurement opportunities more accessible to qualified women-owned businesses, ensure transparent bidding processes and promote timely payment for completed contracts.

On AfCFTA, she said many women entrepreneurs remained inadequately informed about rules of origin, documentation and the procedures required to access cross-border markets, despite the enormous opportunities offered by the continental trade agreement.

She further identified poor roads and unreliable electricity as major challenges affecting women in rural agriculture and food production, noting that inadequate infrastructure contributes to post-harvest losses and increases the cost of transporting goods to urban markets.

She called for stronger protection of women’s property rights, particularly land ownership, arguing that removing cultural and institutional barriers would enable more women to invest in agriculture, manufacturing and other productive ventures.

On her part, Segera said the decision to bring WIM’s global platform to Africa was driven by the need to recognise the contributions of African women and connect them to international business and investment opportunities.

She explained that WIM was established 16 years ago in Sri Lanka to identify, celebrate and promote women whose work contributes significantly to economic development and professional advancement.

She disclosed that the organisation now has members and award recipients in 29 countries, providing an international network through which accomplished women can collaborate, exchange expertise and establish business relationships across borders.

Recounting her relationship with Oyewole, Segera said they first met in India, where the Nigerian entrepreneur was representing Africa at an international conference. She said their subsequent engagements in Dubai, the United Kingdom, Malaysia and Sri Lanka strengthened their relationship and exposed them to the achievements and challenges of women across different economies.

According to her, Oyewole’s commitment to bringing the WIM Top 50 recognition platform to Africa provided an opportunity to showcase the continent’s women and demonstrate their capacity to contribute to the global economy.

Segera stressed that the recognition initiative would go beyond celebrating professional titles and positions to highlighting the talents, resilience, innovations and achievements of African women.

She described Africa as an increasingly important market in the global economy, adding that women remained central to unlocking the continent’s economic potential.

She emphasised that the gathering was not intended to be merely another conference and awards ceremony but a platform for business partnerships, investment, trade and long-term economic cooperation.

Segera also called for reforms in financial institutions, arguing that women entrepreneurs should be assessed on their business potential and capacity rather than traditional assumptions about their economic roles.

She further emphasised the need for shared family responsibilities, noting that women often combine professional commitments with domestic responsibilities, thereby limiting the time and opportunities available for business expansion and career advancement.

“You cannot keep half of your population inactive in the economy and expect the economy to grow,” she said.

Also speaking at the press conference, Seun Oyewole, Managing Director of NOXIE Limited and Founder of Legend of Legend Productions Ltd, described Nigeria’s hosting of the maiden African edition of the global gathering as an important opportunity to showcase the country’s achievements and Africa’s growing economic potential.

Seun, who is also a member of WIMAFRICA and oversees event planning for the organisation, particularly the Global Economic Forum 2026 and the 16th Professional & Career Awards Gala 2026, said the gathering would bring together women and men from different countries and professional backgrounds to celebrate women’s achievements and explore opportunities for collaboration.

He expressed pride that the first African edition was taking place in Nigeria, noting that Lagos, as the country’s commercial capital, offered an appropriate platform to showcase the entrepreneurial talent, commercial activities and business opportunities available across the continent.

He said the preparations had provided an opportunity to bring together stakeholders committed not only to highlighting the challenges facing women but also to showcasing their achievements across different sectors.

Providing further details of the programme, Dr. Ngozi Oyewole said the November 10 sessions would feature discussions on Africa Trade 2035, AfCFTA, resilient supply chains and the continent’s role in the next decade of global growth.

Other sessions would examine financial inclusion, economic power, ownership, capital mobilisation and wealth creation in the artificial intelligence economy.

The programme would also feature discussions on women’s leadership, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, the future of finance, sustainability, green capital and climate resilience.

Participants are expected to examine how digital transformation can strengthen Africa’s banking sector, improve global competitiveness and create new opportunities for women-owned businesses.

The conference will also feature sessions on global human capital, the future of business, talent development, leadership and productivity in the emerging economy.

A global forum recognition ceremony, executive networking and business matchmaking sessions are also scheduled as part of the programme.

The event will culminate in a gala night on November 11, during which outstanding women who have distinguished themselves in business, leadership, innovation and professional practice will receive awards and recognition.

The organisers said the ultimate measure of the gathering would be the partnerships and practical opportunities created after participants returned to their respective countries, particularly in expanding women’s access to capital, contracts, international markets and economic decision-making.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/wim-leaders-seek-increased-access-to-capitalglobal-opportunities-for-african-women/

posts.title: Kartel, LuxWatt Push Smarter Solar for Nigerian Homes, Businesses
posts.excerpt: Peter Uzoho Kartel Energy and LuxWatt Nigeria, solar brands of Skyville Company Limited have showcased a widening portfolio of solar and storage solutions designed for Nigerian homes and businesses, a
posts.content:
Peter Uzoho

Kartel Energy and LuxWatt Nigeria, solar brands of Skyville Company Limited have showcased a widening portfolio of solar and storage solutions designed for Nigerian homes and businesses, as competition intensifies and demand for reliable power continues to grow.

The two brands exhibited their products at the just-concluded Nigeria Energy 2026 held recently in Lagos, where they presented intelligent hybrid inverters, lithium batteries and efficient solar panels developed to support dependable supply and help close Nigeria’s energy deficit.

Luxwatt’s high-voltage lithium battery solutions also demonstrated how solar and storage can support commercial and industrial operations where reliable electricity is essential to productivity and business continuity.

Chief Executive Officer of Skyville Company Limited, Mr. Ola Ogunsemowo, who spoke on the sidelines of the exhibition, said the company is currently focused on continuous expansion of its product portfolio in response to changing needs in the Nigerian market.

Through LuxWatt, the company now offers lithium batteries ranging from 1.28kWh to 25kWh for low voltage applications, and up to 705kWh for the high voltage series, alongside hybrid inverters from 4.2kVA to 8kVA. The range is designed to serve different requirements, from homes and small businesses to larger installations. Kartel also newly introduced affordable rechargeable fans, providing another practical option for households seeking comfort especially during this period of high temperatures and unreliable electricity. Together, the products reflect the company’s focus on accessible, durable and adaptable solutions for everyday Nigerian conditions.

On competition, Ogunsemowo said Kartel remains focused on product durability, dependable customer support and long-term value. As an original equipment manufacturer (OEM), the company places emphasis on products designed with Nigerian operating conditions in mind, supported by warranty offerings and a dedicated customer-experience function.

Its technical team provides after-sales support to help customers get the best from their systems. The company also invests in building local expertise through Kartel Energy Academy, which helps strengthen the skills and knowledge of solar professionals.

On opportunities, he said Kartel sees significant prospects driven by the need for more reliable electricity across homes, businesses and industry. Solar and storage can help households manage interruptions, enable businesses to plan and operate more consistently and profitably, and provide commercial and industrial users with additional options for meeting their energy needs.

Continued growth, he said, will depend on making dependable systems more accessible, developing skilled installers and technicians, and building customer confidence in the quality and performance of solar products.

The rapid growth of the market also presents challenges, including the risk of counterfeit or substandard products, inconsistent product quality and the need for greater consumer awareness. These issues, he warned, can undermine trust and make it harder for customers to distinguish reliable products from unsuitable alternatives.

“Kartel believes stronger oversight and enforcement by relevant government agencies, clearer product standards, and consumer education are important to protecting customers and supporting sustainable market growth. Customers should also be encouraged to buy from reputable suppliers and confirm product warranties and after-sales support before making a purchase,” Ogunsemowo said.

He gave an update on Kartel Academy, saying it is currently functional through its Masterclass programme, which travels to major cities across Nigeria to train and empower solar professionals. The programme is designed to help bridge knowledge gaps and strengthen technical capacity. Last year, the academy trained over 1,500 solar experts.

“The Academy’s institutional training arm is still being prepared for launch. Kartel will announce further details when it opens, giving interested Nigerians the opportunity to learn more and participate,” he said. On observations from the exhibition, Ogunsemowo said participation provided an opportunity to engage with industry stakeholders and observe the range of solutions being developed for Nigeria’s energy needs.

The exhibition highlighted the importance of offering products for different applications, from household backup to commercial and industrial storage, and of pairing technology with reliable service and technical expertise.

He also observed the strong interest in renewable solutions that can help businesses and households manage energy reliability, pointing to the growing importance of practical, scalable alternatives as Nigeria’s population and energy needs continue to expand.

Kartel also noted the significantly increasing dominance of Chinese technology compared with those from India. This, the company said, points to the growing need for stakeholders to channel efforts into developing Nigeria’s own local solar solution and technological capability, as homegrown, scalable alternatives cannot be overemphasized.

Kartel noted the growing presence of stakeholders and a broader range of solar and energy solutions at this year’s exhibition, which it sees as an encouraging sign of continued activity in the sector and of the role alternative energy sources can play in expanding access to reliable power.

Through its brands and ongoing investment in products, service and training, Kartel Energy aims to contribute to a more accessible and dependable energy future for Nigerians.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/kartel-luxwatt-push-smarter-solar-for-nigerian-homes-businesses/

posts.title: Deadly floods hit Iraq as thunderstorms sweep across region
posts.excerpt: Violent storms lash northern Iraq and parts of Iran, while Portugal faces strong winds and Japan braces for further snowfall Deadly flash floods hit northern Iraq on Saturday as severe thunderstorms s
posts.content:
Violent storms lash northern Iraq and parts of Iran, while Portugal faces strong winds and Japan braces for further snowfall

Deadly flash floods hit northern Iraq on Saturday as severe thunderstorms swept across the region, including in neighbouring Iran. The city of Erbil, in Iraq, was particularly badly hit, with extensive damage to homes and businesses. Streets were inundated as torrential rain fell over a short period.

posts.title: Veterans Day 2026 brings free meals at popular restaurants — and some deals don't end Nov. 11
posts.excerpt: About 30 restaurants are offering Veterans Day deals on Nov. 11, from Outback Steakhouse's free Bloomin' Onion to Buffalo Wild Wings' boneless wings.
posts.content:
Veterans and active-duty military members can find free food and other promotions at restaurants across the country on Veterans Day, Nov. 11. Some offers also give customers a reason to return for another deal later.

About 30 restaurant brands are included in Dinova's 2026 Veterans Day Dining Guide, according to Alison Quinn, the company's Florida-based president.

The guide is in its fifth year and includes national and regional chains like Bonefish Grill, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Hooters, Outback Steakhouse and Red Lobster.

102-YEAR-OLD NAVY VETERAN STILL CRAVES HOT WINGS AFTER 102 COMBAT MISSIONS IN KOREA: 'I MIGHT MAKE IT TO 115'

"What we're starting to see now is it's going beyond Veterans Day, to try to give back to the vets in a way that is more meaningful," Quinn told Fox News Digital. "Just not about one day but come back, and we'll give you something again."

Quinn pointed to California-based Hofman Hospitality Group, which is offering select meals to veterans and a $10 bonus card for a future visit. Lucille's Smokehouse Bar-B-Que is among the group's brands.

Outback Steakhouse is offering a complimentary Bloomin' Onion and soft drink, along with a meal offer for a return visit, she said.

Other deals listed in the guide include 10 free boneless wings and fries at Buffalo Wild Wings, a complimentary Red's Big Tavern Burger at Red Robin, free shrimp at Red Lobster and a free All-American Smash at Smashburger.

Dinova started the guide to share offers with veterans and, in some cases, active-duty military personnel, Quinn said. The company's business dining network includes about 25,000 restaurants and 600 corporate partners, she said.

Downloads of the guide have increased over the years, Quinn said, and the promotions may be useful for veterans or active-duty personnel who are struggling or "living under a tight budget."

Asked which deal she would choose, Quinn singled out Eddie Merlot's complimentary cheeseburger. Her father is an 85-year-old veteran, she said, and she plans to tell him about it.

posts.title: 2027: Only Yari, Alake, Idris can speak for Tinubu campaign, APC-PCC declares
posts.excerpt: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has restricted the right to speak on its behalf to three persons, ordering that everyone previously announced
posts.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has restricted the right to speak on its behalf to three persons, ordering that everyone previously announced in that role be dissolved into the Directorate of Media and Strategic Communications as members.

The Chief of Staff to the President and Deputy Director-General (Administration) of the Council, Femi Gbajabiamila, announced the changes in a statement issued on Wednesday, titled “Reorganization of Media and Communications Structure”.

According to the statement, “The Council has approved that only the campaign’s Director General, Senator Abdulaziz Yari; the Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, as official Spokesperson; and the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, will speak on behalf of the Council.”

Gbajabiamila said the Council made the changes “to ensure more cohesive, disciplined, and effective public engagement”.

He said that “all previously announced persons in this capacity shall henceforth dissolve into the Directorate of Media and Strategic Communications as members.”

The statement also put broadcasters on notice. Radio and television stations were advised “to take note of these changes and act accordingly”.

On appearances by other persons, the statement said: “The campaign will delegate appropriate person(s) for appearances where and when necessary.”

posts.title: 2027: Obi is desperate, not wired for long-term solutions — Oshiomhole
posts.excerpt: Oshiomhole alleged that Obi was not inclined to develop long-term solutions that could produce sustainable growth. The post 2027: Obi is desperate, not wired for long-term solutions — Oshiomhole appea
posts.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Senator Adams Oshiomhole has accused Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi of focusing on importation rather than job creation and long-term solutions, alleging that his promise to serve only four years reflects desperation to become president.

Oshiomhole made the remarks while campaigning for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, on Wednesday.

Framing the 2027 election as a choice about Nigeria’s future, he urged young voters to back Tinubu and contrasted what he described as the President’s long-term development agenda and plans to improve the power sector with Obi’s business record and four-year pledge.

Addressing young Nigerians, the APC chieftain urged students, graduates and young workers to compare the time it takes industrialists such as Aliko Dangote to establish factories and create jobs with what he described as Obi’s focus on setting up shopping malls.

“That said, I need to talk to us, you young people. What this election is about is you. You as students, some of you are graduates, some of you are young workers. You talk to Dangote and ask him how long does it take him to set up a factory, to set up a refinery that today employs 10s of 1000s of workers. Then go and ask Obi how long it takes him to set up a shopping mall. To set up a shopping mall, you need short-term funds, and that is the logic of Peter Obi,” he said.

Oshiomhole alleged that Obi was not inclined to develop long-term solutions that could produce sustainable growth. He also questioned Obi’s business record, asking why an unemployed person should accept advice on job creation from someone he accused of selling imported products instead of locally made Yoruba Adire.

“He cannot; he’s not wired to think of long-term solutions that produce sustainable growth and development. Another one: if there is anybody who is unemployed, ask Obi, why are you selling imported products?” Oshiomhole asked.

He further argued that a person whose main business was importation could not credibly lecture Nigerians on job creation, and described Obi’s pledge to serve for four years as evidence of what he called desperation.

“So, anyone whose main business is importation cannot lecture us about job creation because he doesn’t mean it. And for you to see the desperation, he will say he will do four years. So he is a man who just wants it to be said that once upon a time there was a Peter in the villa. Nigeria needs statesmen, not petty traders in politics,” he added.

Turning to Tinubu’s re-election bid, Oshiomhole said the President knew the need to increase the purchasing power of poorer Nigerians and create jobs. He described electricity as central to employment and industrial activity, and said Tinubu was prepared to tackle the power sector.

“The president is aware that we need to boost the purchasing power of the poor. He also understands that we need to create jobs.”

“He understands that the enemy of jobs is darkness, and to fight darkness, the president is ready to carry out a radical review of the power sector,” the APC chieftain said.

Furthermore, Oshiomhole blamed the power sector’s condition on previous leadership, saying it was easier to destroy the system than rebuild it, arguing that Tinubu was willing to take on difficult challenges and said the President’s second term would prioritise higher power generation and a lasting solution to transmission problems.

According to him, Tinubu understood the need to improve the purchasing power of poorer Nigerians, create jobs and address persistent power shortages. Oshiomhole also said Tinubu was prepared to undertake a radical review of the power sector and argued that restoring manufacturing would help spread the benefits of economic growth.

“You know who destroyed the power sector? It is easy to destroy anything, but it is difficult to reconstruct. But this president doesn’t run away from difficult institutions or difficult situations, and so in this second term, Nigeria’s power generation will not only double.”

“The issue of transmission will be solved on a sustainable basis, so that the hardworking industrialists will return to work,” he added.

Oshiomhole also said Tinubu believed that reviving manufacturing was the best way to share the gains of economic growth.

“The President believes that the best way to share the fruit of prosperity is to bring the manufacturing sector back,” he said.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027-obi-is-desperate-not-wired-for-long-term-solutions-oshiomhole/

posts.title: 2027 Polls: EU flays rising violence, hate speech, pledges support for NHRC
posts.excerpt: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The European Union (EU) on Wednesday expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of the 2027 general electio
posts.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA – The European Union (EU) on Wednesday expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Speaking at the opening session of the 2026 Civil Society and Human Rights Defenders Forum on the State of Human Rights, held in Abuja, the EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, H.E. Gautier Mignot, maintained that such incidents undermine democratic gains and discourage citizens from participating fully in the electoral process.

He described open forums, free media, peaceful assembly and civil society organisations as essential to elections, noting that they promote transparency and enable citizens to share facts, debate and scrutinise candidates for elective office without fear of censorship or retaliation.

“Free civic and political spaces also help hold leaders and institutions accountable by enabling CSOs and active citizens to monitor election administration, track campaign promises and challenge government policies.

“By enabling free association and assembly, robust civic and political spaces prevent authorities from backsliding or from manipulating rules.

“It is vital to ensure credibility and public confidence in an election.

“The absence or weakening of these safeguards will directly undermine citizens’ rights to participate meaningfully in elections. This is why the European Union, together with its member states, is committed to ensuring the sustenance of free civic and political spaces in Nigeria,” the EU leader added.

He further pledged the EU’s commitment to support key institutions like the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and CSOs to synergise efforts towards strengthening democracy and good governance in the country.

“Our objective is not to interfere in the elections but to support legitimate Nigerian stakeholders to fully play their roles in order to contribute to a free, fair, credible electoral process.

“Stakeholders, the public sector, civil society, political parties, the media, all have a very important role to play,” Mignot stated.

The event, which was organised by the NHRC, was themed “Protecting Human Rights in Civic and Political Spaces in the 2027 Elections.”

In his address, the Executive Secretary of the NHRC, Dr. Tony Ojukwu, SAN, said the forum was convened because democracy does not survive on election day alone.

“It survives in the space between elections: in the freedom of citizens to speak without fear, to assemble without permits, to associate without obstruction, and to choose their leaders without intimidation.

“Section 14 of our Constitution declares that sovereignty belongs to the people of Nigeria; Sections 39 and 40 guarantee expression, association and assembly; and Article 13 of the African Charter, which Nigeria has domesticated, makes the right to participation directly enforceable.

“The right to participate in the conduct of public affairs, including through free and genuine elections under Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), is the heartbeat of every freedom we defend.

“When that right is suppressed, democracy does not merely stumble; it begins to die, quietly, through apathy, fear and distrust,” the NHRC boss stated.

He decried that, with the elections drawing near, journalists and human rights defenders continue to operate in challenging environments marked by harassment, arbitrary arrests and the misapplication of laws, including provisions of the Cybercrimes Act.

“We are concerned by political and voter intimidation, by political exclusion through prohibitive nomination fees that bar women, youth and persons with disabilities from candidature, by the persistence of hate speech and incitement, and by regulatory uncertainties around digital platforms.

“And we are concerned, above all, by impunity, evidenced by the absence of accountability for electoral crimes.

“As I said recently when I received the UNOWAS delegation led by Special Representative Leonardo Santos Simão: as long as people can commit these election-related offences and go scot-free, then anybody can try anything they like.

“These are warning lights, not yet verdicts. The window to correct course is now, and that is precisely why this Forum meets today,” Ojukwu, SAN, added.

In his goodwill message, the National Chairman of the Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC), Dr. Yusuf Dantalle, said the experience of recent off-cycle elections, particularly the campaign period preceding the recent governorship election in Osun State, underscored the urgent need to address election-related violence and protect citizens throughout the electoral cycle.

The IPAC leader, in his speech, which was read by Mr. Chinedu Obi, said: “Democracy is not defined by election day alone; it must be reflected in the entire process, from political campaigns and voter mobilisation to voting, collation and declaration of results.

“As we approach 2027, political competition must not become warfare. Political opponents are not enemies, and electoral victory must never be pursued at the expense of human lives, public peace and national unity.

“IPAC therefore calls on political parties, candidates and their supporters to embrace issue-based campaigns, political tolerance and responsible communication.

“We must collectively reject electoral violence, hate speech, voter suppression, political intimidation and every conduct capable of undermining credible elections,” he added.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027-polls-eu-flays-rising-violence-hate-speech-pledges-support-for-nhrc/

posts.title: 2027: Learn from Jonathan, don’t rely on governors, group tells Tinubu
posts.excerpt: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — A political group, Ndigbo for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu (NDI-ABAT), has cautioned President Bola Tinubu against making state governors the principal pillars of his 2027
posts.content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe

UMUAHIA — A political group, Ndigbo for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu (NDI-ABAT), has cautioned President Bola Tinubu against making state governors the principal pillars of his 2027 re-election strategy, urging him to build direct relationships with Nigerians and strengthen independent political structures.

The group advised Tinubu to learn from the experience of former President Goodluck Jonathan, whose re-election bid ended in defeat in 2015, arguing that excessive reliance on governors and political office holders could expose the President to similar challenges.

In a statement jointly signed by its National Coordinator, Mazi Okechukwu Isiguzoro, and Chairman of its Board of Trustees, Dim Uche Okwukwu, NDI-ABAT warned that political loyalty should not be taken for granted, particularly when personal interests and political survival come into play.

The group alleged that some governors publicly identified with Tinubu’s re-election project while secretly supporting opposition candidates.

It described the situation as one in which political leaders could publicly support the President during the day but work for his opponents behind the scenes.

NDI-ABAT urged Tinubu to study the political lessons of the 2015 presidential election and pay greater attention to managing political alliances, party structures and competing interests.

“Our advice to President Tinubu is clear: Do not repeat the political miscalculations associated with 2015. Do not put excessive reliance on the governors. Do not confuse public loyalty with guaranteed commitment.

“Do not surrender your political future to the calculations of individual governors, build wider relationships with Nigerians and strengthen independent political structures before the 2027 election.

“Political alliances are important, but they must never become a substitute for direct engagement with the people,” the statement said.

The group expressed concern that some governors publicly supporting the President might reconsider their positions as political pressures mounted and their own electoral interests came into focus.

It urged Tinubu to distinguish between public declarations of support and consistent political commitment.

NDI-ABAT also warned that confrontations between some governors and opposition figures, particularly the presidential candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, respectively, could produce unintended political consequences.

It argued that political intimidation, hostility and unnecessary confrontations could deepen divisions and generate sympathy for opposition platforms.

The group maintained that politicians should be allowed to participate freely in the democratic process without unnecessary hostility.

It further advised the President to adopt a broader national outreach strategy that would connect directly with citizens, grassroots organisations, community leaders and independent political movements rather than relying exclusively on governors.

Push for South-East engagement

The group identified the City Boy Movement as an important platform for expanding political engagement and proposed strategic collaboration with the movement to strengthen outreach, particularly across the South-East.

It also argued that regional structures and partnerships could help rebuild political communication between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Igbo people.

According to NDI-ABAT, the APC’s presidential election performances in the South-East in 2015, 2019 and 2023 demonstrated the need for a different approach to political engagement in the region.

It said rebuilding confidence would require sustained dialogue, political inclusion, respect and visible commitments to the interests of Ndigbo.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/2027-learn-from-jonathan-dont-rely-on-governors-group-tells-tinubu/

posts.excerpt: New Jersey Democratic Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy repeatedly dodged CNN's Pamela Brown when asked whether he views Iran or Israel as a U.S. adversary.
posts.content:
New Jersey Democratic Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy struggled to answer whether he viewed Iran as an adversary and Israel as an ally to the U.S. on Tuesday.

During an interview on CNN's "The Situation Room," co-host Pamela Brown repeatedly asked Hamawy about his views on both of the countries regarding his demand that the U.S. pull all military funding from Israel in the wake of the war with Iran.

"Well, now, what I see is that we were pushed into this war by Israel," Hamawy said. "It's not helping Americans. Americans didn't ask for it. It's illegal and immoral. And at this point, I think the U.S. and the Iranians want this war to end."

RAHM EMANUEL ACCUSES ANTI-ISRAEL DEMS OF HAVING NO MIDDLE EAST PLAN BESIDES CUTTING FUNDING TO JEWISH STATE

"Do you see Iran as the adversary?" Brown asked.

"I see that we pushed them into a fight. And so, I think we both have to step back and say, is this helping either one of us?" Hamawy answered.

Brown repeatedly pressed Hamawy on whether he viewed Iran as an adversary, and the conressman-elect continued to avoid answering despite Brown reminding him that Iranians have chanted, "Death to America."

"We've been saying ‘Death to Iran’ for decades as well," Hamawy responded. "And so, what we need to do is use diplomacy."

"They've killed a lot of Americans," Brown said.

"And we've killed a lot of them as well," Hamawy said.

PRO-ISRAEL LEADER WARNS DEMOCRATS FAILING TO CONDEMN ‘VICIOUS JEW HATERS’ IN CONGRESS

Hamawy pushed for diplomacy over war, though Brown pointed out that he still refused to clarify his views on Iran or Israel.

"I'm saying that that doesn't help us. We're in the middle of a war right now that is making American lives worse. We're putting our troops at risk. We're creating, you know, an economic crisis that we don't need. And so, the blame game doesn't help. So, how do we get out of this?" Hamawy said.

He later referred to the Iranian government as a "dictatorship" and "authoritarian," though he suggested that America's actions have made the country more radical.

Fox News Digital reached out to Hamawy's team for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Hamawy's comments resembled Michigan Democratic Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who refused to say whether Israel or Iran was the greater threat to America despite repeated questioning.

AOC-BACKED DEMOCRAT WITH PAST TIES TO AL QAEDA-LINKED GROUP WINS NJ HOUSE PRIMARY

"I think both of them have proven dangerous in their own way," El-Sayed said in October. "One at risk of attacking us, one getting us into wars. We have no business fighting."

Hamawy won a House seat despite scrutiny for his previous volunteer work with the Benevolence International Foundation (BIF) — a Chicago-based charity that federal authorities later identified as providing financial and logistical support to al-Qaeda.

He was also scrutinized over his past relationship with Sheikh Omar Abdel-Rahman, commonly known as the "Blind Sheikh," whom he accompanied on a trip in 1991.

Roz Rothstein, co-founder and CEO of StandWithUs, an international nonpartisan education organization that supports Israel, condemned Hamawy's comments, accusing him of refusing to acknowledge a "moral reality."

"Representative-elect Hamawy refused to acknowledge a basic factual and moral reality. Iran's oppressive regime has made itself the enemy of both the United States and its own people. American officials who don't understand that should have no role in our country's foreign policy decisions," Rothstein told Fox News Digital.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/media/newly-elected-nj-democrat-repeatedly-dodges-question-whether-iran-adversary

posts.title: ADP demands electricity reforms, proposes 2027–2035 transformation plan
posts.excerpt: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Action Democratic Party (ADP) has called on the Federal Government to embark on urgent electricity-sector reforms, demanding greater transparency in public investments and a
posts.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Action Democratic Party (ADP) has called on the Federal Government to embark on urgent electricity-sector reforms, demanding greater transparency in public investments and accountability in the management of funds committed to the power sector.

The party also proposed a National Electricity Transformation Programme covering 2027 to 2035, saying Nigeria could not achieve meaningful industrialisation while millions of citizens and businesses remained without reliable electricity.

ADP National Chairman, Engr. Yabagi Yusuf Sani, made the demands in a statement issued on Wednesday, while reacting to the global electrification initiative emerging from the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31).

The initiative seeks to increase electricity’s share of global final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035.

Sani described the development as an opportunity for Nigeria to address one of its major obstacles to national development, urging the government to translate the global ambition into tangible economic benefits.

He said Nigeria was endowed with natural gas, hydroelectric resources, abundant sunshine and other energy sources, yet millions of citizens continued to experience inadequate electricity supply.

According to him, industries, small businesses and households also bear enormous financial burdens from generating their own electricity.

The ADP chairman argued that the country’s electricity crisis was not simply a problem of inadequate generating capacity but also involved governance, infrastructure, institutional efficiency, investment discipline and accountability.

He expressed concern that decades of substantial public expenditure and repeated interventions in the electricity sector had failed to deliver improvements commensurate with the resources committed.

Sani said continued dependence on expensive alternative power sources had undermined manufacturing competitiveness, increased production costs, contributed to inflation, discouraged investment and limited employment opportunities.

“No nation can achieve sustainable industrialisation, technological advancement or meaningful economic independence without dependable electricity,” he said.

ADP’s proposed reforms

To address the challenges, the party called for the establishment of a National Electricity Transformation Programme (2027–2035), supported by a comprehensive and adequately funded strategy to expand electricity access, improve supply reliability, modernise transmission and distribution infrastructure and promote industrial electrification.

It also demanded an independent technical and financial audit of major electricity projects, public expenditure, subsidies, loans and contractual commitments, with the findings made accessible to Nigerians.

The party further advocated a publicly accessible framework for monitoring electricity-sector contracts, expenditure, project completion and actual service delivery.

It said public officials and contractors should be held accountable for proven cases of mismanagement, diversion of resources and failure to fulfil contractual obligations.

On industrial development, the ADP urged the government to prioritise electricity investments in manufacturing clusters, agricultural processing facilities, small and medium-sized enterprises, healthcare institutions, educational facilities and digital infrastructure.

The party also called for greater utilisation of Nigeria’s domestic energy resources through a balanced mix of natural gas, hydropower, solar energy, storage technologies and decentralised electricity systems.

It advocated climate financing arrangements that would promote technology transfer, domestic manufacturing, employment and infrastructure development without imposing unsustainable debt obligations on future generations.

On institutional reforms, the party urged the government to ensure effective implementation of the Electricity Act 2023, strengthen cooperation between federal and state governments and establish transparent performance standards for electricity-sector operators and regulatory institutions.

Electricity as development infrastructure

The ADP maintained that electricity should be regarded as essential national economic infrastructure rather than merely a commercial commodity.

It said reliable electricity was indispensable to food security, industrial development, healthcare, education, digital transformation and poverty reduction.

The party called for a shift from measuring performance through government announcements, budgetary allocations and installed generating capacity to assessing the actual electricity delivered to homes, farms, hospitals and industries.

“Nigerians deserve results, not endless promises, abandoned projects or recurring explanations for institutional failure,” Sani said.

He also cautioned against allowing the global energy transition to become another avenue for accumulating foreign loans, awarding opaque contracts or enriching a privileged few while ordinary citizens remained trapped in energy poverty.

The ADP chairman said Nigeria possessed the human and natural resources required to become a major industrial economy but needed disciplined leadership, institutional competence, transparency and accountability to realise its potential.

He urged the Federal Government, National Assembly, state governments, private investors and development partners to work towards a credible, transparent and nationally coordinated electricity transformation agenda.

Sani said the success of Nigeria’s energy transition should ultimately be measured by functioning factories, thriving businesses, job creation, electrified communities and improved living standards.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/adp-demands-electricity-reforms-proposes-2027-2035-transformation-plan/

posts.title: Moderate Dem governor-elect in hot seat after signaling one of her 'top priorities' in presser: 'Resist'
posts.excerpt: Amy Klobuchar's push for Minnesota gun safety legislation drew fierce conservative backlash over a bill that would ban AR-15 sales and limit magazines.
posts.content:
Minnesota Governor-elect Amy Klobuchar, who has positioned herself as a moderate during her years in Congress, is facing blowback over comments made shortly after the election suggesting she will push for gun control when she takes office.

"The gun safety bill is going to get passed, and I am so excited to be working with the leaders on this, and it certainly should be one of our top priorities," Klobuchar said during a press conference. "I think that bill makes a lot of sense. I’m sure that we’ll make some changes … but the basics of that bill I hope will remain in place."

The bill Klobuchar referenced is SF 4067, an omnibus gun-control package that passed the Minnesota Senate 34-33 earlier this year but has not received a House vote. The measure would prohibit federally licensed firearms dealers from selling certain semiautomatic military-style assault weapons, including AR-15s, as well as large-capacity magazines capable of holding more than 17 rounds.

The legislation would allow current owners to keep the covered firearms and magazines, but require them to obtain an ownership certification from the state Bureau of Criminal Apprehension and renew that certification every three years. Knowingly possessing an uncertified weapon or magazine would be a gross misdemeanor, with a subsequent violation punishable as a felony.

INSIDE TRUMP'S UNPRECEDENTED BATTLE PLAN TO EXPAND SECOND AMENDMENT RIGHTS THROUGH JUSTICE DEPARTMENT

Klobuchar quickly faced criticism from conservatives and pro-Second Amendment groups on social media, accusing her of pushing a liberal gun control agenda on law-abiding Minnesotans, particularly in rural areas.

"Democrats don't care about affordability. They only care about taking away our Second Amendment rights," conservative communicator Steve Guest posted on X. "Amy Klobuchar can't contain her excitement as she goes after law-abiding gun owners."

"In one of her first acts as governor-elect, Sen. @amyklobuchar affirmed that she will go after Minnesotans' firearms under the guise of ‘safety,’" the National Rifle Association (NRA) posted on X.

"When Amy Klobuchar told you over and over she was going to do a top-to-bottom audit, she meant of your guns, not your tax dollars," Minnesota attorney and former immigration judge Nathan Hansen posted on X.

DEMOCRATS' LATEST GUN-CONTROL PUSH RUNS INTO INCONVENIENT FACT ABOUT HOW SCHOOL KILLER WAS STOPPED

"Why are you babbling about gun control?" Minnesota Miners, a pro-mining grassroots nonprofit in Minnesota, posted on X. "Instead you should be coming out with your plan to stop government fraud and lowering taxes. But you can't do that you have to come out attacking & trying to violate lawful gun owners constitutional rights."

"We have a duty to our nation to not comply," Minnesota Republican state Rep. Ben Davis posted on X. "Resist."

"AMY KLOBUCHAR ISN'T EVEN SWORN IN AND SHE'S ALREADY COMING FOR MINNESOTA'S RIFLES," conservative influencer Gunther Eagleman posted on X.

Fox News Digital reached out to Klobuchar’s team for comment on what aspects of the bill she does and does not support but did not receive a response.

"I am committed as ever to moving our state forward, not moving our state to the left or to the right, but moving our state forward," Klobuchar said during the press conference.

Klobuchar, who has served as a Minnesota senator since 2007, defeated Minnesota Republican House Speaker Lisa Demuth 13 points in the gubernatorial election earlier this month and will take office in January, replacing Gov. Tim Walz, who dropped his re-election bid in January amid fallout from a massive fraud scandal.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/moderate-dem-governor-elect-hot-seat-signaling-top-priorities-presser-resist
