posts.title: Ari Aster Movie Gets Star-Studded Cast Including Alexander Skarsgård, Hunter Schafer, & More
posts.excerpt: Ari Aster is teaming up with a Canadian filmmaking trio for a new feature film starring Alexander Skarsgård and Hunter Schafer. The film brings together actors from different backgrounds. Skarsgård re
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Steve Wilkie/Courtesy of Apple Ari Aster is teaming up with a Canadian filmmaking trio for a new feature film starring Alexander Skarsgård and Hunter Schafer. The film brings together actors from different backgrounds. Skarsgård recently featured in Wicker, while Schafer will appear in the upcoming series Blade Runner 2099.

According to Variety, The Confessions will also feature Maya Hawke and Harry Melling. Hawke gained recognition for playing Robin Buckley in Stranger Things, while Melling recently featured in Pillion.

Guy Maddin, Galen Johnson, and Evan Johnson will direct the film. Aster and his longtime producing partner Lars Knudsen are producing it through their company, Square Peg.

What do we know about The Confessions?

The Confessions is described as a cautionary psycho-dramedy. Its plot follows a group of condemned nuns who witness an accursed, globe-spanning love triangle involving a missing sea captain and his poet wife. The filmmakers have described the film as “part religio-maritime rough-music psychomachy, part hallucinated saltwater shaming parade,” suggesting an unconventional storytelling approach.

The project reunites the three directors with Square Peg after their work on Rumours. The 2024 film features Cate Blanchett, Alicia Vikander, and Charles Dance in a political satire about world leaders stranded in a forest during a G7 summit. It premiered at the Cannes Film Festival in 2024.

The production team also includes Daniel Bekerman’s Scythia Films and the directors’ Canadian company, Thin Stuff. Telefilm Canada is supporting the film. CAA Media Finance and WME Independent are jointly handling North American rights, while Charades is overseeing international sales. Elevation Pictures will distribute the film in Canada.

The filmmakers are taking the project to the American Film Market (AFM), where distributors can explore its international sales opportunities. However, they have not yet announced a production start date or theatrical release window.

With Aster and Knudsen producing, the film also adds another collaboration between Square Peg and filmmakers known for unconventional storytelling.

The Disney project is being written and directed by Joe Nussbaum, best known for Just Add Magic, Will vs. The Future, and Upside-Down Magic. Although Kealoha is reported to lead the live-action, Disney has not confirmed her involvement and has declined to comment.

Furthermore, details about Stolen Wishes remain undisclosed, as neither its storyline nor additional cast details have been announced. The movie also doesn’t have a confirmed release date. The reported casting, however, has added another Disney project to the actress’ career.

From a breakout debut to a growing Hollywood career

Maia Kealoha made her feature-film debut as Lilo Pelekai in the 2025 hit Disney live-action adaptation of Lilo & Stitch by Dean Fleischer Camp. The movie went on to become a billion-dollar box-office hit as it grossed $1.038 billion worldwide. This success also introduced the young Hawaiian actress to the global audience that year.

Apart from the Disney movie, Kealoha also appeared alongside Dave Bautista and Jason Momoa in Prime Video’s The Wrecking Crew. She played Lani Hale, the daughter of the disciplined Navy SEAL James Hale (Bautista) and the niece of Jonny Hale (Momoa). Kealoha also guest-starred in an episode of Electric Bloom.

Apart from these, her upcoming project includes Lilo & Scratch, where she voiced Lilo. This short animated movie is scheduled to release in theaters on November 25, 2026, playing exclusively before the upcoming Disney movie Hexed. Moreover, she is set to star in Nutmeg & Mistletoe as Alma. The Christmas comedy feature is scheduled to release in theaters on December 25, 2026.

Kealoha will next be seen in Lilo & Stitch 2, which will arrive in theaters on May 26, 2028.

posts.title: Netflix’s New No. 1 Show Revisits a Disappearance That Shocked the World
posts.excerpt: A true-crime series revisiting one of the most widely publicized missing-person cases has claimed the top spot on Netflix’s English TV chart. The docuseries debuted at No. 1 for the week of November 2
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Netflix A true-crime series revisiting one of the most widely publicized missing-person cases has claimed the top spot on Netflix’s English TV chart. The docuseries debuted at No. 1 for the week of November 2–8, 2026, drawing millions of viewers. Its arrival has brought renewed attention to a case that remained unresolved for years.

Taken: Natalee Holloway leads the chart with 12.9 million views following its debut. The three-part docuseries examines the May 2005 disappearance of 18-year-old Natalee Holloway during a high school graduation trip to Aruba. She never returned home, and her disappearance prompted extensive media coverage and an island-wide search.

The case continued to draw public attention for nearly two decades, with investigators struggling to find answers. A major development finally emerged in 2023, bringing new information about what happened to Holloway. The Netflix series revisits the case and the events surrounding her disappearance.

What other shows made it to Netflix’s Top 10 in November?

Other Netflix releases and returning series also featured on the English TV chart during the same week. The One About Matthew Perry claimed the No. 2 spot with 4.4 million views, followed by Season 3 of Nobody Wants This at No. 3 with 4 million views.

The romantic comedy follows agnostic podcaster Joanne (Kristen Bell) and unconventional rabbi Noah (Adam Brody) as they move in together and take their relationship to the next level. The series has also been renewed for a fourth season.

Season 2 of Black Doves debuted at No. 4 with 3.8 million views. The spy thriller brings Helen (Keira Knightley) and Sam (Ben Whishaw) together for another mission that threatens the people they love. WWE Raw took the No. 5 spot with 2.3 million views.

Meanwhile, Josh Hartnett-led series Below landed at No. 6 with 2.2 million views. Season 11 of Love Is Blind came in at No. 7 with 2 million views after its reunion episode aired over the weekend.

Will Trent Season 1 secured No. 8 with 1.9 million views, matching Season 4 of The Diplomat at No. 9. Finally, East of Eden, based on John Steinbeck’s novel, secured the No. 10 spot with 1.7 million views in its sixth week on the chart.

posts.title: Passport Legacy Hosts Business Leaders, Partners with CEO IMA Grenada to Drive Strategic Global Mobility Solutions
posts.excerpt: Passport Legacy under the division of the Passport Legacy Group is a leading firm that specializes in global citizenship, residency, international real estate, and corporate solutions like company set
posts.content:
Passport Legacy under the division of the Passport Legacy Group is a leading firm that specializes in global citizenship, residency, international real estate, and corporate solutions like company setup, hosted an intimate cocktail evening featuring Special Guest Thomas Anthony, CEO of IMA Grenada. The event gathered founders, executives, and everyday professionals to explore generational wealth protection, strategic investments, and second citizenship opportunities.

The evening commenced with a welcome address delivered by Weyinmi Oritsejiafor, Managing Director of Passport Legacy Nigeria setting the tone for the night and reaffirming the firm’s commitment to providing tailored advisory services to forward-thinking individuals.

“At Passport Legacy, We are a Swiss owned advisory. We do much more than Passports. We do investment migration and government advisory” Oritsejiafor said, emphasizing that when global mobility is crucial for families and businesses to safeguard their wealth, protect their assets against volatility, and scale internationally, investment migration is a secure foundation for long-term growth.

Oritsejiafor also highlighted that the Passport Legacy Group offers access to international real estate opportunities across key hubs such as Cyprus, Greece, Thailand, Bali, and Dubai. Beyond private advisory, she noted that the firm delivers government advisory services through specialized programs and framework tools, citing their engagement with the government of São Tomé and Príncipe as a key example of this institutional work.

The centerpiece of the evening was a keynote presentation by Special Guest Thomas Anthony, CEO of the Investment Migration Agency Grenada (IMA Grenada). Anthony shared key insights into Grenada’s premier Citizenship by Investment (CBI) framework, detailing its unique economic advantages, tax efficiencies, and strategic global access for business owners and proactive individuals.

Anthony highlighted that Grenada’s Investment Migration framework delivers a transparent gateway for global flexibility and security. Unlike direct US programs like the EB-5, which expose global income and assets to US taxation, Grenada’s E-2 visa pathway allows investors to establish business operations in the US without subjecting their offshore wealth to worldwide taxes.

Anthony further explained that while Grenada itself is an intimate market, the membership in the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) expands direct business reach across an integrated regional market of over 700,000 people. Through a partnership with Passport Legacy, the firm provides tailored guidance to unlock international business opportunities and position Grenada as a premier destination for discerning global investors , giving Nigerian founders a dual advantage of sovereign asset protection and unhindered global growth.

Following the presentation and an interactive Q&A session, the event transitioned into an executive networking session, giving founders, attendees, and professionals the opportunity to connect and exchange ideas in an intimate and welcoming setting.

posts.title: Russell Brand jailed for 10 years for rape, assault
posts.excerpt: Russell Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the rape case, "we'll be OK", before being led down to the cells The post Russell Brand jailed for 10 years for rape, assault app
posts.content:
British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences including rape, as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him.

Brand, 51, showed no emotion as judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims, who had suffered significant and lasting harm.

“About 20 years ago Russell Brand, you were becoming famous, you were clever, and in many people’s eyes you were funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator,” he said.

The judge said Brand’s status protected him until he was exposed in 2023 by journalists from the Sunday Times, The Times and the Channel 4 Dispatches programme, leading to women coming forward to make complaints to police.

Bennathan paid tribute to the “determination and bravery” of the women, adding Brand had repeatedly acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”.

Brand’s wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children, slumped in her seat in the public gallery of London’s Southwark Crown Court as the total sentence of 10 years and six months was announced.

Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the case, “we’ll be OK”, before being led down to the cells.

The disgraced star was convicted by a jury last week of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009.

Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen.

She said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004.

“For many years as his star was rising it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court.

‘Celebrated’

A second woman, a 21-year-old fan he raped in 2009 after they met at one of his shows, told the court she had felt she simply would “not be believed” if she reported him.

“His fame, wealth and influence created a power imbalance which made me feel powerless,” she said.

The hearing came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to be “relentless in making whatever improvements we can” to provide more support for victims.

Brand was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault. But he is facing further investigations after London police revealed rape allegations by two more women.

From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous primetime show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian’s obsession with sex and his no-holds barred delivery contributed to his notoriety.

Brand denied the charges, but he admitted to being “extremely promiscuous” and using his fame to “facilitate sexual access”.

‘Wake-up call’

Born to working-class parents in Essex, east of London, in 1975, Brand dropped out of drama school before joining MTV at the age of 25.

He had his own radio show at the BBC, which last week apologised for the “culture and failings” when Brand worked there between 2006 and 2008.

Brand left the BBC after leaving a well-known actor sexually explicit messages on his answering machine about having slept with his granddaughter.

He made a foray into Hollywood after a brief marriage in 2010 to US pop star Katy Perry.

The court found him guilty of sexual assaults against an MTV worker, a Channel 4 worker and a Capital Radio employee, as well as raping a fan.

The organisations that propped up Brand for years are now facing questions about how he continued for so long.

British culture minister Lisa Nandy said men in power were still exploiting women in the media industry, saying his case was a “wake-up call”.

Speaking outside court, the lead detective in the case Andy Furphy said the sentence was a “milestone” that had seen Brand finally “held accountable for his crimes”.

And he praised the “immense bravery, dignity and resilience” of the victims who had had “to revisit deeply traumatic experiences”.

As he left court, Brand’s father Ron Brand told reporters his son had been a “victim” and that both Russell and his daughter-in-law would be alright.

“Yeah, he’s strong, he’s strong,” he said, when asked how his son would cope in jail, adding “she’s strong as well”, referring to Laura.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/russell-brand-jailed-for-10-years-for-rape-assault/

posts.title: Toluwanisings laid to rest in Ibadan
posts.excerpt: Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has been laid to rest at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State, bringing an end to weeks of disagreement among members of
posts.content:
By Wasiu Rokibat

Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has been laid to rest at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State, bringing an end to weeks of disagreement among members of his family over his final resting place.

The gospel artiste was buried on Monday, November 9, 2026, in a private ceremony attended by family members following a funeral service at Banjola Event and Conference Centre, Alakia, Ibadan.

His burial came after a disagreement between his widow, Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola, and his paternal relatives over where his remains should be interred.

While his paternal family had expressed concerns about the circumstances surrounding his death and initially pushed for his burial in Ikirun, Osun State, his widow and associates were involved in discussions over the final arrangements.

The disagreement attracted public attention and eventually prompted the intervention of the Oyo State Police Command.

On November 3, the parties involved signed a peace undertaking at the police command headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, agreeing to avoid further public exchanges and actions capable of escalating tensions.

Speaking on the agreement, the police command stated that, “All parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace.”

The intervention paved the way for the family to settle on burying the singer at his Ibadan residence, where his wife and children live.

Toluwanisings, who was widely recognised for his energetic worship ministrations and gospel songs, including A Very Big God, died on October 14, 2026.

His death generated reactions across the gospel music community, while the disagreement surrounding his burial further drew public attention to the family’s situation.

Vanguard News

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/toluwanisings-laid-to-rest-in-ibadan/

posts.title: ‘I’m not a paedophile,’ Baba Ijesha insists, recalls living with Oga Bello’s daughters
posts.excerpt: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nollywood actor Olanrewaju Omiyinka, popularly known as Baba Ijesha, has again maintained his innocence, saying he did not know the meaning of “paedophile” until his arrest in 20
posts.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Nollywood actor Olanrewaju Omiyinka, popularly known as Baba Ijesha, has again maintained his innocence, saying he did not know the meaning of “paedophile” until his arrest in 2021 over the alleged sexual assault of a minor.

In a recent interview with Agbaletu TV, the actor also recalled living in the home of veteran actor Adebayo Salami, known as Oga Bello, where he said he shared the house with Salami’s daughters.

“I am not a paedophile. I only got to know the word paedophile when I was arrested,” Baba Ijesha said.

“I once lived in Oga Bello’s house. He has many daughters. We would all gather in the sitting room with a big fan. If you live in Oga Bello’s house and you are not wise, you cannot survive anywhere else, because God helped him to raise his children well.

“Femi cannot look at his father’s face when it comes to theatre work. He dares not. All his children value education. I used to eat with him.”

A Lagos High Court convicted and sentenced him to 16 years in prison in July 2022 and he was released in November 2025, about three years and four months after his July 2022 sentencing, having completed the custodial term calculated for his convictions.

Baba Ijesha’s case began on June 24, 2021, when prosecutors filed six charges, including indecent treatment of a child, sexual assault and attempted sexual assault by penetration.

On July 14, 2022, a Lagos High Court sentenced him to 16 years in prison for sexually assaulting a minor. The sentences were to run concurrently.

The actor maintained his innocence while in prison. In April 2024, he alleged that he had been set up and was “acting according to a script” provided by a colleague.

He was released in November 2025 after completing his sentence. His name was also added to the Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency’s sexual offenders register in 2025.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/im-not-a-paedophile-baba-ijesha-insists-recalls-living-with-oga-bellos-daughters/

artists.name: Burna Boy
artists.bio: Damini Ebunoluwa Ogulu, known professionally as Burna Boy, is a Nigerian singer, songwriter, and record producer. He gained recognition in 2012 after releasing "Like to Party", the lead single from his debut studio album L.I.F.E (2013). In 2017, Burna Boy signed a record deal with Atlantic Records and its parent company Warner Music Group. His third studio album Outside, which became his major label debut, was released in 2018.

artists.name: Davido
artists.bio: David Adedeji Adeleke, known professionally as Davido, is a Nigerian-American singer, songwriter, and record producer. Davido was born in Atlanta, U.S, and raised in Lagos, Nigeria. He made his music debut as a member of the group KB International. Davido studied business administration at Oakwood University before dropping out to make beats and record vocal references. He rose to fame after releasing "Dami Duro", the second single from his debut studio album Omo Baba Olowo (2012), from which six additional singles—"Back When", "Ekuro", "Overseas", "All of You", "Gbon Gbon" and "Feel Alright"—were taken. In 2012, Davido won the Next Rated award at The Headies. Between 2013 and 2015, he released the singles "Gobe", "One of a Kind", "Skelewu", "Aye", "Tchelete (Goodlife)", "Naughty", "Owo Ni Koko", "The Sound" and "The Money".

artists.name: YoungBoy Never Broke Again
artists.bio: Kentrell DeSean Gaulden, known professionally as YoungBoy Never Broke Again or NBA YoungBoy, is an American rapper, singer, and songwriter. Gaulden released eight mixtapes from 2015 to 2017, and garnered a regional following for his work. He signed with Atlantic Records and Artist Partner Group in the latter year to release the singles "Untouchable" and "No Smoke", both of which marked his first entries on the Billboard Hot 100. Released in January 2018, his single "Outside Today" became his first to peak within the chart's top 40, and received quadruple platinum certification by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). It served as both his mainstream breakthrough and the lead single for his debut studio album, Until Death Call My Name (2018), which peaked at number seven on the US Billboard 200 despite mixed critical reception.

artists.name: Frank Edwards (gospel musician)
artists.bio: Frank Ugochukwu Edwards is a Nigerian musician, record producer, sound engineer, worship singer and songwriter from Enugu State. He is the founder and owner of the record label Rocktown Records, which is home to recording artists such as Edwards himself, Gil Joe, King BAS, Nkay, Dudu and, among others. He lives in Lagos, Nigeria.

artists.name: Wizkid
artists.bio: Ayodeji Ibrahim Balogun, known professionally as Wizkid, is a Nigerian singer and songwriter. Born in the Ojuelegba suburb of Surulere, Lagos, Wizkid is a voice in the emerging Afrobeats movement. His music is a blend of Afrobeats, afropop, R&B, afrobeat, reggae, dancehall, and pop. He began recording music at the age of 11 and released a collaborative album with the Glorious Five, a group he and a few of his church friends formed. In 2009, Wizkid signed a record deal with Banky W's Empire Mates Entertainment (E.M.E). He gained recognition after releasing "Holla at Your Boy", the lead single from his debut studio album, Superstar (2011), which also spawned the singles "Tease Me/Bad Guys" and "Don't Dull".

artists.name: Michael Jackson
artists.bio: Michael Joseph Jackson was an American singer, songwriter, dancer, and philanthropist. Dubbed the "King of Pop", he is widely regarded as one of the most culturally significant figures of the 20th century. His musical achievements broke American racial barriers and made him a dominant figure worldwide. Through his songs, music videos, concerts, and fashion, he transformed visual performance in popular music, popularizing street dance moves such as the moonwalk, the robot, and the anti-gravity lean. Jackson is often deemed the greatest entertainer of all time.

artists.name: Asake
artists.bio: Ahmed Ololade, known professionally as Asake, is a Nigerian singer, rapper, and songwriter. His debut album, Mr. Money with the Vibe (2022) broke the record for the biggest opening day for an African album on Apple Music at the time and debuted at number 66 on the Billboard 200 chart. His second album Work of Art (2023), matched the chart position of its predecessor. Asake's third album Lungu Boy (2024) became his third consecutive number one album in Nigeria and the longest-running number one in Nigeria chart history.

artists.name: Fela Kuti
artists.bio: Fela Aníkúlápó Kútì was a Nigerian musician and political activist. He is regarded as the principal innovator of Afrobeat, a Nigerian music genre that combines West African music with American funk and jazz. At the height of his popularity, he was referred to as one of Africa's most "challenging and charismatic music performers". AllMusic described him as "a musical and sociopolitical voice" of international significance.

artists.name: Seyi Vibez
artists.bio: Balogun Afolabi Oluwaloseyi known professionally as Seyi Vibez, is a Nigerian singer and songwriter. He is known for his breakthrough single "Chance " from his second studio album Billion Dollar Baby which debuted at No. 19 on the UK Afrobeats singles chart and peaked number 7 on the TurnTable Top 100 chart.

artists.name: Central Cee
artists.bio: Oakley Neil Caesar-Su, known professionally as Central Cee, is a British rapper from Shepherd's Bush, London. Regarded as a leading figure in UK rap, he rose to prominence in 2020 with the release of his drill singles "Day in the Life" and "Loading". His first mixtape, Wild West (2021), debuted at number two on the UK Albums Chart, while his second, 23 (2022), debuted atop the chart.

artists.name: Lil Durk
artists.bio: Durk Devontay Banks, known professionally as Lil Durk, is an American rapper. Regarded as a pioneer of the Chicago-based hip-hop subgenre drill music, he is often considered the subgenre's most commercially successful rapper. He initially garnered local success with the release of his Signed to the Streets mixtape series (2013–2014), which led to him to sign with Def Jam Recordings. The label released his debut studio album, Remember My Name (2015), and its follow-up, Lil Durk 2X (2016), to moderate commercial reception before parting ways with the rapper in 2018.

artists.name: Drake (musician)
artists.bio: Aubrey Drake Graham is a Canadian rapper and singer. He is credited with popularizing R&B sensibilities in hip-hop music through rap-singing. Drake first gained recognition as Jimmy Brooks in the CTV teen drama series Degrassi: The Next Generation (2001–2008) and began his music career by independently releasing the mixtapes Room for Improvement (2006), Comeback Season (2007), and So Far Gone (2009), before signing with Young Money Entertainment.

artists.name: Eminem
artists.bio: Marshall Bruce Mathers III, known professionally as Eminem, is an American rapper, songwriter, record producer, and record executive. Known for his rap flow and conscious rap, which includes political criticism and social commentary, he is widely regarded as one of the greatest and most influential rappers of all time, often credited with popularizing hip-hop in Middle America and the acceptance of white rappers. While much of his transgressive art during the late 1990s and early 2000s made him a controversial figure, Eminem has become a representation of popular angst in lower-income America.

artists.name: Lil Baby
artists.bio: Dominique Armani Jones, known professionally as Lil Baby, is an American rapper, singer, and songwriter. He rose to prominence following the release of his 2017 mixtapes Harder than Hard and Too Hard — the former of which spawned his first Billboard Hot 100 entry with its lead single, "My Dawg." He signed with Quality Control Music, an imprint of Motown and Capitol Records to release his debut studio album Harder Than Ever (2018), which peaked at number three on the Billboard 200 and was supported by the Billboard Hot 100-top ten single "Yes Indeed". Later that year, he released the collaborative mixtape Drip Harder with fellow Georgia-based rapper Gunna, and his solo mixtape Street Gossip; the former spawned his second top-ten single "Drip Too Hard", while the latter peaked at number two on the Billboard 200.

artists.name: Chioma Jesus
artists.bio: Amaka Okwuoha, known professionally as Chioma Jesus, is a Nigerian gospel singer, songwriter, and worship leader. She rose to prominence with the release of her 2003 song "Chioma," from which her stage name is derived. She is recognized for her contributions to the popularization of indigenous gospel music, particularly songs performed in the Igbo language.

artists.name: Sparqlyn
artists.bio: Ahmmed Kanneh Larweh, popularly known as Sparqlyn, is a Ghanaian Afrobeats musician and songwriter. He was a member of the defunct hiplife group, Dunsin. In January 2023, he was enstooled as the Development Chief at Krobo Odumase in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

artists.name: Theophilus Sunday
artists.bio: Theophilus Sunday is a Nigerian gospel minister, singer, and songwriter.

artists.name: Olamide
artists.bio: Olamide is a Nigerian rapper and singer known professionally as Olamide. He is associated with Nigerian hip-hop and Afrobeats.

artists.name: DeeYasso
artists.bio: Dennis Hope Yasso, professionally known as DeeYasso is a Nigerian record producer, mixing & mastering engineer, multi-Instrumentalist, songwriter and a lawyer. He made his mainstream debut when he produced Yemi Alade's song titled "Tomorrow" which received a nomination at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards for Best African Music Performance

artists.name: Chella (singer)
artists.bio: Uzochukwu Michael Ikechukwu, known professionally as Chella, is a Nigerian singer-songwriter. He gained recognition in 2024 with the release of his single, "Nyash Na Nyash". He followed up with "My Darling", which peaked at number 1 on the Shazam Global chart and became the fourth Nigerian song in history to top the chart. It also peaked at number 1 on the official Nigeria TurnTable Top 100 songs, and at number 8 on the Billboard U.S. Afrobeats Songs chart.

artists.name: Speed Darlington
artists.bio: Darlington Okoye popularly known as Speed Darlington, is a Nigerian rapper. He was born in Bronx, New York, USA, to musicians Pericoma Okoye and Queen Achakpo. Darlington was raised in the Bronx, New York, and began his journey in the arts as a dancer in the 1990s. His shift to music came in 2017 with the release of his single "Bangdadadang!" His style blends Afrobeat, pop, and rap. Over the years, he has released several other tracks, including "Akamu," "Cash & Carry," "Ogiriga Owuwa" and "Baby Oil".

artists.name: Portable (musician)
artists.bio: Habeeb Okikiola Badmus, popularly known as Portable, is a Nigerian singer, songwriter and rapper. He is known for controversies and online buzz.

artists.name: Chike
artists.bio: Chike is a Nigerian singer and songwriter known for soulful Afrobeats and R&B-influenced music. He gained wider recognition after appearing on Nigerian Idol.

artists.name: Coolio
artists.bio: Coolio was the stage name of Artis Leon Ivey Jr., an American rapper, songwriter and record producer. He was best known for "Gangsta's Paradise" (1995), which won a Grammy Award, and also released singles including "Fantastic Voyage" (1994) and "C U When U Get There" (1997).

artists.name: 50 Cent
artists.bio: Curtis James Jackson III, known professionally as 50 Cent, is an American rapper, actor, television producer, record executive, and businessman. Born in Queens, a borough of New York City, Jackson began pursuing a musical career in 1996. In 1999–2000, he recorded his debut album, Power of the Dollar, for Columbia Records. During a shooting in May 2000, he was struck by nine bullets, causing its release to be canceled and Jackson to be dropped from the label. His 2002 mixtape Guess Who's Back? was discovered by Detroit rapper Eminem, who signed Jackson to his label Shady Records that year.

artists.name: Kirk Franklin
artists.bio: Kirk Dewayne Franklin is an American gospel singer, rapper, songwriter, composer, record producer, and choir director. Franklin's accolades include 20 Grammy Awards, and Variety has called him a "Reigning King of Urban Gospel", with Franklin being one of the inaugural inductees into the Black Music & Entertainment Walk of Fame. In his earlier career, his act included choirs such as the Family, God's Property, and One Nation Crew (1NC).
